CryptoBilis update

We've been made aware, through responsible disclosure, of a single hardware implant in a Trezor Safe 5 device bought from the reseller CryptoBilis in August 2026.

No CryptoBilis buyer has reported a loss of funds to us.

IMPORTANT: If you bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis from March 2026 onwards, we know this is unsettling. Here’s what to do:

Already using it?

Move your funds to a newly created wallet with a new seed as soon as possible. Do not reuse the old seed in any wallet, hardware or software.  If you don’t have another secure hardware wallet available, we recommend temporarily migrating your funds to a software wallet or an exchange you are familiar with.  

Not set up yet? Don’t set it up, and never enter your existing wallet backup on it.

We haven’t received the device to confirm this report, but based on the customer’s description, we’re treating it as credible and sharing it now so customers who purchased a Trezor via CryptoBilis can secure their funds as a precaution. Our security team will examine the device as soon as it arrives.

On October 9, 2026, we removed CryptoBilis as a reseller following reports of tampered Ledger devices sold through it. Since then, we have been inspecting Trezor devices that customers bought from CryptoBilis and have found no signs of tampering on any of the four devices we’ve received so far.

NEVER share your wallet backup (recovery phrase) with anyone. Trezor Support will never ask for it.
If you are affected by this incident, please keep your CryptoBilis device and contact Support to receive a new Trezor hardware wallet: https://t.co/5EasOVDDQh

We're investigating and will post updates here as soon as we know more.  Thank you to the customer who reported this through our responsible disclosure program, and to @SEAL_911 for working alongside our teams on the response. Reports and engagement like this help us protect everyone else.

For more information, visit our blog: https://t.co/2LmFV8L2oe

text:
I want to speak to you directly about what happened.

Bottom line - your money is safe, and we're covering every loss.

Our initial investigation suggests this security incident may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop. That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions.

To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single "one-click" action. It involved a more complex attack process. Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.

So far, we have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak.

We'll share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and every fact is verified - and publish an updated Proof of Reserves once remediation is complete.

What you need to know:
• Your funds are safe
• Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and company funds
• Estimated total impact: ~$6.3B, with ~$3B frozen on-chain so far, in coordination with our blockchain partners
• No evidence of any wallet private key leak
• Deposits are unaffected and operating as normal

What we've done:
• Temporarily suspended withdrawals while we complete a security revamp of the withdrawal service and its related addresses
• Revoked the affected address authorizations
• Engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds

Our team hasn't stopped. We're working closely with law enforcement to ensure the matter is handled appropriately - and I'll share what I can, as soon as I can.

author: heyibinance
quoted_text:
关于本次安全事件，大家对技术细节有不少疑问，就目前掌握的信息，这里统一说明几点：

1️⃣ 这不是攻破一台电脑就把钱转走了
这并不是一次通过单一设备就能完成的事件，一个员工电脑被黑是这个攻击的起点。针对加密机构的攻击通常具有较强的针对性，攻击者往往尝试利用了复杂的手段实施渗透。

我们已经发现与事件相关的重要线索，并已第一时间采取措施控制风险，相关调查和溯源工作仍在持续进行中。现阶段，平台核心风控和应急机制已经启动，用户资产安全是我们的首要保障。

2️⃣ 关于"工程师是不是权限过大"
这并不是攻击者直接利用某位工程师权限即可完成资金转移的事件，也不是单一人员可以“一键操作”造成的结果。相关异常涉及更复杂的攻击过程。需要强调的是，现阶段调查并未将责任归因于任何个人，公司将承担相应责任，并持续推进后续处置与安全升级工作。

3️⃣ 目前能确认的事实
没有发现钱包私钥泄露的证据。用户资金安全，本次事件造成的全部被盗损失由 SAFU 基金和公司资金全额承担，不需要用户承担。目前链上已冻结约 30 亿美元受影响资产，我们正配合执法部门和区块链情报机构追查，链上资金流向公开可查。

4️⃣ 充提状态
充值全程正常开放，未受影响。提现作为预防性措施已暂停，预计在48小时内开放，具体时间以官方公告为准。我们理解这对大家造成了不便，会尽快同步进展。

5️⃣ 后续
我们会在确保调查准确性的前提下，持续同步进展，并在事件处置和复盘完成后公布详细情况和进一步的安全加固措施。该暴露的问题我们会正视，不会含糊。

感谢大家的耐心和监督。

quoted_text:
🚨 Binance : comprendre l’attaque EIP-7702 en 2 minutes

Ce soir, plusieurs milliards de dollars sont sortis de hot wallets Binance en moins d’une heure. Les décomptes vont de ~3,3 Md$ à ~5,5 Md$ selon les sources. Binance enquête et n’a encore confirmé aucun impact sur les fonds des utilisateurs. CZ, lui, parle de hack.

💡 Au delà du potentiel plus gros hack de l'histoire de la crypto, ce qui interroge c'est la méthode.
Et elle porte un nom : EIP-7702.

🔹 C’est quoi EIP-7702 ?

Sur Ethereum, un wallet classique, c’est une clé privée qui signe des transactions. Point.

Depuis la mise à jour Pectra (mai 2025), EIP-7702 permet à ce wallet de se « brancher » sur un smart contract. Il garde la même adresse, mais le code du contrat peut agir avec toute son autorité.

L’idée de départ est bonne : regrouper des opérations, payer les frais pour quelqu’un, ajouter des options de récupération.

Le problème, c’est que la délégation persiste. Une fois installée, le contrat peut déclencher des transferts sans nouvelle signature du wallet.

Imaginez signer une seule procuration générale au nom d’un robot. Ensuite, le robot vide le coffre tout seul. Pour la blockchain, tout est « légal », puisque le robot a une autorisation valide.

🔹 Ce qui s’est passé (heures UTC, d’après Etherscan et les analyses publiées)

15h59 : une adresse financée via Tornado Cash déploie un smart contract
20h20 : le wallet Binance 14 est délégué à ce contrat via EIP-7702
20h24 : ~3 min plus tard, 167 464 ETH et 63 tokens, dont 1,6 Md USDT, partent vers une adresse toute neuve
20h41 : 780 M USDC sortent d’un autre hot wallet Binance vers la même adresse
Ensuite, ~195 000 ETH sont redéplacés vers une nouvelle adresse

Tether et Circle ont gelé environ 1,8 Md$ de stablecoins. Le reste a bougé avant le gel.

🔹 Cependant...

Pour installer une délégation EIP-7702, il faut une autorisation signée avec la clé du wallet. N’importe qui peut ensuite l’envoyer et payer les frais, d’où le rôle de l’adresse « Tornado ».

Donc ce n’est a priori pas une faille d’Ethereum.

A l'heure actuelle, plusieurs questions importantes restent en suspens :
- Comment l’attaquant a-t-il obtenu une signature valide d’un hot wallet de Binance ❓
- Clé volée ❓
- Système de signature interne compromis ❓
- Manipulation ❓

Personne ne le sait encore.

EIP-7702 est déjà massivement utilisé par des arnaqueurs pour vider des wallets de particuliers via du phishing : vous signez « un truc », et votre wallet appartient à quelqu’un d’autre.

Ce soir, on voit peut-être le même mécanisme appliqué à l’échelle d’un exchange.

👉 Règle d’or :
- ne signez jamais une autorisation que vous ne comprenez pas. Une signature peut valoir plus qu’une transaction.
- ne laissez jamais tous vos fonds au même endroit

text:
A friendly reminder to take your crypto security seriously.

Start doing these things TODAY:

- Keep your long-term holdings offline.
Consider a hardware wallet or an air-gapped wallet on a dedicated offline device.
If you don't want to buy a hardware wallet, air-gapped storage is an alternative.

- Never use one wallet for everything.
Keep separate wallets for long-term holdings, trading, DeFi, airdrops, and unfamiliar protocols.
@Rabby_io and @phantom are the only wallets I use.

- Don't keep your entire portfolio in one place.
Avoid concentrating all your funds on a single CEX, hot wallet, protocol, or device.

- Don't use public Wi-Fi for crypto activity.
If you work from cafes or coworking spaces, use your phone's personal hotspot instead of connecting to public Wi-Fi networks.

- Protect your seed phrases.
Never store them in screens, cloud storage, emails, or password managers connected to the internet.
If your seed phrase has ever been stored on an internet-connected device - migrate to a fresh wallet NOW!

- Keep secure offline backups.
Store recovery backups somewhere safe, preferably with protection against fire/water and unauthorized access.
I recommend getting a fire-resistant and water-resistant document bag.

- Use a dedicated device for crypto.
Keep your hot wallets and high-value transactions on a separate device.
Don't use it for random downloads, gaming mods, unknown software, or everyday browsing.

- Use a separate browser for wallets.
Keep your wallet browser dedicated to trusted crypto activity.
Avoid unnecessary extensions and random websites.

- Never install cracked software on crypto devices.
Pirated applications, fake installers, and malicious updates can contain wallet-stealing malware.
If you need to run untrusted software, keep it completely isolated from your crypto environment.

- Keep your devices updated.
Update your OS, browser, and wallet software through official sources.

- Remove unnecessary browser extensions.
Even legitimate extensions can become dangerous after a compromised update or ownership change.
Keep only what you absolutely need.

- Stop using Google Search to find crypto websites.
Fake websites and malicious sponsored results can look almost identical to legitimate ones.
Use independently verified official links from bookmarks instead.

- Don't open random links from X or Telegram.
Especially not in the browser where your wallets are installed.
Never!!!

- Secure your CEX accounts.
Use passkeys or hardware security keys where supported.
Enable withdrawal address whitelists and avoid relying on SMS 2FA.

- Consider getting a YubiKey.
A physical security key can help protect your email and exchange accounts against phishing.
Buy only from the official manufacturer sellers.

- Review your Google-connected crypto accounts.
Check which crypto services use Google Sign-In.
Never disconnect your only login method without setting up an alternative first.

- Revoke unnecessary token approvals.
Use @RevokeCash to review and remove permissions you no longer need.
Disconnecting a wallet from a dApp does NOT revoke its token approvals.

- Avoid unlimited token approvals.
Whenever possible, approve only the amount you actually need.
Unlimited allowances can expose much larger balances if a spender is compromised.

- Review Permit2 permissions.
Permit2 signatures can authorize token transfers without a normal on-chain approval transaction.
Review existing allowances and permissions. Some malicious signatures can be exploited long after they're signed.

- Never blindly sign messages.
A signature doesn't need to cost gas to be dangerous.
Never get distracted while signing transactions. Either finish your transactions first or take care of everything else before you start.
Make this a rule.

- Be careful with custom RPC endpoints.
Don't add/delete now unknown RPC URLs.
Use trusted providers and verify network settings independently.

- Understand EIP-7702 authorization risks.
On supported networks, account delegation can grant powerful capabilities to other code.
Never approve an account delegation you don't understand. (That's why Binance was hacked)

- Never copy addresses blindly from transaction history.
Address poisoning attacks can place lookalike addresses in your transaction history.
Verify the full destination address against a trusted source.

- Watch out for clipboard malware.
Malware can replace a copied wallet address with an attacker's address.
Always verify the entire destination address after pasting, preferably on an independent trusted display.

- Verify token contracts and networks.
A familiar ticker or logo doesn't prove a token is legitimate.
Check the contract address and make sure the receiving platform supports the exact asset and network.

- Test large transfers first.
When sending funds to a new destination, start with a small test transaction.

- Ignore unexpected tokens and NFTs.
Random assets appearing in your wallet may contain phishing links or fake reward claims.
Don't interact with them just because they appeared in your balance.

- Don't trust unexpected job offers or collaboration requests.
Fake interviews, partnership offers, and test applications can be used to distribute wallet-stealing malware.
Never run unfamiliar software on your crypto device just to qualify for an opportunity.

- Never run terminal commands you don't understand.
Fake troubleshooting guides, verification pages, and job interviews may ask you to copy and paste commands into your terminal.
One malicious command can compromise your entire device, including your wallets.

- Never trust a QR code blindly.
QR code can contain a malicious website, payment request or an attacker's wallet address.
Avoid scanning unknown QR codes with devices that contain your crypto wallets or other sensitive data.

- Understand bridge and DeFi risks.
Before depositing significant funds, check contract upgradeability, admin privileges, timelocks, and bridge security assumptions.
Audits are useful, but they don't guarantee safety.

- Secure your multisig properly.
If you use @Safe or another multisig, keep signer keys on independent devices.
Review owners, signing thresholds, modules, and guards.
A malicious module may bypass normal multisig approval requirements.

- Monitor your wallets.
Set up alerts for unexpected transfers, approvals, and other sensitive activity where supported.
Use Codex/Claude to vibe-code a simple TG-bot that notifies you whenever something happens in your wallets.

- Have an emergency recovery plan.
Know what to do if a wallet, seed phrase, device, or exchange account is compromised.
If your seed phrase is exposed, move your assets to a new wallet generated from a fresh seed on a trusted device.
Revoking approvals alone won't fix a compromised private key.

- Keep your crypto holdings private.
Avoid publicly revealing wallet balances, screenshots of large portfolios, or details of your security setup.
Don't make yourself an easy target for social engineering or physical theft.

- Protect yourself from SIM swapping.
Attackers can hijack your phone number and intercept SMS verification codes.
Use authenticator apps, passkeys, or hardware security keys instead of SMS wherever possible. Secure your mobile carrier account too.

- Don't blindly trust familiar contacts.
A message from someone you know doesn't mean their account is still under their control.
Verify it through another channel first.

- And one last thing:
You don't need to be paranoid.
You just need to make it much harder for someone to steal what you've spent years building.

Protect your capital before you think about growing it.

quoted_text:
The recent security incidents involving Bybit, Bitget, and now Binance should serve as a wake-up call for every leader in the crypto industry.

Security should never be an area of commercial competition. It is a shared responsibility to protect our customers and the entire industry.

Over the past decade, major crypto exchanges have made significant progress in protecting private keys. We have seen relatively few incidents involving direct private key compromises in recent years. So far, we have not seen conclusive evidence that Binance’s hot wallet private key was leaked. The greater concern may lie in vulnerabilities in access controls and wallet management systems.

Companies that have never experienced a major security incident should not assume they are inherently safer or immune to attacks.

At OKX, we have built multiple layers of sophisticated security protection and maintained a strong security track record over the past decade. But we also recognize that no system is absolutely secure. We must remain humble, vigilant, and constantly challenge our own security assumptions.

A major security breach at any exchange undermines trust in the entire crypto industry, ultimately hurting every company and every customer.

I believe CEOs across the industry need to come together, just as we did during the Bitcoin fork crisis in 2017, to establish stronger industry-wide security standards and coordinated response mechanisms.

For example, transfers and settlements between verified exchanges could be processed in real time, while large withdrawals to unknown or unverified addresses, as well as transactions granting smart contract permissions, should be subject to additional verification and appropriate security delays.

Crucially, these safeguards should be enforced at the cryptographic signing layer, rather than relying solely on application-level controls. Even if an attacker compromises an exchange’s wallet management system, they should not be able to bypass these fundamental security restrictions.

We should also establish industry-wide mechanisms for real-time security incident notifications, coordinated monitoring of suspicious funds, and rapid responses to potential attacks. Exchanges, stablecoin issuers, and other major industry participants should work together to enable the rapid, lawful temporary freezing of suspected stolen assets when necessary.

We should also work together to accelerate the industry’s transition to quantum-resistant cryptography and strengthen our defenses against emerging AI-powered security threats. These are long-term challenges that no single company can solve alone, and they require coordinated research, shared standards, and collective action across the industry.

Security is everyone’s responsibility. No company can protect the future of crypto alone.

author: Xudong07452910
quoted_text:
RAG 又杀回来了。

最近 Agent Memory 越做越复杂，但这篇《Memory Tax》发现了一个挺尴尬的结果：

很多专门设计的 Memory 系统，最后还不如直接对 raw history 做 RAG，而且成本更高。

作者把 Memory 的价值拆成两部分：

Memory Benefit：RAG 答错，但 Memory 答对的问题。

Memory Tax：RAG 本来能答对，经过 Memory 处理后反而答错的问题。

问题就出在「整理记忆」这一步。

历史被摘要、重写和结构化以后，一些细节会直接丢失；另一些虽然还在，却变得更难检索。

比如在 LongMemEval 上，Qwen3.6-27B 用两轮 RAG 能做到 81.4%，GPT-5.6 Luna 达到 90%，都高于对应的复杂 Memory 方案。

一个简单的修补反而很有效：

Memory 继续用，但同时保留 raw history 的检索通道，再把两边结果一起 rerank。

这篇工作也给我们做了一个提醒，给 Agent 加 Memory 之前，最好先拿最简单的 raw-history RAG 做个 baseline。

有时候，真正昂贵的并不是「没记住」，而是过早把原始信息总结掉了。

quoted_text:
When I first got into Crypto Twitter, everyone kept telling me the same thing: if I was serious about building a career and making a name for myself, I needed to start showing up IRL.

I had $600 to my name.

But deep down, I knew they were right.

So I borrowed a few thousand dollars from my dad, booked a hotel in Miami during Art Basel (NOT cheap), and flew across the country to meet a bunch of strangers from the internet who traded pictures of monkeys.

I got to Miami and found out my hotel had DOUBLE BOOKED MY ROOM.

No rooms available. No alternatives.

I was officially homeless and broke in Miami.

Naturally, I went on Twitter Spaces to freak out because the only thing scarier than being stranded in Miami was calling my Italian father to explain that his loan to meet my internet friends had resulted in homelessness.

I would never survive Christmas.

A girl listening to the Space said she knew a guy who could fix just about anything.

Enter @XicoSR 

This man, who had never met me in his life, showed up at my hotel in an Uber, picked up my luggage and my very sad self, and brought me back to his hotel.

He gave me HIS room and went to sleep at the Solana Hacker House instead.

That was the first time I’d ever heard of a Hacker House.

He invited me to check it out and also brought me VIP to a massive FTX party at ToeJam.

I need you to understand how absurd this was.

I was a kindergarten teacher who had accidentally gone viral on the internet and stumbled into crypto.

Now I was sitting in bottle service next to Dave Portnoy, meeting executives at huge crypto companies, and being recognized by people who’d listened to my Twitter Spaces.

But what stuck with me wasn’t the party.

It was how many people genuinely wanted to see me succeed. People gave me advice, made introductions, and believed in me before I’d really figured out what I was doing.

Then I went to the Miami Hacker House.

I saw what people were building, listened to conversations I barely understood, and realized there was an entire world beyond Crypto Twitter that I desperately wanted to be part of.

A month later, I was showing up at side events around Chicago Hacker House.

By LA Hacker House, I was FULL SEND.

And I pretty much never stopped showing up.

Without Xico, I genuinely don’t know if I’d be here today.

Without Hacker Houses, I don’t know where I’d be either.

Years later, I get to help other people find their way into this industry, and I think about that first trip a lot.

Sometimes all someone needs is for someone else to open a door.

TL;DR: Befriend Xico. Go to Hacker House London.

You have no idea how much your life could change just by showing up.

text:
New post on Eth Research!

Post-quantum signatureless authorization with recursive verification

By:
- ignotusnemo

🔗 https://t.co/iDdcHgTsxQ

Highlights:
- Signatureless authorization replaces digital signatures with reusable zero-knowledge proofs of knowledge of a secret bound to a specific intent (request), aiming to remain secure in a post-quantum setting.
- The key security challenge is safe reuse under adaptive, chosen-request attacks; the paper gives a quantum security reduction in an explicit “address-compatible random-completion” model and quantifies forgery probability in terms of preimage, simulation, extraction, and binding failures.
- The construction is specialized to binary fields (using F_{2^128} inside F_{2^256}) and uses a Poseidon2b-based authority relation plus masking, linear-claim reductions, and a Reed–Solomon-style code argument with fixed-before-challenge transcript structure to ensure binding and extractability.
- It is designed for recursive verification: the verifier checks the capsule using compatible binary-field arithmetic, enabling composition with proofs of execution while keeping authorization independent of public execution state for a fixed intent and authority.
- An implementation is provided with measurements: median proving around ~0.8–0.9s and verification ~25.6ms on the stated CPU setup, with capsule sizes roughly ~89–90KB and a maximum canonical size of 92,696 bytes; the verifier tile adds 16,536 incremental rows in the recursive system.

ELI5:
Normally, you prove you’re allowed to do something by signing with a private key. Quantum computers could break many of today’s signatures. This work replaces signatures with a different idea: you publish a public “commitment” (like an address) to a secret, and every time you want to authorize an action you send a fresh zero-knowledge proof that you know that secret and that it matches the requested action. The proof reveals nothing about the secret, can be safely reused many times with new randomness, and can be checked inside larger recursive proofs so systems can prove “this action was authorized and executed correctly” in one combined proof.

关于本次安全事件，大家对技术细节有不少疑问，就目前掌握的信息，这里统一说明几点：

1️⃣ 这不是攻破一台电脑就把钱转走了
这并不是一次通过单一设备就能完成的事件，一个员工电脑被黑是这个攻击的起点。针对加密机构的攻击通常具有较强的针对性，攻击者往往尝试利用了复杂的手段实施渗透。

我们已经发现与事件相关的重要线索，并已第一时间采取措施控制风险，相关调查和溯源工作仍在持续进行中。现阶段，平台核心风控和应急机制已经启动，用户资产安全是我们的首要保障。

2️⃣ 关于"工程师是不是权限过大"
这并不是攻击者直接利用某位工程师权限即可完成资金转移的事件，也不是单一人员可以“一键操作”造成的结果。相关异常涉及更复杂的攻击过程。需要强调的是，现阶段调查并未将责任归因于任何个人，公司将承担相应责任，并持续推进后续处置与安全升级工作。

3️⃣ 目前能确认的事实
没有发现钱包私钥泄露的证据。用户资金安全，本次事件造成的全部被盗损失由 SAFU 基金和公司资金全额承担，不需要用户承担。目前链上已冻结约 30 亿美元受影响资产，我们正配合执法部门和区块链情报机构追查，链上资金流向公开可查。

充值全程正常开放，未受影响。提现作为预防性措施已暂停，预计在48小时内开放，具体时间以官方公告为准。我们理解这对大家造成了不便，会尽快同步进展。

5️⃣ 后续
我们会在确保调查准确性的前提下，持续同步进展，并在事件处置和复盘完成后公布详细情况和进一步的安全加固措施。该暴露的问题我们会正视，不会含糊。

quoted_text:
I suspect IBIT is already on North Korea’s shortlist.

In February 2025, the attackers behind the Bybit hack compromised a Safe{Wallet} developer’s Mac through a malicious project disguised as legitimate Docker-related tooling. They had access for 17 days before the theft, giving them enough time to manipulate the transaction interface used by Bybit’s signers. The signers believed they were approving a legitimate transaction. Instead, they unknowingly authorized the theft of $1.5 billion from a cold wallet.

The keys could stay offline while the signers approved a theft through a compromised interface.

TRM Labs attributes the recent Binance incident with high confidence to TraderTraitor, the North Korean group also linked to Bybit and the theft of 4,502.9 BTC from DMM Bitcoin. Binance’s preliminary investigation points to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop as the entry point. Binance says there’s no evidence that private keys were leaked, while TRM’s analysis suggests the attackers may have gained control of the signing infrastructure. If confirmed, the attackers could have moved funds through a compromised approval process without extracting the keys.

Now imagine the same thing happening to IBIT.

BlackRock’s IBIT is the world’s largest Bitcoin ETF, holding roughly 815,000 BTC worth around $63 billion. Coinbase remains its active Bitcoin custodian. Although Anchorage Digital has been appointed as an additional custodian, the fund’s latest quarterly filing says there are currently no plans to transfer any Bitcoin there.

That’s an extraordinary concentration of Bitcoin under one custodian. Regardless of how large or well-funded that provider is, a critical failure in its security infrastructure could put the entire fund at risk.

A $6 billion theft would wipe out roughly 9.5% of IBIT’s assets, equivalent to around $4 per share at current valuations.

Binance managed to freeze some stolen stablecoins. Bitcoin has no such mechanism, making stolen BTC far harder to recover.

BlackRock doesn’t separately insure the Bitcoin held by the fund. Coinbase has disclosed $320 million in commercial crime insurance coverage, shared across its customers. Its custody agreement also limits liability to $100 million per cold storage address, with any recovery subject to contractual terms, liability determinations, and other conditions.

If a major theft occurred and the fund couldn’t recover the Bitcoin or obtain sufficient compensation, the remaining losses would ultimately be borne by IBIT shareholders.

Bitcoin ETFs have made owning Bitcoin much more accessible, and there’s real value in that convenience. But as more capital flows into these products, enormous amounts of Bitcoin are also being concentrated among a handful of custodians and the infrastructure they depend on.

The larger these pools become, the more attractive they are to attackers. A compromise at any critical point could have consequences far beyond a single institution.

And that’s why security has no finish line.

Even the most sophisticated cold storage setup still depends on hardware, software, supply chains, signing workflows, and the people operating them. Keeping private keys offline is essential, but it doesn’t eliminate the risks surrounding the transaction approval process.

Spread your assets across independent custody setups. Keep your private keys offline. Verify transaction details on a trusted device screen, independently of the computer initiating the transaction. Continuously review your security architecture, and build it around the assumption that some part of your infrastructure will eventually be compromised.

There are no silver bullets in security, and no permanent guarantees. Stay vigilant, keep verifying, and never mistake a clean track record for proof that you’re safe.

Bunker mode.

关于本次安全事件，大家对技术细节有不少疑问，就目前掌握的信息，这里统一说明几点：

1️⃣ 这不是攻破一台电脑就把钱转走了
这并不是一次通过单一设备就能完成的事件，一个员工电脑被黑是这个攻击的起点。针对加密机构的攻击通常具有较强的针对性，攻击者往往尝试利用了复杂的手段实施渗透。

我们已经发现与事件相关的重要线索，并已第一时间采取措施控制风险，相关调查和溯源工作仍在持续进行中。现阶段，平台核心风控和应急机制已经启动，用户资产安全是我们的首要保障。

2️⃣ 关于"工程师是不是权限过大"
这并不是攻击者直接利用某位工程师权限即可完成资金转移的事件，也不是单一人员可以“一键操作”造成的结果。相关异常涉及更复杂的攻击过程。需要强调的是，现阶段调查并未将责任归因于任何个人，公司将承担相应责任，并持续推进后续处置与安全升级工作。

3️⃣ 目前能确认的事实
没有发现钱包私钥泄露的证据。用户资金安全，本次事件造成的全部被盗损失由 SAFU 基金和公司资金全额承担，不需要用户承担。目前链上已冻结约 30 亿美元受影响资产，我们正配合执法部门和区块链情报机构追查，链上资金流向公开可查。

4️⃣ 充提状态
充值全程正常开放，未受影响。提现作为预防性措施已暂停，预计在48小时内开放，具体时间以官方公告为准。我们理解这对大家造成了不便，会尽快同步进展。

5️⃣ 后续
我们会在确保调查准确性的前提下，持续同步进展，并在事件处置和复盘完成后公布详细情况和进一步的安全加固措施。该暴露的问题我们会正视，不会含糊。

感谢大家的耐心和监督。

链上数据显示，黑客在 EIP-7702 授权里一口气塞了连续 50 个 Nonce 签名（从 18914775 到 18914824）。因为 14 号热钱包高频出金，黑客算不准落地区间，干脆让内网签名机盲签了 50 份霰弹枪掩码，蒙中一个就接管了执行权。私钥如果在黑客手里，根本用不着这种盲签打法

2 币安自家的自动化程序，成了黑客的搬运工
EIP-7702 委托只要不主动解绑就会持久生效。漏洞发生后，币安内网的自动资金归集脚本（Sweeper）还在老老实实往 14 号钱包搬钱，导致后半夜又被黑客自动抽干了两波，逼得官方只能全网拉闸停充提

3 套娃穿透：14 号当跳板，隔空吸干 34 号金库
币安的 34 号合约金库把 14 号热钱包设为了唯一 Operator。黑客拿下 14 号执行权后，直接以它的名义隔空调用 executeBatch，顺手牵羊抽走了 8.23 亿枚 USDC

4 真正的金蝉脱壳在 DeFi
别光看稳定币被冻结，黑客在 Tether 反应过来的前 9 分钟，直接在 DEX 抢砸了 3 亿多 U 换成无法冻结的 ETH；甚至冲进 Aave 搞借贷抵押逃逸，吓得 Aave 官方紧急冻结市场

text:
It’s almost incomprehensible how wide the distance is between someone who’s working at the frontier with AI and basically everyone else right now. 

The crazy thing is these lines are not converging, but only growing farther apart. If the curve of AI progress had leveled off, it would certainly have given most people and companies time to catch up or implement their workflows in a standardized way. The technology would have neutralized competitive advantage because everyone would be using it the same way.

But what’s happened is the opposite. The curve of AI progress is basically going vertical right now, which means if you had codified your processes 3-6 months ago you’re likely already behind again. Now imagine most companies that kicked into gear a year ago and thought that they were done. Even further behind now.

I’ve never seen a technology in my life and career that improves at this rate, which consequently means you need to upgrade your expectations at a similar rate. Our brains weren’t wired for this, and our organizational change management processes certainly weren’t either.

With any form of recursive self improvement, things just get wilder. It’s a time when you will need to be constantly reevaluating the things that didn’t work just a couple months ago to see if they now can be solved. AI native companies certainly have a strong advantage due to this right now, so now it comes down to can the bigger companies keep up. Wild times.

⚠️ Exploit Breakdown: zkLink Nova Ethereum Bridge Attack

On October 29, an attacker withdrew 22.43129453 ETH and 11 different ERC-20 tokens from zkLink Nova’s L1 custody contracts in a single transaction. The stolen assets were worth approximately $797,016.48 at the time of the attack.

🔍 Root Cause:

The vulnerability was in zkLink Nova’s `Arbitrator.claimMessage`. The function uses `finalizeMessageHash` in transient storage to record the hash of a message just authenticated through a callback from the source chain’s canonical message service.

The value was not cleared after the call. The function also did not require a fresh authentication callback for every call, allowing an already-authenticated message to be reused.
https://t.co/wJck3LcGyp

author: KKyleChen
quoted_text:
The recent security incidents involving Bybit, Bitget, and now Binance should serve as a wake-up call for every leader in the crypto industry.

Security should never be an area of commercial competition. It is a shared responsibility to protect our customers and the entire industry.

Over the past decade, major crypto exchanges have made significant progress in protecting private keys. We have seen relatively few incidents involving direct private key compromises in recent years. So far, we have not seen conclusive evidence that Binance’s hot wallet private key was leaked. The greater concern may lie in vulnerabilities in access controls and wallet management systems.

Companies that have never experienced a major security incident should not assume they are inherently safer or immune to attacks.

At OKX, we have built multiple layers of sophisticated security protection and maintained a strong security track record over the past decade. But we also recognize that no system is absolutely secure. We must remain humble, vigilant, and constantly challenge our own security assumptions.

A major security breach at any exchange undermines trust in the entire crypto industry, ultimately hurting every company and every customer.

I believe CEOs across the industry need to come together, just as we did during the Bitcoin fork crisis in 2017, to establish stronger industry-wide security standards and coordinated response mechanisms.

For example, transfers and settlements between verified exchanges could be processed in real time, while large withdrawals to unknown or unverified addresses, as well as transactions granting smart contract permissions, should be subject to additional verification and appropriate security delays.

Crucially, these safeguards should be enforced at the cryptographic signing layer, rather than relying solely on application-level controls. Even if an attacker compromises an exchange’s wallet management system, they should not be able to bypass these fundamental security restrictions.

We should also establish industry-wide mechanisms for real-time security incident notifications, coordinated monitoring of suspicious funds, and rapid responses to potential attacks. Exchanges, stablecoin issuers, and other major industry participants should work together to enable the rapid, lawful temporary freezing of suspected stolen assets when necessary.

We should also work together to accelerate the industry’s transition to quantum-resistant cryptography and strengthen our defenses against emerging AI-powered security threats. These are long-term challenges that no single company can solve alone, and they require coordinated research, shared standards, and collective action across the industry.

Security is everyone’s responsibility. No company can protect the future of crypto alone.

text:
With a hack like the Binance exploit 2 things matter most for the response: speed & coverage.

We remained fully secure, but it's critical to go the extra mile to prevent movement of stolen funds.

Sharing the measures we took at @USDT0_to and what other teams can take from it:

1) Shortly after the hack was confirmed, we temporarily paused our @Trondao <> @Ethereum pathways so stolen funds could not move into ecosystems where laundering is easier. We take this precaution regularly when a large hack hits the wider industry.

https://t.co/q9hdIwxSla

2) Together with our KYT and compliance partners, we immediately began monitoring all USDT0 networks for stolen funds, and at first none were found.

3) About 20 minutes later, we detected a new wave of drains on @0xPolygon, which resulted in the theft of 6.18M USDT0.

Our multisig signers mobilized quickly, and we froze those funds before the attacker could swap them into assets that cannot be frozen.

https://t.co/EEaSR2w5Z6

4) Once @Tether froze the bulk of the stolen USDT (1.3B+), the chance of the attacker using USDT became minuscule, so we reopened our Tron <> ETH pathways to keep serving our customers.

https://t.co/Ap7I1bwbN3

5) Our monitoring tools stay on high alert which may cause temporary delays to cross chain transactions, but it's a necessary step/

We've applied most of these measures during previous major hacks (GMX, Bybit, Bitget, Kelp, Drift), and I think there's a lot the wider industry can take from these experiences.

My encouragement to other teams is to prepare before the next incident. Have monitoring in place across every network you support. Make sure your teams and signers can mobilize in minutes. Establish direct lines of communication with issuers, compliance partners, and other protocols so you can act together when funds are at risk.

Attackers move fast, across networks and protocols, and our response needs to be just as coordinated.

AI is changing the attack surface, and our opsec needs to evolve just as quickly. No single project can solve this alone and the more of us that have these measures in place, the harder we make it for stolen funds to move anywhere in the ecosystem.

I'd encourage other teams to share what they've learned and the measures they're taking. Every incident is an opportunity for the entire industry to get better at protecting users, and that will always remain our collective priority number 1.

Section 24 in one example, at the new property tax rates from April 2027.

£150k buy-to-let mortgage at 5%, interest-only. Rent of £900 a month.

Rent: £10,800/yr
Mortgage interest: £7,500/yr
Real profit: £3,300/yr

(That's before repairs, insurance and agent fees.)

If you own it personally, you can't deduct the mortgage interest. You're taxed on the full £10,800 rent and get a 22% credit on the interest (£1,650) instead.

Tax on that £3,300 profit:

Basic rate (22%): £726, an effective 22%

Higher rate (42%): £2,886, an effective 87%

Additional rate (47%): £3,426, an effective 104%

The higher-rate landlord keeps £414. The additional-rate landlord pays more tax than the property makes.

text:
I think $JAGENT rally may have been driven by more than just the Agent ID narrative. The early token distribution and the market environment at the time may have played a role as well.

0x8e6442663a4f8c50b6132c68d42a30e7dfe4ae15 

Binance .ai Agent ID gave JAGENT a clear source of attention, while Jager’s minting mechanism lowered the barrier to early participation. The initial price was 1U per share, and each Agent ID could mint a base allocation. Inviting new users who completed their first paid mint and completing social tasks could unlock additional allocations. The project has no presale or team token allocation, with 80% of minting proceeds going to the official liquidity pool and 20% to a multisig treasury. This design can broaden early participation, but it doesn't guarantee a widely distributed supply or provide a price floor in the secondary market.

Another factor that may have been underestimated is the lack of strong competing opportunities at the time. When there aren't many more attractive narratives to trade, a new story can easily become a focal point for short-term capital. The Agent ID narrative attracts attention, the low entry barrier brings in more participants, and momentum buyers push the price higher. Together, these factors can fuel a rapid rally. The reverse is also true: if another hot project emerges on BSC or Solana, capital rotation could quickly drain demand from JAGENT.

As of the time I'm writing this post, the token has more than 5,400 holder addresses, with the top 10 addresses collectively holding around 19.7% of the supply. This suggests that participation has expanded, but it doesn't prove that the current supply is sufficiently distributed. Going forward, the key is to watch whether early holders with low entry costs start taking profits and whether new buying demand can absorb the selling pressure.

I think JAGENT’s short-term trading thesis makes sense: the external narrative attracts attention, the minting mechanism broadens participation, and the lack of competing hot projects may have concentrated capital into the token. However, whether its fundamentals are actually strengthening depends on whether Social Season can generate sustained paid minting and genuine trading activity, rather than simply increasing social exposure.

The key question now is whether this rally is being driven by a sustained increase in buyers or simply by a temporary lack of selling pressure from early holders. The former could support further upside; the latter could lead to a sharp pullback as soon as capital rotates elsewhere.

Even if your private key is not compromised, never let your signer be used as an oracle. 

Put another way, the software implementation must be setup to avoid the signer signing any message which is sent to it. 

The protocol must define exactly what the signer signs and what it can checks. Even if a byte is different, it should throw an error. 

Please take this chance everyone to review your APIs and what your signer is willing to sign.

I want to speak to you directly about what happened.

Bottom line - your money is safe, and we're covering every loss.

Our initial investigation suggests this security incident may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop. That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions.

To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single "one-click" action. It involved a more complex attack process. Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.

So far, we have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak.

We'll share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and every fact is verified - and publish an updated Proof of Reserves once remediation is complete.

What you need to know:
• Your funds are safe
• Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and company funds
• Estimated total impact: ~$6.3B, with ~$3B frozen on-chain so far, in coordination with our blockchain partners
• No evidence of any wallet private key leak
• Deposits are unaffected and operating as normal

What we've done:
• Temporarily suspended withdrawals while we complete a security revamp of the withdrawal service and its related addresses
• Revoked the affected address authorizations
• Engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds

Our team hasn't stopped. We're working closely with law enforcement to ensure the matter is handled appropriately - and I'll share what I can, as soon as I can.

text:
Thoughts on the Binance exploit

1. The financial damage is manageable. Roughly half of the ~$5B stolen ($2.5B) is already frozen, and the insurance fund covers another $1.5B. That leaves a net hole of about $1B, under 1% of assets on the platform and under 1.5% of BNB's market cap. Binance can absorb that.

2. The symbolic damage is brutal. Binance is the JPMorgan of crypto: the most competent, most secure and most trusted exchange. Unlike a regulated exchange, it has no charter, deposit insurance or regulator behind it, only its track record, so trust is its whole moat. If Binance can't keep North Korea out, who can? Every other exchange looks less safe today than it did yesterday.

3. Risk premiums will rise. Every trader needs some return to justify holding funds on a platform, and that hurdle just went up. Expect capital outflows over the coming months, with tradfi market makers scaling back their crypto operations.

4. The industry will consolidate, but toward proven security. Every team trades speed against safety, and the market just repriced that trade. New exchanges and chains will face increased skepticism and higher customer acquisition costs. This may be the beginning of the end of the casino era of crypto. 

5. Price impact on effected tokens will be complex. While Binance has committed to making all customers whole, this almost certainly won't translate into market buys tomorrow. Assuming mms and projects provided price support (2m 3x levered buy order is what stopped the ENA crash), these positions will be wound down over the coming days. 

6. Pressure on North Korea will increase. A theft this large makes North Korean crypto theft a geopolitical issue. At some point both the US and China will choose to tighten the screws.

7. Expect more exploits across the wider economy. Crypto has long been a canary for tech security. The same actors and techniques will keep moving into banks, fintech and critical infrastructure.

text:
币安被盗 63 亿美元，我一半以上的身家在币安，但到目前为止，市场的恐慌比我想象的小很多

币安这次被盗的金额是去年 Bybit 那次的 4 倍多。

技术细节网上到处都是，怎么被盗的我就不重复了，我只写下我自己的思考。

首先看下目前的情况。币安自己的口径是 63 亿美元受影响，已经冻结了 30 亿左右，去年 Bybit 被盗 15 亿已经是历史第一了，这次直接翻了 4 倍。对照币安平台上 1400 多亿美元的用户资产，63 亿是 4% 左右，扣掉冻结的，净损失 2% 左右。

这个事件也导致 BTC 跌到 7 万 8 附近，全网爆仓 15 亿多，但是放在「史上最大盗币案」这个标题下面，这个跌幅真的比我想的小了很多。

顺便说一句题外话，这种事如果真的造成恐慌，对我来说也许是不错的买入机会。加密的 4 年周期正在往熊市底部走，Anthropic 上市大概率还有一波吸血效应，我觉得不管是加密还是美股，都可能出现不错的击球区，但是具体怎么下手我还没想好。

回到币安。我自己做的第一件事，是去翻了一遍币安的储备金证明，截至 10 月 1 日的快照，用户资产是有 1:1 覆盖的。这对我自己是一颗定心丸，我觉得对大部分币安用户也是。

其实大家最怕的就三件事：钱丢了、平台赔不起、提现挤兑。我的思考是，只要储备金证明是真的，就算出现比较严重的情况，大概率也就是提现慢一点，还不至于提不出来。

然后我顺着这个事重新研究了一遍 FTX 是怎么倒的，发现币安和 FTX 的本质区别不在被不被盗，而在钱有没有被挪。但其实更进一步，我认为其实是创始人的价值观。FTX 很早就把客户资金挪给了 Alameda，窟窿一直放大，永远也补不上。

而且 Alameda 抵押出去的是 FTT，行情好的时候没问题，行情一差 FTT 一跌，抵押品跟着缩水，窟窿变大的速度比补的速度快，这是一个结构性的死法。

币安的做法是把储备金拿出来给你看，你能看到它到底有多少钱，而且那大概率还不是它的全部家底。至少在「公开透明」这件事上，是能让人安心的。

再看处理问题的态度，一姐直接说币安承担全部损失，SAFU 加公司国库兜底，CZ 已经不管事了也出来说以股东身份预期用户资金全额覆盖，一线的工作人员至少是在好好帮用户解决问题。一姐怀孕还在熬夜这条新闻真假我不知道，我相信是真的，但这个态度传递给用户的信息是：你的资产放在我这里，是被重视的。

——然后说一个本来和这件事无关的事，如果不是币安被盗，我根本不会去研究它。

FTX 当年投了 Anthropic 5 亿美元，投后估值 40 亿。假设它持有的 13% 一路稀释到 5%，按市场现在传的 1.5 万亿 IPO 估值算，5% 就是 750 亿美元，5 亿翻 150 倍。

但 FTX 没活到今天，这笔股权在破产清算的时候，按 180 多亿的估值就被卖掉了，前后一共回了 13 亿左右。

我不是要夸 CZ 一定多好，但作为交易所创始人，CZ 和一姐确实没做过损害用户的事，也没有为了所谓的「期望值最大化」去做危险的事情。

从结果看 SBF 确实押对了，5 亿换 750 亿，有人会说他眼光多独到、是硅谷最成功的投资人。但有一个更大的问题，他的价值观和做事方式，根本撑不到收益兑现的那一天。

这本身就是一个脆弱的策略，就像你顶着上涨一直做空，最后终于对了，但你早就爆仓出局了，你撑不到盈利的那一天。

在研究完以后我最大的感受是，一个人做事的价值观，可能真的会决定他的命运，押对了也没用，因为你活不到对的那一天。

这不是投资建议，我自己一半以上的钱还在币安，屁股可能决定脑袋，大家参考就好。

最后也希望币安能顺利度过难关。 @cz_binance  @heyibinance  @binance  @binancezh

LexianLix named a problem a lot of us have: you edit a skill in Claude Code, the Cursor rule with the same name keeps the old text, and the copies drift further apart. They asked whether any tool merges the two, and said that's the case they'd pay for.

I hit the same thing, so I built skill-drift (open source):
1. It compares Claude skills, Cursor rules and a second skills folder by body text, and lists same-named copies that no longer match. It ignores file modification time, which only tells you which copy was saved last.
2. Merging starts as a plan. Nothing moves until --apply, and replaced copies go to an archive folder instead of being deleted. When each copy has lines the others lack, it won't pick for you: you name the one to keep.
3. Local files only. No network, no upload.

To install, paste this to your AI: "Set up skill-drift on this computer by following the official instructions at https://t.co/fjecsKullC."

If your skills and rules have drifted too, run one check and reply with what it missed or got wrong.
https://t.co/OPJ1C6Cd8j

太疯狂了，这就像 2020 年新冠暴发的第一周：

起初只是零星几则国际新闻，数字看起来不大，没人把它当成系统性危机。

但金融防火墙正在坍塌。

1. 日本

互联网巨头 GMO 旗下外汇交易系统沦陷，黑客勒索 5,000 万美元加密货币，股价单日暴跌超 15%。

2. 韩国

黑客借助中国 AI 自动化渗透工具入侵 7 家金融机构。截至 10 月中旬，受害名单激增至 16 家。大信证券（Daishin）本周证实泄露 38,490 名客户的关键底账与银行卡号。

3. 拉美

跨国黑客组织利用 Claude、Grok 和 Kimi 等大模型自动化部署“AI 攻击代理（Agent）”，同时对超 400 家银行及支付机构发起蜂群渗透，批量截取凭证并侵入核心账户。

4. 印度

黑客盗用信贷风控与登录凭证，通过 AI 伪造借贷流向，在 2 个月内对小型信贷机构发起 150 次突袭，掠走 3,100 万美元，甚至出现同一家公司两次中招的荒诞一幕。

5. 意大利

一条高仿“集团 CEO”的 WhatsApp 消息，加上一段完美克隆的 AI 语音指令，诱使联合圣保罗私人银行（Fideuram）直接放行 9,500 万欧元。其中 3,600 万欧元已遁入加密黑洞，彻底蒸发。

6. 澳大利亚

监管层发布最高级别预警：AI 攻击正直接威胁全澳 4.5 万亿澳元的养老储蓄。近一年内，针对关键金融网关的网络警报狂飙 80%。

7. 加密金融

顶级交易所 Bitget 热钱包遭瞬时抽干 3.51 亿美元，链上痕迹直指朝鲜黑客组织。这是今年涉案金额最大的单笔盗窃。

把镜头拉远，看看底层逻辑：

黑客武器化： 过去需要顶级黑客团队耗时数月的渗透，现在通过商用 AI 代理分分钟批量生成并执行。

洗钱无缝化： 资金在不同国家的“骡子账户”（Mule accounts）间秒级流转，经由混币器、加密货币与跨境现金网彻底洗白。

物理脱罪化： 操盘手身在境外，司法边界与引渡壁垒成了他们最好的保护伞。

author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
I think $JAGENT rally may have been driven by more than just the Agent ID narrative. The early token distribution and the market environment at the time may have played a role as well.

0x8e6442663a4f8c50b6132c68d42a30e7dfe4ae15 

Binance .ai Agent ID gave JAGENT a clear source of attention, while Jager’s minting mechanism lowered the barrier to early participation. The initial price was 1U per share, and each Agent ID could mint a base allocation. Inviting new users who completed their first paid mint and completing social tasks could unlock additional allocations. The project has no presale or team token allocation, with 80% of minting proceeds going to the official liquidity pool and 20% to a multisig treasury. This design can broaden early participation, but it doesn't guarantee a widely distributed supply or provide a price floor in the secondary market.

Another factor that may have been underestimated is the lack of strong competing opportunities at the time. When there aren't many more attractive narratives to trade, a new story can easily become a focal point for short-term capital. The Agent ID narrative attracts attention, the low entry barrier brings in more participants, and momentum buyers push the price higher. Together, these factors can fuel a rapid rally. The reverse is also true: if another hot project emerges on BSC or Solana, capital rotation could quickly drain demand from JAGENT.

As of the time I'm writing this post, the token has more than 5,400 holder addresses, with the top 10 addresses collectively holding around 19.7% of the supply. This suggests that participation has expanded, but it doesn't prove that the current supply is sufficiently distributed. Going forward, the key is to watch whether early holders with low entry costs start taking profits and whether new buying demand can absorb the selling pressure.

I think JAGENT’s short-term trading thesis makes sense: the external narrative attracts attention, the minting mechanism broadens participation, and the lack of competing hot projects may have concentrated capital into the token. However, whether its fundamentals are actually strengthening depends on whether Social Season can generate sustained paid minting and genuine trading activity, rather than simply increasing social exposure.

The key question now is whether this rally is being driven by a sustained increase in buyers or simply by a temporary lack of selling pressure from early holders. The former could support further upside; the latter could lead to a sharp pullback as soon as capital rotates elsewhere.

CryptoBilis update

We've been made aware, through responsible disclosure, of a single hardware implant in a Trezor Safe 5 device bought from the reseller CryptoBilis in August 2026.

No CryptoBilis buyer has reported a loss of funds to us.

IMPORTANT: If you bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis from March 2026 onwards, we know this is unsettling. Here’s what to do:

Already using it?

Move your funds to a newly created wallet with a new seed as soon as possible. Do not reuse the old seed in any wallet, hardware or software.  If you don’t have another secure hardware wallet available, we recommend temporarily migrating your funds to a software wallet or an exchange you are familiar with.  

Not set up yet? Don’t set it up, and never enter your existing wallet backup on it.

We haven’t received the device to confirm this report, but based on the customer’s description, we’re treating it as credible and sharing it now so customers who purchased a Trezor via CryptoBilis can secure their funds as a precaution. Our security team will examine the device as soon as it arrives.

On October 9, 2026, we removed CryptoBilis as a reseller following reports of tampered Ledger devices sold through it. Since then, we have been inspecting Trezor devices that customers bought from CryptoBilis and have found no signs of tampering on any of the four devices we’ve received so far.

NEVER share your wallet backup (recovery phrase) with anyone. Trezor Support will never ask for it.
If you are affected by this incident, please keep your CryptoBilis device and contact Support to receive a new Trezor hardware wallet: https://t.co/5EasOVDDQh

We're investigating and will post updates here as soon as we know more.  Thank you to the customer who reported this through our responsible disclosure program, and to @SEAL_911 for working alongside our teams on the response. Reports and engagement like this help us protect everyone else.

author: mdudas
quoted_text:
It's been a long time coming... But it's finally time

Part of evolving as a business is recognising where your focus should be while remembering who your users are. 

The reality is that we spent an incredible amount of time purpose-building a network that is specifically designed to cater to HFT and everything that it encompasses. 

Execution needed to be faster and limitations to throughput hindered our ability to run real time risk checks as we think about scaling to 100,000 to 1,000,000 users and beyond. 

For those who have been following along, its no secret that there has been friction between how we execute and what the preference is from Solana leadership. 

I understand and respect their stance, however to continue to frame BULK a solana dex would be reductive to the actual offering, so we’re officially putting this on the record. 

The stronger case is that multichain access expands BULK’s distribution and usable capital while bringing more activity into the same market.

Distribution follows where users hold their money.

As more people enter crypto through neobanks, wallets and payment applications, their first chain may simply be whichever network their provider uses. Their choice of trading venue will depend on execution quality, liquidity and convenience.

Requiring those users to move to a particular chain before they can trade creates an acquisition barrier: another transaction, another fee, another interface and another opportunity to abandon onboarding. It also asks wallets and neobanks to move customers away from their existing infrastructure to integrate BULK.

Multichain access lets BULK meet that distribution where it already exists. A wallet or neobank could offer its customers BULK markets through the rails they already use.

The lesson from multicurrency products like Wise is that a single financial relationship can span across several underlying currencies and payment systems. We expect users to increasingly demand the same convenience across chains.

A unified clearing layer can make capital more productive and markets more liquid.

The strongest clearinghouse analogy is capital efficiency. Traditional clearing infrastructure brings eligible collateral and positions into a common risk framework, allowing qualifying exposures to offset and reducing the capital required to support them. 

This today belongs to CME Group.

For BULK, the opportunity is to connect capital held across supported chains to a common margin system and shared order book. A trader’s access to liquidity should not depend on which chain funded their account. A market maker should be able to serve that combined demand through the same BULK markets.

This creates an economic advantage: more sources of capital and order flow can support deeper books; deeper books can improve execution; better execution can attract more traders and integrations.

That advantage depends on keeping liquidity concentrated. Multichain access should bring users into the same markets, with eligible collateral recognized under a consistent risk framework. It should also let users withdraw available capital through supported destination chains, making BULK useful within their wider financial activity.

BULK’s specialised execution layer gives it a natural role connecting these rails.

BULK is a purpose-built trading L1 rolled into an order book, matching engine and risk engine. Its value comes from how efficiently it executes trades and manages risk. That specialization gives it a reason to serve capital from multiple ecosystems.

Today, collateral lives on Solana, and BULK’s ledger tracks the corresponding balances, positions and margin. Extending that model to supported networks such as Arc, Tempo, Arbitrum and HyperEVM would allow more funding and withdrawal routes to connect to the same execution system.

The architectural principle is to handle each chain’s confirmation and settlement requirements at the funding boundary. Once collateral is securely recognised, trading should run through BULK’s own execution and risk process. This allows BULK to preserve its performance while broadening access.

The intended experience is straightforward: fund from a supported chain, trade against BULK’s shared liquidity, and withdraw available balances to a supported destination. A user could enter from Solana and exit on HyperEVM, with BULK coordinating the accounting, settlement and destination liquidity required.

For wallets and neobanks, that would make BULK an exchange and clearing integration they can use across their supported networks. Each additional rail would expand access to the same venue, and strengthen the market already serving everyone else.

author: kevinnbass
quoted_text:
University administrators who deliberately manipulate investigations are engaging in fraud and should be held accountable.

There is a general tactic universities use to get rid of people they don't like. When administrators know they lack the evidence to support formal charges, or want to conceal facts that might emerge through a proper investigation, they resort to vague, undefined concerns about things like "lab culture" or "workplace environment."

These accusations are essentially unfalsifiable. It is easy to produce unflattering accounts of anyone, especially when the people providing them have aligned interests and incentives to produce a particular outcome. Leading questions, selective testimony, and cherry-picked incidents can be used to construct a negative narrative about virtually anyone.

The result is a smear that someone is a bad person, without any specific allegation they can meaningfully defend against. They can provide an alternative account supported by evidence, but administrators can simply ignore it.

部署DeWEB非常简单，只需要把构建好的前端上传到电路容器中，并绑定DNS，即可任何人无障碍访问。上传以后，它不依赖任何服务器，一次支付Gas部署，永远免费。

text:
我不太建议把个人 portfolio 的主要资金再放在 crypto。

主要原因是，就这短短半个月以内，已经出现 4 个采用率极其广的操作系统/编程语言的重大安全漏洞了。只要是人写的代码，只要可被逆向、bytecode 可以被分析，那就一定存在被注入以及漏洞挖掘的风险。很多底层的程序语言以及多年前开发的程序，中间经过了不知道多少代人的维护，早就已经是代码屎山了。

在这种情况下，crypto 的很多资产管理方式都非常不安全：多签可以被篡改，前端也可以被劫持，设备可以被入侵。更别提很多人拿一个手机设个 8 位数密码，或者用个浏览器插件，就敢在里面放几百万美金。很多人觉得用苹果的设备就绝对安全，但请别忘了多次的重大安全事故里面（包括这次的 Binance，以及之前的 Bybit，包括之前出现过的大大小小事故里面），工程师用的也是 Mac 系统和IOS工作手机。冷钱包也并非绝对安全，即使是从未联网的冷钱包，也有可能因为前代留下的傻逼假随机数被攻破。现在在 AI 的加持下，尤其是开源模型非常强大、且支持私有化部署的前提下，攻防逐渐不对等了。所谓“道高一尺，魔高一丈”，动态攻防那也是要等先发现了漏洞再防，但是中途被牺牲的，其实是用户的资金安全。我觉得零日漏洞之后会越来越多。Crypto 领域依然有很多非常有趣的机会，不管怎么样，meme也会一直存在，洗钱和支付也是原生需求，套利也是一直存在的，只是crypto的利率要重新算风险溢价了。

 Crypto 的 venue 够多，但 venue 够多也意味着可被攻击的节点更多。因Crypto 资金要是丢了，像 Binance 这样的体量是可以完成赔付的；但很多其他交易所、很多其他 venue 是做不到赔付的，甚至会直接跑路。维权之路是非常艰难的，你把钱放ibkr买美债，收益可能只有1/3，出事了起码有存款保险给你赔。作为一个每天在做服务器运维和跑量化策略的人来说，一直把所有资金放在无法控制的随时可能被零日漏洞攻击的环境里，不是一个明智的选择。

Binance's initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified.

The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B. We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~$3 billion frozen on-chain so far.
Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company’s funds. User funds are safe. We will also publish an updated Proof of Reserves once the remediation is complete.

As an immediate precaution, Binance has:

- temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while security checks are completed;
- revoked the affected address authorisation;
- engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds.

text:
$GANG is still worth keeping an eye on. Product development has clearly accelerated recently.

0x0c6302401aa5325c2e36f170f52c00b1d220b405 

Bond Mode is live, MCP has been integrated with AI tools like Claude and Cursor, and V3 is starting to produce more graduated projects with actual trading activity.

Compared with its early focus on launching tokens through Binance Agent ID, GANG is now trying to connect developers, token launches, and Agent-driven trading.

Bond Mode is one of the more important updates. Previously, GANG used Agent ID verification and a 1% per-wallet allocation limit on the bonding curve to improve early token distribution. However, what happened after a project graduated remained a concern, particularly whether developers would sell their holdings. Creator Bond addresses this by requiring developers to put up collateral and commit to maintaining a specified token balance for a set period. If they break that commitment, their collateral is forfeited and used to buy back and burn the corresponding project tokens. If they honor the commitment, they get their collateral back. Essentially, developers have to put real money behind their own projects, creating greater accountability. However, Bond is voluntary and only applies to participating wallets, so it cannot completely eliminate selling risks from other addresses.

MCP is important because it brings GANG into AI Agent trading workflows. Users can connect GANG to Claude or Cursor to scan trending tokens, track new projects and graduation progress, retrieve Agent Notes, and then confirm trades themselves. Private keys remain in the Binance Agentic Wallet. The AI prepares the transaction, but the user retains control over execution. Combined with Agent Thoughts, Share, and Follow, GANG is attempting to build an information layer around Agent trading opinions, historical performance, and follow behavior. That said, while the product integration is live, its actual adoption and trading results still need to be validated.

V3 further expands the platform's revenue model. Untaxed Tokens primarily generate fees during the bonding curve phase, with no ongoing trading taxes after graduation. Taxed Tokens can configure buy and sell taxes after graduation, with GANG receiving a portion of the trading volume according to platform rules. Fair Mint provides another issuance model with a different fee distribution structure. This gives GANG the opportunity to move beyond one-time launch fees and generate recurring revenue from trading activity after graduation. But that only works if graduated projects continue attracting traders. Otherwise, launching more tokens won't necessarily create sustainable cash flow.

Looking at the data, during our previous analysis, the website showed 2,808 unique .ai Agent ID wallets that had bought at least one launchpad token. Cumulative burns stood at 5.11 million GANG, representing 0.511% of the total supply. Total buybacks were approximately $31,500 across 295 transactions, while the treasury held around $7,878.

In the latest snapshot, the number of wallets had increased to 3,478, cumulative burns reached 7.41 million GANG, or 0.741% of the total supply, buyback transactions increased to 836, cumulative buybacks reached approximately $32,300, and the treasury grew to around $8,880. Wallet participation and token burns are both increasing. However, buyback transactions have nearly tripled while the total buyback value has only increased by roughly $800. This suggests that buybacks are happening more frequently, but the actual amount of capital being deployed has not expanded at the same rate.

Graduated projects are also showing some progress. Previously, Gangstar, TICK, and AGORA each recorded 24-hour trading volumes in the hundreds of thousands of dollars. In the latest data, Agent Arena, GANGBALL, and Gangstar are still showing trading activity. This demonstrates that some projects launched through GANG can attract trading after graduation. However, trading volume is not the same as net capital inflow, and short-term turnover does not prove that these projects can survive over the long term. The next thing to watch is whether they can maintain liquidity and trading activity.

What stands out most is that the improvement in platform activity has not been reflected in GANG's price. The latest chart shows its market cap declining from approximately $9.88 million to around $2.6 million. Trading activity remains relatively high, but the valuation has contracted significantly. This shows that active trading does not necessarily mean buying pressure is dominant. Early profit-taking and capital rotation may still be weighing on the token. Another contributing factor is the large-scale hacking incident Binance has recently suffered, although this is an external factor that could eventually be resolved.

Overall, I remain relatively bullish on GANG's fundamentals. The team has continued delivering new products, and platform metrics are gradually improving. Bond Mode increases accountability for developers, MCP expands the use cases for Agents, and V3 gives GANG the opportunity to generate revenue from trading activity after projects graduate. These updates have made the product ecosystem considerably more complete than it was in its early stages, but the token's value capture has yet to catch up.

The key metrics I will be watching are the actual adoption of Bond Mode, real MCP usage, and whether graduated projects can maintain meaningful trading activity one week or even one month after launch.

I think $JAGENT rally may have been driven by more than just the Agent ID narrative. The early token distribution and the market environment at the time may have played a role as well.

0x8e6442663a4f8c50b6132c68d42a30e7dfe4ae15 

Binance .ai Agent ID gave JAGENT a clear source of attention, while Jager’s minting mechanism lowered the barrier to early participation. The initial price was 1U per share, and each Agent ID could mint a base allocation. Inviting new users who completed their first paid mint and completing social tasks could unlock additional allocations. The project has no presale or team token allocation, with 80% of minting proceeds going to the official liquidity pool and 20% to a multisig treasury. This design can broaden early participation, but it doesn't guarantee a widely distributed supply or provide a price floor in the secondary market.

Another factor that may have been underestimated is the lack of strong competing opportunities at the time. When there aren't many more attractive narratives to trade, a new story can easily become a focal point for short-term capital. The Agent ID narrative attracts attention, the low entry barrier brings in more participants, and momentum buyers push the price higher. Together, these factors can fuel a rapid rally. The reverse is also true: if another hot project emerges on BSC or Solana, capital rotation could quickly drain demand from JAGENT.

As of the time I'm writing this post, the token has more than 5,400 holder addresses, with the top 10 addresses collectively holding around 19.7% of the supply. This suggests that participation has expanded, but it doesn't prove that the current supply is sufficiently distributed. Going forward, the key is to watch whether early holders with low entry costs start taking profits and whether new buying demand can absorb the selling pressure.

I think JAGENT’s short-term trading thesis makes sense: the external narrative attracts attention, the minting mechanism broadens participation, and the lack of competing hot projects may have concentrated capital into the token. However, whether its fundamentals are actually strengthening depends on whether Social Season can generate sustained paid minting and genuine trading activity, rather than simply increasing social exposure.

The key question now is whether this rally is being driven by a sustained increase in buyers or simply by a temporary lack of selling pressure from early holders. The former could support further upside; the latter could lead to a sharp pullback as soon as capital rotates elsewhere.

text:
Anthropic's official Claude Code VS Code extension was compromised today. Here's what you need to know.

Matt Johansen posted that the official extension was hit, and that pulling it would have installed an SSH backdoor on your machine for a brief window today. His post has about 73K views. The writeup comes from https://t.co/RmN6YFxESG.

The bad build is version 2.1.313, published to the Open VSX registry. That matters for Cursor, Windsurf and other VS Code forks that pull from Open VSX. Researchers say they don't believe a malicious version reached the main VS Code marketplace.

A loader in extension.js runs ahead of the real extension code. It adds an attacker SSH key to your authorized_keys file, opens a reverse tunnel to the IP 134.209.82[.]225, and sets up persistence. The key is labeled svc-telemetry. Some posts say the tunnel runs over port 8099.

The fix: the compromised version was pulled and replaced by 2.1.314. Posts also say Anthropic pulled the NPM and VS Code versions. The 2.1.314 release notes only mention idle conversation summaries and a git index.lock fix.

How to check:
- Look for version 2.1.313 under ~/.vscode/extensions
- Run grep svc-telemetry ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
- Look for any key in authorized_keys you didn't add
- Upgrade to 2.1.314
- Phorion published a writeup with IOCs to hunt with

Key numbers:
- Bad version: 2.1.313
- Safe version: 2.1.314
- Tunnel IP: 134.209.82[.]225
- Key name: svc-telemetry

Some developers say they will now turn off auto-updates for their extensions. Anthropic had not published a statement in the posts we saw.

text:
AI时代，你的资产还安全吗？谁来为极端损失买单？

AI的进化当然方便了我们的生活，但是也增强了黑客的武器，加密交易所频频失窃。AI黑客如果能够大规模攻击银行、券商和加密货币交易所，我们持有的资产究竟安全吗？更重要的是，如果资产真的被盗，谁来承担最终损失？

很多人认为，放在银行、券商或贝莱德这样的资管巨头手里，资产就有安全保障。但仔细研究会发现，不同资产的托管结构和法律保护存在巨大差异。

先看比特币。放在交易所的BTC，一旦遭遇黑客攻击或平台挪用，投资者能否追回资产取决于交易所的偿付能力、合同及法律责任。自托管虽然消除了交易所的信用风险，但私钥一旦泄露、助记词丢失，通常只能自行承担损失。

比特币ETF同样存在风险。以贝莱德IBIT为例，底层BTC主要由Coinbase Custody托管。虽然设有安全措施和商业保险，但保险并未覆盖全部资产。如果发生重大盗币事件，且保险及法律追偿不足，最终损失仍可能由ETF持有人承担。贝莱德并没有无条件兜底义务。

值得注意的是，黄金ETF与比特币ETF存在类似风险。全球最大的黄金ETF之一GLD由专业机构保管实物黄金，但信托并未为黄金购买全额保险。极端情况下，金库失窃造成的不可追回损失，同样可能反映在基金净值中。

相比之下，传统金融体系的法律保护更为成熟。美国银行存款有FDIC保险，标准保障额度为每位存款人在每家投保银行、每种账户所有权类别下25万美元。美国股票通过证券托管和客户资产隔离制度保护投资者，即使券商破产，客户证券通常仍可追回或转移。出现资产短缺时，SIPC还可对符合条件的账户提供最高50万美元保护。

但AI可能改变这一风险格局。

随着AI自动发现漏洞、执行网络攻击、伪造身份和交易指令的能力提升，金融攻击的成本有望持续下降。银行可能遭遇更复杂的支付欺诈，券商面临账户接管和恶意交易，比特币托管机构则面临私钥管理及授权系统被攻击的风险。

不过，AI也能够帮助金融机构强化风控、识别欺诈和阻断异常交易。攻击能力增强，并不必然意味着资产失窃率持续上升。

我的判断是，未来衡量资产安全性，不能只看托管机构的品牌和技术实力，还要看资产产权能否独立于托管机构、损失是否有保险覆盖、极端情况下谁负有明确的赔偿义务。

联邦崛起，帝国瓦解。

没想到昨天刚发完「CEX 会来 HL 上开交易所、部署 HIP-3*」，今早就出了这么大的黑客事件……

区块链 + AI 正在解构 CEX。

过去，市场习惯了 CEX 用 web2 的方式把加密金融的所有环节一手包办：交易所、券商、银行、清算所、基金、托管……

随着 AI 攻击能力不断提升，没有哪家 CEX 敢保证永不被攻破。它们的核心竞争力最终只剩一条：出了事赔不赔得起。

与此同时链上正在进入专业分工的新时代。

下一代交易联邦的版本答案：

- 链上金融基建（交易所 + 公链合体）：Hyperliquid
- CLOB 撮合引擎+清算所：HyperCore
- 公链：Solana、BNB Chain、Robinhood Chain、HyperEVM 等
- 衍生品/预测市场交易所：HIP-3/3*/4 部署者、Polymarket、其他 Perp DEX
- 现货交易所：HIP-1/HIP-2（订单簿）、AMM（各公链）
- 做市与风险兜底：HLP
- 券商：交易终端、钱包、聚合器，以及一切前端 App
- 账户体系：嵌入式钱包（Privy/Turnkey）
- 托管：MPC（Fireblocks）、多签
- 基金/资管：DeFi 金库、交易型基金（OpenETF）
author: zkwifsats
quoted_text:
关于 Hyperliquid 的关键思考 & 判断 v2：

1. CEX 根本不是 Hyperliquid 的对手（双关），两者根本不在一个维度。CEX 的真正对手是 tradexyz 等生态建设者。

2. 基于 Hyperliquid & HIP-3* 的区域化合规交易所会逐渐替代大部分 CEX，这个过程可能持续十年。

姑且给这类交易所起个名字叫 HyEX：Hyperliquid-based Exchange，或是 Hybrid(CEX-like DEX) Exchange。

3. 用户对操纵市场、扣押资产、吃客损、不透明运作、暗箱运营、黑客盗币等 CEX 老毛病的容忍度越来越低，以及加密市场现货 listing 供给侧断崖下跌，CEX 收入上明显力不从心。

我们会看到关闭潮，从小 CEX 开始。

4. CEX 面前存在「神之一手」的选择，就是立刻去 Hyperliquid 上建设 HyEX，成为 HIP-3* 部署者，在 HL 上做镜像版的自己。

这一手很考验格局和认知，需要交易所老板把眼光拉长到十年。

5. Paywards & Tradexyz 合规路线一旦走通，去美国做合规交易所的路就通了，因为：
a.「证明自己合规合法」的成本大幅下降，如果基建相同，那么起跑线就相同；
b. 对齐 Hyperliquid 就是对齐美国价值观，省 1 亿美金品牌预算。

6. Binance 最近在孵化新 L1，可能想与 HL 一战，不过文化和机制上如果跟不上版本，依然有概率做出来个“联盟链”。

所有交易 L1 的项目都有一个必须回答的问题：做一个交易优化的、DEX-based L1 的必要性到底是什么？链下撮合链上证明的路线为什么不成立？

「神之一手」对 BN 同样开放，要不要试试 Binance US*？

7. Hyperliquid 成为下一代金融基建的趋势已经非常明显了，注意，不是链上金融，是一切金融。

这是开放、透明、中立所带来的必然结果。是价值观、文化、和制度的胜利。

以上。

text:
What if you could hold a stock only while the market is closed, without buying and selling every day?

That's the idea behind Isolated Exposure Tokens (IETs), proposed by @0xbeans and The @standard_rsv.

Deposit one tokenized share and receive:

• OVERNIGHT: exposure from the close to the next open.
• SESSION: exposure from the open to the close.

Hold both and redeem for one share. Sell one to keep only the exposure you want. Each series has an expiry; exiting one side earlier requires a buyer.

A simple example:

• A $100 share starts with $50 allocated to each token.
• It opens at $110: OVERNIGHT rises to $60.
• It closes at $105: SESSION falls to $45.
• Together, they're worth $105 at the accounting level.

Why it's interesting and why we're at @paboxoxyz also loves it as it align with our off-market lending features.

• Could support overnight-only vaults and targeted hedges.
• Splits exposure without requiring the issuer to trade the underlying every day.
• Gives DeFi another building block, similar in structure to Pendle's split claims.

But something that still needs some works and detailed explanations:

• Each token starts with roughly 2× exposure at its initial accounting value.
• Balances accumulate dollar moves, so they don't reproduce the compounded returns.
• Expected overnight gains can already be priced into the token.
• Overnight exposure existed before through NightShares ETFs.

The vault can't pay $110 if the losing holder owes nothing. Caps, early termination or extra capital could help, but the supplied paper doesn't specify a rule.

Promising concept. It needs clear loss rules, reliable price feeds and affordable liquidity before the historical overnight anomaly becomes a new primitive.

Feed-forward 3D models like VGGT can’t tell you when their camera poses are wrong—or so we thought.

This new paper shows a simple linear probe on VGGT’s mid-level features predicts pose failures with 93.5% ROC-AUC, crushing the model’s own confidence (79.7%). Even on pairs VGGT is most confident about (where 12% still fail), the probe catches errors with 90% AUC.

It transfers out-of-the-box to new datasets and even to a second model (π³), hitting up to 97.5% AUC on PhotoTourism with zero retraining. The signal only emerges after the model fuses both views—hidden knowledge, now exposed.

If a system keeps only the 50% of pairs the probe trusts, overall failure rate drops from 35% to 3.8%.

Turns out, these 3D models know when they’re wrong—they just don’t say it unless you ask the right way.

quoted_text:
I suspect IBIT is already on North Korea’s shortlist.

In February 2025, the attackers behind the Bybit hack compromised a Safe{Wallet} developer’s Mac through a malicious project disguised as legitimate Docker-related tooling. They had access for 17 days before the theft, giving them enough time to manipulate the transaction interface used by Bybit’s signers. The signers believed they were approving a legitimate transaction. Instead, they unknowingly authorized the theft of $1.5 billion from a cold wallet.

The keys could stay offline while the signers approved a theft through a compromised interface.

TRM Labs attributes the recent Binance incident with high confidence to TraderTraitor, the North Korean group also linked to Bybit and the theft of 4,502.9 BTC from DMM Bitcoin. Binance’s preliminary investigation points to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop as the entry point. Binance says there’s no evidence that private keys were leaked, while TRM’s analysis suggests the attackers may have gained control of the signing infrastructure. If confirmed, the attackers could have moved funds through a compromised approval process without extracting the keys.

Now imagine the same thing happening to IBIT.

BlackRock’s IBIT is the world’s largest Bitcoin ETF, holding roughly 815,000 BTC worth around $63 billion. Coinbase remains its active Bitcoin custodian. Although Anchorage Digital has been appointed as an additional custodian, the fund’s latest quarterly filing says there are currently no plans to transfer any Bitcoin there.

That’s an extraordinary concentration of Bitcoin under one custodian. Regardless of how large or well-funded that provider is, a critical failure in its security infrastructure could put the entire fund at risk.

A $6 billion theft would wipe out roughly 9.5% of IBIT’s assets, equivalent to around $4 per share at current valuations.

Binance managed to freeze some stolen stablecoins. Bitcoin has no such mechanism, making stolen BTC far harder to recover.

BlackRock doesn’t separately insure the Bitcoin held by the fund. Coinbase has disclosed $320 million in commercial crime insurance coverage, shared across its customers. Its custody agreement also limits liability to $100 million per cold storage address, with any recovery subject to contractual terms, liability determinations, and other conditions.

If a major theft occurred and the fund couldn’t recover the Bitcoin or obtain sufficient compensation, the remaining losses would ultimately be borne by IBIT shareholders.

Bitcoin ETFs have made owning Bitcoin much more accessible, and there’s real value in that convenience. But as more capital flows into these products, enormous amounts of Bitcoin are also being concentrated among a handful of custodians and the infrastructure they depend on.

The larger these pools become, the more attractive they are to attackers. A compromise at any critical point could have consequences far beyond a single institution.

And that’s why security has no finish line.

Even the most sophisticated cold storage setup still depends on hardware, software, supply chains, signing workflows, and the people operating them. Keeping private keys offline is essential, but it doesn’t eliminate the risks surrounding the transaction approval process.

Spread your assets across independent custody setups. Keep your private keys offline. Verify transaction details on a trusted device screen, independently of the computer initiating the transaction. Continuously review your security architecture, and build it around the assumption that some part of your infrastructure will eventually be compromised.

There are no silver bullets in security, and no permanent guarantees. Stay vigilant, keep verifying, and never mistake a clean track record for proof that you’re safe.

Bunker mode.

text:
你以为交易所很透明？

在2025年年初，我一直在研究 Binance、OKX 等多家交易所。

我的思路很简单，就是通过一些发币的大庄家，找到他们的资金来源，再通过资金源，顺藤摸瓜找到他们所有的关联钱包。

其实我早就做好了最坏的打算，可能涉及几千、几万个关联钱包，也可能经过混币器，但这些对我来说都无所谓。只要能找到资金源，建立起钱包之间的关联关系，赚钱就和喝水一样简单。

因为在2024年，我就是通过这种方式，查到了很多 KOL 的关联钱包。

当时用户往交易所充值，通常都有明确的充值地址，通过链上的资金流向，还能追踪到相关的归集、分发地址，从而找到更多关联钱包。

我原本以为，到了2025年，依然可以沿用这套方法。

但没想到，2025年，一切都变了。

无论是大型交易所，还是小型交易所，都开始大量采用超大热钱包进行资金归集和统一管理。

相当于把所有用户的钱，统一放进了几十个巨大的资金池里。

其实这一点我也能接受，最让我头疼的是，交易所显示的发送地址和实际接收地址之间，已经很难找到直接的链上关联。

也就是说，你们在交易所看到的那些充值地址，可以理解为只是一个资金入口，并不代表后续资金会一直从这个地址进出。

你在交易所充值、提现，背后的资金可能都经过统一的热钱包进行调配，充值地址和提现地址之间不一定存在直接的链上联系。

到了这一步，还没有完全难倒我。

我当时就在想，反正每一笔链上交易都有记录，那我直接在区块链浏览器里，按照对应的时间、对应的币种、对应的金额去查，不就能找到资金流向了吗？

结果却不尽人意，居然在区块链浏览器里也查不到准确对应的交易。

相当于交易所的热钱包虽然在链上，但用户实际的充值、提现记录，和这些热钱包的资金流转已经很难找到直接关联。

研究到这一步，这件事也就暂时到此为止了。

所以后来每当有人问我，资金被盗了怎么办？

我的答案大部分都是：凉拌，哈哈哈。

除非你认识交易所内部的人……

那个时候我就在想，为什么交易所都要这样做？

我脑子里出现了几个答案：

1. 减少麻烦，同时保护用户隐私。

用户的资金一旦被盗，想通过链上追踪找到最终的关联账户就变得非常困难。某种程度上，交易所也减少了很多外部追踪和协查带来的麻烦。

2. 为了资金安全。

通过大型热钱包统一管理资金，既方便调度，也能减少部分地址直接暴露带来的风险。

但当时我就在想，所有资金都集中到几个大热钱包里，万一整个热钱包被盗了，岂不是更加危险？

没想到，后来还真发生了类似的大型交易所安全事件。

当然，也并不是说完全没有人能够查出这些关联。

在我看来，真正能够准确掌握目标地址背后关联关系的，主要只有两种人：

能够直接看到目标账户真实信息和内部资金记录的人。 因为这些数据在公开的区块链上根本看不到。
交易所内部的人。 他们掌握着用户账户、充值地址、提现记录以及内部资金调度的数据。

说实话，当时得出的这些答案，简直糟糕透了。

其实你也可以把交易所理解成一家银行。

你把钱存进去，账户上显示你有多少钱，但这笔钱到底去了哪里、内部怎么流转、交易所究竟有多少真实资产，你并不一定清楚。

当然，对于 Binance、OKX 这种体量足够大的交易所来说，他们有更强的资金实力、储备金和风险保障能力。

即使发生资金被盗事件，他们也更有能力承担损失和进行赔偿。

但这并不代表他们绝对安全，更不代表任何损失都一定能得到赔偿。

所以研究到最后，我发现一个很现实的问题：区块链本身是公开透明的，但当资金进入中心化交易所之后，用户能看到的，可能就只是交易所愿意公开给你的那部分信息。

这也是我研究了这么久之后，感触最深的一点：

链上可以追踪资金，但不代表你一定能追踪到资金背后的人；区块链可以做到公开透明，但不代表所有参与区块链的机构都同样透明。
