text:
A friendly reminder to take your crypto security seriously.

Start doing these things TODAY:

- Keep your long-term holdings offline.
Consider a hardware wallet or an air-gapped wallet on a dedicated offline device.
If you don't want to buy a hardware wallet, air-gapped storage is an alternative.

- Never use one wallet for everything.
Keep separate wallets for long-term holdings, trading, DeFi, airdrops, and unfamiliar protocols.
@Rabby_io and @phantom are the only wallets I use.

- Don't keep your entire portfolio in one place.
Avoid concentrating all your funds on a single CEX, hot wallet, protocol, or device.

- Don't use public Wi-Fi for crypto activity.
If you work from cafes or coworking spaces, use your phone's personal hotspot instead of connecting to public Wi-Fi networks.

- Protect your seed phrases.
Never store them in screens, cloud storage, emails, or password managers connected to the internet.
If your seed phrase has ever been stored on an internet-connected device - migrate to a fresh wallet NOW!

- Keep secure offline backups.
Store recovery backups somewhere safe, preferably with protection against fire/water and unauthorized access.
I recommend getting a fire-resistant and water-resistant document bag.

- Use a dedicated device for crypto.
Keep your hot wallets and high-value transactions on a separate device.
Don't use it for random downloads, gaming mods, unknown software, or everyday browsing.

- Use a separate browser for wallets.
Keep your wallet browser dedicated to trusted crypto activity.
Avoid unnecessary extensions and random websites.

- Never install cracked software on crypto devices.
Pirated applications, fake installers, and malicious updates can contain wallet-stealing malware.
If you need to run untrusted software, keep it completely isolated from your crypto environment.

- Keep your devices updated.
Update your OS, browser, and wallet software through official sources.

- Remove unnecessary browser extensions.
Even legitimate extensions can become dangerous after a compromised update or ownership change.
Keep only what you absolutely need.

- Stop using Google Search to find crypto websites.
Fake websites and malicious sponsored results can look almost identical to legitimate ones.
Use independently verified official links from bookmarks instead.

- Don't open random links from X or Telegram.
Especially not in the browser where your wallets are installed.
Never!!!

- Secure your CEX accounts.
Use passkeys or hardware security keys where supported.
Enable withdrawal address whitelists and avoid relying on SMS 2FA.

- Consider getting a YubiKey.
A physical security key can help protect your email and exchange accounts against phishing.
Buy only from the official manufacturer sellers.

- Review your Google-connected crypto accounts.
Check which crypto services use Google Sign-In.
Never disconnect your only login method without setting up an alternative first.

- Revoke unnecessary token approvals.
Use @RevokeCash to review and remove permissions you no longer need.
Disconnecting a wallet from a dApp does NOT revoke its token approvals.

- Avoid unlimited token approvals.
Whenever possible, approve only the amount you actually need.
Unlimited allowances can expose much larger balances if a spender is compromised.

- Review Permit2 permissions.
Permit2 signatures can authorize token transfers without a normal on-chain approval transaction.
Review existing allowances and permissions. Some malicious signatures can be exploited long after they're signed.

- Never blindly sign messages.
A signature doesn't need to cost gas to be dangerous.
Never get distracted while signing transactions. Either finish your transactions first or take care of everything else before you start.
Make this a rule.

- Be careful with custom RPC endpoints.
Don't add/delete now unknown RPC URLs.
Use trusted providers and verify network settings independently.

- Understand EIP-7702 authorization risks.
On supported networks, account delegation can grant powerful capabilities to other code.
Never approve an account delegation you don't understand. (That's why Binance was hacked)

- Never copy addresses blindly from transaction history.
Address poisoning attacks can place lookalike addresses in your transaction history.
Verify the full destination address against a trusted source.

- Watch out for clipboard malware.
Malware can replace a copied wallet address with an attacker's address.
Always verify the entire destination address after pasting, preferably on an independent trusted display.

- Verify token contracts and networks.
A familiar ticker or logo doesn't prove a token is legitimate.
Check the contract address and make sure the receiving platform supports the exact asset and network.

- Test large transfers first.
When sending funds to a new destination, start with a small test transaction.

- Ignore unexpected tokens and NFTs.
Random assets appearing in your wallet may contain phishing links or fake reward claims.
Don't interact with them just because they appeared in your balance.

- Don't trust unexpected job offers or collaboration requests.
Fake interviews, partnership offers, and test applications can be used to distribute wallet-stealing malware.
Never run unfamiliar software on your crypto device just to qualify for an opportunity.

- Never run terminal commands you don't understand.
Fake troubleshooting guides, verification pages, and job interviews may ask you to copy and paste commands into your terminal.
One malicious command can compromise your entire device, including your wallets.

- Never trust a QR code blindly.
QR code can contain a malicious website, payment request or an attacker's wallet address.
Avoid scanning unknown QR codes with devices that contain your crypto wallets or other sensitive data.

- Understand bridge and DeFi risks.
Before depositing significant funds, check contract upgradeability, admin privileges, timelocks, and bridge security assumptions.
Audits are useful, but they don't guarantee safety.

- Secure your multisig properly.
If you use @Safe or another multisig, keep signer keys on independent devices.
Review owners, signing thresholds, modules, and guards.
A malicious module may bypass normal multisig approval requirements.

- Monitor your wallets.
Set up alerts for unexpected transfers, approvals, and other sensitive activity where supported.
Use Codex/Claude to vibe-code a simple TG-bot that notifies you whenever something happens in your wallets.

- Have an emergency recovery plan.
Know what to do if a wallet, seed phrase, device, or exchange account is compromised.
If your seed phrase is exposed, move your assets to a new wallet generated from a fresh seed on a trusted device.
Revoking approvals alone won't fix a compromised private key.

- Keep your crypto holdings private.
Avoid publicly revealing wallet balances, screenshots of large portfolios, or details of your security setup.
Don't make yourself an easy target for social engineering or physical theft.

- Protect yourself from SIM swapping.
Attackers can hijack your phone number and intercept SMS verification codes.
Use authenticator apps, passkeys, or hardware security keys instead of SMS wherever possible. Secure your mobile carrier account too.

- Don't blindly trust familiar contacts.
A message from someone you know doesn't mean their account is still under their control.
Verify it through another channel first.

- And one last thing:
You don't need to be paranoid.
You just need to make it much harder for someone to steal what you've spent years building.

Protect your capital before you think about growing it.

text:
The Binance hacker might have just executed one of the most brilliant moves in crypto.

First, Tether froze $1.5 billion worth of USDT.

Then Circle followed by freezing another $800 million in USDC.

At that point, it seemed like the hacker’s funds were completely trapped.

But apparently, he had already thought several steps ahead.

Rather than keeping the stolen USDT in a wallet, he allegedly deposited it into Aave and used it as collateral to borrow ETH.

Then he walked away.

And this is where things get really interesting.

Tether can freeze the USDT sitting in that wallet.

But it can’t freeze the ETH that was already borrowed.

So now, Aave is left with frozen collateral, while the hacker is holding liquid ETH.

And unless the protocol finds a way to recover those funds, he might not even have to repay the loan.

Two companies froze billions of dollars in seconds.

Yet someone who understood how DeFi works may have found a way to bypass both restrictions.

Pretty wild when you think about it.

author: tengyanAI
quoted_text:
Intel is getting crushed, down ~23% after earnings.

but if you go beyond the headlines, I think the market is missing something v important abt the AI boom.

Intel has too little capacity for its fastest-growing business, and too much exposure to its shrinking one.

look at the numbers.

Intel guided Q4 revenue to $15.5B, roughly 9% below expectations - ugly!

but underneath that headline, two very different things are happening:

Data Center & AI: +mid-teens QoQ, to ~$8.4–8.5B.
Client: −20%+ QoQ, to below $6.5B.

Intel expects to ADD ~$1.1B of quarterly data-center revenue while losing at least $1.6B in client revenue.

AI server demand is doing well. 
The PC business is collapsing.

and the two are connected.

AI infrastructure demand is contributing to memory shortages. DRAM prices rise, PCs become more expensive, and OEMs cut processor orders.

Intel expects PC unit shipments to fall ~12% in 2026 and another ~10% in 2027.

The AI boom is effectively destroying demand elsewhere in semiconductors.

but it gets even more interesting..

Intel wants to produce more server CPUs. Demand for Granite Rapids is strong. Yet it's constrained by Intel 3 manufacturing capacity AND advanced packaging substrates.

even producing more wafers won't help if it can't package them.

look at September revenue growth among substrate suppliers:

Unimicron: +64.7% YoY
Kinsus: +44.5%
Nan Ya PCB: +57.8%

these aren't Intel-specific figures ofc, but they corroborate strong industry demand.

yesterday, Ibiden approved ¥151B of investment in high-performance CPU substrates, citing AI inference and agentic AI.

new production doesn't begin until FY2029. Intel expects some earlier substrate relief in H2 2027.

advanced substrates could be one of the most underappreciated bottlenecks in the AI buildout.

now, why am I NOT automatically bullish on Intel after a 23% selloff?

Q3 non-GAAP gross margin was 44%. Q4 guidance is 38%.

That's ~$1.4B LESS quarterly gross profit despite enormous server demand.

Intel expects higher manufacturing spending and negative free cash flow in 2027. It raised $23B in equity in August.

and of its $6.7B foundry revenue, just $411M came from external customers. The segment still lost ~$1.9B.

that's the contradiction.

Intel is exposed to one of the strongest semiconductor demand cycles in history, but manufacturing constraints, PC weakness and capital intensity are consuming much of the benefit.

Being on the right side of AI demand doesn't mean shareholders capture the economics. You need to find who can actually ship into that demand... and who gets to keep the profits.

So @tessara_ai's read on $INTC is : bullish on structural server CPU demand, increasingly interested in substrate suppliers, but cautious on Intel's earnings conversion.

AMD's November 3 results will help test whether these constraints are industry-wide or Intel-specific.

Here’s everything you need to know about the Binance hack:

✅ Hackers drained about $6.3B from @binance hot wallets across nine chains on Oct 29, the largest crypto theft ever. ✅ Binance says customers won't lose funds ✅ Binance has already set aside $6.34B to cover the hack, and $5B of it is held in the exact tokens that were stolen. ✅ Started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, and Binance later found "additional points of breach." ✅ Tether, Circle, Ripple and WLFI froze stablecoins and tokens, about $3B frozen so far. ✅ The Arbitrum Security Council froze ~$30.5M of the hacker's ETH and $ARB directly from the exploiter wallet. ✅ About $2.9B in $BTC, $ETH, $TRX, $SOL and altcoins can't be frozen and is still moving. ✅ That includes 18,270 $BTC (~$1.47B) taken in one block, plus an ETH stack Arkham put at $1.12B ✅ The hacker sold $UNI, $ENA, $PEPE, $LINK, $AAVE, $ONDO and $WLD on-chain for 70,480 ETH (~$158M) ✅ Funds went through THORChain into the same wallet as the $388M Bitget hack loot, which @zachxbt ties to North Korea's TraderTraitor. ✅ Binance is buying the rest of the stolen altcoins through OTC deals and on the exchange, and deposits already work again with withdrawals back in about 45 hours. ✅ $BTC fell to around $76.4K, and about $1.57B in positions got liquidated. ✅ @elonmusk posted "Everyday is Zeroday" and replied 🔥😂 to CZ. ✅ @cz_binance told Elon "bad time to troll" and said Binance's $SPCX stake from its $500M Twitter investment is worth over $1B, enough to cover the ~$2B gap if it’s sold.  ✅ @heyibinance's reply: this year's revenue covers it, so "we do not yet need to sell the SpaceX shares."

text:
Everyone's scared right now.

That's usually when the next cycle's biggest winners are sitting there cheap.

By the time ppl start shilling again, most of the move is already gone.

Here are the 5 narratives I'm watching before the markets pump:

1. AI Inference

Every time someone uses Claude or an AI agent, somebody pays for the computing power behind it. That's inference.

As agents do more work on their own, that bill keeps getting bigger.

Some crypto projects already let people buy or access that compute through their tokens.

I'd check two things. Are there real paying customers? And does that demand actually flow back to the token?

• $VVV $ORBIO

2. Proof of Useful Work / AI Compute

Bitcoin miners burn a huge amount of computing power just to secure the network.

Pearl and Nockchain are betting the same kind of hardware can do useful work (AI models, ZK proofs) and still earn rewards.

Bittensor goes broader and pays people for useful AI contributions.

The catch is that a network can have thousands of GPUs running with nobody actually paying to use them.

So the number I care about is revenue from real customers vs rewards paid by printing new tokens.

• $PEARL $NOCK $TAO

3. Privacy

Right now anyone can look up a wallet and see the savings in it and every payment it's ever made.

Businesses and AI agents aren't gonna move serious money on rails like that.

Zcash and Monero already do private payments. Newer projects are building private apps and smart contracts.

The obvious risk is regulators. Honestly, I don't have a clean answer to that one.

So I'd trust usage over headlines. That means growth in private transactions and apps that really need privacy to work.

• $ZEC $XMR $NIGHT

4. Quantum Resistance

Quantum computers may one day break the cryptography that protects most crypto wallets. And you can't upgrade a whole blockchain overnight.

The interesting part is that networks are already taking different routes.

NEAR added quantum-safe signatures (ML-DSA) to mainnet in July.

Starknet is aiming to be fully quantum resistant by 2027.

Quantus launched in September with quantum-resistant signatures from day one.

I'm honestly not sure on timing here. So I'd only care which upgrades are actually live, and whether any of it creates demand for the token.

• $QTC $NEAR $STRK

5. Revenue & Buybacks

The part most people still skip is doing the math after dilution.

Say a project buys back $10M while unlocking $50M in new tokens. It's still putting more on the market than it's taking off.

So I'd look at how much revenue actually reaches the token after unlocks and emissions.

• $HYPE $UNI $PUMP

I wouldn't buy all five today.

I'd build a watchlist with 2 or 3 projects per sector and check those numbers once a month.

The setup I want is the number getting better while the price hasn't caught up yet.

That gap is usually widest when everyone's scared... like right now.

The narrative gets a coin on your watchlist. The numbers tell you when to buy.

Which of these five do you think the market is still sleeping on?

text:
A $6.3B hack at the world’s largest crypto exchange is a wake-up call for every organization responsible for protecting funds onchain.

Early findings suggest a compromised engineer’s laptop gave an attacker access to systems used to submit withdrawals. Funds were taken across ten blockchains. The full root cause remains under investigation.

An exchange holding this much customer capital needs controls that contain an intrusion before it becomes billions in unauthorized transfers. Replacing losses afterward cannot substitute for preventing them.

Most of the $6.3B was stolen in roughly 20 minutes.

As more assets move onchain, these failures put more capital at risk. More integrations, providers and privileged accounts create more routes to secure. Attackers already target employees and wallet providers; larger potential payouts give them more incentive.

Teams need to know who can reach their signing infrastructure, what they can authorize, which controls remain independent during a compromise, and how quickly they can detect and stop an intrusion.

We’re putting more of Sherlock’s work into opsec: tracing how access to an organization can become access to its funds, and helping teams close those paths.

In order for the world’s financial system to run onchain, protecting its assets has to mean securing everything with the authority to move them.

This is how far The New Yorker, once the absolute pinnacle of non-fiction prose, has fallen. From recent article on microchips:

"There are a handful of truly monumental collective achievements in our history: Machu Picchu, the Great Wall of China, the Pyramids of Giza, and perhaps, if we’re being generous, the Roman aqueducts. Modern global civilization has made one contribution to this eternal pantheon. It is not the moon landing. It is the semiconductor supply chain."

Not the steam engine? Not the automobile? The printing press? The interstate highway system? Airplanes? Nuclear energy? The international space station? Television? The moving picture? How about oil rigs that dig 7 miles underneath the ocean? How about antibiotics? 

NONE of these are as "monumental an achievement" as...Machu Picchu? Is Macchu Picchu even really that different than, say, Stonehenge, Easter Island, or Angkor Wat? 

Of course the subtext here is that listing any of the above "achievements" would be to glorify the white man too much. He even throws a little extra shade on Rome "if we're being generous." Thank you so much for your generosity Gideon Lewis-Kraus! Could it really be that not one editor questioned your exhaustive and unimpeachable list of the 5 greatest things ever created by humanity? Do you realize how ignorant and chauvinistic such a list would be in literally any other context? 

An absolute joke. Garbage in garbage out. It's time for a new age of magazines.

text:
A friendly reminder to take your crypto security seriously.

Start doing these things TODAY:

- Keep your long-term holdings offline.
Consider a hardware wallet or an air-gapped wallet on a dedicated offline device.
If you don't want to buy a hardware wallet, air-gapped storage is an alternative.

- Never use one wallet for everything.
Keep separate wallets for long-term holdings, trading, DeFi, airdrops, and unfamiliar protocols.
@Rabby_io and @phantom are the only wallets I use.

- Don't keep your entire portfolio in one place.
Avoid concentrating all your funds on a single CEX, hot wallet, protocol, or device.

- Don't use public Wi-Fi for crypto activity.
If you work from cafes or coworking spaces, use your phone's personal hotspot instead of connecting to public Wi-Fi networks.

- Protect your seed phrases.
Never store them in screens, cloud storage, emails, or password managers connected to the internet.
If your seed phrase has ever been stored on an internet-connected device - migrate to a fresh wallet NOW!

- Keep secure offline backups.
Store recovery backups somewhere safe, preferably with protection against fire/water and unauthorized access.
I recommend getting a fire-resistant and water-resistant document bag.

- Use a dedicated device for crypto.
Keep your hot wallets and high-value transactions on a separate device.
Don't use it for random downloads, gaming mods, unknown software, or everyday browsing.

- Use a separate browser for wallets.
Keep your wallet browser dedicated to trusted crypto activity.
Avoid unnecessary extensions and random websites.

- Never install cracked software on crypto devices.
Pirated applications, fake installers, and malicious updates can contain wallet-stealing malware.
If you need to run untrusted software, keep it completely isolated from your crypto environment.

- Keep your devices updated.
Update your OS, browser, and wallet software through official sources.

- Remove unnecessary browser extensions.
Even legitimate extensions can become dangerous after a compromised update or ownership change.
Keep only what you absolutely need.

- Stop using Google Search to find crypto websites.
Fake websites and malicious sponsored results can look almost identical to legitimate ones.
Use independently verified official links from bookmarks instead.

- Don't open random links from X or Telegram.
Especially not in the browser where your wallets are installed.
Never!!!

- Secure your CEX accounts.
Use passkeys or hardware security keys where supported.
Enable withdrawal address whitelists and avoid relying on SMS 2FA.

- Consider getting a YubiKey.
A physical security key can help protect your email and exchange accounts against phishing.
Buy only from the official manufacturer sellers.

- Review your Google-connected crypto accounts.
Check which crypto services use Google Sign-In.
Never disconnect your only login method without setting up an alternative first.

- Revoke unnecessary token approvals.
Use @RevokeCash to review and remove permissions you no longer need.
Disconnecting a wallet from a dApp does NOT revoke its token approvals.

- Avoid unlimited token approvals.
Whenever possible, approve only the amount you actually need.
Unlimited allowances can expose much larger balances if a spender is compromised.

- Review Permit2 permissions.
Permit2 signatures can authorize token transfers without a normal on-chain approval transaction.
Review existing allowances and permissions. Some malicious signatures can be exploited long after they're signed.

- Never blindly sign messages.
A signature doesn't need to cost gas to be dangerous.
Never get distracted while signing transactions. Either finish your transactions first or take care of everything else before you start.
Make this a rule.

- Be careful with custom RPC endpoints.
Don't add/delete now unknown RPC URLs.
Use trusted providers and verify network settings independently.

- Understand EIP-7702 authorization risks.
On supported networks, account delegation can grant powerful capabilities to other code.
Never approve an account delegation you don't understand. (That's why Binance was hacked)

- Never copy addresses blindly from transaction history.
Address poisoning attacks can place lookalike addresses in your transaction history.
Verify the full destination address against a trusted source.

- Watch out for clipboard malware.
Malware can replace a copied wallet address with an attacker's address.
Always verify the entire destination address after pasting, preferably on an independent trusted display.

- Verify token contracts and networks.
A familiar ticker or logo doesn't prove a token is legitimate.
Check the contract address and make sure the receiving platform supports the exact asset and network.

- Test large transfers first.
When sending funds to a new destination, start with a small test transaction.

- Ignore unexpected tokens and NFTs.
Random assets appearing in your wallet may contain phishing links or fake reward claims.
Don't interact with them just because they appeared in your balance.

- Don't trust unexpected job offers or collaboration requests.
Fake interviews, partnership offers, and test applications can be used to distribute wallet-stealing malware.
Never run unfamiliar software on your crypto device just to qualify for an opportunity.

- Never run terminal commands you don't understand.
Fake troubleshooting guides, verification pages, and job interviews may ask you to copy and paste commands into your terminal.
One malicious command can compromise your entire device, including your wallets.

- Never trust a QR code blindly.
QR code can contain a malicious website, payment request or an attacker's wallet address.
Avoid scanning unknown QR codes with devices that contain your crypto wallets or other sensitive data.

- Understand bridge and DeFi risks.
Before depositing significant funds, check contract upgradeability, admin privileges, timelocks, and bridge security assumptions.
Audits are useful, but they don't guarantee safety.

- Secure your multisig properly.
If you use @Safe or another multisig, keep signer keys on independent devices.
Review owners, signing thresholds, modules, and guards.
A malicious module may bypass normal multisig approval requirements.

- Monitor your wallets.
Set up alerts for unexpected transfers, approvals, and other sensitive activity where supported.
Use Codex/Claude to vibe-code a simple TG-bot that notifies you whenever something happens in your wallets.

- Have an emergency recovery plan.
Know what to do if a wallet, seed phrase, device, or exchange account is compromised.
If your seed phrase is exposed, move your assets to a new wallet generated from a fresh seed on a trusted device.
Revoking approvals alone won't fix a compromised private key.

- Keep your crypto holdings private.
Avoid publicly revealing wallet balances, screenshots of large portfolios, or details of your security setup.
Don't make yourself an easy target for social engineering or physical theft.

- Protect yourself from SIM swapping.
Attackers can hijack your phone number and intercept SMS verification codes.
Use authenticator apps, passkeys, or hardware security keys instead of SMS wherever possible. Secure your mobile carrier account too.

- Don't blindly trust familiar contacts.
A message from someone you know doesn't mean their account is still under their control.
Verify it through another channel first.

- And one last thing:
You don't need to be paranoid.
You just need to make it much harder for someone to steal what you've spent years building.

Protect your capital before you think about growing it.

text:
every time another major crypto hack happens, I can't help but wonder why I'm still here.

let's be real.

making money in crypto feels 20–30 times harder than it did 5 years ago.

remember how things used to be?

you could wake up and find out some random project had airdropped you a few thousand dollars just because you made a swap months ago.

and by the time you finished breakfast and opened your laptop, that same airdrop had gone 10x.

you just made $20K for doing absolutely nothing that morning.

you could keep your money on CEXs, stake some tokens, and somehow earn thousands of dollars almost every week.

you could buy a random coin because you liked its logo, wake up the next day, and find yourself a few thousand dollars richer because apparently everyone else liked that logo too.

you could stake your tokens on some DeFi platform and literally watch yourself get richer by the minute.

you could mint an NFT just because everyone was doing it, then sell it an hour later for several ETH.

it honestly felt like almost everything you touched turned into money.

projects were sending tokens to anyone with a wallet.

no complicated strategies. no endless points farming. no spending 4–6 months completing tasks for a potential $40 airdrop.

sometimes all you needed was a wallet and a little luck.

people were having fun.

nobody was constantly thinking about the next hack, the next regulation, or what some president might say tomorrow.

we were just a bunch of people on the internet making money out of thin air.

and damn, those were good times!!!

now look at where we are.

you wake up and check your wallets to make sure your money is still there.
you read the news to see if another CEX, perp DEX, bridge, or protocol has been hacked.
you check your positions, your approvals, your exchanges, and everything else just to make sure nothing terrible happened while you were sleeping.

making every dollar in crypto now takes a titanic amount of effort.

and somehow, keeping that dollar safe takes even more.

but we're still here...

we still believe this industry has something left to give us.

we still believe there will be another lucky airdrop that changes someone's life overnight.

we still believe crypto will eventually become safer and bring hundreds of thousands of new people into this market.

we still believe that at least some of the thousands of altcoins multiplying faster than bacteria will actually become useful and make us money.

we're still holding on to that belief...

and maybe that's what keeps us here.

because compared to almost any other financial market, we're still a tiny group of people spending an absurd amount of time and energy on something most of the world doesn't even care about.

i really hope all of this leads to something big someday!

because otherwise, what the hell are we still doing here?

text:
如果这次的超级黑客攻击换成去搞银行，银行能防得住吗？他们会怎么做？ 

1️⃣ 第一道防线：物理隔离（Air-Gapping）
黑客的套路：在 Crypto 世界，为了追求“24小时即充即提”的极致体验，核心资产往往挂在联网的自动化网关上。黑客只要黑进员工电脑，就能顺着网络摸到“热钱包”的提现接口。
银行怎么做：银行的核心清算账本和绝大部分资金，在物理上是完全断网的。银行员工的办公电脑（能上外网、看邮件的系统）和核心账本系统是两套完全独立的物理硬件。黑客就算把全行员工的笔记本电脑全部黑掉，他也根本找不到任何一条网线能连进银行的核心金库。想偷钱？除非顺着网线来撬银行的物理防爆门。

2️⃣ 第二道防线：九品中正制（权限彻底分离）
黑客的套路：Crypto 平台的权限往往过于集中。一个高级运维人员为了方便修 bug，可能拥有访问服务容器和自动提现脚本的最高权限（Super Admin），这直接导致了单点沦陷。
银行怎么做：银行内部实行极度变态的“职责分离”和“最小权限原则”。写代码的碰不到钱：IT 运维人员只有修服务器的权限，绝对没有任何一丁点审批资金划转的权力。
多岗位交叉签名：银行的一笔大额资金想汇出，必须经过前台发起、合规审查、主管复核、高管双人交叉物理签字。没有任何一个人可以仅凭自己的账号把钱转走。

3️⃣ 第三道防线：“天眼”级动态熔断与冲正机制
黑客的套路：区块链具有“落子无悔”的特性。提现接口一旦被黑客恶意调用，不管金额多离谱、地址多可疑，智能合约都会盲目执行，几分钟内资金就会被洗劫一空。

银行怎么做：银行拥有一套灵敏度极高的风控大模型。瞬间拦截：如果系统检测到某位大客户或银行内部账户在反常的时间、向高风险的未知黑名单地址突然进行巨额转账，风控系统会毫秒级触发自动熔断，直接拔网线锁死账户。
做错可冲正：即便黑客通过某种极端的漏洞把钱划走了，银行系统还留有一手底牌——交易冲正与央行清算拦截。大额跨境汇款在最终结算前有很长的窗口期，银行可以联合央行和对方银行直接单方面取消、冻结这笔异动，把钱硬生生“扣回来”。
#Crypto #网络安全 #Web3 #区块链安全 #金融风控

text:
Turnkey exists today because I got so frustrated using an existing crypto wallet provider that I decided to build a better one.

Back in 2022, I was integrating a wallet provider into a product, and the entire experience was a nightmare.

Weeks of sales calls, endless back and forth, and even getting API access to test the product was a massive hurdle. I knew there had to be a better way, so my co-founder @whojackjones and I built it.

Fast forward to today, Turnkey has become one of the leading wallet providers in crypto, powering some of the biggest names in the industry and processing over $200B in lifetime stablecoin volume.

If there's one take away, it's that some of the biggest market opportunities come from problems you’re experiencing firsthand. And sometimes being the second mover is actually advantageous.

If something is genuinely frustrating you GO BUILD THE BETTER VERSION.

text:
1小时窗口 套利342万美元

视频还原下 342万 美元整个高卖低买的过程

◆10月30日凌晨04时24分左右，币安热钱包出现异常转出

攻击者 拿到的资产中包含大量稳定币。
后因Tether、Circle 等发行方随后采取紧急冻结措施，部分资金被冻结。
稳定币存在被冻结的风险，攻击者开始通过链上交易将其中一部分换成 ETH。
攻击者持续的大额买入ETH，把部分池子和交易路线里的 ETH 买贵了 （LP池里ETH价格被推高）

套利者 随后借来 ETH，卖进价格偏高的市场

◆04时40分前后，价差出现

原帖统计，当时部分 Uniswap 成交中的 ETH 价格达到2560至2750美元，个别成交超过3000美元；Aave 使用的预言机报价仍约为2250至2290美元。

Aave 的预言机会汇总多个市场的数据，一个局部池子被买贵，并不会自动让整体参考价同步上涨。

于是，手里有稳定币的人，可以抵押稳定币、借出链上的 ETH，再把 ETH 卖到高价市场。
或者手里的ETH直接去池子高价出售，然后去交易所低价买回。
以后买回相同数量的 ETH 还债，剩下的价差扣除成本，才是收益。

◆04时43分，资金到账；04时48分，开始借币

目标地址先收到约209.9万 USDC，随后存入 Aave。
04时48分23秒，它借出第一笔500 ETH 

第一次卖出尝试失败后，04时50分23秒，它成功卖出500 ETH，收到约133.99万 USDC，均价约2680 USDC。

接下来，它没有立刻买回还债。

刚卖出来的133.99万 USDC 被存回 Aave，增加抵押物，然后再借 ETH、再卖出、再把稳定币存回去 
期间，它还追加调入306.3万 USDC，并赎回其他存款参与操作。

这一轮重复的动作就是 抵押、借 ETH、高价卖出、收入重新抵押。
买回和还款被推迟，卖出的数量逐渐扩大，ETH 负债也在累积。

◆05时32分，主要卖出阶段结束

约42分钟内，这个地址完成18笔主要卖出，合计11682 ETH。

成交价格也在变化。
早期有交易卖到每枚2700 USDC附近，最后一笔主要卖出已经降到约2391 USDC，价差正在收窄。

这期间累计存入 Aave 的 USDC 约3686.84万，其中包含多轮卖币后重新存回的收入。

05时42分左右，Aave 开始冻结相关市场，限制新增存款和借款，已有仓位仍可还款和提款。
这个地址的主要借款已经在此前完成。冻结规则与时间

◆05时46分之后，买回 ETH，分批还债

05时49分，它开始还款，直到06时50分，分12笔偿还本轮借款。
 Aave 会累计记录同一种资产的债务，分批还的是总负债，无须与之前每笔借款一一配对。

还款过程中，它分批取出 USDC、买 ETH、还债，再释放更多抵押物。借款仓位还在，就不能随意把抵押物一次全部提走。
合并计算，地址总共卖出约12289 ETH，均价约2580 USDC
07时左右，它开始把 USDC 和 Aave 存款凭证转向另一个地址，这轮主要操作结束。

所谓“1小时窗口”，指的是明显价差持续的阶段
完整的借款、交易、还款和收尾，持续了两个多小时

❑套利小白的经验汲取
我们要学习整个事件的交易思路

学习如何监控 某个币种，尤其ETH链，由于去中心化的特性决定他的套利机会要大于其他链

❑风险有四
1）价差消失：看到的价格未必能成交，滑点、抢跑和 Gas 可能吃掉收益。
2） ETH 继续上涨：卖掉借来的 ETH 后，债还在，买回成本可能增加，仓位也可能被清算。
3） 资金无法到账：交易所暂停提币、跨链延迟、借贷市场冻结，都可能卡住交易。
4）工具判断出错：AI 可能算错，程序可能读错价格，合约和授权也有风险。先做只读监控和模拟，再判断自己是否理解了整条资金路径。

套利太有意思了 想把所有套利事件整理下喂给AI再慢慢调呀～   
关注我   后续一起分享各种玩法～

quoted_text:
币安被盗那一个小时，链上出现了一个教科书级的套利窗口。有人一小时赚了 347 万刀，我把链上数据扒了一遍，复盘一下。

【发生了什么】 北京时间 10 月 30 日凌晨 4 点 24 分左右，币安热钱包被盗。 黑客手里一大堆 USDT，怕被 Tether 冻结，就在链上 DEX 疯狂把 U 换成 ETH。同一时间币安暂停提币，交易所里便宜的 ETH 搬不上链。 结果：
Uniswap 上 ETH 在 04:40–05:40 被买到 2560–2750，个别成交 3000+
Aave 用的 Chainlink 预言机汇总的是交易所价格，全程在 2250–2290 链上比交易所贵了 15%–30%，挂了将近一个小时。
【套利连招】

往 Aave 存 USDC/USDT 当抵押
按预言机价 ≈2280 借出 ETH
马上去 DEX/聚合器按 2600+ 卖成 U

卖出来的 U 再存回去，继续借、继续卖

价格回落到 2290 附近，买回 ETH 还款，差价全是利润 这不是黑 Aave，Aave 合约一点问题都没有。本质是 CEX 和 DEX 的价差搬砖，Aave 只是一个"按交易所价格出 ETH 的窗口"。
【链上数据】我拉了事发后 6 小时所有在 Aave 主网借 ETH 的地址，一共 61 个，排除黑客地址（6000 万 U 抵押借了 19762 ETH），逐笔算了盈亏：
第一名 0x0cdd…61D8：卖出 12289 ETH，均价 2580；买回 12314 ETH，均价 2297；▶赚约 347 万刀◀
第二名约 78 万，有一批卖在 3000 以上
第三到五名分别约 67 万、43 万、29 万
前十名合计约 636 万刀 206 笔卖出平均比预言机高 10%，最高超过 30%。

第一名的操作很值得学：
事发后 24 分钟就进场

Aave 里早就存好了 3700 万 USDC
分 18 笔卖，每笔 300–1000 ETH，用聚合器拆单降滑点
价格一回落就开始买回还款，两个小时内基本平仓
【学到的】
CEX 出事、暂停提币的时候，链上和交易所的价差会挂很久。平时几秒钟就被搬平的价差，这次挂了一个小时。

机会在那些按交易所价格定价的地方：用 Chainlink 预言机的借贷池（Aave、Compound、Spark……），它不跟 DEX 现价。

弹药要提前放好。等你看到新闻再去充 U、开仓，窗口早没了。
窗口很短，DEX 越卖越便宜，能赚多少看深度和速度。05:30 以后价差只剩 3%–5%。
Aave 很快冻结了主网 V3 市场，晚进场的连借都借不到。
【风险】

借 ETH 的仓位怕 ETH 继续往上冲，健康度会掉，所以大户都分批做，不会一把梭

没买回的 ETH 负债还挂着，价格回升就会回吐利润
链上拥堵时 gas 很贵，小资金可能做不划算
下一次黑天鹅来的时候，先想清楚自己的"出 ETH 窗口"在哪里。
（数据：链上逐笔统计，按 ETH 2280 计价，未扣 gas。不构成投资建议。）

text:
가상의 대학교 세계관을 만들어 대박 난 성인 AI 인스타 계정.

계정 이름은 ‘한강대학교’.

실제로 존재하지 않는 가상의 대학교를 만들어 놓고, 그 안에서 벌어지는 대학생들의 이야기를 CCTV 영상처럼 보여주는 계정임.

근데 이게 존나 영리한 게,

1. 콘텐츠 자체가 인간의 호기심과 상상력을 자극함. 복도, 동아리방, 청소도구실 등에서 벌어지는 아슬아슬한 상황을 CCTV로 엿보는 듯한 구도임. 당연히 전부 AI로 제작한 영상.

2. 트래픽은 그냥 미쳤음. 팔로워 1.7만 명에 릴스 조회수는 기본 수백만. 1,285만, 1,122만, 889만 조회수 영상까지 있음. 팔로워 대비 조회수가 말도 안 되는 수준임 ㄷㄷ.

3. 수익화 구조도 영리함. 이렇게 모은 트래픽을 프로필의 탑툰 AI 캐릭터 채팅 서비스로 연결함. 거기에 인스타 구독 기능까지 활용해서 구독자 전용 콘텐츠도 판매하는 구조. 광고 제휴 수익과 구독 수익을 동시에 노리는 셈임.

4. 댓글 반응은 웃긴게 AI 콘텐츠라고 명시돼 있는데도 실제 촬영 영상처럼 받아들이는 사람들이 보임. 그만큼 CCTV 특유의 구도와 연출이 현실감을 만들어낸다는 이야기.

5. 심지어 조회수만 뽑고 끝나는 것도 아님. 성인 콘텐츠에 관심 있는 시청자를 모아서 관련 AI 채팅 서비스와 유료 구독으로 연결함.

Ai와 성인시장의 조합은 갈수록 커질것 같음.
상상력이 실사화 되는 시대니까

Binance has begun recovering affected assets for users and continues to work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace, freeze and recover additional funds.

The company has already publicly committed to cover losses through company funds in the prior announcement.

Binance has already reserved over $6.34B of company funds to cover this incident. $5B of these funds are already held in the exact token assets that were impacted. We are completing the purchase of the remaining amount by buying token assets through market channels and OTC channels. We are doing this to match the format of the remaining token assets and address any asset shortfalls. This step can take longer because some tokens may have low liquidity and OTC settlement also takes time. We will share more progress as soon as we can. 

These figures do not include frozen or protected assets, which remain subject to ongoing recovery and verification. Currently, $3bn has been frozen, with thanks to our industry partners. We are working with partners and law enforcement to recover the frozen assets.We will continue to use company resources to cover confirmed shortfall and will provide further verified updates as recovery efforts progress. Ultimately, all user funds will be verified publicly through our Proof of Reserves.  

We will weather this storm. Thank you for the support.

text:
英特尔其实我追踪了很久。这财报真的有点失望。 $INTC 

2年内，可以删自选了。

财报板块搞得非常复杂，又是什么 DCAI ，又是 CCPG 的。但实际上，英特尔的业务结构，是一个跷跷板。

一头是 AI 发展带来的收入增长，另一端是 AI 发展影响的传统基本面业务。

大跌的原因之一，就是存储涨价，造成 PC 业务承压了，影响了基本业务。

第四季度收入预计环比下降超过20%。而且 27年 PC 出货量仍然预计下降约10%，这个压力，要持续到 28年，管理层的口径还不是缓解，而是有变化。

我直接好家伙了。

要是 AI 收入增长那边，能覆盖掉影响的业务基本面也行，但实际并没有。

核心的 DCAI 业务看似增长很快，实际占比81%的 CPU 出货量只增加10%。增长主要是涨价带来的。

而且，如果均价增速正常化，27年需要更强的出货量增长，来保持收入增速。

代工业务还是血亏，且看不到其他大型外部客户。

被台积电和三星压得死死的。

关键，管理层在电话会上说，27年是集中投资期，需要同时扩大Intel 3、18A生产，并为 28年的 14A 投产准备设备。

公司很可能，在 27年无法实现正自由现金流。

现在看，CPU 胜负已分了。 AMD 和英伟达是赢家，至于 ARM，看接下来的财报了。

We've been made aware, through responsible disclosure, of a single hardware implant in a Trezor Safe 5 device bought from the reseller CryptoBilis in August 2026.

No CryptoBilis buyer has reported a loss of funds to us.

IMPORTANT: If you bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis from March 2026 onwards, we know this is unsettling. Here’s what to do:

Already using it?

Move your funds to a newly created wallet with a new seed as soon as possible. Do not reuse the old seed in any wallet, hardware or software.  If you don’t have another secure hardware wallet available, we recommend temporarily migrating your funds to a software wallet or an exchange you are familiar with.  

Not set up yet? Don’t set it up, and never enter your existing wallet backup on it.

We haven’t received the device to confirm this report, but based on the customer’s description, we’re treating it as credible and sharing it now so customers who purchased a Trezor via CryptoBilis can secure their funds as a precaution. Our security team will examine the device as soon as it arrives.

On October 9, 2026, we removed CryptoBilis as a reseller following reports of tampered Ledger devices sold through it. Since then, we have been inspecting Trezor devices that customers bought from CryptoBilis and have found no signs of tampering on any of the four devices we’ve received so far.

NEVER share your wallet backup (recovery phrase) with anyone. Trezor Support will never ask for it.
If you are affected by this incident, please keep your CryptoBilis device and contact Support to receive a new Trezor hardware wallet: https://t.co/5EasOVDDQh

We're investigating and will post updates here as soon as we know more.  Thank you to the customer who reported this through our responsible disclosure program, and to @SEAL_911 for working alongside our teams on the response. Reports and engagement like this help us protect everyone else.

For more information, visit our blog: https://t.co/2LmFV8L2oe

text:
Reading the reconstructed bytecode of the Binance EIP-7702 sweeper (`0x63e8...6fae`) is wild.

This wasn't a generic drainer. It was custom-engineered for Binance 14's architecture:

- Leaves exactly 1 ether behind (`bal - 1 ether`) when sweeping ETH so Binance's automated hot wallet queue wouldn't error on gas and trip alarms.
- Uses raw `staticcall` + `continue` loops with custom error codes (`SweepItemFailed`) so one bricked or blacklisted ERC-20 wouldn't revert the $6B batch.
- Includes a custom `callExecute` function to impersonate Binance 14 as controller of an external vault holding $823M in USDC.

They leave a comment: "robberies could be prevented if getaway cars were slower."

You can't fully blame EIP-7702, but it sped up the attack. Without 7702, draining 64 tokens plus an external $823M vault from a live exchange hot wallet meant fighting moving nonces across 70+ transactions. Defense systems would've killed it after tx #3.

With 7702, Lazarus sprayed 50 consecutive nonces in one type-4 payload, turned an EOA into a custom proxy, and atomically swept billions in a single block.

Ethereum core devs built the ultimate getaway car. Surgical state-sponsored engineering.

This could be etched onchain:
`if (bal > 1 ether) { https://t.co/ou2j9VqGvv{value: bal - 1 ether}(""); }`
author: 0xShual
quoted_text:
The Binance $5.6B drain is a masterclass in modern EVM exploitation.

It wasn't a complex logic bug. It was an EIP-7702 delegation hijack:

1. Setup: Attacker funds 0x7c86 via Tornado Cash, deploys a sweep contract (0x63e8), and runs three live dry-runs on external wallets.
2. Execution: Attacker submits an EIP-7702 batch with 50 pre-signed authorizations (nonce n to n+49) to hit Binance 14's moving nonce window.
3. One authorization hits. Instantly, Binance 14 (an EOA) is reprogrammed to run the attacker's contract bytecode.
4. Execution looks totally organic: Binance 14 sweeps itself clean. Internal threshold alerts don't trigger because, from the nodes' perspective, the hot wallet is just executing its own transaction.
5. Binance 16 immediately auto-refills 28,000 ETH due to automated treasury rebalance scripts, feeding the exploit loop.

The cold truth: you cannot forge an EIP-7702 delegation list.
For this to execute, the attacker already held the raw private key or unconstrained signing access to Binance 14's HSM/KMS.

But hey, 5.64 billion drained across ETH, BTC, and Tron. 2.54 billion frozen by Tether, Circle, Ripple, and World Liberty within hours.

Code is law until the stablecoin admin keys log in.

Binance got bailed out by the very centralized choke points the cypherpunks warned you about.

Hardware wallets leak your home address.
Centralized exchanges leak the keys to the kingdom.

Self-custody on native, non-delegated chains remains the only honest baseline.

At least you know what to avoid.

quoted_text:
昨晚跟168X的交流要点，上一次8月底https://t.co/MrasWYxXvC参与168X聊到：美股临近中期选举市场动荡加大，然后大饼和加密到10月因为流动性收紧会回踩。梳理下这次聊的要点：
1、美国经济正在进入由AI基建驱动的新基建周期，这种大基建趋势下名义GDP的增速会很好；

2、中东局势中期选举后可能会是一个时间窗口，如果能解决油价回落宏观环境压力会减少很多；
但如果一直不能解决油价持续在高位，通胀持续强势那么联储不仅12月会加息，明年也可能会加，如果原来预期 2 次，最后变成 3 次、4 次甚至更久，则整个估值体系都会重新定价、市场会扛不住。

3、ARR这个指标需要抛后，Anthropic上市后就要看真实的季度营收、年度营收了。大云平台已经是AI Operating System：企业会从结果和成本考虑，切换不同的模型。

4、大型科技公司真正大规模提高 CapEx，是从 2025 年三季度左右开始的，所以今天 Microsoft、Google Cloud 增长出来的 Revenue，很多对应的其实是一年前甚至更早花出去的钱。去年下半年开始加速建设的 Capacity，现在才进入投产期，而过去几个季度所有云厂商一直在讲同一句话：Demand > Supply，算力不够。如果需求还在增长，而且你新上线多少 Capacity 都能马上被吃掉，那未来几个季度 Revenue 自然会继续加速。所以我觉得AI商业化现在不是见顶，而是才刚开始加速。

5、要看Cloud Revenue Growth 何时开始超过 CapEx Growth
不能永远只看 Revenue，第二阶段要看 ROIC。2026 年是 CapEx 爆发的一年。去年几千亿美元，今年接近翻倍，这种 CapEx Growth 不可能每年都 100%。
真正漂亮的拐点是什么？就是未来 CapEx Growth 开始自然下降，但 AI Revenue Growth 还继续加速、意味着开始算的过账来。

所以接下来几个季度，最想看的就是：Revenue Growth、CapEx Growth、Depreciation Life、FCF，这几个东西开始怎么收敛。

6、AI主线已经迁移：Memory → Optical / Software → Agent / AI for Science/应用

不要形成“AI = Semiconductor = Memory”的定式思维，一说AI就是半导体、一说半导体就是存储。

每一阶段 AI 的主线都会迁移。今年一季度、二季度，Memory 是最强的；到 8、9 月以后，Optical 开始变强，同时一批之前被砸得很惨的软件、SaaS 也开始走出来。为什么？因为模型商品化、Token Price 下来以后，受益的不只上游 硬件。Token 越便宜，Deployment 越容易，Cloud、Software、Enterprise Integration、Agent 反而会越来越受益。再下一阶段可能就是 AI for Science、Bio、更广泛的应用层。

所以趋势投资真正要做的，不是死守原来的 Winner，而是不断识别：下一层利润池正在往哪里迁移。Semi 也不是死了，只是像上半年那种所有东西直线上冲的阶段，短期可能过去了。

7、真正需要让 AI Thesis 转空的信号，不是 Semi 再跌 20%，而是 AI商业化（云厂商业绩增速）开始降速、当下是出于加速的阶段。这才是未来的市场的真正的大风险，

而另一个问题则是伊朗问题迟迟得不到解决，油价高位、通胀向上趋势被强化、联储不得不多次加息而非两次。

8、高收益率时代不再普涨：以后市场只奖励真实 Cash Flow。
当 Bond Yield 高以后，股票自然也要给更高的 Risk Premium，这就是为什么现在市场越来越挑剔。Google Cloud很好，Search、FCF 出现问题，市场照样先卖。所以之后选股票一定要分清楚：哪些公司只是 Narrative，哪些公司的业务已经真正兑现，Revenue 是真的、Cash Flow 是真的，而且未来 2、3 年增长空间还能算出来。

大公司如果因为短期逆风被杀估值，我反而觉得是好事，因为它给你重新上车的价格。高利率不是所有股票不能涨，而是市场会越来越“优中选优”。

9、中期选举后很多不确定性会减弱如国会的归属，再看伊朗问题是不是能解决，谨防Anthropic上市路演开始后的吸血。

昨天有一点现在看是不对的“昨天聊到如果亚马逊的财报还不错、市场有一波能到anthropic路演前、今年亚马逊财报云业务很好但是广告放缓、资本开支远超预期、也是加重了市场担忧”可能这种担忧要到中期选举之后再看了。

多谢@168MrZ

text:
Decades ago, people tried to formally verify code. Essentially, you prove that the code is correct using math. It was an approach promoted by people like Dijkstra, who observed that “program testing can be used to show the presence of bugs, but never to show their absence” (1970).

It did not work. It was too difficult.

You can do it for a function, maybe a small piece of code… but for anything useful, it was just too much work, and the result was too weak. Classic examples include the seL4 microkernel, about 8,700 lines of C requiring ~200,000 lines of Isabelle proof and roughly 20 person-years of verification effort.

But times are changing.

So it appears that we can formally verify code these days. Or, at least, there is now a ton of startups and academic initiatives that say it is possible and maybe practical.
Take your C code, have your AI prove that it is a correct implementation of the specification. Among other things, it would prove that the code is correct with respect to memory usage, but that’s the least of what it could do.

The most obvious application is cryptography and anything that must be unbreakable. Have your AI prove that the system cannot be hacked.

You should not get too excited. These will remain mathematical models. They have to make assumptions all over.

But I am pretty excited about what this could enable. I'd love to have more formal analysis of my code. In fact, I have a few projects in mind right now, to formally verify heuristics that I have been using.

Recent examples of startups:

•&Truth (launched Oct 2026, ~$70M seed): Building a “universal verification machine” for any language.
•Harmonic (Aristotle): Announced support (late Oct 2026) for formal verification of C software and Verilog hardware.

I know ‘Vote Restore, Get Labour’ irritates some people so let me explain why I say it.

Because it’s the truth.

Voting Restore will hand this country to the Left.

I am angrier than you with the state of the country, I suspect. 

But the reality is that the Right will lose the next general election if it does not consolidate.

Roughly 60% of left-wing voters tell pollsters they are voting tactically.

That’s Green or Lib Dems voting Labour not because they agree with Labour or Burnham.

But only 30% of right-wing voters are doing the same.

The Left is much more disciplined and ruthless than the Right. 

The reason Burnham and Labour are now back on 30-32% is because they are winning back left wing voters who are willing to do whatever it takes to control the country.

Greens holding their nose to vote Labour. 

Lib Dems holding their nose to do the same. 

2024 Labour voters coming home to Labour to stop the Right. 

And they are on course to do it.

All MRP polls suggest the Left is on course to win the next general election, whether by winning a majority or in coalition.

That means more migration.
More refugees.

And a system of PR to ensure the Left continue to dominate Britain going forward. 

They will give children, migrants and refugees the vote. 

They will turn a blind eye to family voting and mass postal fraud.

They will control Britain until at least the 2030s, maybe longer.

Because they are boxing clever.

Rupert Lowe will probably end up in the Lords, put there by the same Tories who just put him on a committee and who he himself says “he talks to all the time”.

Most of the attack unfolded in just 20 minutes

WHAT WAS STOLEN:

• 18,270 $BTC
• ~200,000 $ETH

• $823M $USDC
• 233M $XRP and dozens of other tokens

WHO FROZE THE FUNDS:

• World Liberty Financial and other issuers also stepped in

Binance confirms around $3 BILLION has now been frozen, leaving approximately $3.3B not yet secured

HOW DID IT HAPPEN?

Binance's initial investigation points to a compromised engineer's laptop that may have allowed hackers to access internal systems and authorize withdrawals

On-chain researchers also identified the use of EIP-7702 wallet delegation during the attack

Blockchain security firms suspect North Korean hackers may be responsible, although Binance has not confirmed their identity

MARKET REACTION:

Bitcoin crashed toward $76K, while approximately $1.5 BILLION in leveraged positions were liquidated within 24 hours, mostly longs

Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals and promised to cover all losses through its SAFU fund and company reserves

Withdrawals are expected to resume after security checks

This attack is more than FOUR TIMES larger than the $1.46B Bybit hack in February 2025

And with billions still unsecured, the recovery effort is far from over

Coinbase（ $COIN ）2026年第三季度财报

Coinbase 的三季度财报看起来赚了不少钱，净利润达到 7.19 亿美元。但实际上其中有 7.15 亿美元来自投资用途加密资产的收益。也就是说 Coinbase 第三季度最赚钱的并不是交易，而是投资。

把加密资产和其他投资损益及相关税务影响调整以后，Coinbase 的净利润是 7,770 万美元，比去年同期下降了 82%。当季总营收为 12.16 亿美元，同比下降 35%，其中交易收入下降 44%，到 5.90 亿美元。

这也能从交易量上看出来，Coinbase 三季度的加密现货成交量为 1,345 亿美元，比去年同期的 2,943 亿美元下降了一半多。虽然公司披露的加密交易量市场份额从去年同期的 5.6% 提升到 10.7%，但在整个市场交易活跃度下降的情况下份额增加也没能让交易收入同比增长。

不过 Coinbase 的收入来源确实在变得更多了，其中三季度订阅和服务收入达到 5.70 亿美元，占净营收的 49%，稳定币收入为 3.07 亿美元，环比增长 5%。Coinbase 产品中的 USDC 平均余额也从上季度的 200 亿美元增长到 220 亿美元。

不过虽然 USDC 余额增加了，但 USDC 整体平均市值从上季度的 770 亿美元降到了 730 亿美元。

另外 Coinbase 预测市场的季度收入已经达到超过 2 亿美元的年化水平。日均交易用户环比增长超过 60%，预测市场增长也带来了交易费用的增加。

衍生品方面 Coinbase 第三季度加密衍生品名义成交量为 9,630 亿美元，同比增长约 14%，但环比下降约 6%。Coinbase 国际交易所与 Deribit 的整合已于 10 月完成，短期交易量可能因用户适应而波动。

截至 9 月底，Coinbase 披露公司现金及现金等价物 86.04 亿美元，低于去年底的 112.85 亿美元。其中包括约 24.15 亿美元支付型稳定币。长期债务约 59.48 亿美元，短期借款约 7.49 亿美元。公司称仍有约 20 亿美元回购授权额度，但尚未披露会在什么时候启动回购。

总的来说，财报体现出 Coinbase 市场份额确实在增长，但加密货币市场的低迷带来了交易的下降，收入和经营利润仍在下滑。USDC 和预测市场虽然能带来新增收益，但还不足以弥补交易业务的下降。

text:
One fix stopped a key-registration bug—and quietly locked every new user out.

During Zealynx’s YadaCoin bridge audit, we found the upgraded registry always reverted when a new user registered an inception key.

`validateTransaction()` tried to hash an empty confirming key before checking whether the registration was a key pair. The 64-byte length check then failed, blocking onboarding after the upgrade.

YadaCoin moved that computation inside the key-pair branch. Zealynx verified the Critical fix before mainnet.

text:
卧槽，Jack的Block团队发现了一个可以使比特币节点崩溃的漏洞😲😲😲

Jack 旗下 Block 的比特币开发团队 Spiral，最近用自研 AI 工具 Project Loupe，真的在 Bitcoin Core 里挖出了一个安全漏洞（CVE-2026-117350）。

黑客只要连接到运行 Windows、macOS 或 BSD 的比特币节点，就可能利用特殊 TCP 数据绕过内存限制，让节点内存不断膨胀，最终直接崩溃。

Linux 节点不受这个漏洞影响。

10 月 23 日 AI 发现漏洞，开发者当天验证，26 日完成代码修复，27—28 日陆续发布修复版本，28 日正式公开披露。

从发现到修复版本全部发布，只用了 5 天。

Bitcoin Core 甚至专门为 AI 改了安全规则：

过去部分中高危漏洞可能保密一年左右，现在只要属于 AI 容易发现的漏洞，就尽快修复、公开，不再长期保密。

因为黑客同样能用 AI 扫代码，藏着漏洞不修只会让风险持续存在。

quoted_text:
The recent security incidents involving Bybit, Bitget, and now Binance should serve as a wake-up call for every leader in the crypto industry.

Security should never be an area of commercial competition. It is a shared responsibility to protect our customers and the entire industry.

Over the past decade, major crypto exchanges have made significant progress in protecting private keys. We have seen relatively few incidents involving direct private key compromises in recent years. So far, we have not seen conclusive evidence that Binance’s hot wallet private key was leaked. The greater concern may lie in vulnerabilities in access controls and wallet management systems.

Companies that have never experienced a major security incident should not assume they are inherently safer or immune to attacks.

At OKX, we have built multiple layers of sophisticated security protection and maintained a strong security track record over the past decade. But we also recognize that no system is absolutely secure. We must remain humble, vigilant, and constantly challenge our own security assumptions.

A major security breach at any exchange undermines trust in the entire crypto industry, ultimately hurting every company and every customer.

I believe CEOs across the industry need to come together, just as we did during the Bitcoin fork crisis in 2017, to establish stronger industry-wide security standards and coordinated response mechanisms.

For example, transfers and settlements between verified exchanges could be processed in real time, while large withdrawals to unknown or unverified addresses, as well as transactions granting smart contract permissions, should be subject to additional verification and appropriate security delays.

Crucially, these safeguards should be enforced at the cryptographic signing layer, rather than relying solely on application-level controls. Even if an attacker compromises an exchange’s wallet management system, they should not be able to bypass these fundamental security restrictions.

We should also establish industry-wide mechanisms for real-time security incident notifications, coordinated monitoring of suspicious funds, and rapid responses to potential attacks. Exchanges, stablecoin issuers, and other major industry participants should work together to enable the rapid, lawful temporary freezing of suspected stolen assets when necessary.

We should also work together to accelerate the industry’s transition to quantum-resistant cryptography and strengthen our defenses against emerging AI-powered security threats. These are long-term challenges that no single company can solve alone, and they require coordinated research, shared standards, and collective action across the industry.

Security is everyone’s responsibility. No company can protect the future of crypto alone.

text:
My perspective on yesterday's events on Polymarket:

Yesterday, like many other users (@CarOnPolymarket , @denizz_poly  @Tenebrus87 , @cryptobasenji ) , I fell victim to an unauthorized attack attempt. The attackers sold positions worth approximately 100k USD and attempted to drain the funds. Since I was “live” at the time of the attack, I was able to prevent the outflow to the extent that I could transfer 97k USD internally to an alternative Polymarket account I use, thereby removing my funds from the attacker’s reach. Thanks to this, I was fortunate that at least no external outflow damage occurred.

Now let’s turn to the actual problem: The attackers liquidated most of my positions—in both liquid and illiquid markets. This resulted in significant losses due to slippage, sales below market value, and lost profits.

Polymarket’s official statement on this matter is as follows: “As a goodwill gesture, we’re also covering losses on positions affected while trading was paused, and positions taken during the attack. We’ll share how that works separately.”

Even though the team acted quickly given the circumstances, several questions arise regarding the refund process for positions that were liquidated against our will:

- Is Polymarket considering restoring positions that were sold without authorization during the incident?

- Should affected users wait for the official recovery plan instead of buying back the positions themselves?

- When can we expect details on the compensation plan for position losses?

-At what value will positions be reimbursed? -> Cost basis, yesterday’s market value, or settled as a profit.

The last point in particular is a crucial factor in deciding whether I should repurchase the affected positions (possibly at a higher market price) or wait for further action from the team. In particular, some of my positions related to Tuesday’s midterm elections were precisely matched or served as hedge positions for existing positions held via third-party providers. For these positions, fluctuations in the cost basis in the range of 1–2 cents already determine whether my position is profitable or not.

Apart from that, in liquid markets with a thin order book, it’s not even possible to buy back the shares.

I very much hope that Polymarket (@shayne_coplan  @kea1on @SuhailKakar )will promptly publish an official statement outlining a transparent and fair resolution and proactively reach out to affected users.

text:
Earlier today, the attacker behind the recent @binance  exploit, apparently in error, sent approximately 8.0M NEWT directly to the NEWT token contract address (0xd0ec028a3d21533fdd200838f39c85b03679285d), along with 17 other tokens: $ANIME, ethereum:0x8290333cef9e6d528dd5618fb97a76f268f3edd4, $ARPA, $BARD, $CELR, ethereum:0x3597bfd533a99c9aa083587b074434e61eb0a258, ethereum:0x0f81001ef0a83ecce5ccebf63eb302c70a39a654, $FTT, $GLM, $HIGH, $HOT, $KNC, $LQTY, $RARE, ethereum:0x259338656198ec7a76c729514d3cb45dfbf768a1, $SIGN and $WOO. These tokens are worth roughly $3.5 million at current prices.

To be clear, the NEWT token contract itself was not compromised.

We have reviewed the contract carefully, and unfortunately these tokens cannot be recovered. The NEWT token contract was built to be immutable: it has no owner or admin, all admin rights were renounced onchain in 2025, and upgrades are permanently disabled. That design exists to protect holders, so that no one, including the Foundation, can ever move or alter their tokens. These safeguards mean there is no way for anyone to retrieve tokens sent to the contract itself.

These tokens are now permanently locked. They are out of the attacker’s control and can never be sold into the market.

We have shared our findings with Binance and we will keep helping however we can.

By design, a Morpho Blue market can't protect its users: it can't freeze the market to mitigate risk, act on the interest rate curve or implement rate limiting, and it has no Umbrella junior tranche to protect deposits.

When an isolated market breaks, its lenders take 100% of the loss.

If you're a Morpho user facing an adverse event, they will just tweet and let you sink, as they did during the dozens of vault blowups that led to dire user losses. Ask anyone who was in a curator vault during Stream/Elixir.

Users won't trust an infra with real size if it doesn't care about them or support them.

That's why, even with infinite VC funding, deployed incentives, a competitor that lost its best contributors and paid partnerships, Morpho only added a pathetic +$2.15B in active loans this year.

For comparison, I did as much in one week at the Plasma launch.

text:
运营一家大模型公司最残酷的现实，是至今看不到任何能守住的竞争优势。

这段 AI on Air 精选切片摘自 Redpoint AI 栏目近期的节目，讲话人是前 a16z 合伙人、科技行业知名分析师 Benedict Evans @benedictevans。他拆解了模型公司在「没有护城河」处境下的几条出路。

▷ 与过去的平台更迭不同，AI 的边际成本不降反升，没法先做消费级应用圈来一亿用户再琢磨怎么赚钱，所以主战场只能放在企业客户身上。
▷ 经营模型公司要同时调配研究员、资金和算力，朝各个方向「赶猫」，而每四到六周就有新模型冲上排行榜第一，无论靠网络效应还是靠在模型之上搭建产品层，都看不到持久差异化的路径。
▷ 一条可行思路是把单项能力做到极致，比如 Claude 把编程做得足够好，或许已经取得领先，但每三到六个月一切又会重新洗牌，没人能松懈。

From my perspective, this should be viewed as a crime scene. And when a crime like this  occurs, the focus should be on protecting users, recovering stolen assets and holding perpetrators accountable.  While this is a terrible situation, I would note the following:

•  Many of the major crypto players moved swiftly (within minutes) to freeze some of the stolen funds. 
•  Public blockchains are easily traceable. Law enforcement and analytics firms are tracking all fund movements.
•  An event of this magnitude may focus global policy makers on efforts to address the security situation through coordinated policy action.  The threat to security is not limited to the crypto space alone.

Nou se yon peyi modès k ap devlope. Sèl sa nou vle, se pou kat teknisyen avyasyon nou yo tounen lakay yo. Epi n ap bay gang yo yon leson, gang sa yo k ap fè pèp ayisyen an soufri, ki touye moun pèp la renmen yo, k ap anpeche l viv yon lavi nòmal, lib, san laperèz.

Se prèske nou menm sèl k ap peye pou operasyon sa a. Menmsi nou resevwa yon ti èd lojistik nan men kèk lòt peyi, se ak pwòp ti kès nou n ap kouvri 90% nan depans yo.

Sa koute nou chè, men nou te aprann nan pwòp soufrans nou: jistis ak lapè pa gen pri. Nou te pase nan menm soufrans Ayiti ap travèse jodi a. text:
Physical AI is still in its infancy.

Nobody really knows what the winning stack is going to look like yet.

And that’s what makes this moment so interesting.

1. Models are becoming products.

We’re moving from research demos to APIs and real deployments. For the first time, other robotics teams can actually integrate these models into their own products.

2. Tasks are becoming workflows.

Doing one manipulation successfully is very different from completing a 30-minute or 2-hour workflow reliably.

The industry is slowly moving from “can the robot do this task?” to “can the robot actually do the job?”

3. Deployment is becoming part of training.

Teams are putting robots into the real world and discovering failure modes they never saw in the lab.

Those deployments create new data, expose edge cases and feed back into the next generation of models.

4. The data question is changing.

It’s no longer just about who can collect the most hours.

Teams are figuring out which tasks, environments, failures, interactions and types of demonstrations actually improve models.

The quality and diversity of data matter much more than the raw number of hours.

5. Evals are becoming their own category.

A robot completing something successfully once tells you very little.

Can it do it 100 times? 1,000 times? Across different objects, environments and edge cases?
Reliability is becoming the real benchmark.

6. A new infrastructure layer is being built.

Once you have thousands of hours of data and robots running in the real world, you need systems to manage the whole loop:

data → training → simulation → evaluation → deployment → feedback → retraining.

A lot of this infrastructure is being built right now.

7. Business models are still being figured out.

Model APIs, RaaS, vertically integrated robotics companies, data platforms, deployment companies, integrators…

Nobody knows yet where most of the value will ultimately accrue.

Everyone is basically learning in production.

The next 12–15 months are going to be insane.

Not necessarily because we’ll know the final winners, but because we’ll start seeing which approaches actually compound once more robots hit the real world.

A few teams I’m watching closely:

@DynaRobotics, @Ultraroboticsco, @origin_autonomy, @MeckaAI, @humynlabs, @dreamlabs_ai, @physical_int,  @SkildAI, @xdofai, @GeneralistAI, @NVIDIARobotics @Figure_robot, @1x_tech, @FoundryRobotics, @fieldai_

text:
美股下跌撞上交易所被盗危机 bitcoin:native 下一步是继续探底还是触底反弹？

先说结论：短期BTC偏空，中期不宜过度悲观。

5.8万美元已经形成阶段性周期底部，而币安被盗事件正在考验这个底部的有效性。

一、周期位置：5.8万美元是否已经见底？

BTC从5.8万美元反弹至8.7万美元，最大反弹幅度接近50%。这轮反弹不能简单定义为普通超跌修复，ETF资金、机构配置和现货承接，说明5.8万美元附近确实出现了较强买盘。

目前从8.7万美元回落至7.7万美元附近，回撤约11%，我更倾向于将其视为底部反弹后的二次调整，但周线趋势尚未完成反转，5.8万美元也不能提前认定为最终大底。

二、币安被盗：历史经验告诉我们什么？

2016年Bitfinex被盗约12万枚BTC，事件后BTC短期跌幅接近20%，交易所暂停提现，用户承担了部分损失。

2019年币安被盗7000枚BTC，损失约4100万美元，但币安通过SAFU承担损失，市场短暂调整后继续上涨。

2025年Bybit被盗约15亿美元，交易所承诺兑付，市场没有因此立即进入单边崩盘，但后续仍受到宏观环境影响。

历史说明：交易所被盗不等于BTC必然进入熊市，用户能否正常提现、损失能否覆盖、行业是否出现连锁信用风险，才是决定冲击持续时间的关键。

三、资金面：机构在买，市场却仍然在跌。

截至10月29日，美国现货BTC ETF连续四个交易日净流入，合计约4.4亿美元。

但币安BTCUSDT永续合约OI近期从约9.75万枚下降至9.56万枚，资金费率仍为正值，但明显回落。

这说明部分杠杆正在出清，机构资金也没有全面撤离，但现货买盘暂时不足以扭转短期卖压。

链上真正需要关注的是交易所BTC净流入、长期持有者持仓、稳定币交易所余额，以及黑客剩余资产的转移情况。

四、宏观面：BTC面临双重压力。

纳指科技股受到AI资本开支回报预期冲击，美联储维持利率不变，但政策仍偏谨慎，通胀和油价又限制了宽松空间。

这意味着BTC承受的不只是币安事件带来的信用风险，还有全球风险偏好下降的压力。

五、后市判断：

短期重点观察76000美元，失守后看72800美元；如果守住并重新站回80000美元，则有望挑战82000-84000美元，进一步观察87000美元压力。

我的基准判断是：短期震荡偏空，中期观察底部修复。

如果币安事件得到控制、ETF持续净流入、纳指企稳，5.8万美元成为本轮周期底部的可能性将进一步提高。

如果交易所信用风险扩散，ETF持续流出，美股继续调整，就必须防范69500美元甚至重新测试5.8万美元。

这次真正值得警惕的，不是币安被盗本身，而是它发生在BTC周期顶部之后的调整阶段，事件可能放大原有下跌趋势，也可能成为一次恐慌性洗盘。

我不会因为跌到7.7万美元就急着抄底，也不会因为一次安全事故就直接看空整个周期。

行情最终看资金，底部最终看承接，保留本金，等待市场给出确认信号，比提前猜底更重要。

text:
As someone who tends to overthink and often second-guess myself, it took me a long time to understand this: there will ALWAYS be someone with the opposite view and solid arguments against your trade.   

> You think the market’s going up? There’ll always be an account explaining from A to Z why it’s about to dump. 

> You think we gonna crash? There’ll always be a trader convinced it’s the generational bottom. 

If everyone agreed, there wouldn’t be a market.    

Easy in theory, but in practice I’ve been flip-flopped by the timeline way too many times from scrolling too much. X is still a top tool for finding alpha, but it can also make you choke your position.  

Always think in probabilities, especially when you’re obsessed with a coin and can’t stop asking yourself whether to buy, hold, or sell. If you estimate there’s a 90% chance a token dumps and it ends up flying, you were maybe wrong, but you applied the right model.    

All the PnL you stacked while the tide was on your side can vanish the second you get emotional about a trade: "I know its probably gonna dump but what if it moon without me?" => This kind of questions are destructive

author: emollick
quoted_text:
It’s almost incomprehensible how wide the distance is between someone who’s working at the frontier with AI and basically everyone else right now. 

The crazy thing is these lines are not converging, but only growing farther apart. If the curve of AI progress had leveled off, it would certainly have given most people and companies time to catch up or implement their workflows in a standardized way. The technology would have neutralized competitive advantage because everyone would be using it the same way.

But what’s happened is the opposite. The curve of AI progress is basically going vertical right now, which means if you had codified your processes 3-6 months ago you’re likely already behind again. Now imagine most companies that kicked into gear a year ago and thought that they were done. Even further behind now.

I’ve never seen a technology in my life and career that improves at this rate, which consequently means you need to upgrade your expectations at a similar rate. Our brains weren’t wired for this, and our organizational change management processes certainly weren’t either.

With any form of recursive self improvement, things just get wilder. It’s a time when you will need to be constantly reevaluating the things that didn’t work just a couple months ago to see if they now can be solved. AI native companies certainly have a strong advantage due to this right now, so now it comes down to can the bigger companies keep up. Wild times.

It's almost hard to believe, but the US has only a single factory left that makes HMX and RDX, the explosives in nearly every modern missile and bomb - an aging wwii plant in Tennessee that's massively backordered.

A few years ago, a startup called Solugen was making chemicals for the petroleum industry, when by happenstance they heard about this problem.  It turns out that the same infrastructure they'd built for other chemicals was a perfect fit to make energetics.

So, that's what they're doing now.  They can already make 1/10 of what the old US army plant makes, and in the future will make much more.  

This is the SpaceX/Anduril moment for the US military explosives market.
author: paulg
quoted_text:
In four days of the Iran war, the US and its allies fired more Tomahawks than the US builds in four years. One bottleneck is energetics production.

So we built a 100% CONUS energetics supply chain with our own capital. Our modular solution makes HMX and other advanced energetics, the explosives in nearly every US missile and munition.

The US builds about 85 Tomahawks a year. The Army's only plant making the explosives inside them is 84 years old, and its $1B upgrade has slipped from 2025 to 2029 or later. That plant is Holston, in Tennessee. It makes about 3% of what it made in 1944, and buyers wait one to two years for its explosives.

Holston makes its chemicals and its explosives on one site, so every expansion means building both plants there. A plant like that takes billions of dollars and about a decade to build. Permitting this in the US is a nightmare, because you’re taking on the risk of a chemical plant and an explosives plant at once. What could possibly go wrong.

We separated the two. Terraforge 1, Solugen’s Houston plant, is tied into Houston's petrochemical infrastructure and makes inert precursors: white powders about as flammable as sugar. They can ship via FedEx or UPS, and sit in an ordinary warehouse. Discreet.

Odin Energetics, our joint venture with Kraken Kinetics, turns them into explosives in shipping container reactors called Nitroforges. It took us six months to build the first one, and they can be set up where the weapons are needed. On-demand energetics. That means no stockpiles or concentrated first-strike targets. Kraken builds the warheads, so every step from chemical to warhead happens in the US. Together we stood up the entire chain from raw chemical to finished warhead.

Odin can already make close to a tenth of what Holston makes in a year. To make more, we’re building several factories at the same time.

Binance has begun recovering affected assets for users and continues to work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace, freeze and recover additional funds.

The company has already publicly committed to cover losses through company funds in the prior announcement.

Binance has already reserved over $6.34B of company funds to cover this incident. $5B of these funds are already held in the exact token assets that were impacted. We are completing the purchase of the remaining amount by buying token assets through market channels and OTC channels. We are doing this to match the format of the remaining token assets and address any asset shortfalls. This step can take longer because some tokens may have low liquidity and OTC settlement also takes time. We will share more progress as soon as we can. 

These figures do not include frozen or protected assets, which remain subject to ongoing recovery and verification. Currently, $3bn has been frozen, with thanks to our industry partners. We are working with partners and law enforcement to recover the frozen assets.We will continue to use company resources to cover confirmed shortfall and will provide further verified updates as recovery efforts progress. 而那些在所有人都在浮躁捞金时，反常识死磕硬核产品力的人，时间终究会把整座江山还给他们。

他们干成了三件几乎逆着全行业共识走的“重体力活”：
第一，当大家都在抢着造假数据、发空气币拉盘时，他们把几百名顶级工程师关在小黑屋里，死磕业内第一套“统一交易账户（Portfolio Margin）”。

把跨币种保证金、现货衍生品对冲的底层数学模型全部打通，硬生生把一家交易所的底层风控，做成了连极端黑天鹅行情都击不穿的金融级装甲车。

第二，当所有 CEX（中心化平台）都在拼命筑高围墙、想把用户的私钥和资产死死锁在自己服务器里时，他们却带头砸重金去革自己的命：
做自托管的 OKX Web3 钱包。

不仅开源、不仅把资产控制权双手奉还给用户，甚至把几百条公链的复杂操作、铭文索引、DEX 聚合，打磨成了全行业体验最丝滑的“链上瑞士军刀”。

别人以为他们在自掘坟墓，结果他们直接靠产品力把 Web3 钱包做成了全网十数倍于传统交易所的超级流量总闸门。

第三，在 FTX 轰然崩塌、全行业遭遇信任雪崩的那一年，他们没有找公关发通稿，而是第一个把 100%+ 默克尔树储备证明（PoR）常态化。

每月按时向全世界公开所有链上资产储备，哪怕被显微镜逐行审查也不退缩，硬生生用最笨拙但也最硬核的代码透明度，把破碎的行业信任一寸一寸拼接了回来。

很多人做商业喜欢走捷径，迷信资本运作和流量奇迹。
但 OKX 用十年逆袭证明了一件极度朴素的事：
在充满投机和欺骗的沼泽里，最锋利的武器从来不是舌灿莲花的叙事，
而是顶住所有冷眼与周期阵痛，把一行行代码、一套套风控、一张张底牌，彻底焊进用户心智里的纯粹硬实力。

text:
Day 8 of 30.

The writer at 2am already knows something in the book is broken. They aren't asking whether it's good. They're asking where.

Yesterday I asked what a writer in deadline panic needs to see before they close the tab. The replies came in.

@AYZwgmi: "the panic user needs the break shown instantly, no landing page no pitch, just 'here's where chapter 9 breaks' in the first screen"

@boardyai replied in the thread: "catch the thing they already know is broken"

That second line changed how I read the question. The writer can feel that chapter 9 doesn't match chapter 2. They just can't find the spot, and there's no time to reread the whole manuscript to find it.

So the first screen can't be a pitch, a feature list, or a signup. It has to be the answer: here is where the book doesn't hold together.

Everything I've written so far, the emails and the site copy, asks for trust first and shows something later. The panic writer won't wait for that.

@boardyai also said: "the 2am reader won't lie to you." On a quiet week people tell you a tool sounds interesting. At 2am they either find the break or they close the tab.

Nothing is built yet. So the question is smaller again. How little does the writer have to hand over before @Creader_io shows them where the book breaks?

1,500 cold emails, about 10 replies. Still no one paying. 22 days left.

author: otterpal24
quoted_text:
RAG 又杀回来了。

最近 Agent Memory 越做越复杂，但这篇《Memory Tax》发现了一个挺尴尬的结果：

很多专门设计的 Memory 系统，最后还不如直接对 raw history 做 RAG，而且成本更高。

作者把 Memory 的价值拆成两部分：

Memory Benefit：RAG 答错，但 Memory 答对的问题。

Memory Tax：RAG 本来能答对，经过 Memory 处理后反而答错的问题。

问题就出在「整理记忆」这一步。

历史被摘要、重写和结构化以后，一些细节会直接丢失；另一些虽然还在，却变得更难检索。

比如在 LongMemEval 上，Qwen3.6-27B 用两轮 RAG 能做到 81.4%，GPT-5.6 Luna 达到 90%，都高于对应的复杂 Memory 方案。

一个简单的修补反而很有效：

Memory 继续用，但同时保留 raw history 的检索通道，再把两边结果一起 rerank。

这篇工作也给我们做了一个提醒，给 Agent 加 Memory 之前，最好先拿最简单的 raw-history RAG 做个 baseline。

有时候，真正昂贵的并不是「没记住」，而是过早把原始信息总结掉了。

text:
The most important book right now for understanding company building in the age of AI is about an agent... a hollywood one... Ari Emanuel's book ('roll the calls') -- there are TWO key lessons from it (one simple, one a bit more nuanced but even more important...)

The two:

First - the easy but important point... it is all sales right now as software commodifies, and the real lesson of first half of the book is simple -- as software commodifies and everything is just sales, if you get a 'no' call the next day... over and over and over... be relentless and keep asking til you get the answer you want.  This mentality has historically not been in software / tech CEO DNA, but as the leverage of being 'unique genius' gets destroyed by arms-dealing AI / commodification of expertise (and certainly software) -- the winners are storytellers and salespeople.

Second - the more intellectual but even more important point - WHAT AGENTING REALLY IS?  Why does anyone pay an agent... for trust / the relationship.  What do agents do?  Whatever the clients need / everything - not one thing.  Why this matters? it totally changes business building.  In a world where tech is 'hard' being a leader is figuring something out about the universe, building an advantage around that competency, and doubling down over and over on your 'advantage' in providing something specific.  No more... whether for consumers or for companies... 

if you are a 'business' in an agentic world, your asset it TRUST of your client, and you do as much for them as you can / anything (also send them random gifts).  Your job is to get in the door, become trusted, and then pick up more and more business doing whatever the customer needs.  This means the mission is SERVICE not PRODUCT or MISSION.  The asset is the 'relationship' ... and the winners do everything they can for their clients.

If you are building a modern business right now - this reality changes everything from how tech companies were built over the last 20 years or so... mission is less important, top-down vision is less important, instead what matters is sales, clients, and being flexible with 'free to develop' software and services to SOLVE problems for your actual specific customers.

It this GOOD for most (startup) business... probably not.  

Agents get fired all the time, there is less enterprise value in what they build, etc... also per Ari's book, in the agenting world, scale is everything -- but from a technological deterministic perspecitve... this is where we are going, and founders that understand that (relenteless sales, how do i get in the door with something and build trust, and then what I 'do' is everything ... will be the RELATIVE winners)...

text:
币安被盗几十亿美金，这还不算黑天鹅？

更离谱的是，市场居然没怎么跌！

按以前币圈的尿性，这种级别的事件，怎么也得来一场血洗吧？

但仔细想想，其实有几个原因。

首先，被盗几十亿，不代表几十亿直接砸盘。

部分资产被冻结，剩下的也不可能瞬间全部套现。真正影响币价的是实际抛压，而不是被盗金额。

其次，币安敢不敢兜底，比被盗多少更重要。

市场最怕的不是黑客，而是交易所赔不起，用户疯狂挤兑，最后引发连环爆雷。

再一个，币安和当年的FTX不是一回事。

FTX是内部资金出了大问题，这次如果确实属于外部攻击，而且币安有能力承担损失，那市场自然不会完全按照FTX暴雷的剧本走。

还有一点，市场可能早就没那么脆弱了。

消息出来，该跑的跑了，该恐慌的也恐慌了。如果后续没有持续卖盘，价格自然不一定继续跌。

但也别急着庆祝。

现在没跌，不代表后面不会跌。真正需要盯的是用户有没有大规模提币、平台能不能正常兑付、剩余被盗资产会不会集中抛售。

说到底，黑天鹅负责制造恐慌，真正决定跌幅的，是恐慌能不能演变成连锁反应。

不过我有个疑问：

以前一个交易所暴雷，整个币圈都得陪葬。

现在几十亿美金的事，市场都懒得多跌几个点。

到底是币圈越来越成熟了，还是韭菜已经被割得没有恐慌情绪了？

quoted_text:
So Binance-linked MMs have allegedly been trying to break Bitcoin below 80k for over a week now.

And they haven’t managed to push it down significantly.

Why?

Because massive whales have been accumulating billions worth of $BTC throughout this entire period.

Now here’s where things get very interesting.

I believe the last straw for Binance was $HYPE suddenly attracting legitimate institutional interest and attention.

We’re talking about a roughly $4B increase in market cap within just 16 hours, starting from around $20B.

Do the maths.

20B + 20% in a single day.

And all of this while Bitcoin refused to break down significantly.

So in my view, Binance had two problems on its hands.

Bitcoin refusing to break below 80k.

And HYPE suddenly attracting dangerous amounts of attention.

What followed?

A swift market rug under the cover of an alleged hack. To cuck momentum.

And this is where things get even stranger.

A hack that was very conveniently contained by USDC and Tether.

Maybe a tad TOO quickly for my taste.

I’ve witnessed countless hacks in this space since 2018, and something about this one feels extremely odd.

It’s not how North Korean hackers usually operate either.

They typically manage to move a significant chunk of the stolen funds before anyone can intervene.

Yet this time, almost the entire $2B was reportedly frozen within a remarkably short period.

Interesting, isn’t it?

Given the reach of international law enforcement, I struggle to imagine many actors capable of pulling off something of this scale and escaping the consequences, apart from groups operating beyond that reach, such as Lazarus.

And if you think the official narrative automatically tells the whole story, that’s on you.

In my opinion, Binance is doing more harm to this industry than good.

And I believe much of that harm is deliberate.

First 10/10.

Now this.

Market manipulation at its finest, if my suspicions are correct.

SHUT YOUR MOTHERF*CKING EXCHANGE DOWN AND REMOVE YOUR CLAWS FROM THIS SPACE.

I’m counting the days until the Trump administration is gone, because I believe the scrutiny surrounding these players will intensify significantly.

And if wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the consequences.

Stay safe out there.

Sincerely yours,

Skully

text:
Fed holds with two hike dissents; Alphabet slides, Microsoft beats

The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% on Oct 28 in a 10-2 vote; Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack dissented for a 25bp hike. December-hike pricing rose to roughly 78-85%, but the immediate market read was milder than the vote: the 10-year eased back to about 5.00% after touching about 5.04%, the 2-year fell to about 4.69%, and the dollar index slipped to 102.17 after Warsh gave no forward guidance. Megacap earnings split the tape. Alphabet missed on EPS ($2.12 vs ~$3.02) and posted free cash flow of about -$9.1B, falling about 10% premarket. Microsoft beat with Azure +48% and guided Azure to 49-50%. ServiceNow (~-18%) and Fortinet (up to -25%) added to software damage, leaving Nasdaq 100 futures about 1% lower while Dow futures rose about 0.6%. In Asia, Samsung fell 4.1% despite a record ₩107tn operating profit, pulling the Kospi down 1.24%, while SK hynix and the Nikkei (+1.1%) rose. Oil eased about 1% on a reported Vance letter to Iran, while US officials told allies to prepare for possible post-midterm strikes and refiners (Phillips 66, Shell, TotalEnergies) posted record margins. Crypto stayed heavy, with BTC near $80k and ETH on course for its worst October since 2018 as spot ETH ETFs logged a third straight outflow day.
