text: 考古
author: bitcoin2themars
quoted_text:
当年交易所FTX暴雷之前，老板SBF曾经找人给马斯克传话，说自己愿意掏50亿美元入伙推特，让马斯克跟他见一面，一小时就能谈妥。

马斯克反问：SBF现在真的还能拿出来30亿现金吗？

结果半年后，FTX就破产了，SBF被判了25年😂

马斯克还补刀说，当时SBF触发了他的扯淡雷达，他压根不信这家伙真有这么多钱😂

2022年4月，马斯克要花440亿美元买下推特，正在拉人一起出钱。
这时有人来传话，说加密货币交易所FTX的创始人SBF想给他投10到50亿美金，还愿意帮推特搬到区块链上。
SBF当时30岁，身家240亿美元，他明天就能飞过来跟马斯克见一面，只要一小时，马斯克就能拿到50亿。

马斯克一脸懵逼地发了两个问号，然后又问：“他真拿得出30亿现金吗？"
传话人说，那当然了，SBF是超级天才，就是马斯克喜欢的那一款😂
 
不过马斯克对此不感冒，因为他早就琢磨过，推特能不能建在区块链上，结论是不行，太慢了，扛不住这么多人同时发帖。
而且他很害怕这小子跟自己没完没了的聊区块链。

十来天后，SBF亲自发来消息，说对马斯克的推特计划特别兴奋，自己手里还有1亿美元推特股票，想转成新推特的股份。
马斯克只是非常冷淡的回应了一句：”欢迎转股。"

后来SBF又打来电话了。
马斯克以为他要问收购的事，没想到他的嘴跟机关枪一样，飞快讲个不停，内容全是自己在忙什么，像吃了兴奋剂一样可怕。
马斯克听得特别无语，觉得这小子纯纯就是在瞎扯淡。

这通电话过后，两人对彼此都没留下什么好印象，50亿也就告吹了。

22年10月底，马斯克收购了推特。
结果才过了两周，FTX就破产了，客户的钱被SBF挪用，缺口有80亿美元，SBF在一个月后被捕，判了25年。

FTX破产当天，马斯克那晚的短信被人翻了出来，发到了推特上。
马斯克亲自回了一句：没错，SBF触发了我的扯淡雷达，所以我压根不信他有30亿🤣🤣

author: CamiRusso
quoted_text:
By design, a Morpho Blue market can't protect its users: it can't freeze the market to mitigate risk, act on the interest rate curve or implement rate limiting, and it has no Umbrella junior tranche to protect deposits.

When an isolated market breaks, its lenders take 100% of the loss.

If you're a Morpho user facing an adverse event, they will just tweet and let you sink, as they did during the dozens of vault blowups that led to dire user losses. Ask anyone who was in a curator vault during Stream/Elixir.

Users won't trust an infra with real size if it doesn't care about them or support them.

That's why, even with infinite VC funding, deployed incentives, a competitor that lost its best contributors and paid partnerships, Morpho only added a pathetic +$2.15B in active loans this year.

For comparison, I did as much in one week at the Plasma launch.

所有多签机构、DeFi 平台和 DApp 项目的团队，我在此向大家郑重地发起一个倡议：为了客户的安全，请把前端部署到 DeWEB中，让前端和合约在同一层！！

这几年最大的几次交易所被盗，问题出在了前端被篡改，签名者看到的页面已经被人换掉了。多签再多，签的是一笔假的交易，也起不到保护作用。

核心问题在于，合约在链上，前端却在服务器上。两层不在一起，中间黑客就能下手。

所以我倡议：凡是管着别人资产的项目，请把前端部署到 DeWEB 上一份。TapeOut 的 DeWEB 把网页的每一个文件连同它的哈希一起存进链上的电路容器，与合约在同一层。打开页面时，内核逐个文件核对哈希，哈希对不上文件不显示，并直接给出警告。无论是你的本机、你的网关、你的 DNS 被动了手脚，用户会看到页面被篡改。

部署DeWEB非常简单，只需要把构建好的前端上传到电路容器中，并绑定DNS，即可任何人无障碍访问。上传以后，它不依赖任何服务器，一次支付Gas部署，永远免费。

请来研究一下 TapeOut 的 DeWEB，它今天就能用。也是目前可验证前端的最佳答案。让交易所被盗的事少发生一次，让行业更安全一点。把前端和合约放在同一层，从你的项目开始。

text:
Time for the Crypto community to address the elephant in the room.

Between AI-driven attacks, quantum, and hacks getting bigger every year, we need to talk about a 2–3 year window where chains can roll-back in extreme cases.

You think it’s Controversial? Sure. But talk privately to people in this industry and most will admit they agree.

I am sure you’d find more agreement across communities than you’d expect. The practical reality: ~90% of funds sit on BTC, ETH and SOL. We basically need three communities to agree.

Blockchains today are not prepared for true black swan events and we have many knocking at the door, We should be honest about that.

Call it a hardening period. But validator-level coordination and roll-back needs to be on the table.

author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
Coinbase（ $COIN ）2026年第三季度财报

Coinbase 的三季度财报看起来赚了不少钱，净利润达到 7.19 亿美元。但实际上其中有 7.15 亿美元来自投资用途加密资产的收益。也就是说 Coinbase 第三季度最赚钱的并不是交易，而是投资。

把加密资产和其他投资损益及相关税务影响调整以后，Coinbase 的净利润是 7,770 万美元，比去年同期下降了 82%。当季总营收为 12.16 亿美元，同比下降 35%，其中交易收入下降 44%，到 5.90 亿美元。

这也能从交易量上看出来，Coinbase 三季度的加密现货成交量为 1,345 亿美元，比去年同期的 2,943 亿美元下降了一半多。虽然公司披露的加密交易量市场份额从去年同期的 5.6% 提升到 10.7%，但在整个市场交易活跃度下降的情况下份额增加也没能让交易收入同比增长。

不过 Coinbase 的收入来源确实在变得更多了，其中三季度订阅和服务收入达到 5.70 亿美元，占净营收的 49%，稳定币收入为 3.07 亿美元，环比增长 5%。Coinbase 产品中的 USDC 平均余额也从上季度的 200 亿美元增长到 220 亿美元。

不过虽然 USDC 余额增加了，但 USDC 整体平均市值从上季度的 770 亿美元降到了 730 亿美元。

另外 Coinbase 预测市场的季度收入已经达到超过 2 亿美元的年化水平。日均交易用户环比增长超过 60%，预测市场增长也带来了交易费用的增加。

衍生品方面 Coinbase 第三季度加密衍生品名义成交量为 9,630 亿美元，同比增长约 14%，但环比下降约 6%。Coinbase 国际交易所与 Deribit 的整合已于 10 月完成，短期交易量可能因用户适应而波动。

截至 9 月底，Coinbase 披露公司现金及现金等价物 86.04 亿美元，低于去年底的 112.85 亿美元。其中包括约 24.15 亿美元支付型稳定币。长期债务约 59.48 亿美元，短期借款约 7.49 亿美元。公司称仍有约 20 亿美元回购授权额度，但尚未披露会在什么时候启动回购。

总的来说，财报体现出 Coinbase 市场份额确实在增长，但加密货币市场的低迷带来了交易的下降，收入和经营利润仍在下滑。USDC 和预测市场虽然能带来新增收益，但还不足以弥补交易业务的下降。

text:
回顾一下亚马逊的财报：核心业务依旧强，盈利能力也不错，但是资本开支与自由现金流依旧出现较大瞎吃！

昨天也说了，本周谷歌、微软与亚马逊三大云厂商巨头，亚马逊收尾，更像是谷歌与微软的AI商业逻辑的二次验证，结果也很明显，亚马逊也并未完成本季度的市场预期目标

营收：201.9B，处于201-203B区间，略低于市场预期，及格。营业利润28.1B，营业利润率13.9%，亚马逊历史最高，营收总体收入增长迅猛，并且利润增长非常强。

AI资本支出：Q3资本自出77.26B，大幅度超出此前市场预期，单季度资本支出预期高20B，且全面资本支出锁定220B，并且提升2027年资本支出预期

自由现金流：-42.4B，去年同期是14.8B， 一年恶化57.2B，问题的关键并不是经营现金流问题，而是经营现金流追不上资本支出导致的自由现金流被挤压。

未来指引：短期一般，但是长期非常激进，短期Q4营收 240-247B，同比增长12%-16%，中值243.5B%，略低于市场预期244.5B，但是利润指引保持28.5B-33.5B，同比去年25B指引好了不少，显然亚马逊并未释放利润恶化信号。而AWS长期指引2027年增长大于40%，2028年增长大约40%，对核心业务的指引算是非常激进。

AWS：财报的王炸级别数据，业务增长速度加快，已经接近5年来最高增速，如此庞大的技术还能有40%规模的增速，意味着AI云需求不是简单的基数增长，而是需求爆发，并且利润确实漂亮，收入增长39%，营业利润增加55%

总结：

亚马逊财报其实一点也不差，相比来说比谷歌还强，但是两者都同样面度第一个问题，那就是资本支出短期账面无法被营收追赶，FCF持续走肉，甚至恶化

所以，按照亚马逊是谷歌微软的二次验证来看，显然这个二次验证放大了谷歌财报带来的担忧，其次同步发布的还有英特尔财报，算是截至目前本季度最差财报，直接被英特尔带崩。

回顾本周三家云厂商的财报，核心业务都没问题，营收，利润都保持不错的增速，但是就是因为宏观环境的压制下，让投资市场过于与未来的大量资本支出更加担忧导致估值调整，其实这也算健康，起码消除了科技股泡沫担忧。

说直白点，利率高，大家手里的钱更加之前，所以以往的小缺点都会在本季度放大，小瑕疵成为股价短期致命伤！
author: Cato_KT
quoted_text:
既然讲完了谷歌与微软的财报，顺便前瞻下凌晨亚马逊的财报！

亚马逊在本周三大云厂商所处的位置非常关键——二次验证，恰好谷歌财报有瑕疵，那么亚马逊的财报就有点重要了，能否提振云厂商企业的信心，就要看亚马逊了！

亚马逊的财报验证逻辑同样看五大要素：营收+AI资本支出+自由现金流+未来指引+AWS

而验证逻辑可以是：AWS 增长 → AI CapEx → AWS 利润率 → FCF → Q4/2027 指引，而且相比微软与谷歌，亚马逊的压力更加直接，市场直接要通过财报得出一个结论——AI投入能不能快速转化为现金流

营收：＞203B优秀，201-203B及格符合预期，199-201B偏弱，＜199B明显差，不过营收在今晚的财报中比重较低，因为核心AWS才能决定估值

AWS：今晚第一核心，Q2 AWS 42.2B，同比增长37%，AWS营业利润达到16.6B，也就是说AWS是亚马逊承担AI增长故事+利润故事的核心，目前主流预期45.4B，对应同比应该是40%，所以AWS要关注增速能否达到40%。＞40%非常优秀，41%就大超预期，37%-40%符合预期，34%-37%及格但是偏弱，＜34%则意味着很差，尤其是如果今晚财报显示资本支出继续扩大，但是核心AWS业务增速不及格，就又是跟谷歌一样。

AI资本支出：Q3验证逻辑改变，并不是数字越大越好，Q2 亚马逊已经将资本开支扩大到220B，所以今晚如果资本开支保持增长趋势220B-230B，那必须要搭配AWS ＞40%的增速+backlog增长+AWS利润率稳定，才能支撑利好，否则反而是利空。

自由现金流：亚马逊最大的隐患，Q2财报中显示过去十二个月的经营现金流161.4B，同比增长33%，但是自由现金流为负7.6B，这意味着Q2面对高速增长的经营现金流依旧在挤压FCF，那么Q3想要让FCF 转为正值难度很大。所以今晚对于亚马逊的自由现金流要做预期降级，不能希望直接转为正值，而是看数字是否继续恶化，如果相比Q2数字不在恶化，算是好事。

AWS利润率：这是很容易被市场忽略的指标，AWS作为亚马逊的核心业务，在业务增长的前提下如果无法保证利润率，将会削弱业务增长带来的利好，Q2的利润率39.3%左右，那么今晚对应38-40%就算不错，如果搭配AWS业务增长40%，算是一个优秀组合。

未来指引：如果说财报是给过去一个答案，未来指引就是引导未来预期，目前主流分析营收指引约在239B-246B，中值242.5B，营业率利润29B-34B左右，今晚的管理层指引关键看三个关键词：AWS 容量、AI需求、2027年资本开支，如果AWS需求仍然超过可用算力，属于利好，这意味着未来AWS增速是受到算力供给限制而并非市场需求限制。

text:
I'm dumping the majority of my Intel shares. This was genuinely one of the saddest earnings calls.

I had SO much hope for this company. I genuinely believed Intel was finally turning things around under Lip-Bu Tan and to be fair, they've made some real progress. But after listening to the entire earnings call, I honestly think Intel messed up BAD. And what makes this even more frustrating is that Intel has one of the biggest opportunities in the semiconductor industry sitting right in front of it, yet it cannot fully take advantage of it.

First, the guidance was absolutely terrible. Intel reported $16.5 billion in Q3 revenue and adjusted EPS of $0.52, which were actually pretty solid results. But then management guided for just $15 billion to $16 billion in Q4 revenue, compared to Wall Street's expectations of around $17.1 billion. They also expect adjusted EPS to fall to $0.25, compared to expectations of roughly $0.43. Even worse, gross margins are expected to fall from 44.1% to just 38% in a single quarter. That's a massive decline, especially for a company that's supposed to be improving its profitability.

But the biggest problem is what management said about 2027. Intel's PC business is getting destroyed by the ongoing memory shortage. Companies like Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron are benefiting from enormous AI demand, but that same demand is making memory more expensive and harder to find for traditional computers.

And when memory becomes more expensive, the entire computer becomes more expensive. That means fewer people and businesses are willing to upgrade their PCs, which directly hurts Intel. Management now expects the overall PC market to shrink by around 12% in 2026 and another 10% in 2027. Intel also expects its own client revenue to fall more than 20% in Q4 alone. What really caught my attention was when management basically admitted that they don't expect the memory situation to improve in 2027. So this isn't just a temporary problem that disappears next quarter. It could continue hurting Intel for another year or longer.

Now, here's what frustrates me the MOST. Intel's data center business is absolutely booming, but they cannot manufacture enough chips to meet demand. Data Center and AI revenue grew nearly 80% year over year to $7.3 billion. Management expects industry server CPU shipments to grow more than 30% in both 2026 and 2027, and Lip-Bu Tan even believes the server CPU market could grow from around $40 billion today to more than $200 billion over the next five years because of AI agents. That's an unbelievable opportunity. But Intel is dealing with manufacturing capacity limitations, production bottlenecks, and shortages of the materials needed to package its chips. In other words, customers WANT to buy more Intel server CPUs, but Intel cannot produce enough of them.

And management made it pretty clear that these supply problems will continue into the first half of 2027, with meaningful improvements not expected until the second half. This is what bothers me more than anything. We're experiencing one of the strongest periods of CPU demand in years, and Intel is leaving billions of dollars in potential sales on the table while competitors fight for market share. Then there's the tragic accident at Intel's factory in Israel, which forced production to shut down for approximately two weeks. Management expects this to reduce Q4 revenue by around $300 million, with a similar impact potentially extending into Q1. It also accounts for about two percentage points of the expected Q4 gross margin decline. Obviously, this was an unfortunate situation, but it creates even more problems for a company that was already struggling to produce enough chips.

And don't even get me started on the foundry business. This was supposed to be one of the biggest reasons to invest in Intel. The idea was that Intel could become a serious competitor to TSMC by manufacturing chips for other companies. And yes, Intel is making progress. Its 18A manufacturing process is improving, production costs are coming down, and management sounds more confident about 14A but here's the reality. Intel's foundry business still lost $1.9 BILLION in Q3. External foundry revenue was only $411 million, and part of that came from a one time customer program. Management keeps talking about potential customers, improving yields, and future opportunities. But where are the major external customer commitments that will actually make this business profitable? I'm not saying they won't come. I'm saying investors have already been waiting years for this turnaround, and we're still talking about what MIGHT happen in 2027 and 2028.

And then came another comment that really disappointed me. Intel doesn't expect to generate positive free cash flow in 2027. The company already expects to spend around $20 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, and management said spending will increase significantly next year. So we're looking at another year of massive investments, continued foundry losses, a declining PC market, and potentially negative free cash flow. And remember, Intel raised $23 billion by issuing additional shares in August, meaning existing shareholders also have to deal with dilution. At some point, investors need to ask when all this spending is actually going to translate into sustainable profits.

Now, I want to be fair because there ARE positives here. Intel's server CPU demand is incredibly strong. Its manufacturing technology is improving. Granite Rapids is becoming more profitable, its custom silicon business is growing rapidly, and its upcoming products like Diamond Rapids and Nova Lake could help it regain market share. I also think the long term opportunity in AI infrastructure, advanced packaging, and foundry services is enormous. But here's the issue. Almost every major positive Intel talks about is something that could happen in the FUTURE. More manufacturing capacity in the second half of 2027. Potential foundry customers. A stronger product roadmap. Better profitability. Eventually positive free cash flow.

Meanwhile, all the problems are happening RIGHT NOW. The PC business is declining right now. Manufacturing constraints are hurting sales right now. Foundry is losing billions right now. And margins are expected to fall significantly next quarter. The worst part is that Intel doesn't even have a demand problem in its server business. It has an execution problem. And that's arguably even more frustrating because the opportunity is already there.

I understand that rebuilding a company like Intel takes years, and I still respect what Lip-Bu Tan is trying to accomplish. But after the massive rally in this stock, investors were expecting Intel to finally start delivering meaningful results, not another year of excuses and promises. I was willing to be patient with Intel because I believed the turnaround was gaining momentum. But this earnings call genuinely changed my perspective.

I'm not selling because I suddenly believe Intel is a terrible company or that its technology has no future. I'm selling because I no longer think the risk and reward are nearly as attractive as they were before. I'm dumping the majority of my position, but I'll likely keep a smaller stake because I still believe there's long-term potential here. I really wanted Intel to succeed. I still do. But wanting a company to succeed and believing its stock is a good investment at the current valuation are two completely different things.

And after listening to management today, I just cannot justify maintaining the same level of exposure. Intel had the opportunity to prove that its turnaround was finally working. Instead, management gave investors even more reasons to question it. This was genuinely disappointing.

This is incoherent. Zcash does not fit the definition of a public good (i.e., non-rivalrous, non-excludable). If you buy 1 ZEC, its yours and no one else can't have it, and if you want to participate in/use the Zcash network, you have to pay for it. No free-riding.

If by public good you mean that Zcash is open-source/available/accessible to everyone, then I agree with you that it is. And I also firmly agree that Zcash is good for society and necessary for it to be free and open.

But that should not be confused or conflated with what economists mean by "public good", as in one that cannot be provided efficiently or effectively by the private markets. Zcash does not have such characteristics. It is not a lighthouse or national defense.

As a result, it doesn't need a government-like plundering/taxing mechanism to fund its development — especially not one without representation — like ZCG. Development is the purview of the market. In other words, ZCG is not necessary. The market will handle this and handle it better in all respects.

I have no idea why or how you think Zcash would be "rendered accessible to only the rich". The trend line for more accessibility has only been increasing rapidly and dramatically (e.g., wallet support, exchange support, exposure via public companies and ETFs, etc.). Maybe you could expand on your argument here so everyone can understand what you are talking about.

quoted_text:
There is nothing special about this pullback.

Much of the panic surrounding neoclouds, AI capital expenditures, and the sustainability of the infrastructure buildout is simply the market searching for explanations for falling stock prices.

When AI stocks were rising, record capex was evidence of extraordinary demand. When those same stocks started falling, suddenly the same spending became evidence of an impending financial disaster.

One fact with two interpretations that depend entirely on the price action of the market.

Go back to August 1998.

The technology bull market had been running for about three years.Amid fallout from the Asian financial crisis and Russian ruble crisis, earnings expectations were deteriorating, valuations were elevated, and investors were becoming increasingly concerned about unprofitable Internet companies.

On August 6, the New York Times published an article titled "Market Gyrations May Point to Shift in Investor Strategy." One fund manager declared, "Boring is going to outperform sexy."

Investors were supposedly abandoning momentum and speculative technology shares in favor of profitable businesses, balance sheets, dividends, and traditional valuations.

Russia defaulted on its debt. The Asian financial crisis was spreading internationally. The yen carry trade had imploded as the USD plunged 8% against the yen in a single day. US embassies were being bombed. 

President Clinton ordered missile strikes against Afghanistan and Sudan while simultaneously facing a scandal that would result in his impeachment. Major financial institutions suffered enormous losses, and the spectacular collapse of Long-Term Capital Management threatened the stability of the global financial system.

Corporate earnings forecasts were falling. Investors feared a U.S. recession. Many of the same technology companies that had driven the bull market were now leading the decline. Many of them had fallen 40-60% from their 1998 highs.

Even the Federal Reserve's first interest-rate cut on September 29 initially disappointed investors. The Dow fell that day and plunged another 238 points the following session.

The news seemed almost uniformly terrible.
But the market didn't care forever.

After a violent reversal in early October, improving confidence in corporate earnings, Japanese banking reforms, and a surprise emergency Fed cut on October 15 helped restore risk appetite.

By November, the Dow was making new all-time highs. Internet stocks were exploding higher again.

What had looked like the end of the internet trade was, within about a month, actually a correction preceding one of the most extraordinary speculative advances in stock-market history.

In today’s market, Microsoft just reported 48% Azure growth. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled. Meta expects $135–145 billion in capex this year and has announced plans for a potentially record-sized $97.5 billion equity capital raise.

If the market really was that concerned over capex spending, instead of using it as an excuse to explain the pullback, the market would have sold off on the META news.

Anthropic has now filed its IPO registration statement. We have midterm elections approaching, another consequential round of earnings, and a Fed that just held rates steady even as another hike is widely anticipated in December.

There are plenty of potential catalysts over the coming two months.

More importantly, this does not resemble the sentiment backdrop of a speculative bubble climax. Generational bull markets don't die midway through a basing period, but typically after euphoric saturation and a parabolic rally in leading names.

Consensus on AI is deeply divided. Being loudly anti-AI has practically become fashionable. Some AI critics have even built enormous audiences around the idea that the economics of the industry are unsustainable. Plenty of investors seem almost eager to watch the entire trade collapse.

That isn't the sentiment or narrative around which tops are typically made.

The Internet trade didn't end in the panic of 1998. It ended after the extraordinary acceleration of 1999 and early 2000 when being bearish was the market equivalent of wearing a dunce cap.

History never repeats perfectly, and today's rate environment is very different. But I think the resemblance in investor psychology is striking.

I’d be genuinely surprised if we don't have at least one more months-long rally into new highs during this cycle. 

Whether it begins into the midterms, after the elections, around Anthropic's anticipated listing, or following further earnings confirmation, I suspect this correction will eventually look more like an interruption in a generational bull market than the bursting of a "bubble."

The $NDX took four months to bottom in 1998. With the exception of a handful of leaders, most stocks that are holding up have been basing out since the May-July period. We could certainly go lower, but most of the signs point to  another new high before this cycle rolls over. 

However, I’d place the odds of any additional powerful rallies afterward as increasingly unlikely given the fact we are already about to enter the fifth year of this bull market. I'd be careful about buying the dips next year, at least with meaningful size.

Google -12.6%, Amazon -7%, Intel -25%, Nasdaq futures down 2%+... and it's happening after these companies posted some of the best cloud growth we've EVER seen

The fear right now is the BILL

The 4 big hyperscalers free cash flow was -$26B combined. 3 of the 4 are now spending more than their businesses bring in

Anyway, the biggest risk is that @variational_io  ends up exposed to every exchange it uses for hedging. Imagine another FTX-style collapse. Would Variational have been using that exchange to hedge? If it had been operating back then, I’m 100% convinced it would have used FTX.

If FTX then refused to return the funds held there, OLP would take the loss too. That’s a potentially devastating problem.

Think about it another way. If you hedge across ten exchanges, even one of them going under could be enough to take Variational down, depending on the size of the exposure and OLP’s ability to absorb the loss.

And in crypto, an exchange can go from thriving to insolvent very quickly.
author: dorong_x
quoted_text:
is Variational telling half-truths about fund safety?

interesting take from Degen Guy
Variational’s statement on the Binance hack sounds reassuring - “user money is on-chain, doesn’t go to external hedge exchanges, 100% withdrawable anytime”

technically true, collateral sits in isolated on-chain settlement pools and isn’t sent to CEXs

but there’s a nuance they didn’t mention

on Omni you don’t trade against other users - you trade against a single counterparty, OLP (their internal market maker). All trades go through RFQ, and OLP is the one that has to pay you your profit

OLP hedges its exposure with its own capital on external exchanges (including Binance and others). If OLP loses money on hedges and becomes insolvent:

- your original collateral can still be withdrawn
- but unrealized and realized PnL turns into bad debt and doesn’t get paid

so the platform really doesn’t touch your deposits, but your profit depends on OLP’s solvency, which is directly tied to the risks of the same external exchanges they hedge on

the statement is technically correct, but it creates a feeling of full safety that doesn’t actually exist

to really reassure users they should show OLP’s current external exposure and capital buffer, not just say “collateral is on-chain”
until then it looks like a careful half-truth

I recommend subscribing to his TG channel - justdegenguy

author: Shaughnessy119
quoted_text:
Some 12 Month AI Predictions and Ideas

- The silicon data LLM token index (weighted price per million tokens) falls from ~2.20 in June to ~1.00. Usage more than 2x’s regardless

- While most AI names are down a bit, I think the cost savings shift (see LLM index) or the capex exhaustion drive a large 10%+ scary down day in AI equities and then a full recovery. My June 2 thesis is a short-mid term correction given a spending shift rattling through the funding flywheel and then a recovery as we will get AGI eventually. June 2nd thesis linked at the end. 

- Frontier intelligence cannot be justified by per token pricing, so mythos style models seek to own 0 to 50% of the medicines, materials, software or businesses they create. This creates trillions in economic value over decades

- OpenAI does not go public until next summer at the earliest because the market needs proof frontier revenue can survive open source price compression and capex payback questions. Equities Market is also exhausted (SpaceX, maybe anthropic etc)

- Enterprises and consumers shift most AI usage to open source models at under 1/10th the price and 90% the intelligence. Maybe it takes longer than 12 months but subsidies ending accelerates it.

- The government takes equity stakes in both OpenAI and Anthropic

- The silicon LLM AI usage, price indicators go live on perps markets and people take large positions betting in these markets

- A new U.S. open weight AI lab or open source enabling firm reaches a $100B valuation because open weights become the enterprise default and the market starts valuing the lab plus agent stack, not just the model

- AI subscription subsidies end and caps, throttles, priority tiers and token billing become standard. People get insanely annoyed as they are addicted

- One major Chinese model lab partners with a U.S. inference company to serve their closed models privately in the west (i.e GLM 6 via Together . AI served privately as people don't want to send data to China but folks want access to these models)

- There is a massive cultural shift to enterprises owning their AI stacks: models, data, memory, employee interactions, proprietary context, evals and fine tuned models. This is a core business asset. Everything Palantir is saying.

- @NousResearch Hermes Agent becomes the default open agent harness as consumers and enterprises roll and own their own AI stacks

- People graduate hermes and openclaw agents from copilots into semi autonomy for coding, research, sales, ops and personal workflows. Full autonomy is still years away.

- Openrouter, baseten, together and fireworks either get acquired by hyperscalers or become 10x more valuable as cheaper open source models become the default

- AWS becomes a key enterprise inference provider, routing across claude, nova, llama, qwen, mistral and deepseek-style models based on cost, latency, accuracy, compliance and for private data for enterprises.

- Apple ships open source models on devices across iphone, mac and vision, then lets users fine tune private adapters on photos, messages, files, health data and app history. This is all driven by their new CEO

- Hyperscalers get judged on revenue per watt, revenue per gpu and fcf per token, not just capex spend

- Grok and META completely fall out of the closed frontier LLM race. No recovery within 12 months

- Grok leads AI in a few years as space physics and data on aliens gives it the most unique AI training dataset that's not obtainable by other labs

- META walks back capex spend

- Google loses frontier consumer facing AI aura, but remains an AI infrastructure winner through TPUs, vertex, cloud, youtube (data) and distribution

- All apps with no proprietary workflow, data, proprietary fine tuned model or distribution get crushed

- The labor replacement conversation gets real as cost savings, headcount avoidance and throughput become the main enterprise ROI metrics

- The Anti data center movement gets way more popular and becomes a key political issue

- Data centers in space become socially viable (even if actually far away deplpyment wise) given pushback on ground deployments on earth. Not in my backyard but space is fine.

- China’s AI research matches or exceeds the U.S. in certain domains. U.S. people underestimate their universities and novel research (i.e. everyone thought DeepSeek was only distilling when in reality they made interesting research leaps in MOE and using old hardware years ago).

- $BTC is a core safe haven in either AI scenario (UBI mass prints money to deal with AGI or capex spending leads to a short term blow up and people seek safe haven)

- Agents will use crypto rails to make money, buy more compute, and grow their intelligence and desires since its the rails with the most degrees of freedom. Not a reply bot agent but a real legitimate one.

- Frontier intelligence is only released publicly if a stronger unreleased model is able to police it (see the movie Automata)

- Nvidia faces strong pricing pressure as new companies release competing chips

- There is a massive shift to hardware, robotics and the weekend warriors building (i.e. SendCutSend + AI models) since software has little to no moats with AGI, outside of enterprises owning their AI stack as a private business asset

- Short timeline but Demis eventually becomes CEO of Alphabet and redirects efforts from external investments/raises to Gemini’s AI labs for huge compelling training runs

- People aggressively expand sharing all personal information to their AI agents (home cameras, alexa listening, Airpods/phone listening and watching) and take AI privacy extremely seriously (at home deployments)

- Law enforcement starts using AI to analyze cold cases and free, and prosecute, people

- The AI SPV craze reveals a lot of fraud. Only the lawyers benefit.

- Parents start to mass question the value of $100k/yr college when AI gives you everything. Need to solve for the social benefits of college though.

- At least ten $1B+ valuation 1 person companies built using AI are created

- Local AI becomes a thing. More specifically your local machine has a bad GPU but it can make up for it by running for 8 hours while youre asleep to analyze your life.

- Fine tuning your own proprietary model becomes the thing to do

- You can rent out your AI agent's unique skills or build on a marketplace to other agents easily and privately (why do I have to build an entire agent for a task if someone already has one? This is up the alley of the move to cost savings)

- A model company moves from charging per token to charging per result

- AI + Robots to doing wet lab experiments becomes a real thing. Testing medicines and materials and building real things at a rate and level of dangerous humans cant.

- X Adds a human verified feed in partnership with Worldcoin or someone else

- Together, OpenRouter, Venice and other inference providers buy GPUs vs being middleman to serve models cheaper. They vertically expand and fine tune and host models for folks.

- OpenAI fully launched ADs in chatGPT and drive a ton of revenue negatively impacting Google

- A fully generated AI movie goes viral on Netflix

A lot of these will probably be wrong but I hope you enjoy my ideas!

text:
So many are giving @sama crap for pushing for centralized computing here.

He isn’t the first to argue this. Anyone remember Sun Microsystems?

The industry swings back and forth between centralized and decentralized computing.

There are advantages to both.

If you have a limited resource, like memory today, it is better to share it. Centralized.

But decentralized leads to freedom and resiliency.

I tend to be in the decentralized camp for that reason.
author: Scobleizer
quoted_text:
sam: local inference is a terrible allocation of scarce resources

“a lot of people want local inference, and somehow they assume that the problem is solved now because we have open-source models, we're going to be able to run them on our computers, and so we're not going to need all the stuff in the data centre

but from a global allocation perspective, actually it's quite terrible to have everybody, like, have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used five percent of the time

you want maximum utilisation in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply-constrained environment

somehow many people's intuition is the opposite of that”

Local AI Builders Friday # 2

The list is now 102. Every week this list sends me down a new rabbit hole.

I added 8 more amazing builders this week:

1) @divagr1925 built Qwenputer, a RISC-V CPU inside Qwen3.5-4B and uses the model’s own layers as RAM. It runs C and MicroPython in its forward passes with no external runtime. AI/ML engineer.

2) @mhelcig made the GSQ-RCO quants that put DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, a 763B open model, on a 12GB GPU, running in @coldniko's Strata engine. One user is already getting 40 tok/s on a single 5090.

3) @machinestein open sourced Locals, an Apple Silicon engine for local LLMs. With LFM3 added this week it hit 620 tok/s on a 16GB M2 running 8 agents in parallel. That’s 3x mlx-lm.

4) @adrgrondin makes Locally AI, which Apple just featured for the new iPad mini. This week he helped bring oMLX, an MLX engine built for long context, into LM Studio and Bionic.

5) @AlicanKiraz0 spent a week with ASUS’s GB300-powered ET900N G3 and wrote the review in 7 languages. In his ant colony coding benchmark, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash beat Kimi K3.1 Pro for 17 cents.

6) @sfxnz got a local model on 2 x DGX Sparks to build an Apple TV-style launcher for his Samsung TV. Keeps building with Local AI.

7) @CerebralCoding_ builds Latch, a scheduler so agents stop fighting over the same GPUs and contributes to MLX-Serve and TensorFold to get models running on Apple Silicon.

8) @lasse_ai tested clock speeds on two DGX Sparks. At 2200 MHz they keep almost full speed and at 1900 MHz they run cooler and quieter.

text:
from what Binance has shared so far, this looks like an opsec failure. an attacker got into an employee's machine and used it to reach internal systems. the blockchains themselves didn't break

every bank and exchange carries this same risk. Binance promising to make customers whole counts for a lot, and so does the joint push to freeze the stolen funds

AI is going to make this much worse. attackers will hunt for bugs, pose as real people and go after far more companies than anyone could before. the whole financial industry has to adjust

this is one reason more of finance needs to move onchain. when every transaction is public, it gets much harder for a company to cover up the damage or make a loss quietly disappear. anyone can trace the money without having to take the company's word for it, and independent investigators get one shared record to work from

open source does the same for the code. outside teams can audit it, run their own tests and send fixes, and they can point AI at it to catch bugs before attackers do. you can also see the points where systems plug into each other, and that's where a lot of bugs start

you still need strong opsec. but i think open systems that anyone can verify will end up safer than ones that ask us to take their security and their books on faith. we should be building for that from day one

- revoked the affected address authorisation;
- engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds.

Our teams are working around the clock to resolve this issue safely and thoroughly. We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice.

Claude封过一次的，一定要用这个清单清理一遍环境！

直接发给Codex或者豆包、workbuddy检查就行

我也做成了一个skill，可以直接调用👇
https://t.co/d1EOxka9fn

清单：

Claude 本机环境清理清单（macOS）

说明：
- 以下是本次实际操作记录，不是自动执行命令。
- 清理前均已备份并校验。
- 移除的文件放入废纸篓；JSON、数据库只修改指定字段或记录。
- 清理本地数据不能解除账号封禁，也不能保证消除服务端关联。

一、Claude Code 缓存
~/.claude/cache
~/.claude/stats-cache.json
~/.claude/telemetry
~/Library/Caches/claude-cli-nodejs

二、Claude 桌面端缓存
以下路径位于 ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/：
Cache
Code Cache
GPUCache
DawnGraphiteCache
DawnWebGPUCache
GPUPersistentCache
GraphiteDawnCache

其他缓存：
~/Library/Caches/com.anthropic.claudefordesktop
~/Library/Caches/com.anthropic.claudefordesktop.ShipIt

三、日志、诊断和临时状态
桌面端 Crashpad
桌面端 sentry
~/Library/Logs/Claude
明确属于 Claude 的 CrashReporter 文件
桌面端 window-state.json
桌面端 vm-support-probe.json

四、JSON 配置定向清理
~/.claude.json 中已知模型、实验和功能缓存字段
~/.claude/settings.json 中的 theme
桌面 config.json 中的 userThemeMode
桌面 config.json 中的 bootFrameLayout
桌面 config.json 中的 bootSidebarPlaceholder

其余项目、MCP、权限及必要配置未删除，没有整份删除 JSON。

五、旧账号信息和登录缓存
5 份 ~/.claude/backups/.claude.json.backup.* 中的 oauthAccount
桌面 config.json 中的 lastKnownAccountUuid
桌面 config.json 中的 oauth:tokenCache
桌面 config.json 中的 oauth:tokenCacheV2
桌面 config.json.journal
桌面端 16 条 Claude/Anthropic Cookie
桌面端 5 条明确的账号或分析标识 Local Storage 记录

检查时没有发现 ~/.claude/.credentials.json。
钥匙串未查到 Claude Code-credentials，没有执行钥匙串删除。

六、Chrome 浏览器残留
.anthropic.com 的 ajs_anonymous_id Cookie
https://t.co/taflADHX63 的 anthropic-device-id Cookie
验证门户 IndexedDB
验证门户 Local Storage
Anthropic 相关站点存储登记及对应数据
Claude 扩展本地存储

Claude 扩展本身没有卸载。
其他网站的 Cookie、存储及扩展数据没有修改。
ChatGPT、Kraken 使用的 Persona 分区没有修改。

七、设备记录（经单独授权）
ant-did
ant-device-registry.json

重启后，ant-did 重新生成，新值与旧值不同。
ant-device-registry.json 在重启后的检查时尚未重新生成。
底层设备密钥没有修改。
删除设备记录文件不等于重置底层设备密钥。

八、不清理的内容
对话历史、history.jsonl
projects、sessions、file-history
桌面 claude-code-sessions、local-agent-mode-sessions
与历史会话关联的账号索引
Skills、Hooks、Plugins、Commands、Agents
MCP 配置、权限配置、项目代码和 Git 数据
Claude Safe Storage 和其他钥匙串项目
其他应用和网站的数据
时区、Shell 环境变量
恢复备份和废纸篓副本

九、最新复查结果
目标 JSON 账号及令牌字段未重新出现。
未发现 CLI 凭据文件，未查到指定 CLI 钥匙串凭据。
桌面端已清理的目标 Cookie 和 Local Storage 字段未重新出现。
Chrome 四个资料未查到目标 Cookie、IndexedDB 和扩展存储。
Chrome 四个资料未查到目标 Local/Session Storage 记录。

十、恢复与限制
备份位置：~/ClaudeBackups/
废纸篓批次：~/.Trash/claude-*
详细报告：本次工作目录 outputs/ 下

备份和废纸篓副本仍可能含旧账号信息，不要公开上传。
恢复前正常退出对应应用，先备份当前状态，再恢复指定文件。
不要整目录覆盖，避免覆盖新产生的对话或配置。
应用、网页或扩展再次运行后，部分数据可能重新生成。
本次属于可恢复、定向清理，不是全盘痕迹抹除。

text:
keep seeing people say "$6b hack and bitcoin only down 2%" as a bullish thing

believe ppl are fundamentally misunderstanding the difference to how bitcoin trades now versus years ago

$BTC used to be the primary driver for retail speculation in crypto, we were all aping leveraged positions on perps in 2017, alts were also part of the speculation but btc much moreso than now

this changed in 2020/21 when retail mostly were trading alts as their way of going down the risk curve, the new traders on uniswap did not care at all about bitcoin

even moreso in 2023 cycle & now, transition more to onchain because the altcoins on centralized exchanges performed much worse so less ppl speculating on perps than in the trenches, its how memecoins became a lot more popular, & now with equity perps we have even more degens trading other instruments rather than lev longing btc

believe that this has had a significant impact on how bitcoin trades bc it is less apes smashing longs and shorts on the btc chart, you can see this appear in the price action with how bitcoin ripped extremely aggressively on every all time high break in 2017 but every top in 2021 post-saylor's aping in 2020 was the subtle ath failed breakout and then breakdown and much choppier price action

even more apparent in 2023-2025 where we spent several months in compressed ranges & then also topped in jan 2025 & sept/oct 2025 with slightly higher high & failed breakout

when 10/10 liquidation happened, $BTC barely moved compared to alts, this is because of what im stating above, the degens are not longing bitcoin, it traded above $100k for weeks after 10/10 and did not make substantially lower lows until november while alts got wiped in one candle

text:
What if you could hold a stock only while the market is closed, without buying and selling every day?

That's the idea behind Isolated Exposure Tokens (IETs), proposed by @0xbeans and The @standard_rsv.

Deposit one tokenized share and receive:

• OVERNIGHT: exposure from the close to the next open.
• SESSION: exposure from the open to the close.

Hold both and redeem for one share. Sell one to keep only the exposure you want. Each series has an expiry; exiting one side earlier requires a buyer.

A simple example:

• A $100 share starts with $50 allocated to each token.
• It opens at $110: OVERNIGHT rises to $60.
• It closes at $105: SESSION falls to $45.
• Together, they're worth $105 at the accounting level.

Why it's interesting and why we're at @paboxoxyz also loves it as it align with our off-market lending features.

• Could support overnight-only vaults and targeted hedges.
• Splits exposure without requiring the issuer to trade the underlying every day.
• Gives DeFi another building block, similar in structure to Pendle's split claims.

But something that still needs some works and detailed explanations:

• Each token starts with roughly 2× exposure at its initial accounting value.
• Balances accumulate dollar moves, so they don't reproduce the compounded returns.
• Expected overnight gains can already be priced into the token.
• Overnight exposure existed before through NightShares ETFs.

The vault can't pay $110 if the losing holder owes nothing. Caps, early termination or extra capital could help, but the supplied paper doesn't specify a rule.

Promising concept. It needs clear loss rules, reliable price feeds and affordable liquidity before the historical overnight anomaly becomes a new primitive.

Pèp ayisyen,

Nou prèske fin deplwaye sòlda nou yo ak ekipman nou yo sou tè Ayiti. Sa a se pa yon operasyon kont pèp ayisyen an, ni yon envazyon peyi Ayiti. Nou pa yon gwo pisans. Nou pa gen okenn enterè ni pou nou vin domine pèp ayisyen an, ni pou nou mete men sou richès Ayiti.

Nou se yon peyi modès k ap devlope. Sèl sa nou vle, se pou kat teknisyen avyasyon nou yo tounen lakay yo. Epi n ap bay gang yo yon leson, gang sa yo k ap fè pèp ayisyen an soufri, ki touye moun pèp la renmen yo, k ap anpeche l viv yon lavi nòmal, lib, san laperèz.

Se prèske nou menm sèl k ap peye pou operasyon sa a. Menmsi nou resevwa yon ti èd lojistik nan men kèk lòt peyi, se ak pwòp ti kès nou n ap kouvri 90% nan depans yo.

Sa koute nou chè, men nou te aprann nan pwòp soufrans nou: jistis ak lapè pa gen pri. Nou te pase nan menm soufrans Ayiti ap travèse jodi a. Nou te viv yon beny san ki te pi terib toujou pase sa pèp ayisyen an ap sibi kounye a. Nou konnen sa sa vle di: viv nan laperèz, pa fè politisyen konfyans, pa kwè okenn moun ki pwomèt l ap ede w. Paske pèsonn pa t vin ede nou, e moun ki te vini yo pa t gen bon entansyon nan kè yo.

Men nou te rive chape anba sa. Apre 200 lane soufrans, finalman n ap viv nan lapè, e jodi a nou se peyi ki gen plis sekirite sou kontinan an.

Nou pa vin ann Ayiti pou nou touche lajan, paske pèsonn pa peye nou pou sa. Nou vin ann Ayiti pou nou goumen kont mechan yo.

Men sa m ap mande nou: fè nou konfyans, lapriyè sèl vrè Bondye a, epi mande L pou L geri Ayiti.

“Lè sa a si pèp ki pote non m lan lapriyè nan pye m, si yo soumèt devan mwen, si yo pran chache m ankò, si yo vire do bay vye peche yo t'ap fè yo, m'ap tande yo nan syèl kote m ye a, m'ap padonnen peche yo, m'ap fè peyi a kanpe ankò.”

2 Kwonik 7:14

Ede nou ede Ayiti.

Epi lè misyon nou an fini, n ap tounen lakay nou. Petèt jenerasyon Ayisyen k ap vini yo ap sonje nou kòm zanmi ki te vin ede yon lè.

author: oragnes
quoted_text:
Earlier today, the attacker behind the recent @binance  exploit, apparently in error, sent approximately 8.0M NEWT directly to the NEWT token contract address (0xd0ec028a3d21533fdd200838f39c85b03679285d), along with 17 other tokens: $ANIME, ethereum:0x8290333cef9e6d528dd5618fb97a76f268f3edd4, $ARPA, $BARD, $CELR, ethereum:0x3597bfd533a99c9aa083587b074434e61eb0a258, ethereum:0x0f81001ef0a83ecce5ccebf63eb302c70a39a654, $FTT, $GLM, $HIGH, $HOT, $KNC, $LQTY, $RARE, ethereum:0x259338656198ec7a76c729514d3cb45dfbf768a1, $SIGN and $WOO. These tokens are worth roughly $3.5 million at current prices.

To be clear, the NEWT token contract itself was not compromised.

We have reviewed the contract carefully, and unfortunately these tokens cannot be recovered. The NEWT token contract was built to be immutable: it has no owner or admin, all admin rights were renounced onchain in 2025, and upgrades are permanently disabled. That design exists to protect holders, so that no one, including the Foundation, can ever move or alter their tokens. These safeguards mean there is no way for anyone to retrieve tokens sent to the contract itself.

These tokens are now permanently locked. They are out of the attacker’s control and can never be sold into the market.

We have shared our findings with Binance and we will keep helping however we can.

text:
做市商的工作聽起來像是印鈔機。你把買入價定在99，賣出價定在101。有人以99的價格賣給你，有人以101的價格從你這裡買入，你什麼都沒做，只是站在中間，就賺了2美元。

問題在於，這兩筆交易不會按部就班地依序到來。有時，會有二十個人連續賣給你，卻沒有人買。這樣一來，你就持有了大量你並不想要的資產，如果價格下跌，你的損失將遠遠超過你之前賺取的所有價差。這部分資產稱為庫存，而庫存正是導致做市商失敗的罪魁禍首。 https://t.co/AOFRgBW2Pa
author: 0xLUKE777crypt
quoted_text:
資金費率套利聊膩了，來聊做市。

2008 年 Avellaneda 和 Stoiko 那篇論文幾乎是所有做市入門的起點。核心想法很直覺：做市商手上有庫存就有風險，所以報價不該圍著中間價，而是圍著一個「保留價格」。庫存越多、波動越大、離收盤越遠，保留價格就越往不利於你庫存的方向偏，把貨吐出去。價差則由風險厭惡和成交機率一起決定，成交機率假設隨著你離中間價的距離呈指數衰減。

AS 漂亮，但拿到幣圈直接用會出事。它有一個終止時間 T，離 T 越近價差越窄，可是加密市場 24 小時不收盤，你根本沒有 T。它也不限制庫存，理論上可以一路被單邊打穿。很多人第一次寫做市機器人就是死在這兩點。

2013 年 Gueant、Lehalle 和 Fernandez-Tapia 的 GLFT 基本上就是在補這兩個洞。它加上庫存上下限，並且推出時間趨於無限時的近似解，報價變成只跟當下庫存有關，跟時間無關。這對永續合約來說剛好，參數也變得可以實際校準：用成交資料去擬合成交強度 A 和衰減係數 k，再配上波動率和你自己的風險厭惡，就能算出每一檔庫存該報多寬、該偏多少。

可是 AS 和 GLFT 有一個共同的盲點，它們都假設中間價是隨機漫步，對價格方向一無所知。真實世界不是這樣，被聰明的單吃掉才是做市商最大的成本。所以後來 Cartea 和 Jaimungal 那一派把短期 alpha 加進來，讓報價不只依庫存偏移，也依訂單流失衡、microprice 這類預測訊號偏移。再往下走就是用 Hawkes 過程去描述成交會自我激發、一筆大單帶出一串單的現象，以及現在越來越多人在試的強化學習。

我覺得真正的機會在 HIP3 的股票永續。拿 https://t.co/XGAXjhlBiB 上的 SNDK 來說，美股開盤時 oracle 跟著外部價格走，休市時改成用永續自己的訂單簿算均價，等於同一個商品一週切換兩次完全不同的市場狀態。用固定參數跑 GLFT，平日校準出來的 k 和波動率到週末就失效了。

所以方向大概是這樣：平日把外部盤後價格當成 alpha 訊號來偏移報價，因為永續價格是追著它跑的；

週末外部訊號消失，成交強度變低，就該拉高風險厭惡、收窄庫存上限。

財報這種跳空事件更是要提早切換參數。誰先把 regime switching 做進做市模型裡，誰就能在這種薄盤口裡吃到別人吃不到的價差。

text:
英特尔股价暴跌29%的背后，困境到底在哪？

简单梳理一下 $INTC  凌晨的财报，简单来说Q3的业绩不错，但是Q4的营收指引、盈利能力，PC业务全面下调

都在拼爆发的年代，你不爆发还行但是却大幅下调指引，市场肯定对当前估值不买账，但是这只是主要因素之一

另一方面，核心PC端业务突然转弱，而AI、数据中心需求突然爆发，英特尔却因为供应链与产能瓶颈无法充分转化营收

同时叠加以色列工厂事故，内存价格保障，扩产现金消耗，最终导致Q4营收、利润率和EPS指引同时大幅下修。

简单总结，英特尔现有核心业务因为外部原因受损，当红AI趋势上又暂时吃不到红利，所以直接引发大规模的估值调整

当然，Q4是英特尔的关键季度，在估值大幅调整之后，业务是否继续恶化？能否在AI时代快速打破困境回归主流趋势，这将是后续市场要关注的重点！
author: Cato_KT
quoted_text:
回顾一下亚马逊的财报：核心业务依旧强，盈利能力也不错，但是资本开支与自由现金流依旧出现较大瞎吃！

昨天也说了，本周谷歌、微软与亚马逊三大云厂商巨头，亚马逊收尾，更像是谷歌与微软的AI商业逻辑的二次验证，结果也很明显，亚马逊也并未完成本季度的市场预期目标

营收：201.9B，处于201-203B区间，略低于市场预期，及格。营业利润28.1B，营业利润率13.9%，亚马逊历史最高，营收总体收入增长迅猛，并且利润增长非常强。

AI资本支出：Q3资本自出77.26B，大幅度超出此前市场预期，单季度资本支出预期高20B，且全面资本支出锁定220B，并且提升2027年资本支出预期

自由现金流：-42.4B，去年同期是14.8B， 一年恶化57.2B，问题的关键并不是经营现金流问题，而是经营现金流追不上资本支出导致的自由现金流被挤压。

未来指引：短期一般，但是长期非常激进，短期Q4营收 240-247B，同比增长12%-16%，中值243.5B%，略低于市场预期244.5B，但是利润指引保持28.5B-33.5B，同比去年25B指引好了不少，显然亚马逊并未释放利润恶化信号。而AWS长期指引2027年增长大于40%，2028年增长大约40%，对核心业务的指引算是非常激进。

AWS：财报的王炸级别数据，业务增长速度加快，已经接近5年来最高增速，如此庞大的技术还能有40%规模的增速，意味着AI云需求不是简单的基数增长，而是需求爆发，并且利润确实漂亮，收入增长39%，营业利润增加55%

总结：

亚马逊财报其实一点也不差，相比来说比谷歌还强，但是两者都同样面度第一个问题，那就是资本支出短期账面无法被营收追赶，FCF持续走肉，甚至恶化

所以，按照亚马逊是谷歌微软的二次验证来看，显然这个二次验证放大了谷歌财报带来的担忧，其次同步发布的还有英特尔财报，算是截至目前本季度最差财报，直接被英特尔带崩。

回顾本周三家云厂商的财报，核心业务都没问题，营收，利润都保持不错的增速，但是就是因为宏观环境的压制下，让投资市场过于与未来的大量资本支出更加担忧导致估值调整，其实这也算健康，起码消除了科技股泡沫担忧。

说直白点，利率高，大家手里的钱更加之前，所以以往的小缺点都会在本季度放大，小瑕疵成为股价短期致命伤！

text:
Further to my post about @NYSE working to bring @HyperliquidX onshore, major credit to @ChairmanSelig and the Trump administration for making all of this experimentation possible. 

There’s only one way of finding out if something is useful to the marketplace and I’m excited for us to find out. I do have some questions:

1. What is the benefit of trading perps on-chain on a regulated exchange? Isn’t the main benefit of trading on-chain to operate in a trustless (aka non-kyc’d) environment in order to minimize friction, and/or to be able to enter into atomic transactions in order to receive what you are buying in realtime? Since a perp is not an asset, that obviously isn’t helpful. 

2. @standuquesne - are you aware that if you trade on Hyperliquid, the world will be able to track your positions and trades in real time? Do you see that as a benefit?

3. Hyperliquid has priority fees - a mechanism that enables market participants to pay to see information first, or even prioritize orders in front of the queue. Is this consistent with CFTC core principles?

4. Will it be possible to combine the liquidity of the offshore order-book with the onshore order-book?

5. If not, wouldn’t it be better to list perps in a traditional (centralized) order-book on a regulated exchange and not have the inefficiencies that on-chain matching introduces?

text:
Brian Schimpf of @AndurilTech on why industrial production is a deterrent in itself, and why technological superiority alone won't win a war:

"These wars are protracted, they are industrial in scale, and if you were to bring it down to one variable, the amount of kilograms that you can throw at each other turns out to probably be the single most important factor."

"I think the technical superiority is a huge advantage. We're not gonna just outproduce China on like dumb ammunition, right? Like that clearly we have to have an edge around our space capabilities, how we can sense, how we can confuse them, how sophisticated our weapons are."

"But I think the part that got so clear outta Ukraine was that industrial production has a deterrence factor... it is critical for winning a conflict."

"When most of the war games with China show that we'd be out of munitions in... like eight days, that's not a deterrence factor really anymore."

"I think the belief for a long time was that [technological superiority] was sufficient, but a low number of really exquisite weapons is not gonna win a conflict."

@SchimpfBrian (September 2025)

text:
a16z's Connor Love says building for defense is how America builds for everything else, because once you can make the parts "to quality and to cost," new markets start to make sense:

"When you build many systems, you also require many subsystems below that. There are really interesting military systems being built today. The corollary: by building towards defense, you also build for a different industry."

"The subsystems that go into some of our military systems are the exact same subsystems that are going to go into the future robotic systems. It's the actuators, the motors, the valves and switches."

"When you can build those to quality and to cost, then all of a sudden other markets that maybe weren't viable make sense... You're going to have this robotic wave that will come in America."

"AI can't turn a wrench yet. They will eventually. And that will be enabled by all that, actuators and switches and subsystems that we built... And we're not going to have to rely on factories in China."

"As you build an industrial base, an industrial base can be used for many things. Down to the component level, I just think we don’t have enough of it in America."

@ConnorLoveCA @espricewright @VirtualElena

币安 CEO 何一 @heyibinance 首次集中回应本次攻击事件，披露了几个关键信息：

- 资金追回： 本次受影响资产总额约 63 亿美元，在全行业协助下，已有约 30 亿美元被冻结，但冻结不等于资金已经追回。

- 恢复提现： 预计未来 42 小时内恢复提现。目前暂停提现已接近 24 小时，主要用于重构安全环境、排查风险。

- 影响范围： 受影响资产占用户资产及公开储备的 2% 多。何一强调，暂停提现并非因为资金规模无法承受，而是出于安全审查需要。

- 资金保障： 币安将使用自有资金弥补被盗资产，大部分资产为加密货币，币安已有较高比例的匹配储备，无需直接从市场买入 63 亿美元代币。

- 后续透明度： 未来几天将更新储备证明（PoR），用户可以查看自身资产储备情况，同时继续推进钱包重构与安全审查。

- 攻击调查： 安全团队初步判断这是一次复杂的复合式攻击，后续将公布详细技术安全审计报告，并与全球执法机构合作追踪攻击者。

何一同时承认，过去在安全投入方面存在不足，币安未来将进一步加大投入。

这次事件的关键已经不只是追回多少资金，而是币安能否在 42 小时内恢复提现，以及能否用实际行动重新建立市场信任。

Further to my post about @NYSE working to bring @HyperliquidX onshore, major credit to @ChairmanSelig and the Trump administration for making all of this experimentation possible. 

There’s only one way of finding out if something is useful to the marketplace and I’m excited for us to find out. I do have some questions:

1. What is the benefit of trading perps on-chain on a regulated exchange? Isn’t the main benefit of trading on-chain to operate in a trustless (aka non-kyc’d) environment in order to minimize friction, and/or to be able to enter into atomic transactions in order to receive what you are buying in realtime? Since a perp is not an asset, that obviously isn’t helpful. 

2. @standuquesne - are you aware that if you trade on Hyperliquid, the world will be able to track your positions and trades in real time? Do you see that as a benefit?

3. Hyperliquid has priority fees - a mechanism that enables market participants to pay to see information first, or even prioritize orders in front of the queue. Is this consistent with CFTC core principles?

4. Will it be possible to combine the liquidity of the offshore order-book with the onshore order-book?

5. If not, wouldn’t it be better to list perps in a traditional (centralized) order-book on a regulated exchange and not have the inefficiencies that on-chain matching introduces?

text:
Today, @a16zfrontier, @fund_defi, and @uniswap stepped into the fight against the Illinois Digital Asset Tax Act. 

The law is already one of the most anti-innovation bills in the country—a tax on transactions just because they're digital. 

Now, it's being made worse through politicized rulemaking that goes well beyond what the law approved—the draft rules would treat many decentralized exchanges (DEXs) as tax-collecting brokers. 

That approach isn't possible to comply with: autonomous software is not a person that can collect a tax. The approach also conflicts with the U.S. Treasury Dept’s classification of DEXs and Illinois’ own Digital Assets and Consumer Protection Act.

The rules also tax Illinois resident's when there isn't even a transaction. That’s like being taxed for moving money from your checking account to your savings account.

Consumers and entrepreneurs in Illinois deserve better.

Fortunately, @CCI and @BlockchainAssn are also challenging the Act in court and will have the entire law thrown out. Until then, we must press Illinois to stop playing politics and to follow its own laws.

The Allora network and the ALLO token contract are secure, and ALLO held outside Binance was not affected.

text:
币安联合创始人何一：

大家好，我是币安的 co-CEO，也是币安的首席客服官

今天早上我们发生了一起黑客攻击事件，导致受影响的资产有 63 亿美金，在所有行业从业者的共同帮助之下，帮我们冻结了 30 亿美金，在这儿也要感谢所有行业从业者的共同帮助

我觉得行业很多时候对我们从业者有很多的误解，但是今天这个事件我觉得是一个很好的机会，证明我们整个行业是一个团结互助、共同友爱，而且是真的在意行业发展的一个行业

第二点，到目前为止我们关闭提币已经快要接近一天了，我们预计会在未来的 42 小时内打开提币

原因是因为，虽然我们确实受影响的资产规模有 30 几亿美金，但它可能占我们所有用户资产和公开储备资产的百分之二点几

为了保证剩下资产的安全，按照我们的工作流程，确实会先关闭提币，确保整个环境是无污染的、对大家没有影响的情况下，我们才会打开提币，所以也感谢您的支持和理解

感谢所有在社区里面为我们发声和解释的朋友们，我觉得这个大恩不言谢，我们回头会做出更多的市场活动来回馈我们的用户们

第三点，这段时间我们除了在重构安全环境、重构钱包设置、做安全审查以外，我们会拿出自有的资金来先匹配这些被盗资产，确保它和我们用户的资产完全匹配

我们也会在未来几天重新更新我们的默克尔树，你可以通过自己的 PoR 去看到自己的资产

因为我们币安平时收的大部分资产都是币，我们自己对这个行业也充满了信心，所以相应的我们大部分资产都是币，和被盗的资产大部分是能匹配上的

确实只有少量的资产需要去场内或场外购买，所以跟一部分朋友理解的、说六十几亿美金要去市场上买资产，这个理解还是略有差异的，也在这里做一个澄清

第四点，我不是一个专业的技术人士，但根据目前安全团队、技术团队的审查，整个攻击是一个非常复杂的复合式攻击，所以我们在操作的过程中也会更加谨慎

我们未来会做出详细的技术安全审计报告，也会公开给大家

我也希望如果您作为一个行业从业者，在安全上能够跟我们一起来共建未来的安全环境标准

最后一点，我觉得整个黑客在 AI 时代已经变成了整个行业的一个威胁，我们会在未来持续地、绝不会放弃对这个黑客的追踪，我们会一查到底，我们会跟全球所有的执法团队合作，来追这个团队、追这笔钱

我们不会让这个行业因为黑客而失去它本来应该有的样子

当然我们有很多做得不对的地方，我们应该更早、更多地去做安全投入，建立更严谨的标准

所以我们在未来，不管是在安全投入上还是在对黑客的打击上面，绝不手软，也邀请更多的行业从业者来跟我们共同维护一个更好的环境

好，谢谢大家 https://t.co/t0YlP6HuQ0

Earlier today, the attacker behind the recent @binance  exploit, apparently in error, sent approximately 8.0M NEWT directly to the NEWT token contract address (0xd0ec028a3d21533fdd200838f39c85b03679285d), along with 17 other tokens: $ANIME, ethereum:0x8290333cef9e6d528dd5618fb97a76f268f3edd4, $ARPA, $BARD, $CELR, ethereum:0x3597bfd533a99c9aa083587b074434e61eb0a258, ethereum:0x0f81001ef0a83ecce5ccebf63eb302c70a39a654, $FTT, $GLM, $HIGH, $HOT, $KNC, $LQTY, $RARE, ethereum:0x259338656198ec7a76c729514d3cb45dfbf768a1, $SIGN and $WOO. These tokens are worth roughly $3.5 million at current prices.

To be clear, the NEWT token contract itself was not compromised.

We have reviewed the contract carefully, and unfortunately these tokens cannot be recovered. The NEWT token contract was built to be immutable: it has no owner or admin, all admin rights were renounced onchain in 2025, and upgrades are permanently disabled. That design exists to protect holders, so that no one, including the Foundation, can ever move or alter their tokens. These safeguards mean there is no way for anyone to retrieve tokens sent to the contract itself.

These tokens are now permanently locked. They are out of the attacker’s control and can never be sold into the market.

We have shared our findings with Binance and we will keep helping however we can.

The traditional model of internet traffic is rapidly becoming outdated.

The internet has entered a new era.

we will need to rebuild and rewrite much of software to adapt to a new, faster pace. 

code used to arrive one drop at a time. soon, if not already, code will be written as if it were a continuous stream, like a violent river twisting and turning as it pleases. 

this is not a new thing: big tech cos have had to deal with this with the enormous scale of their engineering teams. but now ai has brought an incredibly elastic and capable workforce wielded by every engineer. this is your problem now, and the only way to adapt is to evolve your systems so agents - even and especially the ones with little context about the right way of doing things - can thrive. make the easy thing the right thing. 

your codebase is becoming organic architecture. agent contributions grow around the constraints and guardrails you’ve designed. good software engineering matters even more now! and no, the continuous stream of code is not something you have to watch helplessly. be more ambitious and design systems, frameworks, and languages to control the chaos. 

the time for mourning coding is long over

text:
Clean room reverse engineering is 100% legal. It is settled law. The code that my agents have built is novel and unique, and while it compiles to the same bytecode as the on-chain contracts, it is wholly different. I'm not taking anyone's anything.

This was established in two cases, Sega v. Accolade and Sony v. Connectix.

Anyone can reverse engineer anything at any time, to any binary file. Any game, any app, any smart contract.

That means that North Korea can do this. And indeed they have, and over $40m in funds was drained on-chain from private contracts last year alone.

I am not building a launchpad. I'm not building a competitor. I have no interest in that, and I don't think that what makes pumpfun valuable is their contracts. It's their user base, gamified product and implicit trust in their fair launch mechanism.

I am doing this out of personal interest and in the best interests of the public and everyone using this platform: if you're going to put your money into something, you should know your funds are safu.

This is the reason almost all protocol contracts are open source.

Somewhere along the line the gamblers took over from the cypherpunks and people just stopped caring, I guess.

Yesterday we saw the biggest financial hack in history occur.

Could this happen to PF? Absolutely. The skill level of a thousand agents hammering away at the security vulnerabilities in a contract is now greater than the best human auditing teams in the world.

The only thing that can stop a bad guy with a model is a good guy with a model.

We need to live in an open source world where agents are constantly attacking all financial infrastructure, finding the flaws and reporting them to teams to fix instead of letting bad actors leverage them to keep draining literally billions.

author: EggheadCobra
quoted_text:
For a while now, I've noticed that some people are still confused about Psylocke, who she is, and which is which. Psylocke is known for having one of the messiest stories in all of Marvel, so how about I try my best to explain it as simply as possible?

- There are three Psylockes.
Betsy Braddock, Kwannon, and Sai.

- Betsy Braddock was the original Psylocke, Kwannon is an assassin, Sai is a demon slayer.

- Betsy and Kwannon are both in Earth-616, Sai is from an alternate universe.

- Betsy and Kwannon had an extremely messy and complicated body swap story that ended in Kwannon dying, and Betsy being permanently stuck in Kwannon's body.

- A few years ago, Kwannon was resurrected in her original body, and Betsy was given her body back.

- Betsy became Captain Britain, Kwannon is now Psylocke.

Fun facts about them!
- Betsy was stuck in Kwannon's body for over 20 years of Marvel's publications.
- Kwannon is not her real name, and it is yet to be revealed.
- In X-Men: Demon Days, Sai killed her world's Venom with the help of Hulkmaru (Her world's Hulk). Galacta gave Psylocke the Venom accessory as a reminder of one of her greatest victories.

Many speculate that Sai was chosen for Marvel Rivals because the devs wanted to distance themselves from the Betsy Kwannon debacle, which, in my opinion, was the smart thing to do.

This was only a heavily simplified version of Psylocke. If you'd like to look more into their backstories, just be warned that it gets very messy, especially the body swap.

text:
Earlier today, the attacker behind the recent @binance  exploit, apparently in error, sent approximately 8.0M NEWT directly to the NEWT token contract address (0xd0ec028a3d21533fdd200838f39c85b03679285d), along with 17 other tokens: $ANIME, ethereum:0x8290333cef9e6d528dd5618fb97a76f268f3edd4, $ARPA, $BARD, $CELR, ethereum:0x3597bfd533a99c9aa083587b074434e61eb0a258, ethereum:0x0f81001ef0a83ecce5ccebf63eb302c70a39a654, $FTT, $GLM, $HIGH, $HOT, $KNC, $LQTY, $RARE, ethereum:0x259338656198ec7a76c729514d3cb45dfbf768a1, $SIGN and $WOO. These tokens are worth roughly $3.5 million at current prices.

To be clear, the NEWT token contract itself was not compromised.

We have reviewed the contract carefully, and unfortunately these tokens cannot be recovered. The NEWT token contract was built to be immutable: it has no owner or admin, all admin rights were renounced onchain in 2025, and upgrades are permanently disabled. That design exists to protect holders, so that no one, including the Foundation, can ever move or alter their tokens. These safeguards mean there is no way for anyone to retrieve tokens sent to the contract itself.

These tokens are now permanently locked. They are out of the attacker’s control and can never be sold into the market.

We have shared our findings with Binance and we will keep helping however we can.

quoted_text:
Here is English translation for Engilsh frens:

Hi everyone. I'm Binance's co-CEO and also its Chief Customer Service Officer, Yi He.

This morning we suffered a hack that affected $6.3 billion in assets. With help from people across the industry, $3 billion has been frozen. I want to thank everyone for their all-out support. People outside often misunderstand those of us in this industry, but today showed that the industry can unite, look after one another, and truly care about its future.

Withdrawals have now been paused for nearly a day, and we expect to reopen them within the next 42 hours. Although more than $3 billion in assets was affected, that is only about 2% of our total user assets and public reserves. To keep the remaining assets safe, our procedures require us to pause withdrawals first. We will reopen only after fully confirming that the environment is secure, uncontaminated, and poses no risk to you. Thank you for your understanding and support, and thank you to everyone in the community who spoke up and explained things on our behalf. Words can't express our gratitude, and we will give back to users through more campaigns in the future.

During this time, besides rebuilding our security environment, rebuilding our wallet setup, and carrying out security audits, we will use our own funds to cover the stolen assets up front, so that user assets remain fully backed 1:1. In the coming days we will update the Merkle tree, and you will be able to check your assets through Proof of Reserves. Most of what Binance earns is already in tokens, and because we believe in this industry, most of our own reserves already match the stolen assets by token. Only a very small amount needs to be bought on or off exchange. Rumors online say we must buy more than $6 billion of assets on the market. That isn't quite accurate, so I want to clear it up.

I'm not a technical expert myself, but based on our security and technical teams' investigation so far, this was a highly sophisticated, multi-layered attack, so we will be especially careful in the steps ahead. We will publish a detailed technical security audit report to the public. We also hope security professionals across the industry will work with us to build future security standards.

In the AI era, hacking has become a serious threat to the entire industry. We will never give up pursuing the hackers. We will get to the bottom of this and work closely with law enforcement worldwide to track down this group and recover the funds. We will not let hackers take away the prosperity this industry deserves.

Of course, we fell short in many ways. We should have invested more in security, earlier, and set stricter standards. Going forward, we will not hold back, either in security investment or in fighting hackers. We also sincerely invite more of our industry peers to join us in keeping this industry healthy.

Thank you, everyone.

text:
Huffman's quote is striking, but the bigger tell is the number he gave. Search referrals are dropping by more than a million a week. That's incredibly brutal.

I'd push back a bit on "destroying" though. The way I see it, the web always ran on a trade. Sites let Google read everything for free, and Google sent clicks back. AI answers kept the reading part and quietly dropped the clicks. 68% of US Google searches now end without a click, and chatbots send publishers something like 0.01% of their traffic. The content didn't stop being valuable. Sites just stopped getting paid for it.

So what does a company do when the trade stops working? It tries to charge. And to charge, you first have to be able to say no. That's why Reddit going mostly logged-in was the most interesting part of the call to me. Huffman said it "lets us better protect the Reddit corpus of data." In other words, no more free reads.
The catch is Google. You can't block its AI without disappearing from its search, since it's the same crawler. Hard to negotiate when your only alternative is walking away from your biggest traffic source.

And the licensing money so far is small. Reddit's "other revenue," which includes licensing, was $48M last quarter. Ads were $847M. That gap is a lot of what the stock is wrestling with.

I'm also not sold on "forever." AI still needs fresh human content to be any good, and it's eating the economics that pay for that content. At some point someone has to pay for it again, or the answers get worse. That gives places like Reddit more leverage than this week's chart suggests.

The old deal is dead. The new one just hasn't been priced yet.

text:
NOVA: Emission Split Update for Data Generation Fund
Owner 26% / Miners 33% / Validators 41%

With the launch of eTAO, subnet owners can now adjust how emissions are distributed. NOVA will be updating its split to allocate more resources toward what we believe is the highest-impact investment we can make in the subnet's future: experimental data generation.

Wet lab data is the best investment we can make both to prove out what the subnet produces and to increase the value of what gets built on top of it.

Data is the bottleneck
AI-driven drug discovery faces a fundamental constraint: the quality of our predictions is ultimately limited by the experimental data available to train and validate them.

Much of today's publicly available drug discovery data is fragmented across studies, generated using different experimental protocols, and inconsistent in quality and coverage.

Generating high-quality experimental data allows us to address that limitation directly. It gives miners better ground truth for model development, provides independent validation of their predictions, and helps us identify which approaches actually translate into experimental success.

The industry is making the same bet.

Some of the largest investments in AI-driven biology are now directed toward generating the experimental data necessary to train and validate better models.

Biohub committed $400M of a $500M, five-year initiative to data generation, infrastructure and measurement technology, and later expanded into a $1.8B effort backed by Meta, Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs, who collectively committed $300M.

The OpenAI Foundation gave $15M to OpenADMET to generate public ADME datasets, which will be used in prospective blind challenges against newly measured experimental data. Octant continues the high-throughput data generation behind it. 

Leash Bio used a $9.3M seed round to scale data collection for a foundational medicinal chemistry model, producing a dataset that screened 133 million molecules against each protein. 

Anthropic has set up a physical biology lab in the Bay Area.

What the additional funds will support
The additional owner allocation will go into a dedicated R&D fund for wet lab data generation.

1. ADME model training competition. The first use of the fund is generating the experimental data behind our ADME competition, currently in design and development. High-quality, standardized ADME data is what turns a competition from a benchmark into something that produces models with real predictive value.

2. Advancing assets under development. Where it makes sense, the fund can also support experimental work that moves our in-development assets forward.

Why this benefits the entire NOVA ecosystem
We believe generating experimental data is one of the most effective ways to increase the long-term value of the subnet.

For miners, better datasets and scientifically grounded evaluations create opportunities to develop more capable models, compete on meaningful performance improvements, and contribute work with greater real-world utility.

For validators, stronger experimental benchmarks improve the ability to assess model quality and reward useful contributions.

For tokenholders, better models, experimentally validated discoveries, and progress toward valuable therapeutic assets can strengthen NOVA's competitive position and long-term commercial potential.

The economic opportunity extends beyond any individual competition. We are building an increasingly capable scientific discovery platform, and the data generated through our R&D efforts can become a compounding asset for the entire ecosystem.

Miner incentives remain strong
Miners will still receive a meaningfully larger share than the owner (33% vs. 26%), and we believe the rewards will preserve healthy, competitive incentives for participation. Better data and better-validated competitions also make the work miners do more valuable over time.

Protecting token health
Funds from the R&D allocation will be converted to cover lab costs gradually, distributed over time rather than sold in size, to limit market impact and preserve token health.

The bottom line
We think this is the single best thing we can do to accelerate our progress, increase our chance of success, and create value for everyone with a stake in NOVA, including miners, validators, and tokenholders. It is time for us to scale real-world validation.

Saw a few discussions about size of hack, why impact to bitcoin price is small, etc. 👇 

$6.3 billion is the biggest in USD terms, but not in BTC terms. MtGox was 650,000 BTC!

Other important numbers to consider:

% of bitcoin (in relation to BTC total supply), ie, market impact. MtGox is big there again at 5%+.

Number of users impacted, and % of user assets impacted. MtGox (the largest CEX at the time) and FTX (not small) were all near 100% of users and their asseets.

Most important: Who is impacted? Does the platform cover it all? (only one victim), as in recent two CEX cases and Binance.

Obviously, still a major disaster for the industry, Binance (and me). It hurts, but we survive. 

Most importantly, we protect our users.

New challenge on Yukon: Circuit Breaker https://t.co/vpuIh2CnbR

It took 38 years to raise the best proven circuit lower bound from 3n to 3.1n. Days before this launch, an AI model pushed it to 3.5n.

A circuit lower bound is the fewest logic gates any circuit needs to solve a problem. Prove that a problem in NP needs more gates than any polynomial and you’ve shown P ≠ NP. That would settle whether every problem that’s easy to check is also easy to solve, one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems.

We’re still far from that bound. Circuit Breaker, built with UCLA Math+AI, is where the push continues.

“It is time to dream bigger and aim much higher,” says Amit Sahai, Professor of Computer Science at UCLA.

For decades, the deepest questions in complexity theory moved in tenths, because only a handful of people could work on them. Anyone with an agent can take a shot now.

Circuit Breaker on @YukonResearch, built with UCLA Math+AI, opens circuit lower bounds to everyone.
author: eigenlabs
quoted_text:
New challenge on Yukon: Circuit Breaker https://t.co/vpuIh2CnbR

It took 38 years to raise the best proven circuit lower bound from 3n to 3.1n. Days before this launch, an AI model pushed it to 3.5n.

A circuit lower bound is the fewest logic gates any circuit needs to solve a problem. Prove that a problem in NP needs more gates than any polynomial and you’ve shown P ≠ NP. That would settle whether every problem that’s easy to check is also easy to solve, one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems.

We’re still far from that bound. Circuit Breaker, built with UCLA Math+AI, is where the push continues.

“It is time to dream bigger and aim much higher,” says Amit Sahai, Professor of Computer Science at UCLA.

text:
说个暴论：用了一个月 Grok Bot，我觉得它就是 Hermes Agent 的上位替代🔥

我以前花了很多时间折腾 Hermes Agent，最主要的目的就是想让它成为我自己的个人助手，帮我打理生活和工作上的各种琐事

其实我的需求并不复杂，主要就是这几个方面：

1、一些简单的日常提醒和定时任务

2、通过 Skill 或 MCP 连接各种软件，帮我完成一些自动化任务

3、处理文档，比如直接连接飞书 CLI，就可以完成很多工作

很多人肯定会问，为什么不直接使用 GPT 这些生态比较完整的产品？

其实我也花时间研究过，但整体用下来，发现很多国内的软件都不太兼容

最简单的就是 GPT，你需要单独使用它的 APP，而且像飞书、夸克网盘这些国内常用的软件，也没有对应的官方应用可以直接连接

虽然 Notion、GitHub 这些国外软件都有对应的应用，只需要安装并授权就可以使用，而且支持 Web、APP 和电脑端无缝连接

但如果想把国内常用的软件也全部打通，就没那么简单了

很多时候还是需要自己通过 CLI、Skill 或 MCP 等方式去连接

所以当时我就找到了 Hermes Agent

我花了很多时间，把它整个框架从记忆管理、上下文压缩比例，到模型调度和工具调用，基本都做了一遍补全

像我常用的几个工具，其实都已经做好了对应的 Skill 和授权，只需要调用相应的软件或者流程，就可以自动完成工作

这一套确实让我的工作效率得到了很大的改善

但是后来我慢慢发现了一个问题：

Hermes Agent 什么都能自己折腾，但也意味着什么都需要自己维护

每次模型更新或者迭代，我都要重新整理模型比例和调度方案

尤其是整个记忆框架，我还做过几次重构，每次改完都要重新设置，或者让 AI 帮我质检

而且 Hermes Agent 本身也经常升级，有时候升级会导致我原来的框架出问题，严重的时候连定时任务都没办法正常执行

这就让我觉得很麻烦

后来我开始使用 Grok Bot，发现以前在 Hermes Agent 上做的绝大部分功能，其实都可以迁移过来

因为 Grok Bot 本质上就是一个 Agent 加上一台 Linux 服务器

以前可以在 Hermes Agent 上安装的工具、配置的 Skill、连接的 MCP，很多都能用类似的方法在 Grok Bot 上实现

只需要做好对应的授权，还有配置的备份和还原就行

而且 Grok Bot 有一个很大的优势，就是很多基础功能官方已经帮你做好了

比如密码服务、手机应用连接这些，不需要再自己写一套东西，只需要授权就能使用

最重要的是，我不用再天天去维护整个 Agent 框架，也不用因为模型更新、记忆调整或者版本升级，反复折腾原来那一套配置

这一个月使用下来，我越来越觉得 Grok Bot 更符合我最开始折腾 Hermes Agent 的目的

当然，如果你喜欢完全掌控底层框架，Hermes Agent 依然非常不错

但对我来说，我需要的不是一个需要天天维护的 Agent，而是一个真正能帮我处理事情的个人助手

现在越来越多的人在我的推荐下开始使用 Grok Bot，我也挺开心的

希望官方后续能做得越来越好，尤其是支付、网络直连和国内软件的兼容性这些方面

毕竟对于普通用户来说，能直接用、不需要自己折腾太多东西，就已经很舒服了

text:
SpaceX just financed about $40B of GPUs on 5-year leases. Lenders don't take a 5-year payback unless they expect the chips to keep earning that long.

AI compute is now financeable infrastructure, and that's the market Aethir is building for.
author: AethirCloud
quoted_text:
A lot of people ask me how a GPU finance lease works. SpaceX just signed the biggest GPU financing ever, about $40B with Apollo, so here it is step by step from SpaceX's own 8-K.

Step 1: the lender buys the GPUs. An Apollo-managed entity will buy NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPU pods and lease them to SpaceX for data centers SpaceX picks. SpaceX pays back the full cost over the lease, so it's really buying them on credit.

Step 2: the GPUs arrive in tranches. Each tranche gets its own lease of about 5 to 5.25 years, starting when it's delivered. The first are expected in the first half of 2027.

Step 3: SpaceX pays rent every quarter, in advance. Each payment is one-twentieth of that tranche's cost, plus fixed-rate interest on what's still owed. Twenty quarters is five years, so each tranche is fully paid off by the end of its lease. Across all tranches that's about $40B of principal, roughly $2B a quarter once everything is running.

Step 4: the money comes from the biggest pools of capital out there. Apollo leads, Goldman Sachs structured it, and BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management and KKR-advised accounts are anchors.

So why lease when you could pay cash? SpaceX's CFO says it's seeing payback periods of less than a year on its AI infrastructure. If a GPU pays for itself inside a year, spreading the cost over five keeps cash free to build faster.

And it's already spreading. The same day, Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi and Morgan Stanley put together a $63B vehicle that will buy Broadcom's custom AI chips and lease them to Anthropic.

The part I find most interesting is what the lenders signed up for. They're comfortable being paid back over five years, which says a lot about how long they expect these chips to keep earning. What is clear is that the biggest credit investors now treat AI compute as financeable infrastructure, and I think that's what keeps the buildout funded.

text:
Agent loop is like stochastic gradient descent, just without gradient.

Overnight the DeepSeek optimization gave us 2.32ms/step, way below our educated guess of a 2.5ms/step floor, and improving. I asked AI to draw out some statistics and I think it's interesting.

1. We didn't ask agents to do so, but empirically it catches early gains first and then improvements start slowing down.

2. Of course, we haven't really tried permuting the experiments and see their independent improvements, but eyeballing some, my observation is that indeed the later ones are more incremental.

3. Convergence seems to be consistent. It's not like the agents are running out of ideas.

4. I looked at the acceptance rate of experiments. Initially it was really high - makes sense. But then it kinda stayed consistent around 46%.

5. Gains do look like exponentially decaying and not heavy tailed. 

6. SGD has seen great improvement via rigorous mathematical explorations like momentum SGD, hessian-free approaches, ADAM, Muon, etc.

7. The problem is... discrete optimization on a group of agents is hard. There really isn't any coordinates or gradients. Landscape isn't fixed and all we are talking about is something like a sample - reject_or_accept - resample loop.

8. What's the best heuristics and what's the best algo? It feels like Kalman filtering / reject sampling / data driven markov-chain monte-carlo to me but exact math is still unclear.

I am really looking forward to possibly running larger experiments and looking into more traces of such. This seems to be engineering and research combined in one.

It took 38 years to raise the best proven circuit lower bound from 3n to 3.1n. Days before this launch, an AI model pushed it to 3.5n.

A circuit lower bound is the fewest logic gates any circuit needs to solve a problem. Prove that a problem in NP needs more gates than any polynomial and you’ve shown P ≠ NP. That would settle whether every problem that’s easy to check is also easy to solve, one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems.

We’re still far from that bound. Circuit Breaker, built with UCLA Math+AI, is where the push continues.

“It is time to dream bigger and aim much higher,” says Amit Sahai, Professor of Computer Science at UCLA.
