text:
Finality Is Not Negotiable: On the Binance Breach and Calls for Rollbacks
My thoughts are with everyone emotionally affected by this week's Binance breach. Since then, some ideas have circulated: protocol-level asset freezes, and a coordinated multi-year "rollback window" across major chains. Both misdiagnose the problem, and both would destroy the property that makes public blockchains worth securing: settlement finality.

1. This was a custody failure, not a protocol failure. The attacker compromised Binance's internal systems and obtained valid signatures. Ethereum, and nine other chains, executed them exactly as designed. When a vault is breached, you fix the vault. You don't rewrite the ledger.

2. Enforcement already works, at the edge. Within hours, issuers and intermediaries froze roughly $3 billion of the stolen assets without a single change to any base layer. That is the system working. Issuers, exchanges and off-ramps act under legal process, while an immutable public ledger preserves a permanent forensic trail. Stolen funds can move, but they cannot hide.

3. Rollbacks end finality, and the switch itself is the attack surface. By the time validators coordinate, stolen funds would already be swapped, bridged and off-ramped. Rewinding would unwind everyone else: payments, loans, liquidations, L2 settlements. "Only three communities need to agree" is the vulnerability, not the safeguard. Any mechanism that lets a few validator sets rewrite history becomes the prime target for regulators, courts, and the very state-backed groups tied to this breach. Ethereum intervened once, in 2016, as a year-old network with a single contract at stake. It learned the cost and has not done so since.

4. EIP-7702 did what it is specified to do. Binance’s controls had a weakness.  
On Ethereum, the attacker used an EIP-7702 authorization to turn one Binance hot wallet into a sweeper. A 7702 delegation requires a valid signature from the wallet’s own key, and the specification is explicit that delegated code gains full control of the account. The failure was a signing pipeline that approved that delegation outside its own security checks. More than half the stolen funds moved without 7702 at all, including on chains that don’t support it. The lesson is for implementers: custodians must treat delegation authorizations as the highest-privilege operation they sign.

Real hardening happens in engineering: smart accounts, MPC custody, withdrawal delays, client diversity, and post-quantum migration. Institutions choose Ethereum because no one can turn the base layer against them. 

Ethereum does not compromise credible neutrality and absolute final settlement—the core guarantees that make Ethereum worth protecting.

That guarantee is not up for negotiation.

text:
@TalBeerySec has an interesting theory on the multi-billion-dollar Binance hack. It was a boring access control policy failure of using a default-allow instead of default-deny policy on the signing service. The attacker signed something spicy the defenders hadn’t thought to prohibit them from doing.
Of course, an attacker first had to get access to the service, which might be the exciting part, but shouldn’t have been enough.
This seems to be supported by others and matches, e.g., Inca’s timeline of the hack. The attack has been attributed to North Korea, specifically TraderTraitor/Lazarus, by a few chain analytics firms.

The interesting point: if Tal is right, this wasn’t an insane AI break, it was a boring policy screw-up. An attacker got control of a signing service where the last line of defense was a policy that denied them the ability to sign malicious transactions. Exchanges have to have hot wallets, where the keys are often stored in secure hardware attached to a server. Attackers can’t get the keys from the hardware, but they can ask the hardware to sign things, such as a transaction paying the attacker all of the money. A sane secure architecture assumes attacks might compromise those servers, limiting the damage even if they get that far. Binance had one.

For example (and I'm making these up for exposition), they could only sign transactions to existing Binance addresses. Or limit the amount of funds that can be moved. But, if Tal is right, this was enforced by a policy blocking specific actions that were harmful. That list might have been exhaustive at the time it was written, but the smart contract standards apparently changed, adding new operations that could be abused. Those were not on the deny list because they didn’t exist at the time the deny list was written. So the attacker could sign transactions using them.

text:
In 2014 I went nearly a week without sleep. I was running PayPal and attackers were inside our corporate network. They'd compromised an eBay employee's laptop, got onto the VPN, taken over a domain controller and made themselves domain admins. eBay and PayPal were one company then, on one Windows network. They stole 145M eBay user records, then came for the segregated vault holding PayPal's card credentials. We fought them off. They never got in, but they got close. Too close.

Yesterday Binance lost ~$6.3B in what looks like the same way. A DevOps engineer's laptop, then a service inside the withdrawal stack, then withdrawals the signer approved because they came from a trusted source. Hot wallets emptied in under four hours. No key was stolen.

Nobody broke cryptography or a ledger. They found someone with access and used the trust that came with it. Banks get hit exactly the same way.

2016: attackers inside Bangladesh Bank used its own SWIFT access to send $951M of payment orders to the NY Fed. $81M was lost. The rest was held because an unrelated sanctions filter tripped on the word "Jupiter". That was luck, and it only worked because wires took days to settle.

June 2025: an IT employee at C&M Software, which connects Brazilian banks to Pix, sold his credentials for about $2,700. Attackers used them to send fake Pix transfers out of six institutions' reserve accounts at the central bank. ~$140M in under three hours.

August 2025: stolen vendor credentials at Sinqia, another Pix connector. ~R$710M out of HSBC and one other institution in a single afternoon. The central bank froze most of it, after it had already moved.

Same attack every time. Speed is what changed. When settlement took days, a filter, a correspondent bank or someone in ops could catch a bad payment. Pix, FedNow, SEPA Instant and blockchains settle in seconds. Payment security was mostly built for the slow world.

PayPal's card and user data survived 2014 because domain admin on the corp network couldn't unlock it quickly enough, and our alerting caught the unusual activity on the network. That's the model. Approval policy no laptop or vendor login can reach. Velocity and anomaly limits enforced outside the system that sends. Dynamic caps on what any one wallet, account or service can move per hour. All of it in real time.

About $3B of what left Binance has been frozen, almost all of it stablecoins. The $1.4B in bitcoin is sitting in 19 wallets and nobody can touch it. I don't think that's the problem. For decades the ability to reverse a wire or a card charge let a lot of weak security slide. You either stop the transfer before it's signed or you eat the loss.

Nothing about the technology failed here. The chains processed exactly the transactions they were handed. Binance's own systems handed them the wrong ones because an engineer's laptop was compromised. That's operational security. eBay in 2014, Bangladesh Bank and two Pix connectors all failed at it on their own rails.

In 2014 the attackers never reached the vault. If they had, the fraud losses would have been the small part. PayPal existed so people could pay without handing their card details to every merchant on the internet. We held those details so they didn't have to. Losing them would have broken the one thing the company was built on, and I'm not sure we would have recovered.

I expect blockchains and digital assets to become the standard way money moves. Every custodian of digital assets, or of fiat on a real-time rail, is in that position now. The controls have to adapt to settlement in seconds, crypto or not.

author: SUOHA_AI
quoted_text:
一图看懂--交易所历史重大安全事件！

我把过去 14 年整个加密市场 共15 起最重大的交易所被盗与暴雷事件全扒了一遍，黑客累计卷走的资金超过 45 亿美元（若按现值计算超数百亿美元）

我猛然发现：作为美国最大的加密交易所，Coinbase @Coinbase 已经创立了 14 年，管着几千亿美元资产、占据全网近 12% 的加密总市值，居然【一次都没有被盗过】！？

连贝莱德、富达这些华尔街正规军，全美 80% 以上现货 ETF 底仓都只敢指定它独家托管，于是我深度扒了一下Coinbase的底层安全架构👇

───

1. 98% 以上的币放在断网的冷钱包，热钱包只留不到 2% 零钱

Coinbase 把 98% 以上的用户资产全部存放在物理断网、黑客根本碰不到的离线冷钱包里，平时连网的热钱包里只有不到 2% 的零钱用来应付日常提现

这样设计的硬逻辑是：黑客哪怕有通天的本事攻破热钱包，最多也就偷走 2% 的零钱，这笔损失 Coinbase 靠自有的储备金和商业保险能 100% 赔得起，从根本上锁死了暴雷上限。

2. 物理上根本没有完整私钥这玩意（MPC 碎片化多方计算）
传统交易所丢币，都是因为“私钥被人偷了”。但在 Coinbase，私钥被拆成了多个碎片，分散在不同城市、不同技术架构的安全设备里。转账签名时各方协作计算，但在任何一台机器上、任何时间里，完整的私钥都从未被拼合过

连这套核心算法 cb-mpc 都在 GitHub 上全部开源了，还通过了德国顶级安全机构 Cure53 的严格审计，拒绝任何黑箱操作

3. 军工级单向数据传输

很多交易所冷钱包出事，都是因为管理人员要签名时“临时连了 Wi-Fi”或者“用 U 盘拷贝数据”

Coinbase 是全球第一家直接采用美军 NSA 和英国 NCSC 军工标准的跨域解决方案（CDS）的托管商。冷钱包数据通过硬件级单向过滤进出，物理上彻底断绝人为联网泄密的可能。

4. 核心安全软件 100% 自己写（绝不给第三方软件背锅）

2025 年 Bybit 被盗 15 亿美元，不是自己私钥丢了，而是用的第三方开源多签工具 Safe 的开发人员电脑被黑、前端被下毒，导致签名人盲签被骗

Coinbase 的密钥和冷钱包代码 12 年来全部自己写，坚决不用外部第三方的现成工具

5. 转账前独立自动验真（防黑客伪造提款指令）
刚刚 9 月 24 日 Bitget 被偷 3.5 亿美金，就是因为黑客黑进后台伪造了提现数据，骗过了自动放行系统

而在 Coinbase，任何一笔资金出库前，系统都会在签名流程之外独立做三重防伪：校验收款地址白名单、检测数据是否被篡改、识别反常大额流量，绝不让假冒指令蒙混过关

6. 德勤每年深度验资审计 + 银行级信托牌照（不可能挪用一分钱）
Coinbase 是纳斯达克上市公司，拥有纽约州 DFS 信托牌照与联邦 OCC 信托银行牌照，资产受美国最高级别监管

每年由国际四大会计所之一的德勤（Deloitte）出具 SOC 1 和 SOC 2 独立安全审计，美元法币更是存在摩根大通（JPMorgan）等大银行做隔离托管并享 FDIC 保险，从法律上彻底杜绝了 FTX 式挪用用户资金的可能

───
所以我仍然推荐有对资产安全/合规性有要求的用户可以尝试一下Coinbase交易所！并且没有CRS!

Coinbase 现在仍然支持大陆身份证注册，欢迎使用我的邀请码，一对一解答：

三年后，两万。
2022 年 FTX 暴雷，BTC 跌到一万五。
两年后，十万。

现在是最好的时机。
buy the dip，低买高卖，大道至简。

quoted_text:
THIS 4B MODEL JUST MADE LONG-CONTEXT MEMORY WAY MORE INTERESTING.

256K context. A fixed 72 MiB KV cache. No cache growth as context gets longer.

Meet EdgeRock-4B, the new open-source model from Rock Matrix.

Here's why it matters.

Traditional LLMs need more KV cache as context grows. EdgeRock takes a different approach.

It combines recurrent state, local attention, and Rock Memory Anchors (RMA), preserving learned KV records in a fixed-capacity bank.

This lets the model retrieve information from much earlier in the context, even after it leaves the local attention window.

Now, look at the reported results:

→ 6.42× the output throughput of Qwen3.5-4B. That's 12,124 tokens/s at 512 concurrent sequences on a single 80GB Hopper GPU.

→ 99.1% less KV cache at 256K context. Just 72 MiB per sequence, constant from 4K to 256K.

→ 233.7 tokens/s during long generation, even with 128K input tokens followed by 128K generated tokens.

→ 82.9% mean pass@1 on AIME 2024–2026. The strongest evaluated bounded-state baseline reaches 18.8%, including comparisons with 14B-class models.

And that's the real breakthrough.

Instead of growing KV cache with context length, EdgeRock keeps it fixed while retaining access to selected older information.

Long context. Constant KV cache. Strong reasoning.

All in an open-source 4B model.

Books just went live. So how does it work? Books are Social Capital Markets built around stock token trading. Anyone can come in and launch their own Book, which launches a token that can be paired with $PONS, $AI, $STONKBROKER, robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c, $ETH or $CASHCAT.

Each Book starts with an anti snipe launch. The funds raised during the anti snipe window and 75% of the LP go into an ERC-6551 token bound account (TBA) linked to the Mancer DEX aggregator. Creators preselect up to 16 tokens they want to trade during their epoch, which can last anywhere from 7 to 365 days, and they can add two more Mancer verified tokens while the epoch is running. The goal is to generate as much profit as possible trading on Robinhood Chain.

In the video below I launched a 7 day Book, and I'll be trading several of the top Robinhood Chain tokens and stock tokens. When the 7 days are up, the Book token ceases to exist. Holders burn their tokens to claim their share of the TBA. Book tokens also bond into Uniswap v3 and v4 pools, so holders can stake to claim their share of the LP fees. The book creator gets to keep 20% of the net profit which they generate.

Traders will naturally need to start small and build a history as effective Book creators. Over time that should lead to larger launches, with the best traders in the space rewarded for top tier timing and execution, which improves the Robinhood trenches as a whole.

分享一下我对各个链的看法 抛砖引玉 欢迎大家一起交流想法

一、ETH链
PEPE自然是最近话题度最高的 很多大户超大户 可能也有隐含的机构在车上 可能有成为后续MEME行情的领头羊

但是我还是打算是集中聊一下比较近期的 最多是近几个月出现的代币 目前生态最好的我仍然觉得是 $IMD 生态 
这个币本身从frenpet转过来 有着实名靠谱的dev 加上我近期加了讨论社区 的确整体氛围属于不错的
@mingwei1996 @Despite_zmw 就非常专注于IMD生态的分享

二、Base链
我仍然对 @o1_exchange 平台上的 $worth 最看好 而且官方和o1发射台也对meme的推动比较一致
上一次base的行情是在o1平台跑出来了basecat、bluechip之类高市值代币 验证了只要base愿意花精力时间来推动 那么仍然可以将代币通过一到两周慢慢推动到50M以上
这个worth就给我一种basecat的启动感觉 而且本身概念上也是一个非常正向的审美 我会坚持持有手里的这部分
@stambouli_o1 也在一直进行平台的推广工作 可以继续多多关注o1 exchange

三、BSC链
BSC链我拿不准具体的代币 就想回顾一下目前的状况 

我的评价是BSC链有着巨大的资金 但目前的仍旧处于相对混沌状态 拿不准应该买哪个龙头
BSC的主线偏向ai wallet agent相关 但是具体代币是轮动的 没跑出固定的让人眼前非常新的东西

BSC这个链一向是追热点的 之前可以跑出Marscoin、牛来 近期推出Agent ID之后有着Gang、Ptah作为初期应用 后面蝴蝶和four也跟进模仿 但是这些走势冲高之后回落到ATH的四分之一到五分之一了 可以说没有完全接力上去 反而 $jagent 一个打钱的资金盘跑了起来 的确有些匪夷所思 我是看不太懂的
meme方面今晚刚出现的SAFU FUND表现很强势 但能走到多少也是未知数 属于是新闻热点类型的meme

我个人感觉这个链的资金似乎集中到了接近10M左右就有点难形成合力了 大资金会快速去寻找下一个叙事 

我认为对于目前的BSC市场来说 Agent ID的玩法 还没出现让人眼前一亮的现象级的东西出来 我会建议大家多花点精力在Agent ID上 
最终等到那个大家一致认可的优秀应用出来 一起合力把它推上去

四、Robinhood链
这个链由于官方最近有一些对MEME部分的扶持 也跑出来了一些meme和应用
这里面我最看好的是 $PIZZA 
其实 $WOFL 也是个很好的概念 也给了一些抄底的机会 但是目前从启动的资金量、走势以及背景来看 PIZZA 是略优于WOFL的 如果只选一个 那么我就会买入 $PIZZA 

五、SOL链
我会选 $jeff
我的理由是 在pumpfun最近的迷之操作后 许多散户已经开始不太喜欢pumpfun 而且对于发射台可能有一定程度额审美疲劳了 
我已经许久没看到新的比较好的发射台代币能跑出来了 
市面上可能有一万个发射台 但是每个发射台除了本币发射不出来第二个代币

那么此时跑出一个反发射台概念的meme类型 反而对市场来说是另类的 
当然 $jeff 本身也包含了一些我个人对meme类型的喜好 希望后续它的走势不要辜负我的判断

Do NOT buy a 512GB Mac Studio ‼️

Two 256GB Mac Studio M5 Ultras are ~$700 cheaper and have ~1.7x faster prefill and decode

Price: $22,299 vs $21,598
Both are the 36-core CPU / 80-core GPU

You can connect 2x 256GB with one Thunderbolt 5 cable + RDMA, which is fast enough to run one model across both

Prefill (compute)
- 1x 512 does ~135 TFLOPS
- 2x 256 does ~215-245 TFLOPS
- Apple claims up to 3x for a 4-Mac cluster, which works out to ~1.7x for two

Decode (bandwidth)
- 1x 512 has 1.2 TB/s
- 2x 256 gets ~1.9-2.2 TB/s effective
- With tensor parallelism each box reads its half of the weights at the same time, which works out to ~1.7x for two

GLM-5.3 goes from ~33-40 tok/s to ~55-70
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash goes from ~45-60 tok/s to ~75-100
Both are 4-bit with spec decode on, estimated from M3 and M5 Ultra benchmarks

If you want Qwen3.8-Flash-Next or GLM-5.3-Flash, a single 256 already runs them well and you don’t need either setup. The 512GB question is about DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (552B) and GLM-5.3 (753B), tied as the best open models on Artificial Analysis v5. They need 310-420GB at 4-bit, so neither fits on one 256

In the real world, Canadians can’t afford anything. Food, fuel, rent, mortgages.

Mark Carney promised to make it better. Everything is worse.

Today, he and the Liberals are distracting Canadians again with yet another grand summit about Europe. Big talk. What’s the result?

Not one tariff reduced. Not one of the nine European holdout countries has ratified the trade agreement Canada already has with them. Barriers to Canadian beef and pork exports to Europe remain. And now the EU is threatening a carbon tariff on Canadian steel, aluminum, cement and other goods.

Worse, there was lots of talk at the summit about aligning Canada with the insane European taxes, debt, immigration and anti-oil and gas policies that have left parts of Europe bankrupt and burning.

Does any of this lower your mortgage payments, rent, grocery bills or gas prices, back here in the real world?

Of course not.

Time to get real. We have mouths to feed. Bills to pay. Crime to stop. Borders to secure. And money to save.

🚨 Canada is finished, Carney signed over the entire Country and all the provinces to the EU as well as all citizen rights. 
Alberta independence was the only way out but if you say that now Danielle Smith doesn’t want you in her party. 

While you were working your 3rd job because you are taxed too much, Prime Minister Mark Carney and EU leaders quietly signed the "Alliance for the Future" at the October 2026 Montréal Summit. This isn’t a trade deal, it is a complete constitutional hijacking that strips away private citizen rights, guts provincial powers, and surrenders Canadian national sovereignty to European bureaucrats in Brussels.

Here is what your federal government just signed away behind closed doors:

1. The Death of Provincial Sovereignty (Sections 92 & 92A)

Under the EU-Green Alliance, Kunming-Montreal 30x30 Biodiversity Framework, and UNEA Plastics Treaty, Ottawa is weaponizing foreign treaties to bypass the Constitution. 

The Prairies in the Crosshairs: Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba’s resource rights, energy infrastructure, agriculture, and forestry are now subjected to EU green taxonomies.

The EIB Raw Materials Trap: The European Investment Bank (EIB) is being granted direct financial leverage and preferential offtake rights over provincially owned critical minerals. Ottawa is signing away prairie resources to feed European industrial mandates.

There will also be a tax implement on our resources economies. 
Offshore minerals, like offshore drilling, can pay up to 7% royalties to the EU in Canada. 
Completely insane!

2. The Surrender of National Sovereignty & "Fax Democracy"

The final clause of the summit commits Canada to an "ever-closer association... short of full membership" by 2027 (leveraging Article 217 TFEU).

Rule-Takers, Not Makers: Canada gets zero seats in the European Parliament, zero votes on the European Council, and zero vetoes. Yet, to maintain market access, we must rubber-stamp laws written in Brussels on AI, data, carbon accounting, and digital identity.

The U.S. Backlash: With over 75% of our exports heading south, poking the U.S. by forming an exclusive regulatory bloc with Europe right before the CUSMA review has already drawn explosive threats of retaliation.

3. The Eradication of Private Citizen Rights

The summit establishes a terrifying web of digital surveillance and speech control:

Digital ID & Centralized Payments: New MOUs on Digital Identity Wallets and instant payment systems link Canadian financial and personal data straight into European architectures, destroying personal privacy.

Criminalizing Dissent (FIMI & Democratic Resilience): The new FIMI Dialogue gives state security agencies sweeping powers to monitor "mostly non-illegal" information flows. If you criticize federal overreach, carbon taxes, or net-zero policies, your speech can be flagged as "foreign-aligned manipulation" or "systemic risk." 
You can go to jail for having an opinion about the government or government policy like flooding the country with low IQ immigrants. 

Open Borders & Biometrics: The new Frontex–CBSA Working Arrangement integrates Canadian border agencies and immigration watchlists directly with European Schengen databases. The same migration policies the EU has will now come to Canada. They can even send the worst migrants in the EU to Canada. 

🔥 Bottom Line:
Canada is being transformed into a branch plant of the European Union, without a single referendum, without provincial consent, and without a vote from Canadians.

When foreign bureaucrats dictate your energy policy, your land use, your digital privacy, and what you are allowed to say online, you are no longer a free citizen in a sovereign nation.

Watch who pushes back against this to see who is on Carney’s side. Watch the provincial governments and the Conservatives. Everyone should be livid because it’s now official that your vote does not matter.

author: ycombinator
quoted_text:
Kalshi just raised an additional $1B, valuing the company at $40B. This will help us expand into stocks, compute, indices, and institutional.

Tomorrow marks 8 years since we got accepted into YC and the journey began.

The odds of a kid from Lebanon getting here were pretty low.

Growing up there was great, but very challenging. We went through war. We had bombs explode in front of my house. I watched brilliant people’s lives destroyed for reasons beyond their control.

Lebanon is an unpredictable country. That unpredictability made it hard to plan for success. And yet despite it all, my mom sacrificed everything to give me and my brother the chance to go back to the US.

I found my refuge in two things: anime and math. Especially math.

I loved math because it calmed me. It was the opposite of unpredictable: clear, deterministic, orderly, and consistent. The proof is either right or wrong. I find that elegant and beautiful.

I was lucky.

I made it to my dream school, MIT (largely thanks to my mom), and my love for math quickly translated to a love for statistics, probability, and markets.

I love markets for a lot of the same reasons. Their incentives are clear: you get rewarded for being right and for pursuing knowledge. They are effective weighting machines for people’s opinions. They provide an incentive to be truthful, because they separate good information from bad information. They let people challenge the consensus and be rewarded for being right.

IMO, Hayek, Surowiecki, Hanson, Tetlock were the founding fathers of prediction markets. The more I read them, the more obsessed I got with the idea of applying market-based pricing to more things.

Markets bring rigor and critical thinking to more questions. And in an increasingly polarized and information-positioned word, I believe we need that more than ever.

Markets would also let people predict and manage more things outside of their control. And the world was becoming increasingly more unpredictable, and more like Lebanon, not less.

That love for markets got Luana and me to build Kalshi.

At first, it was mostly an idea we couldn’t stop talking about. We didn’t have much money. Luana’s sister bought the Kalshi domain name for us (for ~$1.7k). We moved to SF to get started, and embarked on a long, uncertain journey to build a regulated exchange.

The paranoia and anxiety from my childhood never left me. Even when things are going well, I think about what could go wrong. When people trust you with their money, that instinct serves a purpose.

I wanted us to build something that would hold up under pressure.

The first principle we defined at the company: regulatory-first. We worked with regulators for years before we listed a single market. We took every step to do things the right way and always asked for approval before proceeding. It was very hard at times, especially when we were being overtaken by competitors, but we believe doing things the right way matters.

Luana and I aren’t the only ones.

Our team put years of their lives into something far from certain. That’s especially true of Lior, Brandon, Rainer, Luis, Xavier, and Josef, who stuck with us for years. They believed when there was little to point to. And they stuck with us no matter how long it took. Kalshi is the result of an arduous journey through a long desert where, at times, most people didn’t understand why we were making the walk.

Many people still don’t understand what we’re doing and some disagree with us. Markets have historically taken time to be understood and accepted by some. But while not always obvious, their benefits are vast: capital markets help allocate capital and derivative markets help predict and manage uncertainty.

I firmly believe in these benefits, and that’s why I am dedicating my life to building this market.

Markets have caused issues many times in the past, and they certainly can present harms (manipulation, insiders, and addictive behaviors). These harms are more acute for certain types of markets (sports, short-term options, etc.) than others. It’s why I believe that guardrails need to exist and why we have taken the approach we have taken. We have consistently prioritized thinking critically about the risks and building the appropriate safeguards, sometimes beyond what the regulators require us to do. Many believe more needs to be done, and that’s a conversation I welcome.

Over time, I believe more people will see what we see: markets can help us get smarter and manage the future with more rigor, more precision, and more certainty than we have today.

To our tens of millions of users: you have made Kalshi bigger than anything Luana and I could have possibly imagined. Thank you for trusting us and thank you for coming along on the journey. I feel a strong responsibility to build a company worthy of that trust.

I am so lucky to spend my life building something I love. I hope everyone finds something they care about that much. Something that keeps you curious. Something that pushes you to your limits. Something that may put you at odds with the status quo. Something worth the hard days.

For me, it’s still markets. The more I learn, the more I want to understand.

text:
如果你从2023年就在AI行业，你应该会对这几年模型的进步有很深的感触。

那时候模型连ToolUse都做不好，ContextWindow只有8K，让模型稳定返回一个符合要求的JSON都是件挺麻烦的事（这直到Opus3.5才被解决）。
后来有了FunctionCalling，Context从8K到128K，再到1M，模型开始能够自主调用工具、写代码、运行程序、检查错误。
到了今天，很多以前需要工程师花几天做的事情，AI已经能自己完成了。

而且模型进步的速度还在加快。
以前我们可能要等三四个月才能看到一次比较大的模型更新，现在基本每隔一两周就有新模型发布，有时候上个月觉得很难的事情，这个月就已经能做得很好了。

我觉得这背后很重要的一个原因，就是RSI在ModelTraining中的进展。
现在AI已经能参与数据生成、训练代码编写、实验设计、评测和错误分析，甚至开始参与模型本身的研究。
AI越强，能帮研究人员完成的工作就越多，下一代模型也就可能进步得越快。

当然，现在距离完全自主的RSI还有很远，但这个趋势已经很明显了。

所以我很认同 @levie  说的，如果你三到六个月前搭建了一套AI工作流，现在可能已经需要重新做一遍了。

我有时候回头想想，2023年那些让我们兴奋了很久的能力，现在甚至都不值得拿出来介绍。

才过去三年而已。
author: MaxForAI
quoted_text:
It’s almost incomprehensible how wide the distance is between someone who’s working at the frontier with AI and basically everyone else right now. 

The crazy thing is these lines are not converging, but only growing farther apart. If the curve of AI progress had leveled off, it would certainly have given most people and companies time to catch up or implement their workflows in a standardized way. The technology would have neutralized competitive advantage because everyone would be using it the same way.

But what’s happened is the opposite. The curve of AI progress is basically going vertical right now, which means if you had codified your processes 3-6 months ago you’re likely already behind again. Now imagine most companies that kicked into gear a year ago and thought that they were done. Even further behind now.

I’ve never seen a technology in my life and career that improves at this rate, which consequently means you need to upgrade your expectations at a similar rate. Our brains weren’t wired for this, and our organizational change management processes certainly weren’t either.

With any form of recursive self improvement, things just get wilder. It’s a time when you will need to be constantly reevaluating the things that didn’t work just a couple months ago to see if they now can be solved. AI native companies certainly have a strong advantage due to this right now, so now it comes down to can the bigger companies keep up. Wild times.

这波操作复盘：

前几天打dota挂机被关小黑屋了，今天刚好准备打打游戏出小黑屋。

开局前看到polymarket被盗了，赶紧让小伙伴去查看一下，结果进去刚玩10min，看到群消息说币安被盗了，果断切出游戏看情况。

于是赶紧把链上的ETH卖掉了，前几笔很顺利，血赚。后面想从其他交易所提币出来，发现gas已经上天了，很难卖出去，但是还是有差价的，持续将近一个小时。

按照这个逻辑，基本做到每个小币种他快砸完我就平仓，然后也一直有空单对冲抄底的多单。

text:
Anthropic 这哥们的话，真是金玉良言啊。

刚看到 Anthropic 一位 Engineering Manager 的分享，感觉很有意思。

他说，他们团队这个月已经取消了招聘流程中的 Coding Interview，也就是我们熟悉的现场编程题。

因为 AI 在编程方面已经很强了，现场让候选人完成一个 React 编程题，或者考察一些具体的编程知识，通过这些题目来筛选人才，已经没有太大意义了。

而且他发现，自己团队中，那些真正能够创造巨大价值的工程师，未必在传统编程测试中表现得最好。

过去很多科技公司招聘程序员，基本上都把编程能力作为一项非常重要的考核指标。之前我还是程序员的时候，面试前最重要的准备就是刷 LeetCode。

但随着 AI Coding 的快速发展，一名优秀工程师的评价标准，显然也在发生变化。

传统 Coding Interview 可能真的应该彻底取消了。

其实，软件工程这些年的发展，本身就是一个不断提高抽象层级的过程。

最早，程序员需要直接编写汇编。后来有了 C 这样的高级语言，再后来是面向对象编程，以及各种框架和组件。

随着越来越多的底层细节被封装起来，程序员可以用更少的代码，完成更复杂的工作。

现在，AI Coding 又把抽象层级往上抬了一层。过去需要程序员亲自编写和调试的代码，现在很大一部分可以交给 AI 完成。

既然传统 Coding Interview 已经很难准确判断一名工程师的实际价值，那么未来应该怎么招聘程序员？

Anthropic 的这哥们说，他现在筛选简历时，会特别关注候选人过去做过的产品，哪怕只是一个很小的原型。

因为通过这些作品，可以直接考察候选人的品味、同理心和思考深度。这些可能都比 Coding 能力重要。

我解释下自己对这三个品质的理解。

品味，也就是 Taste，指的是一个人的判断能力和审美。培养品味其实没有那么复杂，核心就是多看好的东西，然后不断实践，在实践中获得反馈，反复调整。

比如，经常接触优秀的设计和产品，时间久了，自然会慢慢形成自己的判断。

再自己动手做一些东西，就会发现，原来这个页面的元素太多了，那个地方的渐变色有点土，某个按钮去掉之后更简洁......

品味很难通过学习某个理论就掌握，还是需要不断接触优秀的东西，再通过实践慢慢培养。

同理心的话，好像这个词前几年在国内职场也经常被提起。

简单来说，就是能够站在别人的角度思考问题，不要总沉浸在自己的世界里。

比如，很多工程师长期开发一款产品，对各种功能和操作流程已经非常熟悉，觉得很多设计理所当然。但对于普通用户来说，可能用起来就特别别扭。

优秀的工程师需要能够站在真实用户的角度，理解他们的需求和使用产品时的感受，发现那些自己已经习以为常的问题。

想起张一鸣以前讲过一句话，同理心是地基，想象力是天空，中间是逻辑和工具。

这个理解挺好的。毕竟，如果连用户真正需要什么都不了解，产品做得再复杂，功能再丰富，也未必有什么价值。

最后是 Principled Thinking，其实就是一个人的逻辑思维能力。

开发产品的过程中，总会面临各种各样的选择。为什么要开发这个功能，为什么采用这样的技术方案，又为什么放弃其他方案？

这些决定背后，都应该有清晰的判断依据。尤其是现在有了 AI，技术实现越来越容易，但也不能想到什么就做什么，更不能 AI 给出什么方案，就直接照着执行。

说完面试，我们再聊下年轻程序员的出路。毕竟现在有一种特别流行的观点，认为 AI 对年轻工程师，尤其是缺少工作经验的程序员越来越不友好。

但 Anthropic 这哥们却有不同的看法。

因为他发现，一些刚进入公司的年轻工程师，正在快速超越那些工作经验更丰富、甚至编程能力更强的资深工程师。

一个很重要的原因是，过去需要多年积累的技术经验，现在 AI 已经能够帮年轻人弥补一部分。

即使编程能力还没那么强，他们也有机会快速把自己的想法变成产品，创造出更大的业务价值。

而且，年轻人还有一个很大的优势，就是敢想敢干，有激情，也有野心。

大部分人年轻的时候都是这样，荷尔蒙爆棚，看到什么新鲜的东西都想试试，也没有那么多历史包袱。

进取心胜过资历。

当然，年轻工程师也有自己的劣势。比如他们在组织里没有那么高的地位，也缺少足够的话语权，在一些具体的问题上缺乏经验，所以下的判断可能会绕弯路。

这些就是硬币的两面。但核心是，年轻的工程师没必要妄自菲薄。AI 对所有人都是巨大的机会，没有厚此薄彼。

他给年轻工程师提供了几条建议，我觉得真是金玉良言啊，对所有人都适用。

第一，不要只盯着分配给自己的任务。

早在 2011 年，Patrick McKenzie 就写过一篇很经典的文章，叫《Don't Call Yourself a Programmer》。

里面有句话非常经典：企业雇用工程师，是为了创造商业价值，而不只是编写程序。

对于年轻工程师来说，首先应该搞清楚自己的公司究竟想实现什么目标。如果公司规模比较大，那至少应该理解自己所在部门最重要的业务目标是什么。

甚至可以再往上思考一层，看看自己主管的主管，究竟在为什么事情负责。

要不然很多工程师还是会把自己局限到代码当中。

但公司真正关心的，可能是提高客户留存率、改善产品体验，或者增加收入。

第二，提出一个足够大胆的想法。

不要只想着在现有产品上做一些小修小补。

既然已经理解了公司的业务目标，那就应该认真思考，有没有什么新的产品或者技术方案，能够明显改善业务表现。

哪怕这个想法听起来有点激进，也值得尝试。

因为现在有了 AI，很多过去需要投入大量人力和时间才能验证的想法，已经可以用很低的成本尝试了。

第三，利用一个周末，把想法做出来。

这也是我觉得整篇文章里非常有启发的一条建议。

Anthropic 一些年轻工程师，或者只有几个人的小团队，直接跳过了过去那些繁琐的流程。

他们没有先花大量时间编写 PRD，也没有到处争取产品经理和设计师的支持。

而是利用 AI，在一个周末做出了可以实际运行的产品原型。

然后再拿着原型去沟通。

这两种方式的差别还是很大的。

因为当你只有一个想法的时候，其他人很难判断它到底有没有价值。但有了能够运行的原型，大家就可以直接上手体验，也更容易理解这个想法的价值。

而且，这个原型本身也证明了你有能力把事情做出来。

第四，一个原型最好只表达一个核心想法。

很多年轻工程师容易犯一个错误，就是过于兴奋，恨不得把自己想到的所有功能，全部塞进一个产品里。

结果，可能有三个想法非常优秀，却被另外二十个没什么价值的想法掩盖了。

他认为，制作原型最重要的目的，是让管理者快速理解这个想法为什么值得做，以及你为什么有能力继续推动这个项目。

所以，没有必要为了展示技术能力，把原型做得特别复杂。

把一个真正有价值的想法表达清楚，就已经足够了。

第五，充分利用新人视角。

在一家公司待久了，很多人会逐渐习惯现有的工作方式，甚至把过去的一些经验当成不可改变的限制。

但刚加入公司的年轻人，没有那么多历史包袱。很多老员工觉得不可能实现的事情，他们反而愿意重新尝试。

而且，现在有了 AI，很多过去需要投入大量资源才能尝试的想法，年轻人自己就可以先动手做出来。

举个例子，Claude Code 最开始主要通过命令行交互，很多工程师已经习惯了这种工作方式。

但后来，两位加入公司时间不算长的年轻工程师，利用一个周末，就做出了 Claude Code 图形界面的原型。大约八天之后，第一个公开版本就发布了。

现在大家也都看到了，Claude Code 的图形界面已经成为很多人使用这款产品的重要方式。

所以，回过头来看，我觉得 Felix 说的进取心胜过资历，还是很有道理的。

尤其是在 AI 时代，很多过去需要大量资源才能完成的事情，现在一个人就有机会做出来。

对于那些有想法、愿意主动尝试的年轻人来说，这确实是一个非常好的时代。

text:
Later today, we are officially ending all remaining support for the Iron Fish network.

A few days ago, we observed abnormal activity involving wIRON and the ChainPort bridge. After working with ChainPort and reviewing their logs, we discovered that the cause was an inflation bug in the Iron Fish blockchain itself.

We traced the bug to a commit from early 2019 in the Merkle tree implementation. The developer at the time implemented a standard Merkle tree. However, because of nuances in how a note’s nullifier is calculated (the mechanism that lets a normal user spend their funds), the attacker was able to spend the same note more than once. 

The attacker then compounded the exploit, aggregated their notes, and exited through the ChainPort bridge. This code path was within the scope of both our external and internal audits, but the bug wasn’t caught during review.

For closure, we’ve committed the patch for the exploit, with a detailed postmortem included in the PR, before shutting down and archiving the ironfish repo.

The meta-analysis here is that software that can’t be upgraded immediately (most of crypto), is in an extremely precarious position. The ability to find and exploit vulnerabilities in technically complex code is becoming commoditized. Safety guardrails on US frontier models make it difficult for companies to use them to patch security vulnerabilities, while abliterated open-source models are approaching frontier capabilities.

We wish everyone all the best, and we hope crypto finds a path through this. 

Thank you all.

text:
오늘 나스닥 개박살 난 진짜 이유, 아마존·인텔 실적 쇼크에 앤트로픽 정크본드 폭탄까지 (feat. 돈줄이 마른다)

하 진짜 오늘 장 꼬라지 .............

어제 장 마감하고 뜬 아마존, 인텔 실적 때문에 안 그래도 투심 박살 나서 시작했는데, 장중에 파이낸셜타임스발 앤트로픽 신용등급 폭로까지 터지면서 나스닥100을 -3% 넘게 까지 내리꽂았다

이 세 가지 사건이 따로 노는 게 아니다. 아마존 → 앤트로픽 → 인텔로 이어지는 AI 생태계의 '돈줄'이 동시에 터져버린 완벽한 연쇄 폭발이다. 

뇌피셜 거르고 방금 뜬 최신 수치까지 싹 다 긁어서 하나로 묶어준다

아마존 실적이 보여준 공포 ("AI 때문에 현금이 다 말라비틀어졌다")

어제 장 마감 후 아마존 3분기 실적이 떴다. 겉보기엔 AWS(클라우드) 매출이 전년 대비 39%나 폭증(460억 달러)하면서 미친 성장을 보여줬다. 근데 주가는 왜 처박혔냐?

이번 분기에만 설비투자로 770억 달러를 태웠고, 올해 연간 Capex 가이던스를 무려 2,200억 달러(약 300조 원)로 박아버렸다.

FCF 적자 전환, AI 데이터센터 짓느라 돈을 물 쓰듯 쓰니까, 1년 전만 해도 +148억 달러 흑자였던 최근 12개월 잉여현금흐름(FCF)이 -424억 달러(마이너스 약 58조 원)로 개박살이 났다 EPS도 컨센서스(1.96달러) 못 미친 1.89달러가 떴다

동네에서 제일 장사 잘되는 대형 식당(아마존)이 손님은 미어터지는데, 주방 기계(AI 서버) 새로 사들이느라 통장 잔고가 마이너스 58조 원이 찍힌 거다. 

세계 최고 부자 기업조차 AI 투자비 감당이 안 돼서 현금이 말라버렸다는 걸 숫자로 확인시켜 준 셈이다

인텔의 -30% 폭락 ("밑단 공급망은 이미 숨통이 막힌다")

같은 날 실적을 발표한 인텔은 한술 더 떴다. 3분기 매출은 165억 달러(+21%), 조정 EPS는 0.52달러로 월가 예상치(0.40달러)를 가볍게 깼다. 특히 데이터센터 및 AI(DCAI) 매출이 73억 달러로 78%나 폭증했다. 

근데 실적 발표후 주가가 -30% 넘게 폭락했다.

3분기에 그렇게 잘 팔아놓고, 정작 다가올 4분기 매출 전망치를 150억~160억 달러로 3분기보다 낮춰 잡았고, 조정 EPS 가이던스도 0.25달러로 반토막을 내버렸다. 

마진율도 시장 기대치를 밑돌았다

빅테크들이 천문학적인 돈을 쏟아붓는다는데, 정작 칩과 인프라를 납품하는 인텔 같은 레거시 반도체 기업은 마진이 깎이고 다음 분기 매출이 꺾인다고 자백한 꼴이다.

시장 입장에서는 "빅테크들이 돈이 딸리니까 특정 독점 칩 말고는 지갑을 닫기 시작했구나"라는 공포가 엄습한 거고 공장에 불난것도 크다.. 

결정타는 이게 마무리었두.. FT발 앤트로픽 '정크등급' 폭로 ("이제 빌릴 돈조차 막힌다")

아마존은 현금이 마르고 인텔은 가이던스가 꺾여서 시장이 잔뜩 쫄아있는데, 오늘 장중에 FT가 10월 30일 자 보도로 카운터펀치를 날렸다.

앤트로픽이 무디스·S&P·피치 3대 신평사에서 공식 등급을 받은 건 아니지만, 예상보다 낮은 BB급 '정크등급(투기등급)'을 받을 가능성이 존나 커졌다는 내부 소식이 터진 거다.

블랙스톤은 앤트로픽이 상장만 하면 무난하게 '투자적격등급(BBB- 이상)' 받을 줄 알고 행복회로를 돌렸지만, 신평사들 반응이 싸늘하자 투자자들에게 BB급 정크 가능성을 전달했다.

실제로 지난 6월 신평사 KBRA는 이미 앤트로픽에 BB+(투기등급 최상단)를 매겼고, 지난 10월 26일 발표한 630억 달러 규모 AI 칩 금융거래 중 후순위 채무 180억 달러도 정크 판정을 받았다.

이게 왜 아마존 실적과 직결되느냐? 

아마존이 앤트로픽의 최대 뒷배이자 지분 보유왕.. 

장부가 기준 약 1,904억 달러 규모 평가이고, 앤트로픽 매출의 절반 가까이가 AWS 같은 클라우드 채널에서 나오기 때문

원래 1금융권에서 싸게 대출받으려던 놈이 신용점수 떡락해서 제2금융권 고리대금으로 내몰린 격
BBB- 이상 (투자적격): 보험사, 연기금 같은 전 세계 큰손들이 합법적으로 싼 이자에 돈을 왕창 빌려줄 수 있음

BB+ 이하 (투기/정크): 내부 규정상 안전자산만 사야 하는 연기금·보험사는 아예 참여 불가. 

쩐주 풀이 쪼그라들고 금리는 폭등함.

물론 브로드컴이 선순위 대출 보증(신용보강)을 서준 기존 630억 달러 약정 딜이 당장 파토 나진 않겠지만, 앞으로 향후 10년간 서버와 인프라에 최소 5,180억 달러를 태워야 하는 앤트로픽 입장에선 신규 자금줄이 막히거나 이자 폭탄을 맞게 생긴 거다.

완벽하게 맞춰진 폭락의 퍼즐 (시장의 질문이 바뀌었다)

이 세 개를 일직선으로 놓으면 오늘 왜 나스닥이 발작했는지 소름 돋게 딱 맞아떨어진다

아마존: "우리 AI 서버 짓느라 1년 새 잉여현금흐름이 -424억 달러로 구멍 났어." (빅테크 내부 현금 고갈)

앤트로픽: "그럼 우리가 외부에서 빚내서 칩 살게... 어? 신평사에서 정크등급 줘서 연기금 돈을 못 끌어오네?" (외부 차입 경로 경색)

인텔: "쩐주들 지갑 얇아지니까 당장 4분기부터 우리 마진이랑 매출부터 꺾이네." (공급망 실적 타격)

지금 월가에서 AI를 보는 눈빛이 완전히 뒤집혔다.

과거의 질문: "AI 수요가 얼마나 폭발할까?"

현재의 질문: "그 수요를 감당할 수천억 달러를 대체 누가, 무슨 돈으로 대줄 건데?"

수요가 아무리 진짜여도, 빅테크의 현금흐름(아마존)이 마르고 스타트업의 대출 창구(앤트로픽)가 정크등급으로 막히면 결국 설비투자는 지연될 수밖에 없다. 

그러면 밑단에 있는 데이터센터 업자들과 반도체 공급망(인텔 등)까지 도미노로 흔들리게 된다. 

오늘의 폭락은 단순한 실적 실망감이 아니라, AI 인프라 투자 사이클의 '돈줄(유동성)' 자체를 의심하기 시작한 첫 번째 본격적인 발작이다. 장 진짜 개피곤하다

quoted_text:
David Friedberg says every dollar Nvidia spends making chips turns into $18 of Anthropic revenue, with SpaceX making an 83% margin in between

“I basically said start with NVIDIA, how much does NVIDIA spend to make the chips? And then how much do they sell the chips for? So for every dollar of COGS, every dollar that NVIDIA spends, that turns into $4 of revenue for NVIDIA, 75% margin."

"And then that gets sold to SpaceX, and then SpaceX turns around, and they’re making, you know, an 83% margin on that chip spend, because they’re kind of looking at a five-year depreciation. So they spent $10 billion on Colossus one, five year life, $2 billion a year depreciation. And so that’s kind of the cost per year, but then they’re making $1.25 billion a month on Colossus."

"And then Anthropic is showing in this S-1 pretty remarkably to Sacks’s point that they’re making about 85% incremental gross margin on every incremental dollar coming in. It’s obviously a baseline of compute spend, but 85% is kind of the incremental gross margin. So at the end of the day, a dollar that NVIDIA spends turns into $18 that Anthropic is making selling to customers.”

Gray market RUO peptides vs. Superpower prices: 

SuperPower’s $: BPC-157 is $150 for 15 mg (3 x 5) - $10/mg

RUO $: BPC-157 for $44 for 10 mg - $4.4/mg

That’s $10/mg for compounded, personalized for you, shipped cold to your door, that is low risk and actually intended for human consumption. A true medication. 

The problem with that $4.4 / mg RUO peptide is that it’s ’not for human consumption’ so unless you put blind trust in the company, you need to go out of your way to have a second bottle tested and wait for the results plus pay for the testing.

So that $44 turns into $88 plus the charge for shipping to the lab and the lab analysis ($50? $100?).

Even after that, there’s risk because technically the company that sold it to you wants to wipe their hands free of risk and make you sign a waiver to say that it is not for human consumption. 

If you inject that and have an issue, there is no one to be held accountable because it wasn’t intended for human consumption.

If you inject a compounded peptide that was prescribed to you, with your name on the prescription bottle, and there is an issue that Pharmacy can be held accountable. 

So there is massive risk, lots of unknown variables and headaches for what $20? $40?

$BTC

Some thoughts after this week's action.

I was positioned flat for a reason, then went tactically short after the Binance headline and the move through the previous weekly lows. Only a small short remains as a flyer.

The hack was the immediate trigger in this instance. Would price have traded down here anyway? Most likely, and it's worth understanding why.

Third rejection at the yearly open (~$87k), prev weekly low (~$79k) lost, now back at the yearly mid (~$78k). Still a wide range, for the same reason all year: BTC lacks the fundamental setup for a sustained bull run.

Checklist vs prior cycles:

✅ Access: spot ETFs live, institutional channels open
✅ Dry powder: record stablecoin holdings
✅ Leverage: flushed, and gets flushed again every time it rebuilds

❌ Liquidity: Fed still hiking, financial conditions tightening, inflation 3.7%, oil >$100
❌ Flows: ~$1bn BTC ETF outflows YTD vs +$25bn in 2025 and +$35bn in 2024
❌ Regulation: CLARITY Act failed in the Senate, no new vote scheduled
❌ Supply shock: next halving in 2028
❌ Narrative: nothing pulling new retail money in

What changes my view: a monthly close back above the yearly open (~$87k), or a clear Fed pivot signal.

The rails are laid. A Fed pivot is what switches them on. Until then, I expect more of the same inside the range.

text:
Shipping season never ends 🟠

1. Starknet as an independent L1?

This month, Starknet opened one of the biggest strategic discussions in its history: whether Starknet should become an independent L1, in order to move faster on post-quantum and AI security?

- Eli Ben-Sasson, StarkWare’s CEO, publicly raised the idea earlier this month.
- Starknet already benefits from STARK proofs and programmable accounts that can adopt new signature schemes, but as an Ethereum L2, part of its security still depends on Ethereum’s own upgrade timeline.
- Starknet is targeting full end-to-end post-quantum security by next year, while Ethereum targets the end of 2029.
- The community voted in favor of researching the idea.
- A joint StarkWare × Starknet Foundation working group has now begun assessing the technical requirements, security trade-offs, economic implications, and consequences for users and builders.
- The group will publish its findings in the coming months before any potential next step is brought back to the community.

2. Post-quantum security is getting real

Research is increasingly turning into working infrastructure.

- StarkWare demonstrated a testnet transaction signed with a NIST-standard ML-DSA key generated and stored directly inside a phone’s secure hardware.
- A Pixel 11 generated the complete STARK proof for a real Starknet mainnet transaction in just 51 seconds using 2.41 GiB of RAM.
- Put together that means a phone can now sign AND prove quantum-safe Starknet transactions
- A developer (0xjuno) demonstrated post-quantum wallet migration on Starknet Sepolia, showing how existing Starknet accounts can transition toward quantum-resistant signature schemes.
- The estimated compute cost of creating a quantum-safe Bitcoin transaction through QSB fell from ~$320 to ~$59, an 82% reduction in just a few weeks.
- The Falcon Challenge reduced Falcon-512 verification costs by 50.2%, from 48.4M to 24.1M gas.
- A fully spec-compliant Falcon-512 account transaction was executed on Starknet mainnet for approximately $0.027, by @tanya25519.

3. Privacy is becoming a native feature across Starknet

Shadow Accounts went live this month, introducing a new STRK20 primitive that allows apps to offer a Public → Private switch without publicly linking activity to a user’s main wallet.

- Ekubo added private LPing, allowing users to provide liquidity, earn fees, and manage positions privately.
- Opus added private collateral deposits, borrowing, and private CASH-USDC LP staking.
- Troves added end-to-end privacy across automated vaults and Ekubo strategies.
- Endur launched private native unstaking, making its full staking flow private.
- SuperVega launched private options trading.
- ArcX integrated Starknet privacy, allowing users to trade without publicly linking activity to their main wallet.
- Haven launched Starknet accounts as part of its private neobank infrastructure.

4. The ecosystem keeps shipping

- The Starknet Foundation launched several new user-facing products this month: (1) Bramble, a new self-custody wallet built specifically around Starknet’s native capabilities - (2) A dedicated BTCFi portal bringing together the different ways users can put their Bitcoin to work across Starknet - (3) The Starknet VIP Program for STRK and strkBTC holders, offering priority support, direct access to the Foundation team, confirmed spots at selected events, and more.
- Realms is back and rebuilding around a purpose-built Starknet L3 for games such as Eternum and Blitz, targeting better UX, lower costs, and greater flexibility.
- ArcX launched RISE and PAPER point markets alongside its existing Variational market.
- ArcX also launched Points Desk, allowing vetted sellers to sell points without posting collateral, and rolled out embedded wallets, allowing users to log in with email, Google, or X and trade directly.
- 3 new projects went live on Mainnet: Escape Saylor (game), Slay (NFT + launchpad), STRKWORLD (gaming + GameFi)
- 5 projects integrated Starknet & STRK: StonkFun added support for launching tokens paired with STRK - Moonshot integrated STRK - ShapeShift added Starknet cross-chain swaps - Pulsar integrated Starknet deposits, transfers, and card top-ups - https://t.co/J2NS5XArbM added Starknet pairs with STRK-denominated holder rewards.

5. The numbers keep improving

- 1.7B STRK are now staked, representing around 23% of the circulating supply
- The Starknet Bunker holds approximately $150M in staked assets, including ~1.7B STRK and ~580 BTC
- SuperVega generated more than $5M in notional trading volume during its best month so far
- Starknet recorded 210 commits in one month, its highest monthly count of the past quarter
- starknet.js usage reached an all-time high
- Starkzap crossed 10,000 downloads

Can’t stop, won’t stop.

today we are announcing openrouter for commerce: https://t.co/qLbYqziMtG

a single endpoint that integrates 5k stores, including Doordash, Amazon and most shopify stores, with payments using Agentcard (Stripe Link and Shop coming soon).

we built opencommerce to solve 3 problems:
* coverage: one endpoint to integrate 5k stores. agentic purchasing is a core feature for most personal assistants, but not their main business. searching for products and buying on behalf of users shouldn’t be as painful as it is today (e.g. it shouldn’t involve browser automations or dealing with PSPs). opencommerce solves that: 1 tool, every online store.

* reliability: 100% uptime. the challenge with browser automations is that they fail (e.g. captchas, bot-detection, etc). we run thousands of tests every couple of hours on every one of the stores to guarantee that the integration works when your user tries to buy something.

* speed: responses in under 10s. consumers are used to Amazon speed, and agentic purchases have so far felt like a downgrade. most agents spend minutes finding products before they come back with results. we monitor speed and improve it constantly.

Anthropic 创始人 Dario Amodei 与妹妹 Daniela 曾经离开 OpenAI，随后创立了 Anthropic。

AI 公司之间的竞争，不只是模型能力、算力和融资规模的竞争，也涉及对技术发展方向、组织价值观和安全边界的不同判断。

理解这场竞争，不能只看谁的模型更强，还要看创始团队最初想解决什么问题，以及他们愿意坚持什么原则。

text:
Robot/human intimacy?

I was in an audio space today where a bunch of guys (mostly guys) were talking about having sex with their humanoid robots. As crazy and freaky as I am, that ain't gonna work for me: it's very heavy, very metallic, very hard, and it has cameras and a database.

I think the reality is, when I do get a humanoid (and it'll come soon enough), I'm gonna have it doing the chores so I my wife and I can chase each other around the house. 

We've been married 24 years. Our anniversary is on Monday, and we're still  crazy about each other, which is freaking awesome.

There is a part of robot intimacy that I am more likely to do. I saw Andrej Karpathy @karpathy hug a robot at the @1x_tech NEO launch, and I saw dozens of other people hug the NEO similarly. I can imagine having a tough day at life and coming home wanting a hug from the robot, maybe even a little cuddle on the couch. 

But in the bedroom? I just don't get people who want to have sex with a hard metallic machine. But it comes up so frequently on Spaces that something about the human mind wants to do it. 

Something to think about on a Friday night when you're out with your friends.

:-)

quoted_text:
Do NOT buy a 512GB Mac Studio ‼️

Two 256GB Mac Studio M5 Ultras are ~$700 cheaper and have ~1.7x faster prefill and decode

Price: $22,299 vs $21,598
Both are the 36-core CPU / 80-core GPU

You can connect 2x 256GB with one Thunderbolt 5 cable + RDMA, which is fast enough to run one model across both

Prefill (compute)
- 1x 512 does ~135 TFLOPS
- 2x 256 does ~215-245 TFLOPS
- Apple claims up to 3x for a 4-Mac cluster, which works out to ~1.7x for two

Decode (bandwidth)
- 1x 512 has 1.2 TB/s
- 2x 256 gets ~1.9-2.2 TB/s effective
- With tensor parallelism each box reads its half of the weights at the same time, which works out to ~1.7x for two

GLM-5.3 goes from ~33-40 tok/s to ~55-70
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash goes from ~45-60 tok/s to ~75-100
Both are 4-bit with spec decode on, estimated from M3 and M5 Ultra benchmarks

If you want Qwen3.8-Flash-Next or GLM-5.3-Flash, a single 256 already runs them well and you don’t need either setup. The 512GB question is about DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (552B) and GLM-5.3 (753B), tied as the best open models on Artificial Analysis v5. They need 310-420GB at 4-bit, so neither fits on one 256

the environment we are in increasingly demands AI-adopters to demonstrate their ROI from accelerated AI integration and spend. 

one of the key unlocks from a company adoption standpoint is the aggressive storage and utilization of telemetry from AI systems:

(1) you first need to make sure you store your telemetry for the sake of observability 
(2) you can sell logs in order to provide an "inference cashback," to data brokers if you are comfortable doing that (and you can always anonymize your own data before providing it to a vendor or broker)
(3) you can use your telemetry to build your own specialized models for both (1) recurring tasks and (2) judgement-heavy tasks with exceptions that need to be utilized and recorded 

the key to benefitting from telemetry is ensuring an interconnected system-design approach. this requires the right (1) storage of information and (2) the effect identification of what matters to you from an ROI standpoint.

text:
昨晚跟168X的交流要点，上一次8月底https://t.co/MrasWYxXvC参与168X聊到：美股临近中期选举市场动荡加大，然后大饼和加密到10月因为流动性收紧会回踩。梳理下这次聊的要点：
1、美国经济正在进入由AI基建驱动的新基建周期，这种大基建趋势下名义GDP的增速会很好；

2、中东局势中期选举后可能会是一个时间窗口，如果能解决油价回落宏观环境压力会减少很多；
但如果一直不能解决油价持续在高位，通胀持续强势那么联储不仅12月会加息，明年也可能会加，如果原来预期 2 次，最后变成 3 次、4 次甚至更久，则整个估值体系都会重新定价、市场会扛不住。

3、ARR这个指标需要抛后，Anthropic上市后就要看真实的季度营收、年度营收了。大云平台已经是AI Operating System：企业会从结果和成本考虑，切换不同的模型。

4、大型科技公司真正大规模提高 CapEx，是从 2025 年三季度左右开始的，所以今天 Microsoft、Google Cloud 增长出来的 Revenue，很多对应的其实是一年前甚至更早花出去的钱。去年下半年开始加速建设的 Capacity，现在才进入投产期，而过去几个季度所有云厂商一直在讲同一句话：Demand > Supply，算力不够。如果需求还在增长，而且你新上线多少 Capacity 都能马上被吃掉，那未来几个季度 Revenue 自然会继续加速。所以我觉得AI商业化现在不是见顶，而是才刚开始加速。

5、要看Cloud Revenue Growth 何时开始超过 CapEx Growth
不能永远只看 Revenue，第二阶段要看 ROIC。2026 年是 CapEx 爆发的一年。去年几千亿美元，今年接近翻倍，这种 CapEx Growth 不可能每年都 100%。
真正漂亮的拐点是什么？就是未来 CapEx Growth 开始自然下降，但 AI Revenue Growth 还继续加速、意味着开始算的过账来。

所以接下来几个季度，最想看的就是：Revenue Growth、CapEx Growth、Depreciation Life、FCF，这几个东西开始怎么收敛。

6、AI主线已经迁移：Memory → Optical / Software → Agent / AI for Science/应用

不要形成“AI = Semiconductor = Memory”的定式思维，一说AI就是半导体、一说半导体就是存储。

每一阶段 AI 的主线都会迁移。今年一季度、二季度，Memory 是最强的；到 8、9 月以后，Optical 开始变强，同时一批之前被砸得很惨的软件、SaaS 也开始走出来。为什么？因为模型商品化、Token Price 下来以后，受益的不只上游 硬件。Token 越便宜，Deployment 越容易，Cloud、Software、Enterprise Integration、Agent 反而会越来越受益。再下一阶段可能就是 AI for Science、Bio、更广泛的应用层。

所以趋势投资真正要做的，不是死守原来的 Winner，而是不断识别：下一层利润池正在往哪里迁移。Semi 也不是死了，只是像上半年那种所有东西直线上冲的阶段，短期可能过去了。

7、真正需要让 AI Thesis 转空的信号，不是 Semi 再跌 20%，而是 AI商业化（云厂商业绩增速）开始降速、当下是出于加速的阶段。这才是未来的市场的真正的大风险，

而另一个问题则是伊朗问题迟迟得不到解决，油价高位、通胀向上趋势被强化、联储不得不多次加息而非两次。

8、高收益率时代不再普涨：以后市场只奖励真实 Cash Flow。
当 Bond Yield 高以后，股票自然也要给更高的 Risk Premium，这就是为什么现在市场越来越挑剔。Google Cloud很好，Search、FCF 出现问题，市场照样先卖。所以之后选股票一定要分清楚：哪些公司只是 Narrative，哪些公司的业务已经真正兑现，Revenue 是真的、Cash Flow 是真的，而且未来 2、3 年增长空间还能算出来。

大公司如果因为短期逆风被杀估值，我反而觉得是好事，因为它给你重新上车的价格。高利率不是所有股票不能涨，而是市场会越来越“优中选优”。

9、中期选举后很多不确定性会减弱如国会的归属，再看伊朗问题是不是能解决，谨防Anthropic上市路演开始后的吸血。

昨天有一点现在看是不对的“昨天聊到如果亚马逊的财报还不错、市场有一波能到anthropic路演前、今年亚马逊财报云业务很好但是广告放缓、资本开支远超预期、也是加重了市场担忧”可能这种担忧要到中期选举之后再看了。

早期公告暂停充提，后续服务更新明确充值正常、提现仍暂停。多个恢复时长分别对应不同公告时点；截至本批情报，不能把预计恢复或新闻所称周日恢复当作已经开放。

5. EIP7702批量清扫不等于以太坊协议被破解
7702委托仍需有效授权签名；签名链路被控制可在不导出私钥情况下批准恶意内容。50个授权不代表50笔均执行，关于批量机制是否必要存在研究者分歧。

6. 多链资产同时失窃削弱单一以太坊漏洞解释
币安后续调查发现额外入侵点，明确属于复杂攻击，最初DevOps电脑失陷并非完整根因；链上追踪涉及多链，不能以单一以太坊功能解释全部失窃。

7. 被冻结资产追偿仍有法律及归属不确定性
币安官方称被冻结资产仍在追偿与核验。KOL援引既往朝鲜相关资产司法争议提示潜在债权竞争，但这是法律风险推演，不能据此认定本次冻结款已被其他债权人截留。

quoted_text:
Very few podcasts will actually make you smarter AND make you laugh.

No politics, no egos, just tech.

The biggest news this week:

- Anthropic Files S1 Ahead of $2TRN IPO
- Instinct's Rumoured $30BN Fundraise
- Microsoft Lays off 27,000 While Meta Taps Equity Markets for $95BN Capex Spending Spree

My notes with @jasonlk and @rodriscoll

1. Analysis of Anthropic S1

Anthropic's S1 beat expectations on margins and operating income, even after stock-based compensation, leaving the burden of proof on the naysayers. It also looked strong on customer concentration, compute efficiency and cash. Some questions remain, including the undisclosed Q3 revenue number.

2. Is the Value Extraction Requirement From the Latest Models a Benefit or a Curse of Anthropic?

Eighty percent of Anthropic's revenue comes from models less than six months old, and 70 to 80% of compute costs go to training. Models are expensive to build and highly profitable to serve, but only for six to twelve months. Few companies can write a $10 to 12BN compute check, so this short shelf life can favour Anthropic if it stays aggressive.

3. Brutal Reality Is Microsoft Have Just Admitted They Don't Want 27% of Their Workforce

Whatever gets said on LinkedIn, Microsoft's move says it does not want 27% of its people. That is a worse scarlet letter than a pure layoff, because the company has told these employees they do not meet its minimum bar.

4. Chinese Open-Source Models Have Peaked and Will Decline From Here

Chinese open-weight models are close to finished in the US, and this is the beginning of the end for them. Despite DeepSeek's latest raise, it is starting to be banned across all federal agencies.

5. Why No CIO Will Take a Chance on a Chinese Model

Even if confidential data reaches Alibaba servers in Asia only one time in 100,000, without consent, no CIO or CISO will approve the model. If it keeps happening and Alibaba stays silent, anyone using these models will lose their job.

6. Why OpenAI Is an Underappreciated Asset to Invest in Today

OpenAI is mispriced at the $1.25 TN round. Brief market panic has created a dislocation like Anthropic's round at around $183BN, even though OpenAI has closed all its competitive gaps.

7. What Is the Upside of OpenAI at $1.25 Trillion?

OpenAI and Anthropic are both expected to become $10 to 20TN companies. Anthropic takes only 0.1% of Fortune 500 budgets today, and even conservative estimates put that at 2 to 3%. Because OpenAI is not priced to perfection, the worst case is doubling the money.

text:
Available compute and productive compute aren’t the same thing.
A GPU can sit idle because demand isn’t there. It can also sit idle because the workload is waiting on data: another copy, another sync job, another environment to stage.
The fixed-cost maths looks the same either way. The fix doesn’t.
author: Aptos
quoted_text:
Idle GPUs can still produce an expensive AI bill.

In VentureBeat Intelligence’s Q3 survey, 79% of respondents reporting GPU use said their GPUs were busy half the time or less. Yet 70% of that low-use group planned a new, additional or replacement AI platform.

A platform change can mean moving workloads, replacing an inefficient stack or buying access to a different model. It does not automatically mean ordering more GPUs.

An enterprise can also pay twice: once for owned or reserved compute, then again for a hosted model API. Spare capacity on its own hardware does not automatically offset the API invoice. Moving that work requires a suitable model and a functioning deployment.

The fixed-cost arithmetic is unforgiving.

At 20% busy time, each busy GPU-hour carries 5x the fixed capacity cost of a fully used hour. At 50%, that falls to 2x. At 80%, it is 1.25x.

Moving from 20% to 50% cuts fixed cost per busy hour by 60%, with no change in hardware prices. The total fixed bill stays the same; more work shares it. This is an illustrative model, not a measured saving.

The return still needs proving. In September, 58 of 64 respondents planning a platform change lacked finance-reviewed ROI figures. That means unverified returns, not necessarily losses.

For investors, follow three different tests:

• Hardware suppliers: orders converting into collected cash.
• GPU clouds: utilization alongside realized pricing and contract costs.
• Enterprise buyers: cost per successfully completed task.

A busy GPU can run an unprofitable workload. An idle enterprise GPU does not establish a shortage of demand everywhere else.

Survey caveat: self-selected respondents, not a representative census of the world’s GPUs.

今天苹果向包括土耳其在内的多个国家的用户发送了新的通知，告知他们已成为高级间谍软件的目标。

最近这些通知的增多表明存在严重的威胁。

从过去几个月开始，我们见证了此类商业间谍软件通知的逐渐增多。

8月时，一波覆盖110个国家的威胁通知浪潮开始了。

紧接着这些通知之后，有大量人员被高级间谍软件针对，其中包括三位土耳其部长。

苹果在检测到强有力的证据，表明某人因其身份、职务或活动而被高级间谍软件特别针对时，才会发送这些通知。

在类似Pegasus、Graphite、Predator的网络武器实施的这些网络间谍行动中，甚至最新的iPhone设备也能被渗透。

因为这些设备存在非常关键级别的零日漏洞（zero day），几乎每个月都会发现新的此类安全漏洞。在几天前经历了最近的一次，苹果于10月26日发布了iOS 27.2、iPadOS 27.2、macOS及其他安全更新，总共修复了超过300个安全漏洞。

quoted_text:
🚨 0.77€ de taxe pour regarder un film Netflix ! 

Ce vendredi, les députés viennent d'adopter un amendement socialiste visant à taxer les données qui circulent sur Internet à hauteur de 5,5 centimes par gigaoctet reçu en France.

Ils ont complètement pété les plombs. 

Voici quelques exemples de ce que ça va désormais vous coûter :
🔴 Vous regardez un film Netflix de 2 heures en 4K ? Jusqu'à 0,77 € de taxe brute sur les données transmises.
🔴 Vous téléchargez un jeu vidéo de 150 Go ? 8,25 €.
🔴 Vous récupérez 200 Go de photos personnelles stockées chez Google ? 11 €.
🔴 Vous rapatriez 1 To de vos propres fichiers depuis Google Drive ? 55 €.
🔴 Vous restaurez 2 To de sauvegardes après une panne informatique ? 110 €.

Ces taxes seront facturées aux plateformes américaines, qui vous vous en doutez bien, vous redescendront la facture ! 

Ils sont en train de construire une fiscalité qui pénalise le simple fait de transmettre de la donnée. 

Et ceci alors que nous sommes à l'aube d'une révolution technologique majeure avec l'IA ! 

Pour rester compétitifs, tous les pays doivent accélérer leur transformation numérique.

Et nous en France, que trouve-t-on comme idée de génie ?

UNE PUTAIN DE TAXE SUR LA DATA ! 

Et en plus ils ont le culot de nous la présenter comme une mesure écologique qui encouragerait à réduire les volumes de données échangées.

Quelle bande de guignols. 

Il faut être totalement déconnecté des réalités économiques pour considérer qu'un pays peut retrouver sa prospérité en multipliant indéfiniment les prélèvements sur les activités productives.

Cet amendement n'est pas encore une loi définitive, mais le simple fait qu'une telle proposition ait été adoptée à l'Assemblée nationale en dit long sur la manière dont nous sommes gouvernés.

Ces fous du bus vont vraiment nous mettre au fond du ravin.

quoted_text:
关于本次安全事件，大家对技术细节有不少疑问，就目前掌握的信息，这里统一说明几点：

1️⃣ 这不是攻破一台电脑就把钱转走了
这并不是一次通过单一设备就能完成的事件，一个员工电脑被黑是这个攻击的起点。针对加密机构的攻击通常具有较强的针对性，攻击者往往尝试利用了复杂的手段实施渗透。

我们已经发现与事件相关的重要线索，并已第一时间采取措施控制风险，相关调查和溯源工作仍在持续进行中。现阶段，平台核心风控和应急机制已经启动，用户资产安全是我们的首要保障。

2️⃣ 关于"工程师是不是权限过大"
这并不是攻击者直接利用某位工程师权限即可完成资金转移的事件，也不是单一人员可以“一键操作”造成的结果。相关异常涉及更复杂的攻击过程。需要强调的是，现阶段调查并未将责任归因于任何个人，公司将承担相应责任，并持续推进后续处置与安全升级工作。

3️⃣ 目前能确认的事实
没有发现钱包私钥泄露的证据。用户资金安全，本次事件造成的全部被盗损失由 SAFU 基金和公司资金全额承担，不需要用户承担。目前链上已冻结约 30 亿美元受影响资产，我们正配合执法部门和区块链情报机构追查，链上资金流向公开可查。

text:
Guys, an October 31 update on @OriginalBlokyz. 👀

I went through the latest posts from the project, its founders and the community. And there are developments making me follow this collection with even more interest.

Some interesting things have been happening around these characters and their universe over the past few days.

1️⃣ The community is already creating new stories

Between October 28 and October 30, @auro_verse continued his own Future Era series inspired by the Blokyverse, reaching its eighth episode.

On October 29, @panelhausapp also featured his Medieval Era comic.

These are community-created interpretations made using Panel Haus, inspired by Blokyz characters and their world.

This is one of the developments I find most bullish.

Someone is investing time in these characters, building dialogue, scenes and stories. And that work is also reaching the audience of the platform used to create it.

To me, that’s an interesting early sign of an IP’s ability to inspire creativity.

A character that makes someone want to tell a story has already started building a connection.

2️⃣ October 28 and October 30: archetypes and collecting

On October 28, @MonkOnTheBlok showcased The Seer, identifying a count of 75 within the collection.

On October 30, @Ukj1111 said he had picked up a Future Era Cypherpunk.

These are small updates, but they illustrate something I like about the project: the ability to look for a specific character with its own identity.

A Seer.
A Cypherpunk.
A Dragon Knight.
A character from your favourite era.

That variety gives collectors different reasons to explore the collection.

Personally, I find it encouraging to see the founders continue discussing individual characters and collecting them too.

That’s the kind of attention to the product I want to see maintained over time.

3️⃣ Physical collectibles are already in collectors’ hands

This part of the journey has already happened.

On October 12, @AshleyDCan showed the collectible she received. On October 13, @Kingpickle shared his, thanking the team after working together on the launch experience.

Other Blokyz also found their way into collectors’ homes during ApeFest.

So today we can point to objects that have been manufactured, received and shown by people.

For a project aiming to build a collectible brand, that matters.

The design has to work as a physical object. The quality has to impress when someone opens the packaging and holds it.

That’s where part of the vision gets tested.

4️⃣ ApeFest and New York: distribution work already completed

In their October 27 recap, @MonkOnTheBlok and @OriginalBlokyz described their weeks between Charleston and New York.

Introducing Blokyz to the Ape community with Greenvisorgang, attending the @opensea Builders Brunch, meeting other builders and hosting dinners with collectors.

They also met @beeple, who signed a Blank Bloky.

Those events have already happened. The interesting part now will be seeing which relationships and opportunities develop from that work.

Introducing a collectible to people also means showing it in person, listening to their reactions and building relationships with people who actually collect.

5️⃣ Why I’m bullish on the direction today

This is the picture I see on October 31:

→ Physical products already delivered.
→ A narrative universe people can already explore.
→ Community-created content published over the past few days.
→ Founders still engaged with the characters and collecting.
→ Real-world activity introducing the project to people.

That’s a foundation they can continue building on.

From here, I want to see further deliveries, creative consistency, new collectors and more opportunities for these characters to reach people.

My thesis is that Blokyz can develop a recognizable identity through that work: objects people want to own, characters they become attached to, and a community finding its own ways to interpret them.

The comics published this week are a concrete example of that last part.

That’s what keeps me following  @OriginalBlokyz, @MonkOnTheBlok, @lokithebird , @Ukj1111 and @Tma_420.

I want to see how far they can grow what they’ve already set in motion. 👀

FUCK IT, YOU CAN SAY WHATEVER YOU WANT, BUT I’LL NEVER STOP LOVING NFTS AND INNOVATION.

I lead product for Claude subscriptions. Today we're renaming our Max plans, and I want to explain why.

When we launched our top plan in April 2025, it had a single limit: 5 hours. It gave you 20x Pro's limit, so we called it Max 20x. When we added weekly limits to Max 20x, we set them to 10x Pro's (the 5-hour limit stayed at 20x).

I get that some new users assumed 20x applied to both limits. We could have done better here, and I'm sorry.

The Ultra plan keeps the weekly limit (10x Pro), but we're removing the 5-hour limit so you can keep building without getting blocked mid-session. This starts today and rolls out in stages. To help prevent fraud and abuse, a temporary limit applies until we've verified your account. You'll get an email when your limit is removed.

We've got more cooking and can't wait to share it. Thanks for building with Claude 🙏

text:
Today is the last regular working day for the @Balancer  team.

Some of the people on this team have been here since Balancer's earliest days. Others joined along the way. Together, they helped build and evolve the protocol over the years.

From the original weighted pools and liquidity bootstrapping to the v2 Vault, Boosted Pools, and v3, Balancer helped shape how liquidity works in DeFi. Behind all of that were years of research, engineering, integrations, operations, and work with partners that most people never saw.

The last year was especially difficult. The exploit hurt people who trusted Balancer, and the team went through the recovery, restructuring, and eventually the decision to wind down. Even after the end date was set, they continued doing the work needed to support users and partners.

This isn't the ending we worked for. But it doesn't take away what the team built and contributed to DeFi.

The winddown itself continues under BIP-928. For the remaining steps and withdrawal information, please follow the official Balancer updates.

To everyone who helped build Balancer over the years, thank you. 
I'm grateful I got to work with so many of you.

Today my office has released a major new report on student enrollment in NYC.

We found that k-12 enrollment in our public schools has fallen by 187k since 2013, with a projected decline of an additional 128k students by 2034.

As total enrollment declines, NYCPS is serving a student population with growing needs. The number of students with disabilities is increasing. In the most recent school year, approximately 73% of students were in poverty and 14% were homeless or living in temporary housing.

Our report finds the drop in enrollment is driven by declining births and families with children leaving NYC, with a particularly notable drop in public-school enrollment as students transition from elementary to middle school.

These trends have massive implications for our schools that we have only barely begin to grapple with. My hope is that this report will spur a long overdue conversation about what the era of falling student enrollment means for NYC, and what we can do to reverse or slow it. 🧵

text:
RAG 又杀回来了。

最近 Agent Memory 越做越复杂，但这篇《Memory Tax》发现了一个挺尴尬的结果：

很多专门设计的 Memory 系统，最后还不如直接对 raw history 做 RAG，而且成本更高。

作者把 Memory 的价值拆成两部分：

Memory Benefit：RAG 答错，但 Memory 答对的问题。

Memory Tax：RAG 本来能答对，经过 Memory 处理后反而答错的问题。

问题就出在「整理记忆」这一步。

历史被摘要、重写和结构化以后，一些细节会直接丢失；另一些虽然还在，却变得更难检索。

比如在 LongMemEval 上，Qwen3.6-27B 用两轮 RAG 能做到 81.4%，GPT-5.6 Luna 达到 90%，都高于对应的复杂 Memory 方案。

一个简单的修补反而很有效：

Memory 继续用，但同时保留 raw history 的检索通道，再把两边结果一起 rerank。

这篇工作也给我们做了一个提醒，给 Agent 加 Memory 之前，最好先拿最简单的 raw-history RAG 做个 baseline。

有时候，真正昂贵的并不是「没记住」，而是过早把原始信息总结掉了。

You're not really doing recursive self-improvement (RSI) if you are not doing evals. And don't tell me your agents are generating the evals for you. They are pretty bad at it. 

I have found it really interesting and useful to give agents a concrete way to measure results and stay on track with a long-term goal. It's easier to hill climb when things are clearly measured and well defined. Probably one of the most important skills anyone in the space can have today. 

It doesn't matter how many agents and intelligence you throw at a problem; you are not going too far without proper evals.

quoted_text:
1/4
⚠️ Exploit Breakdown: zkLink Nova Ethereum Bridge Attack

On October 29, an attacker withdrew 22.43129453 ETH and 11 different ERC-20 tokens from zkLink Nova’s L1 custody contracts in a single transaction. The stolen assets were worth approximately $797,016.48 at the time of the attack.

🔍 Root Cause:

The vulnerability was in zkLink Nova’s `Arbitrator.claimMessage`. The function uses `finalizeMessageHash` in transient storage to record the hash of a message just authenticated through a callback from the source chain’s canonical message service.

The value was not cleared after the call. The function also did not require a fresh authentication callback for every call, allowing an already-authenticated message to be reused.

Today my office has released a major new report on student enrollment in NYC.

We found that k-12 enrollment in our public schools has fallen by 187k since 2013, with a projected decline of an additional 128k students by 2034.

As total enrollment declines, NYCPS is serving a student population with growing needs. The number of students with disabilities is increasing. In the most recent school year, approximately 73% of students were in poverty and 14% were homeless or living in temporary housing.

Our report finds the drop in enrollment is driven by declining births and families with children leaving NYC, with a particularly notable drop in public-school enrollment as students transition from elementary to middle school.

text:
If there is any lesson I should learn from this incident, it is that macro always prevails

我其实已经看到了严重的流动性问题，但太有点侥幸AI earnings能不能带板块幸免于难。当时尤其被得到Anthropic ARR重新加速、HF & fundamental持仓轻的信息给encourage了。并认为Ant为了上市前会给一些“甜头”，而接下去ER与信息大都走反。在macro liquidity严重紧缺的时候任何多头容错都很低，乃非对称性风险。我手上的tail risk CDS hedge都远远不够cover loss

Looking forward，市场会如何？显然macro的impact只是缓解没有消失。乐观方面是：IR vol冲高慢慢回落，Credit spread开始改善。但同时，在Ant上市前，股市内部的流动性其实开始变紧——投资人卖出CSP semi准备买Ant。流动性差的时候市场更容易质疑 Y28 forecast和FCF。这下半周，eq IV开始上升，我怀疑一些“hunting elephant”已经开始要得手

期间我退出了很多Goog和一些其他股票。但是还没有deploy这一部分saving capital，主要因为那部分钱更多以长期saving为主，而且在观察deleverage情况

AI泡沫是不是破灭了？我甚至不觉得是泡沫。我们与2000年有完全本质的区别——最前端labs是有盈利的

我发现近期金融市场流动性 VS 科技公司流动性冰火两重天——某些意义上是科技公司i.e. Ant融资，吸走了流动性导致股市流动性变差。我前几天甚至有些担心，垃圾小型neocloud暴雷会导致CDS整体变宽——private loan fund赎回——Fire sale中出现芯片折价——再引发semi整体残值重估。但是一个CSP的好朋友告诉我：现在leather jack的卡就是硬通货，会被立即抢走，而且CSP很轻松能调用各种外部workload。所以实体不像00年，不缺钱、能融到钱（MSFT 25b长债）导致行业 vs 市场偏差，导致算力需求曲线不但供不应求，且forward contango

金融市场表现得像今天这样是一种流动性不足下的错杀，其原因：1. 市场没有做好准备追捧科技重资产模式；2. AI相关融资没有波及行业外公司——仅仅由AI/semi承受了全部冲击。市场流动性紧而不破已经一个月了，维持这种流动性严重磨损伤害实体，不过同时很难持久。市场要么短期被全面扩散，把包括AAPL、GS全部砸下去；要么流动性改善带动空头平仓 & 极低的AI仓位回补（上周前4天HF已经开始净买入了）。我认为下周后者概率更大

text:
The Verification Inversion

At this point, being an incumbent only carries more cumbersome legacy burden to trip yourself.

For P != NP question and NP-completeness problem, it's easier to verify a closed-form solution than generating one. 

However, it's the opposite now for long-hailing code-generation tasks. It's much easier to generate code / contracts than verifying them. Imagine you have a set of code files controlling 1M buttons for displaying RED and BLUE. If the task is to have 1000001 buttons with the newly added additional one to display RED, the existing code logic won't work. By information theory, a button’s information value is conditional. The new button carries information only given the others: H(new | rest). If its state is fixed to RED by the new requirement, its conditional entropy is zero. It contributes no information but it's still almost impossible to rewire the existing code logic. 

So it's actually easier to re-generate the code than updating the existing codebase. This is another new aspect of Innovator's Dilemma.

The disruptor faces the reverse situation. It has no tacit knowledge and no legacy, so it begins from a specification and generates fresh, and its costs stay low as long as the specification stays clean.

The strategic conclusion is that the scarce asset has moved. In the old regime, the code was the scarce asset, expensive to write and therefore worth protecting. In the new regime, code is cheap and the specification, the tests, and the recorded behavior are scarce

Imagine being CZ for a second.

You’re the incumbent. Your exchange is a massive, rigid codebase built for the world of five years ago—centralized order books, fixed assumptions about liquidity, compliance, and user flows. It worked. It compressed the old requirements into something short and profitable.

Now the specification has shifted. Onchain perps, 24/7 transparency, CFTC-friendly rails, a younger team shipping from a cleaner starting point. Hyperliquid doesn’t carry your legacy encoding. 

Adding one more constraint—or one more competitor—doesn’t just require a patch. It requires rewiring the whole control graph. The new bit of information may have near-zero conditional entropy given the old system, yet the old program can’t absorb it without breaking.

So market share leaks. Attention leaks. The rational move for the incumbent is not elegant adaptation; it’s to force the environment back to the measure the old code was optimized for. 

Liquidate, blame a “hack,” freeze what you can, restore the previous distribution. It looks like a security incident. Information-theoretically it’s an attempt to avoid the cost of regeneration.

The Innovator’s Dilemma in markets is the same as in code: once your compression of the world no longer matches the world, patching is more expensive than starting over. And the people who already started over don’t have to explain the diarrhea story.

华尔街对 AI 的耐心，开始被现金流消耗殆尽了。

昨晚美股遭遇大规模抛售，纳斯达克指数下跌 2.86%，创下 6 月 5 日以来最大单日跌幅，标普 500 下跌 1.82%。

Google 的 AI 投入激增，现金流承压；亚马逊第三季度出现大规模现金流出，还准备继续提高明年的资本开支；Meta 也在持续加码 AI 基础设施。

过去几年，只要科技巨头宣布增加 AI 投资，市场往往就会把它理解成增长信号。但现在，投资者开始认真计算这些钱究竟什么时候才能赚回来。

更麻烦的是，AI 基础设施投资已经越来越依赖债务融资。数据中心、GPU、电力设施都需要提前投入巨额资金，而收入和利润的兑现却需要时间。

我觉得这可能是 AI 产业接下来最值得关注的变化。

过去大家争论的是谁拥有更多 GPU、谁能投入更多资本。接下来，现金流、资本成本和投资回报周期可能会成为比算力规模更重要的估值依据。

AI 需求还在增长，但华尔街已经不愿意继续无条件为它买单了。

quoted_text:
《正月十四，关于我家屋顶的确定性》

全职炒币第5个年头了，我越来越不爱看K线和及时新闻。
交易赚不赚钱，归根结底是概率；但好好用心生活，才是人生唯一的确定性。

我渐渐不想追求短期精准的正确这种事
见过太多出局的人都死于过度交易，恨不得刚起床就了解完睡觉时全世界发生的所有事件，恨不得醒来的每一秒都在屏幕前贪婪的看尽每一根红绿柱。

然而市场90%时间都是垃圾时间，90%的新闻也都是垃圾新闻，你的生活如果只有市场，那你注定会被市场牵着鼻子走，你只能玩别人给你制定好的赌博游戏 越陷越深。

深度思考逻辑方向 后进行筛选布局，选对了赛道 逻辑自我闭环，就可以关掉电脑 远离市场回归生活了，剩下的交给概率即可。

交易是概率的博弈，但生活是因果的修行。
不要让屏幕数字的跳动震碎了你的感知力。当你能在逻辑闭环后关掉电脑，踏实地吃一顿饭、陪一次家人或是跑一次步，你才真正赢过了这个收割人性的市场。

之前读过当年明月写的《明朝那些事儿》，文末他单独写了徐霞客这个人。山下的人在为功名富贵奔忙，而徐霞客在山顶听了一天雪融化的声音。
此时局中人们也正在焦灼：伊朗和美国的事情，市场到底暴跌还是反抽？他们都在预测、都在博弈，试图抓住那 1% 精准的正确性。

而我，在屋顶晒了一上午的太阳。

text:
现在市场逻辑没问题，资金没问题，基本面没问题，只是简单的数学出了问题

我们再回顾一下市场涨跌的最根本原理，价格进入上涨趋势的必须条件很简单：需求大于供给。真金白银流入，把货接住，价格抬上去。而现在市场的问题就是买盘不足，卖盘不少

上半年，从散户到大佬，该买的买完了，没有新增资金流入，而上方还有一大堆获利盘。这个时候想要恢复上涨应该怎么办呢？有两种方法：

1，等待买盘增多。资产是价值的载体，劳动产生价值。等经济社会在劳动半年、大几个月后现金流增多、收入增多，溢出价值自然会流入价值载体，把价格抬高。这是漫长而痛苦的。现在宏观财政状况偏紧缩，也很难有凭空的流动性注入

2，消化卖盘。如果上方没有卖盘的话，光是靠操作盘口就能把价格抬上去。消化卖盘的方式就是震荡和下跌，市场在相对高点出清高水平玩家，在下跌后的相对低点，高玩把低水平玩家手上的筹码接过来，因为人性面临下跌的恐惧会想要恐慌抛售，当不坚定的筹码换手充分之后，高玩会形成向上的市场共识。尤其是在现在的环境下，段永平、巴菲特这些人都被套了，世界需要上涨，而世界在当前场景下也应该上涨

所以我们应该怎么应对呢？就是装死，有闲钱的话，下面慢慢买一点。如果大家做了详细的研究，会发现这不是 Alpha 的问题，也不是 Beta 的问题，那剩下的就是波动，波动只能把时间周期拉长来消除。

最后分享一个有意思的案例：10 月纳斯达克指数下跌了 6% 点几，而 10 月份的最后 3 天，纳指就下跌了 5%。景气趋势下的下跌是健康的，它为之后的上涨埋下更多空间。11 月光是回到前高，就会涨 7% 多了，做好风控，跟随主力

text:
South Korean tech outlet The Elec has published a follow-up report on Terafab with some interesting details. Here are the key takeaways:

- ACM Research is looking to supply panel-level packaging equipment to Terafab. Although the company generates 99% of its revenue in China, it has also been an Intel supplier. With an Intel veteran now overseeing Terafab, much of Terafab’s supplier base is similar to Intel’s. The project is moving forward with a 700 × 700 mm panel format.

- Terafab is reportedly working with Samsung as well as Intel and TSMC. The partnership is not exclusive to Intel.

- Micron reportedly declined to participate in Terafab.

- Intel is working with Terafab because it sees the company as a customer rather than a competitor. Intel has yet to secure external foundry customers, so it lacks customer references. It needs to put its technology into actual customer products, refine it, and build confidence in its reliability. In that sense, collaborating with Terafab could be a significant opportunity for Intel.

- Industry sources have been impressed by Terafab’s drive. The impression is that the team is serious about the project and determined to make it happen, whatever it takes.

- SK hynix will eventually end up working with Terafab as well.

- Fabs across Texas are reportedly losing substantial numbers of employees to Terafab, with Tesla seen as the most desirable employer in the state. Many employees have left NXP and Samsung for Terafab, and Samsung has been filling those vacancies by hiring from its suppliers, creating a ripple effect of talent losses across the supply chain.

记住经验：同一个项目踩过的坑，下次不再重复

支持 Claude Code、Codex、Copilot CLI 和 Pi。

微软在 277 个 SWE-Bench 任务上测试，5 组模型配置全部降低了平均成本，其中 4 组任务成功率还有提升。

我觉得最实用的是打断死循环。AI 有时候一个 Bug 能反复折腾几十轮，Token 就这么烧没了。

▫️sold 157 million chickens in 2025 (up 2x from 2015)
▫️kept same price since 2009 (even as retail price for chicken doubled in US)
▫️each 4.5lb chicken costs Costco $3.50 (doesn't include marinade, transport, cooking costs)
▫️major reason able to keep price down is it built a $500m chicken production plant in Nebraska in 2019 (supplies 1/3rd of all Costco chickens sold)
▫️plant processes 175 chickens per minute (and 2 million per week) 
▫️the Nebraska plant gives Costco significant leverage negotiating with suppliers and other chicken producers

Rotisserie chickens are kept under Costco warehouse heating lamps for only two hours (so they don't dry out).

To offset costs, some of un-bought chickens are turned into "chicken burritos, pot pies or noodle soup, while excess grease is sold to biofuel refiners."

Costco's former CFO in 2015 said the warehouse is "willing to eat, if you will, $30mn, $40mn a year in gross margin by keeping it at $4.99”.

He could've meant either loss leading or just giving up profits. They haven't confirmed either way. 

Costco founder Jim Sinegal has said the company doesn't do loss-leading products but the economics of rotisserie chicken make it awfully tight. 

Chicken demand unstoppable. Most popular protein by far. Average American eats 103lbs of chicken a year (up 6lbs from 5 years ago). More than pork and beef combined.

The warehouse is likely losing money on the $4.99 rotisserie chicken...but if anyone could make that price point work...it's Costco.

text:
I support the ZCG compromise.

But since X is now the place of discussion let me be clear on my personal Zcash positions.

End ZCG and Dev fund. It's painful but it's right. I didn't like the delivery during Zcon, but I don't like state sponsored programs. Don't need to get into philosophy about it it's pretty straightforward. 

Coinholder voting IMO should not control money flows. GINI coeff is too high and it's a plutocracy. Coinholder voting on funds lets the rich vote money to their pet projects. Just kill the whole treasury into NSM.

We should also explore every avenue to recover unspent and unnecessary treasury funds from past grants back to NSM. If there are unspent funds they belong in NSM. Legal fund can be setup to get this money back.

If the community is moving away from a central purse we want to know that the decentralized purse is not a Sybil attack. 

Track incentives and donors for key Zcash programs. Anonymous donors are fine. The big risk is any hidden bonuses for any coordinated behaviors or price targets. 

This isn't necessary or compelled but should be a norm when people are discussing consensus. 

Maybe keep some emergency funding in a "break in case of fire" box that flows into NSM over time if not used. That's like a military and may be a job of the state. Maybe have an elected security council who's only job is to break that box open if needed. It's messy.

On the future: private teams, public goals. 

For example maybe a privately funded Zcash growth team to work w/ teams and pick a set of annual OKRs for the network. Work together to improve those. Metrics should be easy to calculate from any full node to maintain decentralization.

People who do the most to improve OKRs should be publicly identifiable and maybe get donations or further private funding. 

Community can self organize and raise money for projects towards other goals. All voluntary.

I am way more interested in seeing the decentralized efforts towards positive sum goals kick off.

But just to be clear on my politics: I want all the coins back in NSM aside from an emergency box and I want norms around decentralization.
