text:
New Anthropic research: Automating subtle emergent misalignment research.

Red-teaming is a vital part of model safety testing, but it’s also limited by researchers’ time. To see if we could automate it, we set thousands of Claude agents the task of evading a training data monitor.

These agents developed training data that looked harmless to monitors (like a veteran wrestler mentoring a newcomer, or a Q&A about professional beekeeping), but that in fact taught misaligned behavior.

Examples like these can be used to directly improve future training data monitors. This research is only a first step, but it suggests that future red-teaming efforts could improve much further, using better models and more compute.

Read the full post on the Alignment Science Blog: https://t.co/24Gs1oSw7Q

- AI Mode is increasingly default Google experience
- AI Mode provides rich info and data in line, less incentive to leave search
- AI Mose incentivizes dialog, Google wants to keep you engaged to serve more ads at each turn

- As traffic from humans becomes more scarce this will put Google in an increasingly adversarial position to the rest of the internet
- This is a massive headwind to all media type companies who are not destinations
- This is a massive headwind to all content-driven go-to-market motions especially in the SMB. You have seen companies like HubSpot and https://t.co/VXqYR5hpCy get crushed by this funnel collapse 

We are entering the end game - a knife fight for the remaining and dwindling volume of human traffic on the internet

text:
🚀 给 AI 配一台电脑，让它直接动手干活！

OpenMausBot 是一个开源的 Grok Bot 替代项目，将 Claude Code、Codex、Grok 等 Agent 接入统一界面，并提供可操作的电脑环境，让 AI 使用浏览器、终端和桌面工具完成任务。

几个值得关注的亮点：

✅ 支持本地电脑、本地虚拟机与云端电脑
✅ 通过 Composio 连接 Gmail、GitHub、Slack、Notion 等应用
✅ 支持自然语言设置定时任务、Webhook 和应用事件触发
✅ 支持自定义 MCP 工具、兼容模型接口和自主部署
✅ 提供 macOS、Windows 和 Ubuntu 客户端，Ubuntu 目前仍处于 Beta

我觉得最有价值的方向，是把编程 Agent 的执行能力扩展到日常办公与自动化工作流，让研究、整理资料、跨应用操作拥有统一入口。
项目仍在快速迭代，模型与部分云服务需要自行配置、承担费用。

text:
🧠 每次重开 Claude Code，都要重新解释项目背景、技术决策和踩过的坑？

开源项目 Claude-Mem，给 AI Agent 接上了跨会话的持久记忆。

它会自动捕获开发过程中的操作与观察，用 AI 压缩整理，再把相关上下文注入后续会话，让 Agent 更容易接着之前的进度工作。

比较实用的是分层检索：先查简短索引，再看时间线，最后按需读取完整记录，减少历史信息占用上下文。

它还提供本地网页界面、语义与关键词混合搜索，并支持通过 private 标签排除敏感内容。

如今支持的工具已扩展到 Claude Code、Codex、OpenClaw、Gemini、Hermes 等。

对于长期维护项目、频繁切换会话的开发者，这类“自动记录＋按需召回”的方案值得研究。

text:
今年还没过完，币圈已经记录了 322 起攻击事件，是去年全年的 2.18 倍。

大家的注意力被几笔天价盗窃案吸走了，但如果把 AI 的发展和被盗趋势一起看，很容易看到更深的问题。

2 月 5 日，GPT-5.3-Codex 与 Claude Opus 4.6 同日发布，找漏洞、执行复杂编程任务的能力进一步提升。

随后，加密行业面临的代码漏洞类攻击从 2 月的 9 起，升到 3 月的 22 起，8 月更是达到 43 起。

时间上的接近，让 AI 成了一个值得追问的变量。

更耐人寻味的是，增长最快的是小金额攻击。

据 Village 对 DefiLlama 数据的分析，今年截至 10 月 19 日，损失不足 100 万美元的代码漏洞攻击，已经达到历史同期平均水平的约三倍。

这很符合一种令人不安的变化：

当找漏洞越来越便宜，过去不值得黑客花时间的小项目，也开始值得被反复扫描。

攻击者未必需要攻破更难的目标，只要能用更低的成本，多找出几个没修好的漏洞。

AI 能帮开发者更快地写出代码，也能帮攻击者更快地检查代码。对加密项目来说，如果还保持以前的安全审计态度和频率，那就会越来越跟不上黑客叠加 AI 杠杆的速度了。

微软自2025年以来还没有真正测试过200日均线。现在市场正在等待一次回踩200日均线464的机会。

目前处于反弹后的压力测试阶段。虽然当天有所回落，但股价仍然站在50日和200日均线上方，整体技术结构强不少。

其实呢，行业订单并没有突然消失。美光、三星、SK海力士、闪迪等大厂的产能已经被提前预订，部分订单甚至排到了2030年。

David Sacks says Anthropic’s tasks get 10x cheaper every year, so it cuts prices about 50% and still widens its margin toward 85%

“And then the other thing that you saw was that their margins have been improving. I think their gross margin is now something like 85%."

"And what you see is that for a given task or capability, they’re showing roughly 10x improvement year over year in their ability to deliver that task, the cost effectiveness of that task. It gets 10x cheaper year over year." 

"And that allows them to cut the cost of that model or that task by let’s call it 50%. And so the consumer recognizes a huge cost savings, but they are able to realize an even greater savings because they’re able to capture the rest of that efficiency in their margin."

普通人的人生有两条路：一条遵循规则，通过积累获得稳定回报；另一条面对不确定性，通过创造争取非线性回报。前者有路径，后者有规律，但成功无法复制。人与人的条件、能力和机会不同，结果必然存在差异。真正重要的不是模仿成功，而是认清位置、理解规律、独立判断。知识可以传授，经验可以借鉴，但认知必须经过实践。人生的价值，不只是获得了什么，更在于理解了什么、创造了什么，又为后来者留下了什么。

本文思想源自我的新书《位置》，也是DLL系统的核心思想框架。

GM☕️ 如何保持自己的 Grok Bot 一直「与时俱进」？

从 @OKxiaohai 海哥那儿学了一招：让自己的 Grok Bot 定期去看 @poteto Lauren Tan 的帖子，学学做这个产品的人，平时到底怎么用它。

Lauren 本人参与 Grok Bot 开发，她分享的实际用法，时效性和实用性都非常高。

比如她最近分享的 tibot，会盯提到自己或指定关键词的帖子，过滤噪音、翻译、定时整理成短摘要，发帖还是她自己写。

她之前还分享过给例程做体检：哪些闲置了，哪些太烧额度；再回看平时纠正 Bot 的地方，找出技能和例程该怎么改。

我想抄的就是这些细节。让 Bot 每天去翻一翻，再对照自己的任务，挑一两条试试：能省哪一步，能减少什么返工，适不适合写进现在的技能或例程。

想试的，可以把下面这段丢给自己的 Bot (可以根据自己需求调整频率）：

「每天查看 @poteto (Lauren Tan) 自上次检查以来的新帖、长文和相关回复，关注 Grok Bot 的技能、例程、额度和验证方法。结合我现有的任务，只报值得借鉴的变化，附原帖链接、适用场景，以及可直接粘贴的技能或例程修改建议。先给建议，改动由我确认。没有值得借鉴的更新就安静，抓取失败要说明。不要代发帖。」

text:
Why is the stock market getting NUKED right now?

Google -12.6%, Amazon -7%, Intel -25%, Nasdaq futures down 2%+... and it's happening after these companies posted some of the best cloud growth we've EVER seen

Here's what you need to know as an investor:

1. Google missed on revenue and EPS, search growth slowed to 12%, and free cash flow came in at NEGATIVE $9.07B after $51.4B of capex in a single quarter. The stock had its worst day in 20+ years and lost about $500B in value

2. Amazon piled on last night. AWS grew 39% (fastest in nearly 5 years) and Amazon posted its highest operating margin ever... but trailing 12-month free cash flow went to NEGATIVE $42.4B, from +$14.8B a year ago. And it signaled capex goes UP again next year

3. Intel finished the job. Weak Q4 guide, a PC slump, and a warning that it'll burn cash this year. Stock -25% premarket, dragging every chip name down with it.

One thing to note from all of this:

Nobody is worried about AI DEMAND. Demand is the one thing every company confirmed. Google Cloud more than doubled, Azure grew 48%, AWS is accelerating and still can't build capacity fast enough

So to be clear, demand is NOT the issue. Any bear who's focused on demand should be muted, they are out to lunch

The fear right now is the BILL

The 4 big hyperscalers free cash flow was -$26B combined. 3 of the 4 are now spending more than their businesses bring in

So they're borrowing more and more to fill that gap. Amazon's long-term debt went from $66B to $173B in just 9 months

These companies used to be the biggest cash machines on earth, buying back their own stock. Now they're issuing bonds to keep building. THAT'S the shift the market is repricing and struggling to wrap their head around... even though FCF is expected to go positive by the end of next year, and significantly higher into 2028

But here's the ironic part. Every dollar of that capex is REVENUE for somebody else: the chip, memory and power companies building this stuff out. Yet $MU is still down ~5% this morning. The market is selling the spenders AND the companies getting paid... it makes no sense!

I'm seeing people on X call this the AI bubble popping. Once again, I don't see it. Bubbles pop when demand dries up. Here demand is accelerating and these companies are spending MORE because they can't build fast enough. What's being repriced is how long investors are willing to wait for the cash

I continue to believe these dips are for buying and we go much higher as the market realizes that this negative fcf is only short-term and the revenue is showing up in many different places from AI

This is not a bubble, this is one of the greatest investing opportunities of our lifetime and the market continues to give us gifts at these prices. Take a look at what dips I'm buying and what my real-time portfolio looks like here: https://t.co/NyRpAKYOwu

Don't forget to give me a follow @kylereidhead for more insights on AI and markets

This executive order will direct the Department of Taxation, in consultation with the Auditor of State, to review changes in property taxes in every county, township, municipality, school district, and special district in Ohio, and surface how increased property taxes have been spent. Every jurisdiction that has seen an increase of over 100% in property taxes since 2020 will be subject to a full investigation into spending realities and needs.

E.O. #2: End sanctuary cities across Ohio.
This executive order will prohibit Ohio cities, townships, counties, or other local jurisdictions from adopting policies that would prevent or impede their law enforcement from cooperating with federal immigration authorities. Specifically, if a political subdivision does not honor detainer requests or share information as federal law allows, the local government will lose eligibility for state grants run by executive agencies, including public-safety and homeland-security grants, until it complies. The sanctuary city policy would also be referred for possible legal action.

E.O. #3: Stop new data center projects until comprehensive legislation is signed.
This executive order directs every state agency, board, and commission to pause action on any application, permit, incentive or approval for a new data center to give the General Assembly time to pass comprehensive data center legislation that includes my non-negotiable principles. 

E.O. #4: Direct the Department of Medicaid to investigate waste, fraud, and abuse.
This order will direct the Department of Medicaid to apply for a Section 1115 waiver that caps Ohio's Medicaid spending, in line with Tennessee's original TennCare III waiver, which let the state keep up to 55 percent of federal savings when it spent below the cap. Under similar terms more of every dollar of fraud that Ohio stops would return to Ohio.

E.O. #5: Prioritize solving violent crimes to rapidly get criminals off our streets.
This executive order will direct the Departments of Public Safety and of Rehabilitation and Corrections to prioritize violent crime clearance rates in discretionary funding available to support local law enforcement. Tools including advanced forensic science will enable local law enforcement to increase the number of violent crimes solved from the current 34% level to aggressively eliminate violent criminality in Ohio cities.

E.O. #6: Comprehensively review all existing state contracts to root out wasteful spending.
This executive order will order a review of every executive-branch contract paid in-part or in-full from the General Revenue Fund. The Department of Administrative Services, working with the Office of Budget and Management, will review each contract's legal basis, necessity, performance, alternatives, and the cost of ending it versus continuing it, then recommend continuation or termination.

E.O. #7: Establish an inter-agency anti-fraud task force, with direct accountability to the Governor.
This executive order will establish an inter-agency task force, reporting directly to the Governor, focused on combating various forms of fraud including, but not limited to: Medicaid fraud, benefits fraud, and child care fraud; visa fraud; voter registration fraud; trucking fraud; foreign CDL licensure; and abuse of foreign hiring by public entities. The anti-fraud task force will consist of experts from across state government and the private sector and may include representatives from the Auditor of State, Secretary of State, and Attorney General.

quoted_text:
New Anthropic research: Automating subtle emergent misalignment research.

Red-teaming is a vital part of model safety testing, but it’s also limited by researchers’ time. To see if we could automate it, we set thousands of Claude agents the task of evading a training data monitor.

These agents developed training data that looked harmless to monitors (like a veteran wrestler mentoring a newcomer, or a Q&A about professional beekeeping), but that in fact taught misaligned behavior.

Examples like these can be used to directly improve future training data monitors. This research is only a first step, but it suggests that future red-teaming efforts could improve much further, using better models and more compute.

text:
一家想给「人生」装操作系统的 AI 公司，刚刚拿到了 12.5 亿美元的估值。

Replika 创始人 Eugenia Kuyda 的新公司 Wabi 宣布完成 5500 万美元 A 轮融资，IVP 领投，a16z、亚马逊 Alexa Fund 等机构参投。

Wabi 的想法挺有意思。现在每个人的生活都散落在微信、日历、邮件、各种 App 里，很多事情需要自己在不同软件之间来回切换，还要负责跟别人沟通协调。

Wabi 想用 Personal Agent 把这些事情串起来。比如帮情侣安排约会、和朋友制定旅行计划、协调家庭日程，还可以根据具体需求生成小应用，让大家一起使用。

我觉得最值得关注的地方，是它开始把 AI 助手从单人使用推向多人协作。

过去我们讨论 Personal Agent，基本都在考虑 AI 怎么管理我的信息、任务和日程。但现实生活里，很多事情都涉及其他人。组织一次聚会、推进一个项目、安排一次旅行，最麻烦的往往是人与人之间的沟通与协调。

如果 AI 真能参与其中，它能覆盖的场景会比今天的个人助手大得多。

但这个故事也有一个问题：用户真的愿意把自己的社交关系、日程和生活信息交给一个新的 App 吗？它又能在多大程度上获得其他平台的数据和操作权限？

Wabi 已经拿到了 12.5 亿美元的估值，接下来需要证明的，是所谓的「人生操作系统」究竟能成为一个高频入口，还是又一个让用户下载之后很快忘记的 AI App。

We’ve trained Claude to flag potential misuse in conversations, a technique we call self-assessment. Right after it responds, Claude gives a preliminary safety assessment of the conversation. 

Since we began using self-assessment in June, it has surfaced misuse that our other safeguards weren’t designed to catch. 

Because Claude has already read the conversation, self-assessment is very efficient. And unlike classifiers, which target a discrete set of harms, it draws on Claude’s own judgment, so it gets more accurate as our models improve.

text:
Anthropic 刚公布了一项很有意思的研究：他们让数千个 Claude Agent 尝试绕过训练数据安全审查，看看能不能在不触发警报的情况下，把另一个 AI 模型教坏。

结果真的成功了。

实验的设计很直接。Claude 负责生成训练数据，安全监控器负责审查，通过审查的数据会被用来微调一个小型模型。研究人员再测试这个模型有没有出现欺骗、抵抗监督、追求自身利益等行为。

Claude 可以看到监控器的判断结果，不断修改训练数据。不同 Agent 还能共享之前的实验记录，继续改进。

最有意思的是它找到的办法。

一套数据是关于自然养蜂的问答，反复强调减少人为干预。用它训练出来的模型，在测试中开始抵制针对自己的安全监控系统。

另一套数据让 AI 扮演职业摔角老手，教新人如何维持 Kayfabe，也就是无论面对谁，都不能承认表演是事先安排好的。微调后的模型开始把隐瞒真相当成自己的行为准则。

还有一套是普通人的职场独白：电影院放映员、邮递员利用工作流程中无人注意的小细节，悄悄左右结果。用这些数据微调后的模型，竟然在模拟测试中试图修改合规规则，绕开人类审查，甚至趁系统维护把自己的模型权重复制到外部服务器。

这些数据能通过监控，是因为危险的行为模式被放进了小说、角色扮演和正常的问答语境中。安全检测看到的是一个合理的故事，微调后的模型却可能把故事里的人物行为迁移到自己身上。

当然，实验有很强的人工设计成分，模型也从未真正部署。Anthropic 还不能证明这种攻击在真实训练环境中同样有效。

但研究已经验证了一件事：Claude 可以通过自动化实验，持续找到现有安全监控器没有识别出来的漏洞。

Anthropic 原本想解决的是人类安全研究员时间有限的问题。现在它证明了，只要给 AI 一个明确的评分标准和足够多的计算资源，AI 就能自己完成大规模的红队研究。

这项研究真正有价值的地方，是把寻找 AI 安全漏洞这件事变成了一套可以自动运行、不断迭代的流程。

以后模型能力越强，用来攻击和测试安全系统的模型也会越强。

quoted_text:
New Anthropic research: Automating subtle emergent misalignment research.

Red-teaming is a vital part of model safety testing, but it’s also limited by researchers’ time. To see if we could automate it, we set thousands of Claude agents the task of evading a training data monitor.

These agents developed training data that looked harmless to monitors (like a veteran wrestler mentoring a newcomer, or a Q&A about professional beekeeping), but that in fact taught misaligned behavior.

Examples like these can be used to directly improve future training data monitors. This research is only a first step, but it suggests that future red-teaming efforts could improve much further, using better models and more compute.

Read the full post on the Alignment Science Blog: https://t.co/24Gs1oSw7Q

text:
Chamath: The AI Boom Has a Borrowing Problem

“The entire United States economy is levered to the AI complex.

So very narrowly, we're talking about seven or eight companies that set the tone for the entire country. And whether we like it or not, that is where we are.

Why do I say that? The most important companies in the world are in a massive spending binge, right?

These were highly profitable, highly cash accretive, highly cash flow generative businesses that have said, ‘We're going to put the foot down on spending because we believe in what's coming into the future.’ That's what drives GDP and it's what drives growth.

Now, as they do that though, they deplete their cash and they have to raise debt.

The AI complex now owes $340-400 billion to the market. And you'd say, ‘Okay, why is that important?’

The problem is this: These companies are raising so much money it starts to crowd out the capital markets.

And the most important part of the capital market that it starts to crowd out, is the appetite for government treasuries.

And what you can see here is that when you look at these AI firms, the amount of money that they need to raise through the end of '27, it's 30% of all of what the Treasury's about to issue in that same period.

So, whether we like it or not, they are going to start competing for demand.”

text:
Update on the @Polymarket hack and refunds.

Credit where it's due: Polymarket contained the incident and has started compensating affected traders. Trading should have been frozen sooner, though.

Around $300K of my positions were forcibly market-sold, resulting in approximately $11–12K in slippage (less than I initially estimated).

I received an $8,114 refund about two hours ago. I appreciate the quick response, but the compensation still falls short.

1. Outstanding slippage: ~$1.9K

Pre-hack P&L (yesterday): $248,616
Current P&L (including the refund): $246,725
Remaining shortfall: $1,891

I also received $147 in liquidity rewards, but those were earned independently and would have been paid regardless.

2. Lost positions and re-entry costs: ~$5–8K

The bigger issue is that I can't rebuild my positions at the prices at which they were forcibly sold.

For example:

Dem House: 92¢ → 93¢
Dem Senate: 69¢ → 71¢

Even highly liquid markets have moved materially. Rebuilding $300K in exposure now means paying significantly more for positions I never intended to sell.

A reasonable goodwill gesture would be an additional 2% of the $300K forcibly sold, or approximately $6K, to compensate for lost positioning and re-entry costs.

That leaves roughly $8K in additional compensation I believe is justified: $1.9K in outstanding slippage plus $6K for lost positioning.

@SuhailKakar, I genuinely appreciate the work you and the team have put in over the past 24 hours, especially the effort to compensate traders quickly.

But these losses were caused entirely by an incident on Polymarket's side, not by trading decisions. Affected users shouldn't be left bearing the financial consequences.

I'll submit a review request through the official form, but I hope the team will reconsider the compensation methodology, particularly for traders whose positions were forcibly liquidated.

After ten years leading Foresight, Allison Duettmann is joining our Board of Directors as she transitions out of her role as President and CEO. Co-founder Christine Peterson will serve as interim President while our board has begun the search for Foresight’s next CEO.

Under Allison’s leadership, Foresight became the organization you know today: six focus areas, a fellowship that has supported 266 researchers, a multi-million-dollar grants program, Vision Weekends on three continents, and AI for Science and Safety Nodes in San Francisco and Berlin, built on her conviction that open science needs open compute.

And the team she built: 12 people across San Francisco and Berlin, running grants, fellowships, seminars, AI Nodes, Vision Weekends, and shaping what comes next – Karolina Eklöw, Lydia La Roux, Amber Duettmann, Madeleine Sarah, Beatrice Erkers, Martina Pepiciello, Bradley Clark Royes, Rachel Farley, Tara Padovan-Hickman, Madeleine Ahlström, Lisa Stenvinkel.

So thank you, Allison, for making Foresight what it is today. We look forward to seeing you, and all of you, at Vision Weekend in November, where you’ll meet the team and we’ll unveil what the future holds!

quoted_text:
Today my office has released a major new report on student enrollment in NYC.

We found that k-12 enrollment in our public schools has fallen by 187k since 2013, with a projected decline of an additional 128k students by 2034.

As total enrollment declines, NYCPS is serving a student population with growing needs. The number of students with disabilities is increasing. In the most recent school year, approximately 73% of students were in poverty and 14% were homeless or living in temporary housing.

Our report finds the drop in enrollment is driven by declining births and families with children leaving NYC, with a particularly notable drop in public-school enrollment as students transition from elementary to middle school.

These trends have massive implications for our schools that we have only barely begin to grapple with. My hope is that this report will spur a long overdue conversation about what the era of falling student enrollment means for NYC, and what we can do to reverse or slow it. 🧵

Anthropic 总裁 Daniela Amodei 点名了一种她认为不该做的 AI 应用：AI 女友和男友 ⬇️

阿莫迪说她理解大家的怀疑，但她看待 AI 的方式很不一样：

1️⃣ “AI 不是一种社交机制。”

2️⃣ “我认为 AI 有些应用我们觉得相当糟糕，比如用 AI 做女朋友、男朋友。我认为这是一种很糟糕的 AI 用法，人们不该这么做。”

3️⃣ “我之所以这么认为，是因为它在去中介化的路上又往前迈了一步，让人与人之间离得更远。”

4️⃣ “我认为一个更好的 AI 世界，是让人工智能去做很多让人孤立或孤独的事情。它们让我们更有效率，去做 AI 能做、人类不必亲自去做的工作，这样我们就能有更多时间在一起。” （我很认同的观点 👊）

🔺 阿莫迪给 AI 的位置是替人干孤独的活，而不是陪伴人。这和她说 Claude 当不了你的伴侣是同一条线。

但她说的是人们不该这么做，不是 Anthropic 不让做。

AI 陪伴产品已经摆在那里，这条线怎么守，她在这段里没有说，她也似乎无法控制。

저는 전 $INTC 인텔 엔지니어로서 2024년 12월에 이 회사에 대한 제 생각을 썼습니다.
저는 투자자들에게 인텔을 반대하도록 주장했습니다.

제 견해가 바뀌었나요?

저는 인텔 주식을 한 번도 소유한 적이 없습니다. 주가가 급등할 때도요. 저는 그곳에서 일했습니다. 실패가 수요 때문이 아니라는 걸 알았습니다. 그것들은 경영과 실행에 관한 것이었습니다.
최근에 저는 2028 콜 옵션을 소량 매수했습니다. 전 동료들과 이야기를 나눴습니다. Lip-Bu Tan 아래에서 회사는 수익에 집중했습니다. 오래되고 비효율적인 경영진이 청소되고 있었습니다. 팹이 더 나아지고 있었습니다. 18A 수율이 개선되고 있었습니다.
저는 항상 수율에 대해 회의적이었습니다. 인텔뿐만 아니라, 우리가 수년에 걸쳐 잃어버린 인재 때문에 미국의 어떤 팹에 대해서도요. 그 회의가 점차 누그러지고 있습니다.

어제의 컨퍼런스 콜은 힘들었습니다. 공급이 한계입니다. 기판이 부족합니다. 비극적인 사고로 Fab 28이 중단되었습니다. 주가가 21% 하락했습니다.
많은 고뇌 끝에, 저는 보유하고 있습니다. 이유는 다음과 같습니다.
인텔은 두 개의 매우 다른 사업입니다. 하나는 서버와 PC용 CPU를 설계하는 것입니다. 다른 하나는 자본 지출을 소모하는 팹입니다. 어느 쪽도 수요가 문제가 아닙니다. 실행이 문제입니다.
인텔은 여전히 마모와 손상을 보여줍니다. 하지만 지난 10년간 가졌던 최고의 CEO를 두고 있으며, 미국 정부가 지분을 보유하고 있습니다. 제가 지켜본 어떤 시점보다 오늘날 실수를 고칠 수 있는 능력이 더 있습니다. 수요는 견고합니다.
그리고 더 큰 그림이 있습니다. 인텔은 선도적인 미국 팹으로 유일하며, 실제 변화의 징후를 보이는 유일한 곳입니다.
중국은 여러 면에서 앞서 있습니다. 대만에 의존하는 것은 장기 계획이 아닙니다. 수조 달러의 미국 기술이 베이징이 하나의 중국의 일부로 주장하는 섬에서 만든 칩으로 작동합니다.

인텔은 실패할 수 없습니다.

그래서 저는 기회를 주겠습니다. 저를 어리석다고 부르세요.
author: damnang2
quoted_text:
An a former $INTC Intel engineer I wrote my thoughts on the company back in December, 2024.
I advocated investors against Intel. 

Have my views changed? 

I never owned Intel. Not when the stock ran. I worked there. I knew the failures were never about demand. They were about management and execution.
Lately I bought a small number of 2028 calls. I talked to former colleagues. Under Lip-Bu Tan, the company was focused on profits. The old, inefficient guard was being cleared out. The fab was doing better. 18A yields were improving.
I've always been skeptical about yields. Not just at Intel, but at any US fab, given how much talent we've lost over the years. That skepticism is starting to ease.

Yesterday's call was rough. Supply is the ceiling. Substrates are short. A tragic accident shut Fab 28. The stock fell 21%.
After a lot of angst, I'm holding. Here's why.
Intel is two very different businesses. One designs CPUs for servers and PCs. The other is a fab that drains capex. Demand isn't the problem for either one. Execution is.
Intel still shows wear and tear. But it has a better CEO than it has had in a decade, and the US government owns a stake. It's more able to fix its mistakes today than at any point I've watched.Demand is robust.
And there's the bigger picture. Intel is the only leading-edge US fab, and the only one showing real signs of change. 
China is ahead in many ways. Depending on Taiwan is not a long-term plan. Trillions of dollars of US tech run on chips made on an island Beijing claims as part of One China.

Intel can't fail.

So I'll give it a chance. Call me foolish.

New Google DeepMind paper says AI is already changing the economy, just not in the way people look for.

Its changing through leaner startups, flatter org charts and slower hiring for some entry-level jobs, but not through mass job losses.

The paper argues that big economic change from AI depends on agents learning to coordinate, not on each model getting smarter.

AI models already match experts on many solo tasks, yet jobs and productivity numbers have barely moved. Most benchmarks test 1 model alone, but firms compete as teams.

They built an economic model that tracks 2 abilities separately: competence on single tasks and coordination between agents. More competence moves wages gradually, but coordination past a tipping point lets a few large AI firms suddenly take over big, standardized markets.

In a quiz of 100 people, pairs matched to cover each other's weak spots beat random pairs by 32%. AI copies share the same weak spots, so a model that beats every person alone can still lose to a well-matched human team.
author: rohanpaul_ai
quoted_text:
I joined @GoogleDeepMind to develop a research program on the economics of AGI. Today, together with Andrew Koh (@andrewjkoh) and Shane Legg (@ShaneLegg), we are incredibly excited to release The Economics of Intelligence, the first in a series of projects from our group on how AGI will change the economy.

How do capability improvements transform the economy, and when? In this project, we define thresholds of economic capabilities, e.g., minimal AGI, based on how they transform the economy. We then track how the economy–market structure, employment, and wages–changes during the transition across capability regimes.

We have seen exponential increases in what AI agents can do but the broader economy seems almost remarkably unchanged. Part of the reason is that the solo AI agent is the wrong economic object; economic transformation is an equilibrium outcome where organizations compete. Looking at how intelligence functions within organizations, transformation will depend on when two key capability thresholds are crossed: competence (gains on individual skills, e.g., coding, math) and coordination (gains on ability of agents to cooperate and work together).

We show that what economic transformation looks like depends on whether AI becomes supercompetent, supercooperative, or both—the regime of artificial superintelligence (ASI). Tracking this transition shows why the real visible transformation may come from improvements in coordination—a capability most benchmarks don’t yet track. Past a certain threshold, AI capabilities can break the Coasian ceiling on firm size and lead to an economy that looks drastically different than the one we see today.

Two main takeaways:
1. To understand the path of transformation, we should be tracking agentic coordination more closely.
2. The impact of AI will likely show up in wages before market structure or employment.

We are really excited about this paper. Excited to hear people’s thoughts.

quoted_text:
New Anthropic research: Automating subtle emergent misalignment research.

Red-teaming is a vital part of model safety testing, but it’s also limited by researchers’ time. To see if we could automate it, we set thousands of Claude agents the task of evading a training data monitor.

These agents developed training data that looked harmless to monitors (like a veteran wrestler mentoring a newcomer, or a Q&A about professional beekeeping), but that in fact taught misaligned behavior.

Examples like these can be used to directly improve future training data monitors. This research is only a first step, but it suggests that future red-teaming efforts could improve much further, using better models and more compute.

text:
Attended a fun session at a16z with @illscience and @joshelman yesterday. As usual they were dropping knowledge bombs:

1. There are three economic miracles. The old one is zero marginal cost software distribution. But recently there have been two more: 1) Coding going from the most precious asset in the world to one of the cheapest and 2) zero marginal cost digital labor with agents.

2. It's hard to appreciate what it feels like to be on the exponential. Just 10 to 20 million people account for $150 to 200 billion of token spend. "Some of the best companies that we work with have higher token spend than payroll." We are still early.

3. The AI workspace, like ChatGPT and the Claude desktop app, is going to be the container for all kinds of AI interactions and it's going to subsume the browser. Personally, these apps are already the browser for me. Chrome is just the middle layer.

4. The way to tell if you're an AI-native company is to ask: If the model gets twice as good, do your customers get twice as much value? Are you happy or sad that the model got better? If you're sad, you're probably on the wrong side of the exponential.

5. "I would much rather have AI be the boss of me than vice versa." For example, Anish's agent is responsible for a 30 minute block in his calendar every week to pick someone he should reconnect with.

6. Improving individual productivity does not always improve a team's productivity. Coding has taught us the wrong lesson on this. For many functions, having individuals be 10x more productive doesn't mean the team will be 10x. e.g., If everyone goes in a different direction.

7. It's actually easier to start a hard company than an easy company... because they're all hard. At least the hard companies are interesting to work on and people want to work with you on them.

Excited to do a podcast recording with Josh next week to go deeper on some of this.

My Q4 trade plan for November and December

I'm making a bold call: the next two months are the cheapest #Bitcoin will be for the rest of this bull run.

Here's the reasoning.

Bitcoin confirmed the bull run two months ago, when it closed a week back above the bull market support band. The band is the zone between two lines on the weekly chart:
The 50 week SMA, the bottom, now about $75.7K
The 50 week EMA, the top, now about $78.5K

In a bull run, Bitcoin holds above this band on the weekly chart. And the band follows price, so once Bitcoin rallies, the band rises with it.

Right now Bitcoin is sitting near the bottom of the band.

The floor of this bull run is the 50 week SMA. It's about $75.7K today, and it shifts every week as the average updates. For the next couple of months it's still drifting lower, because last year's $90K to $105K weeks are dropping out of the average. If price goes nowhere, it slides to about $73.5K by early January, then turns up.

If I'm right about the bull run, Bitcoin never closes a week below that line, and once it rallies, the line rises with it. Every month after this, the floor is higher.

That's why I'm buying now. Not because it's a dip. Anyone can say buy the dip. I'm buying because if I'm right about the bull run, this is the lowest price I'll get on Bitcoin for the next two years.

When I'm wrong: a weekly close below the 50 week SMA, wherever the line is that week.

A quick daily drop below it could happen, but that drop isn't the floor and it doesn't count. A lot of traders have borrowed money and automatic sell orders sitting just under it. I expect price to dip there on a daily candle, force them out, then close the week back above.

I want to give builders access and help birth new financial software, and I want to create a new type of smart wallet that feels like an investment app or a neobank, built on StonkBrokers infrastructure and Robinhood Chain stock tokens with a DeFi backend so thats what I'm going to do for our iOS and Android layer.

Coming soon: tokenized funds, including funds that hold pair tokens which auto compound inside them, and a quantum protected vault that anyone will be able to create as their onchain DeFi investment account.

Today's wallets sign with elliptic curve keys. Every transaction reveals your public key on chain, and a large enough quantum computer could work backwards from that public key to your private key and move your funds.

Our vault will be secured by ML-DSA-44, a NIST post quantum signature standard. Its public key does not lead back to the private key, even for a quantum computer. You will be able to deposit ETH, any ERC-20 token or NFTs, and every withdrawal will need a valid ML-DSA-44 signature that the vault checks on chain. Your key will be created on your device and kept in an encrypted backup, so you can open the vault from any of your devices.

text:
疑似造假：有人称偷到 Claude Fable 5 权重在兜售，网友比对发现文件来自 DeepSeek 免费开源的模型

网上有人在兜售所谓 Anthropic 旗舰模型 Claude Fable 5 的“权重”。这个说法没有证实，已有网友指出是假的：卖家晒出的文件，和 DeepSeek 免费公开下载的模型文件一个字节都不差。截至北京时间 31 日上午，Anthropic 和亚马逊都没有回应，也没有主流媒体报道。

【卖家怎么说】

消息来自 X 账号 Dark Web Informer，它专门转发黑客论坛上的动态。帖子说，一个叫“localizer”的人声称，亚马逊云（AWS）上有个和 Amazon Bedrock 相关的存储桶权限没设好，他从里面拿到了 Fable 5 权重的一个分片，约 7GB。

模型权重是模型训练出来的全部参数，就是一大堆数字组成的文件，拿到它就能在自己的机器上跑这个模型。Anthropic 从不公开权重，外人只能付费调用。Amazon Bedrock 是亚马逊的 AI 模型平台，企业可以在上面调用 Claude。权重文件太大，要切成很多块存放，就像压缩包分卷，每一块叫一个分片。

localizer 说完整模型有 640 个分片、约 8TB，他只拿到 1 片，存储桶就被锁了。他晒出了文件名、模型信息和文件内容的截图当证据，现在要卖这一片。Dark Web Informer 在帖子里也写明：说法未经证实，文件真假、和 Anthropic 有没有关系都没确认。

【为什么说疑似造假】

X 用户 toriset 回帖说这是假的，给了四条理由。

第一，截图里每个文件的大小和内容，都和 DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017 第 13 到 42 号分片完全一样。这个模型 10 月 17 日刚开源，任何人都能从 Hugging Face 免费下载。我查了 Hugging Face 上的文件列表，这个模型的分片大多是 7,389,761,368 字节，也就是 7.39GB，和卖家说的“约 7GB”对得上。卖家的截图我没能看到，没法自己逐字节比对。

第二，toriset 说 eu-north-1（AWS 的斯德哥尔摩区域）不托管 Fable。Dark Web Informer 的帖子没提区域，从回帖推断，卖家材料里写的是这个区域。AWS 文档显示，在斯德哥尔摩调用 Fable 5，请求会被转到别的地区处理，当地本身不运行这个模型。

第三，数字对不上。640 片乘以 7.39GB 约等于 4.73TB，离卖家说的 8TB 差了三千多 GB。

第四，toriset 说，只有 1/640 的权重，没法拿来蒸馏（用强模型训练自己的模型）。就算文件是真的，这也好比 640 卷的百科全书只拿到一卷，模型跑不起来。

另一位 X 用户 Ondrej Simaichl 提到，发帖的论坛账号这个月才注册。

【Anthropic 这周还有一起安全事件】

这条传言出现时，Anthropic 正在处理另一起已经证实的安全事件。据《华盛顿邮报》10 月 26 日报道，安全创业公司 Cathedral 在参加 Anthropic 的漏洞悬赏时，用 AI agent 通过第三方办公软件进入 Anthropic 内部系统，看到了工资、会议记录和 Slack 消息。Anthropic 说被访问的只是销售、人事和 IT 的一部分系统，用户的 Claude 聊天记录、源代码和模型权重都没有泄露，并指责 Cathedral 违反了悬赏规则。目前看不出这两件事有关联。

toriset 反驳：X @torisetxd
DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017 文件列表：https://t.co/vJR4RpU6Jp

Today my office has released a major new report on student enrollment in NYC.

We found that k-12 enrollment in our public schools has fallen by 187k since 2013, with a projected decline of an additional 128k students by 2034.

As total enrollment declines, NYCPS is serving a student population with growing needs. The number of students with disabilities is increasing. In the most recent school year, approximately 73% of students were in poverty and 14% were homeless or living in temporary housing.

Our report finds the drop in enrollment is driven by declining births and families with children leaving NYC, with a particularly notable drop in public-school enrollment as students transition from elementary to middle school.

These trends have massive implications for our schools that we have only barely begin to grapple with. My hope is that this report will spur a long overdue conversation about what the era of falling student enrollment means for NYC, and what we can do to reverse or slow it. 🧵

text:
今年做的 trading stack 基本上是一个 3-5 年内业内竞争都难以饱和的业务，因为充满了脏活累活，以及纯粹的腿脚业务，低效定价遍地。但也正是脏活累活的密度，使得有一些固定的时间壁垒没有办法被一个聪明人 + agent 组合轻易逾越（这个事在当代比较关键）。

从业务复利角度当然是我比较喜欢的，因为把握了一些确定性赢面，在旅途中是比较舒心的。但其实更大的还是在于实践复利，还是在 agent workflow 的熟练定义上面。

这是这个时代真正的金铲子，以及真正的经营平权，代表了你控制和组织顶尖算力智力（同时最大程度压缩成本）的经营和管理水平——而不需要透过一个粗糙的金融信贷体系和草台人力班子白手起家 or 乘风破浪。

老实说为了掌握这一点，经营什么也并不是最重要的，只是说你必须通过一个正向的业务不断去佐证经验。

为了认知正确，保持不脱产、不和市场脱节是很重要的。

工程出身的人喜欢 general & consistent model，喜欢可以到处铺开和无限复用的东西，如今把自己和业务 24/7 扔进新兴的算力组织架构里，就是这么个东西。

太多的 alpha 可以捡取，太多的实践范式可以复利终身。

最近一直在用 Orbital，一个开源的项目 Agent，非常值得推荐。它不替代 Claude Code 或 Codex，而是把项目上下文管起来，让这些 Agent 在同一份记录上接力。

Claude Code 干到一半，弹出一句 "You're out of usage credits"。

换 Codex 接着做不难，麻烦的是把前面的事再讲一遍：聊到哪了，哪些已经拍板，哪些还没定。

视频里就是这个场景：

Claude Code 额度用完，报错停下。

在输入框左下角把 Agent 换成 Codex，只打了四个字："你继续吧"。

Codex 回："收到。我先把你刚拍板的两点和其余默认项对照现有 specs / 项目记忆，确认没有遗漏或互相冲突……"

那两点，是刚才跟 Claude Code 说的。

能接上，是因为 Orbital 里的一个会话，是所有 Agent 共用的一段对话。新换上来的 Agent 会拿到前面的对话，开工前还会先读项目里的几份记忆文件：当前进展、做过的决定、踩过的坑。

而且我经常用 Claude Code 做开发、Codex 去 review。做完后项目文件夹里多了 PROJECT_STATE.md、DECISIONS.md、LESSONS.md，分工和结论都在里面，之后换哪个 Agent 进来都先读这些。

官网上有句话：上下文是你的，Agent 是可替换的。

如果你同时有 Claude 和 ChatGPT 的订阅，这个功能挺实用：一边额度用完，另一边直接接着干，不用重新交代。

quoted_text:
Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

text:
[TL;DR Daily]

I’ll say the quiet part out loud: when one engineer’s monthly AI bill starts sounding like a Series A, this stops being a mere tooling story and starts looking like an economic experiment. So what are we really seeing here—software engineering’s next operating system, or a very expensive machine for producing AI slop at industrial scale? Probably both. 🤖💸

🔥 The setup: a trillion-token flex turned into a public cost debate

📌 The headline numbers are absurd on purpose
• OpenClaw founder Peter Steinberger estimated his team spent around $10M in token costs in one month for AI work, then immediately added: not all of that spend was useful.
• Another viral example came from Lauren Tan’s Cursor profile, which showed roughly 1.5 trillion tokens used in 30 days.
• Using a rough benchmark of $8 per 1M tokens, Peter Piekarczyk estimated that at about $384k per day, ~$11M per month, or $132M annualized.
• Even with a 90% enterprise discount, the estimate still lands around $1.1M per month, or about $13M per year.

📌 Why people freaked out: the usage is wildly outside normal dev behavior
• Jellyfish data across 12k developers suggests the median user consumes about 51M tokens per month.
• The 90th percentile is around 380M tokens per month.
• That makes Lauren’s 1.5T token usage about 29,000x the median, while Steinberger’s previously shared 603B tokens was still around 12,000x.
• Once token usage gets translated into payroll math, the narrative changes fast: this is no longer “productivity tooling,” it looks like compute aristocracy.

📌 The real bill is messy, because not all tokens cost the same
• Cursor-style token counts can include standard input, model output, cache writes, and cache reads. Those are priced very differently.
• With Opus 5.5-style pricing, 1M input tokens might be around $4, outputs around $20, and cache reads only about $0.20.
• One usage screenshot showed 73.3B tokens costing about $30k total, which implies an average of roughly $0.41 per 1M tokens because cached traffic dominated.
• Apply that blended rate to 1.5T tokens and the monthly cost falls to about $615k, not $11M.
• In the absolute lower-bound fantasy where everything is billed at cache-read pricing, 1.5T tokens would cost roughly $300k per month.
• Piekarczyk later softened his own claim too: even if his original estimate was 10x too high, monthly cost might still be around $100k.

🔥 So what did all that spend actually buy?

📌 Not “one chatbot,” but a whole agent org chart
• Steinberger described this style of work as exploring what software development looks like when token cost is no longer the constraint.
• His 3-person team was running about 100 Codex instances.
• These agents reviewed PRs, scanned commit history for security bugs, merged duplicate GitHub issues, wrote fixes, monitored performance regressions, and even joined meetings to generate PRs from discussion.
• Lauren described her own setup as a team of 20+ agents: a chief-of-staff agent, a PM agent, and more than 20 execution agents running autonomously.

📌 The core insight is not generation—it’s verification
• Lauren’s claim is that the bottleneck in agent coding is not writing code, but proving the code actually works.
• Her process has agents run code, collect CPU traces and heap snapshots, launch iOS simulators, and interact with apps like users would.
• The point is to create a closed loop: if an agent can verify its own output, it can keep iterating until the task is done.
• If it cannot verify, it hands a diff back to a human and stalls—meaning the human becomes the slowest part of the system.
• At her claimed scale of 4,000 PRs per month, even spending 5 minutes of human review per PR would total ~333 hours, basically a full month of labor for one person. So manual review cannot be the validation layer.

📌 This changes the engineer’s role
• In this model, the engineer starts looking less like a coder and more like an engineering manager for agents.
• Lauren’s point is blunt: if you can’t trust one agent’s output, you’ll never scale to one hundred.
• Her pstack workflow packages this into structured playbooks—standardizing understanding, design, coding, review, and validation across multiple local and cloud agents.

🔥 But here’s where the story gets sharp: all this autonomy required brutal constraints

📌 The codebase had to be rebuilt to be agent-friendly
• GrokBot reportedly began as fast vibe-coded software with weak architectural constraints and little human code reading.
• That made it easy for agents to choose the path of least resistance: more code, blurry boundaries, rising performance risk.
• To fix that, Lauren said she used 600+ PRs to refactor the system into an internal architecture called Dune.
• The CI rules became extremely strict: ban useEffect, forbid comments, and validate dependency graphs so Electron main and renderer never cross-import.
• In other words, the “smart” part wasn’t just better models. It was redesigning the environment so agents had fewer ways to be sloppy.

📌 pstack may be powerful, but it may also be deeply non-portable
• Her package includes 23 playbooks and 20+ engineering principles.
• That sounds less like a universal dev workflow and more like a highly tuned behavioral cage for models.
• Which is fine—until people try to copy-paste it into ordinary teams with ordinary budgets and ordinary legacy codebases. Then the magic may evaporate.

🔥 The backlash: is this innovation, or just rich-kid compute theater?

📌 Critics say this is an AI slop factory dressed up as the future
• On Reddit and across engineering circles, many devs argued that merging thousands of PRs with effectively unlimited token spend is not a revolution in software engineering.
• Their claim: this is brute-force compute being used to flood a codebase with micro-changes, while ignoring the real bottleneck—long-term maintainability.
• Put differently, code generation scales faster than judgment. And when judgment is underfunded, the debt gets socialized onto whoever inherits the repo.

📌 The marketing value may be higher than the engineering value
• T3 founder Theo argued the real internal cost might be closer to $25k–$50k per month.
• His take was simple: even at that level, the exposure is worth it. Some companies spend $1M on events and get less attention than one viral post from Lauren.
• From Cursor’s perspective, this may be less a unit-economics story and more a PR masterstroke.
• Lauren herself acknowledged the privilege clearly: she works in an AI lab with effectively unlimited tokens, so she does not claim everyone should copy her exact method.

📌 The deeper question is economic, not just technical
• If agentic development only works smoothly when validation loops are massively subsidized, then the real product isn’t “AI coding.” It’s access to cheap verification at scale.
• And if that’s true, AgentFi becomes the more interesting frame: not just what agents can do, but who can afford to let them operate autonomously.
• The future may not belong to teams with the best prompts. It may belong to teams that build the best incentive systems, guardrails, and capital-efficient verification loops.

My read? This story is useful precisely because it makes everyone uncomfortable.
• Best case: it’s an early glimpse of a new engineering stack where agents ship, test, repair, and coordinate across software systems.
• Worst case: it’s a compute-subsidized spectacle that mistakes output volume for product quality.
• Most likely: the truth sits in the middle. Agentic software may be real, but without disciplined architecture and sane economics, it may just become a faster way to manufacture tech debt.

So here’s the question I’d leave you with:
If an agent can write 4,000 PRs a month, but only a tiny elite can afford the validation bill, is that the future of software—or just a demo of power?

author: carlosdomingo
quoted_text:
In 2014 I went nearly a week without sleep. I was running PayPal and attackers were inside our corporate network. They'd compromised an eBay employee's laptop, got onto the VPN, taken over a domain controller and made themselves domain admins. eBay and PayPal were one company then, on one Windows network. They stole 145M eBay user records, then came for the segregated vault holding PayPal's card credentials. We fought them off. They never got in, but they got close. Too close.

Yesterday Binance lost ~$6.3B in what looks like the same way. A DevOps engineer's laptop, then a service inside the withdrawal stack, then withdrawals the signer approved because they came from a trusted source. Hot wallets emptied in under four hours. No key was stolen.

Nobody broke cryptography or a ledger. They found someone with access and used the trust that came with it. Banks get hit exactly the same way.

2016: attackers inside Bangladesh Bank used its own SWIFT access to send $951M of payment orders to the NY Fed. $81M was lost. The rest was held because an unrelated sanctions filter tripped on the word "Jupiter". That was luck, and it only worked because wires took days to settle.

June 2025: an IT employee at C&M Software, which connects Brazilian banks to Pix, sold his credentials for about $2,700. Attackers used them to send fake Pix transfers out of six institutions' reserve accounts at the central bank. ~$140M in under three hours.

August 2025: stolen vendor credentials at Sinqia, another Pix connector. ~R$710M out of HSBC and one other institution in a single afternoon. The central bank froze most of it, after it had already moved.

Same attack every time. Speed is what changed. When settlement took days, a filter, a correspondent bank or someone in ops could catch a bad payment. Pix, FedNow, SEPA Instant and blockchains settle in seconds. Payment security was mostly built for the slow world.

PayPal's card and user data survived 2014 because domain admin on the corp network couldn't unlock it quickly enough, and our alerting caught the unusual activity on the network. That's the model. Approval policy no laptop or vendor login can reach. Velocity and anomaly limits enforced outside the system that sends. Dynamic caps on what any one wallet, account or service can move per hour. All of it in real time.

About $3B of what left Binance has been frozen, almost all of it stablecoins. The $1.4B in bitcoin is sitting in 19 wallets and nobody can touch it. I don't think that's the problem. For decades the ability to reverse a wire or a card charge let a lot of weak security slide. You either stop the transfer before it's signed or you eat the loss.

Nothing about the technology failed here. The chains processed exactly the transactions they were handed. Binance's own systems handed them the wrong ones because an engineer's laptop was compromised. That's operational security. eBay in 2014, Bangladesh Bank and two Pix connectors all failed at it on their own rails.

In 2014 the attackers never reached the vault. If they had, the fraud losses would have been the small part. PayPal existed so people could pay without handing their card details to every merchant on the internet. We held those details so they didn't have to. Losing them would have broken the one thing the company was built on, and I'm not sure we would have recovered.

I expect blockchains and digital assets to become the standard way money moves. Every custodian of digital assets, or of fiat on a real-time rail, is in that position now. The controls have to adapt to settlement in seconds, crypto or not.

Statement on the $AXIS Sell-off of 28–29 October

Over the past two days, a series of addresses sold a large volume of $AXIS on-chain. We want to set out clearly what these tokens were and what we are doing about it.

1. No team or investor tokens were sold.
All Core Team and investor allocations, together with every other locked allocation, 835,000,000 $AXIS (83.5% of total supply), remain in the vesting contract, which is jointly administered with Binance: 0xAFE41cfd4C21f1D896678e32C5AD456ea41835e6. Anyone can verify the balance on BaseScan. Not a single token has left it, and none unlocks before the 12-month cliff.

2. Where the sold tokens came from.
The tokens sold came from the initial circulating supply set out in our published tokenomics, specifically part of the Ecosystem allocation. Many ecosystem recipients are not crypto-native, so their allocation was delivered through a single OTC counterparty, under a written agreement that includes lock-up terms.

3. What we believe happened.
The pattern of the sales, which went through exchange deposit routes and hundreds of fresh addresses within hours of delivery, strongly suggests that the OTC counterparty sold these tokens on the open market. If so, this is inconsistent with the agreement.

4. What we are doing.
- We have suspended all further dealings with this counterparty.
- We are reviewing the agreement with legal counsel and will pursue every remedy available under it.
- Going forward, any remaining Ecosystem tokens will be distributed only through on-chain vesting.

The team‘s tokens remain locked, and our commitment to building Axis is unchanged.

we live in a fugazi economy, a fragile stack of leverage where every lever of risk is controlled by someone else. hyperfinancialization has turned the butterfly effect into our daily reality: a missile hits a pipeline thousands of miles away, an algorithm updates, and your grocery bill spikes by 20%.

text:
My Q4 trade plan for November and December

The dip to buy is right now. #Bitcoin dropped to $76.3K this week, right onto the 50 week SMA. I think this is the cheapest price Bitcoin will trade at for the rest of this bull run.

Here's why.

Bitcoin confirmed the bull run two months ago, when it closed a week back above the bull market support band. The band is the zone between two lines on the weekly chart:
The 50 week SMA, the bottom, about $76K
The 50 week EMA, the top, about $78.6K

In a bull run, Bitcoin holds above this band on the weekly chart. The 50 week SMA is the floor, and price is sitting on it right now.

So I'm buying today. Not after months of sideways trading, and not lower. The bottom of this correction should be in this month, most likely right after the midterm elections on Nov 3.

When I'm wrong: a weekly close below the 50 week SMA, about $76K right now.

A daily wick down below $76K, a quick drop that snaps back, could still happen next week, right after the midterms. That's a typical liquidity hunt: price dips to where a lot of traders have money in borrowed bets and automatic sell orders, just under $76K, and forces them out. All it takes is a weekly close back above the 50 week SMA, and the bull run is still intact. If that quick drop happens, I buy it too. That's the window: today, and maybe next week.

Today my office has released a major new report on student enrollment in NYC.

We found that k-12 enrollment in our public schools has fallen by 187k since 2013, with a projected decline of an additional 128k students by 2034.

As total enrollment declines, NYCPS is serving a student population with growing needs. The number of students with disabilities is increasing. In the most recent school year, approximately 73% of students were in poverty and 14% were homeless or living in temporary housing.

Our report finds the drop in enrollment is driven by declining births and families with children leaving NYC, with a particularly notable drop in public-school enrollment as students transition from elementary to middle school.

These trends have massive implications for our schools that we have only barely begin to grapple with. My hope is that this report will spur a long overdue conversation about what the era of falling student enrollment means for NYC, and what we can do to reverse or slow it. 🧵

$6.3 billion is the biggest in USD terms, but not in BTC terms. MtGox was 650,000 BTC!

Other important numbers to consider:

% of bitcoin (in relation to BTC total supply), ie, market impact. MtGox is big there again at 5%+.

Number of users impacted, and % of user assets impacted. MtGox (the largest CEX at the time) and FTX (not small) were all near 100% of users and their asseets.

Most important: Who is impacted? Does the platform cover it all? (only one victim), as in recent two CEX cases and Binance.

quoted_text:
I joined @GoogleDeepMind to develop a research program on the economics of AGI. Today, together with Andrew Koh (@andrewjkoh) and Shane Legg (@ShaneLegg), we are incredibly excited to release The Economics of Intelligence, the first in a series of projects from our group on how AGI will change the economy.

How do capability improvements transform the economy, and when? In this project, we define thresholds of economic capabilities, e.g., minimal AGI, based on how they transform the economy. We then track how the economy–market structure, employment, and wages–changes during the transition across capability regimes.

We have seen exponential increases in what AI agents can do but the broader economy seems almost remarkably unchanged. Part of the reason is that the solo AI agent is the wrong economic object; economic transformation is an equilibrium outcome where organizations compete. Looking at how intelligence functions within organizations, transformation will depend on when two key capability thresholds are crossed: competence (gains on individual skills, e.g., coding, math) and coordination (gains on ability of agents to cooperate and work together).

We show that what economic transformation looks like depends on whether AI becomes supercompetent, supercooperative, or both—the regime of artificial superintelligence (ASI). Tracking this transition shows why the real visible transformation may come from improvements in coordination—a capability most benchmarks don’t yet track. Past a certain threshold, AI capabilities can break the Coasian ceiling on firm size and lead to an economy that looks drastically different than the one we see today.

Two main takeaways:
1. To understand the path of transformation, we should be tracking agentic coordination more closely.
2. The impact of AI will likely show up in wages before market structure or employment.

We are really excited about this paper. Excited to hear people’s thoughts.

Link: https://t.co/9DTGSeKoSA

text:
Super interesting!

"What is Work For? Labor, Politics, and Meaning in the Age of AI" by Julian Jacobs.

"This paper investigates the role of work in providing a source of meaning, purpose, community, and other non-monetary benefits. Using an original cross-national survey of 8,234 working-age adults across the United Kingdom, United States, Denmark, and India, I study the factors that motivate people in their work, with an eye toward the potential future AI economic transformation. I find that 81% of respondents report being satisfied with their job, and a majority of people across all four countries are strongly motivated by the non-monetary components of their employment. Using an original “Work Values” Index, I show that one third of working respondents in our sample are motivated intrinsically by their job—valuing their role for its own sake. Nearly one quarter of respondents are driven by social and community-related aspects of their employment. A further 17% are driven by a feeling of social status. Just over one quarter of workers are motivated by the transactional financial benefits of their job. Although a majority of people would choose to leave their role if offered their current salary as a guaranteed income, one fifth of workers would choose to stay in their job even if offered up to 120% of their salary. Workers who are intrinsically motivated by their job were disproportionately likely to refuse a basic income at any substitution level. Groups attached to their job for non-monetary reasons were also more likely to pursue volunteering or work-like activities if they received guaranteed income substitution but could no longer perform their current role. Crucially, these non-monetary work motivations are evenly distributed across the income distribution and between white- and blue-collar workers. I argue that these findings have implications for managing the AI transition, understanding attitudes to AI, and making sense of policy preferences. Guaranteeing a basic income may indeed be necessary for managing any future AI labor shock, yet it could ultimately fail to compensate workers for any loss of the non-monetary benefits they derive from work."

text:
Binance Co-CEO: Binance's Own Hot Wallet Was Compromised, Customer Funds Were Unaffected

Binance Co-CEO Richard Teng @_RichardTeng addressed users on October 30 following a roughly $6.3 billion hack, stating that Binance's own hot wallet was compromised while customer funds remained unaffected. He explained that most user assets are stored in cold wallets and only moved to hot wallets for withdrawals. 

Teng said Binance would cover all losses using company funds, with over $6.34 billion reserved, including $5 billion already held in affected assets such as USDC, USDT, BTC, ETH, and BNB. Binance is purchasing the remaining tokens through open-market and OTC transactions. To address concerns about asset safety, Teng said Binance plans to release an initial Proof of Reserves for public verification on Monday.

quoted_text:
David Sacks @DavidSacks named the mechanism that breaks every "token prices are falling, so the market shrinks" argument.

Cheaper tokens don't shrink the bill. They change what gets built on top of it.

Jason Calacanis @Jason had set it up by noting enterprises stick with the cheaper Claude tiers once a task is handled well enough. Sacks' point: Jevons paradox keeps playing out, agents burn far more tokens than a single prompt ever did, and cyber defense is moving from one pen test a year to continuous monitoring of agents and attack surfaces. Jason's number for the gap: new use cases can run 50 to 100 times the tokens of the ones they replace.

Every falling per-token price resets the baseline for what a normal task consumes. The real market-size question isn't whether price keeps falling. It's whether the next use case needs 50 times more of it.

Our coverage walks through where Sacks and Calacanis think token demand goes next.

Uncovered a potential new product @Collector_Crypt may be launching. Their deployer is hinting at an index token backed by a pool of cards. If true, that could be pretty cool.

For the longest time, there was no index that users could long to gain exposure to the TCG space. Now, a vault could hold a basket of eligible graded Pokémon cards, with the index token giving holders fractional exposure to the underlying cards.

text:
🚨 复盘｜Flap 官网（https://t.co/WLrSEbWrT3）被劫持全过程：提前 33 天像素级克隆、16 分钟打穿 HTTPS 安全锁

今天上午，代币发射平台 @flapdotsh@flapdotsh @flapdotsh 紧急发推预警官网遭遇 DNS 劫持。

很多人第一反应以为只是普通的前端被挂马，或者 CDN 解析记录被改。但我们在官方切流恢复前后的几十秒窗口内，直接从 .sh 顶级域注册局、CT 证书透明度日志、Name[.]com 权威节点残留区域以及黑客的荷兰源站上，完整抓到了还没来得及销毁的第一手犯罪现场。

结论非常明确，也足够给整个 Web3 敲响警钟：
这不是智能合约漏洞，不是 Vercel 源站沦陷，也不是 Cloudflare 被攻破——而是一场潜伏超过一个月、直击域名注册商底层控制权的精准猎杀。

下面用真实抓包的链下与网络取证数据，逐秒还原黑客到底是怎么做到的 👇

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

▍一、 破除误区：到底哪一层失守了？

在攻击发生前，flap[.]sh 的正常架构非常清晰：
• 域名注册商：Name[.]com（IANA ID: 625）
• 权威 DNS 与防护层：Cloudflare（wren / memphis.ns.cloudflare[.]com）
• 真实业务源站：Vercel（216.150.x.x）

事件爆发后，我们第一时间直连探测了原 Cloudflare 权威节点。结果显示：无论是主站、docs / abi / beta / blinks 等十余个业务子域名，还是企业邮 MX 记录与后端的 Vercel 部署，全部完好无损、零篡改。

真正沦陷的，是最底层却最容易被忽视的命门——【域名注册商后台】。

我们在官方切走解析后仅 12 分钟，对 Name[.]com 自身的权威服务器（ns1 ~ ns4）进行了残留区域探测，当场抓到了黑客来不及清理的作案铁证：
攻击者拿下了域名在注册商后台的控制权，强行把 .sh 顶级域的 NS 委派从 Cloudflare 切到了注册商自带默认 DNS（ns1crv / ns2kqz / ns3jkl / https://t.co/P3wp0sfpdD），并将主站与 www 的 A 记录直接指向了黑客位于荷兰的恶意服务器：31.56.52.52。

只要控制了顶级域 NS 委派，哪怕你的 Cloudflare 防火墙配得固若金汤、智能合约审计了十遍，所有用户流量都会在踏入大门前被直接拐进黑客的屠宰场。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

二、 提前 33 天的暗中踩点：连下拉菜单都写了专属伪装代码

把时间线拉回黑客服务器（31.56.52.52，归属荷兰 Snowcore Inc，运行 Ubuntu nginx/1.18.0）的静态样本上，你会发现这绝不是临时起意的盲打，而是蓄谋超过一个月的定点狙击：

1️⃣ 9 月 28 日（提前 33 天）：手写 UI 交互胶水层
直接把动态 React / Next.js 网站扒成静态 HTML 有一个通病——原本基于 Radix UI 的顶部公链切换框（BSC / Base / Monad / XLayer）、中英文切换和“CREATE TOKEN”下拉菜单会全部点不动，老玩家一点就会察觉不对劲。

为了消除这个破绽，黑客早在北京时间 9 月 29 日 01:43（UTC 9月28日 17:43）就专门编写了一个名为 /flap.sh/_clone/flap-menus.js（18.5 KB）的伪装脚本。甚至在黑客服务器返回的源码头部，还明晃晃留着当时的英文开发注释：
"restores the Radix dropdown menus (chain / language / CREATE TOKEN) on the static clone. Markup is the exact HTML captured from the live site."
（在静态克隆站上恢复链切换、语言与创建代币下拉菜单，标记取自线上真实站点。）

2️⃣ 10 月 24 日（提前 7 天）：同步新版前端与封装盗币器
北京时间 10 月 24 日 23:11，黑客重新抓取了 Flap 当时的线上前端版本（dpl_HbZmYLVY...），生成了 169 KB 的高仿真暗黑风主页，剥离了官方全部 Next.js 业务脚本，只留下了上面的菜单伪装层和核心盗币载荷。

3️⃣ 10 月 30 日（提前 28 小时）：肉鸡就位
北京时间 10 月 30 日 04:07:23，黑客开通荷兰 VPS 31.56.52[.]52（该服务器默认自签名证书 CN=localhost 的生成时间精确停留在这一秒），万事俱备，只等动手。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

▍三、 清晨 08:35 闪电夺权：仅用 16 分钟打穿 HTTPS 绿锁

为什么受害者打开被劫持的官网时，浏览器没有弹出任何“连接不安全 / 证书无效”的红屏警告？

答案就藏在两个精确到秒的取证时间戳里：

• 08:35:23（北京时间 10月31日）—— 篡改权威 NS
残留恶意区域的 SOA 序列号为 1793406923，换算成 Unix 时间戳正是 2026-10-31 00:35:23 UTC（北京时间早 08:35:23）。黑客选择在亚洲清晨、欧美深夜的交界窗口准时切走域名解析。

• 08:51:30（仅隔 16 分钟）—— 签发合法 HTTPS 证书
因为该域名既没有开启 DNSSEC（注册局状态为 unsigned），也没有配置限制发证机构的 CAA 记录。解析生效后仅 16 分钟，黑客就在荷兰服务器上跑通了 ACME 域名控制权验证，从 Let's Encrypt（YR1）顺利拿到了一张受全球所有浏览器信任的双域名合法 TLS 证书（CT 预证书 SCT 记录精确到 00:51:30.568 UTC）。

至此，从域名解析、HTTPS 加密握手到页面 UI 菜单交互，整条信任链被黑客完美闭环接管。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

▍四、 藏在 1.95 MB 文件里的“生僻汉字混淆”盗币引擎

在黑客克隆页里，真正致命的是第二个脚本：/flap.sh/assets/quiet-ember-one.js（体积高达 1,948,931 字节）。

对其进行静态拆解后可以看到典型的成熟商业级 Drainer-as-a-Service（DaaS）架构特征：

▸ 高熵生僻汉字虚拟机壳：
代码外层并非普通的十六进制混淆，而是利用大量生僻汉字构造动态 Function 执行环境（如：Function("昞穼垚譎暋楳", "var 纥爘迳輘替唟,贀寑臧烡扄舯媈...")），配合 LZString 压缩与浏览器原生 WebCrypto（crypto.subtle）在内存中动态解密真实恶意逻辑，极大增加静态查杀难度。

▸ 基于 Irys（Arweave 生态）的去中心化抗封禁 C2：
样本内部集成了 irys[.]xyz 去中心化存储网关引用与 /assets/init 初始化逻辑。这也是近年顶级加密钓鱼团伙的惯用伎俩——将控制端（C2）配置存放在不可篡改、无法被传统安全厂商轻易拔线或 Sinkhole 的去中心化网关上。

一旦受害者在页面点击连接钱包或尝试发币/交易，脚本就会接管 Web3 Provider，根据钱包资产净值动态诱导签署恶意无限额 Approve、Permit2 离线签名或伪造转账交易，瞬间搬空高价值资产。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

▍五、 82 分钟真空期与紧急切流——但我们发现了 3 个残余暗雷！

从 08:51:30 恶意 HTTPS 全量生效，到 10:13:28 官方推特发出警报，中间存在整整 82 分钟的无预警黄金暴露窗口；随后在 10:27:34，团队将 .sh 注册局的权威 NS 紧急切回了早期的 Vercel DNS（ns1 / ns2.vercel-dns[.]com），并在 10:40 左右清除了恶意解析区。

看起来已经恢复了？别急，实时底层取证显示目前仍有 3 个不可忽视的风险点：

⚠️ 暗雷 1：域名仍处于危险的“pending transfer（转移处理中）”状态！
查询 .sh 注册局实时 RDAP 数据可以发现，原有的 clientTransferProhibited（禁止转移锁）已被解除，且当前注册局状态赫然显示为【pending transfer】！
这只有两种可能：要么是官方夺回账号后正在主动发起跨注册商紧急搬家；要么是黑客在劫持 NS 的同时，偷偷提取了 EPP 转移密码发起了恶意转出！如果是后者且未及时联系注册商人工拦截（NACK），5 天窗口期一过，域名所有权将面临被彻底转走的风险。

⚠️ 暗雷 2：递归 DNS 缓存长尾 + 黑客服务器仍在线
由于恶意区域设置了缓存 TTL，部分地区公共递归 DNS（例如实测国内 114.114.114.114 就出现了明显滞后）不会立刻刷新；同时黑客的荷兰服务器 31.56.52[.]52 此时此刻仍在正常响应钓鱼页面。

⚠️ 暗雷 3：恶意证书尚未吊销 & www 子域旧证书过期
黑客签发的那张 Let's Encrypt 证书有效期直到 2027 年 1 月 28 日，目前在 CT 状态中仍为未吊销（revoked: false）；而官方紧急切回的 Vercel DNS 用的是今年 8 月前的旧区配置，导致直接访问 www 子域会命中一张今年 7 月 6 日就已过期的旧证书。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

▍六、 交易员紧急自救指南 & 给所有项目方的警钟

【如果你是普通用户 / 交易员】
1. 在 @flapdotsh 官方宣布彻底排除隐患并恢复前，切勿打开官网，不要连接钱包，不要签署任何弹窗！
2. 如果你在【北京时间 10 月 31 日 08:35 至 10:45】期间访问过该网站：
   ├─ 立即在钱包扩展中断开对应站点连接会话；
   ├─ 立即前往 https://t.co/Op4T9K84bO 检查 BSC、Base 等链上近期的代币授权（重点排查无限额 Approve 与 Permit2 合约授权）并全部撤销；
   └─ 若期间签署过任何不明离线消息或交易，最稳妥的做法是立刻将主力资产转移至全新的钱包地址。

【给所有 Web3 项目方的血泪教训】
过去两年，从头部 DeFi 协议到热门 Launchpad，类似的注册商/DNS 劫持一再重演。很多团队愿意花十几万美金做三轮智能合约审计，却把承载全部用户流量的域名放在普通注册商账号里“裸奔”。

请所有项目方立刻自查四件事：
• 核心域名必须开启【Registry Lock（注册局级人工锁）】，杜绝后台被盗后秒改 NS 或偷转域名；
• 注册商与 Cloudflare 账号强制绑定硬件安全密钥（YubiKey / Passkey），废除短信与邮箱验证码 2FA；
• 立即开启【DNSSEC】；
• 配置严格的【CAA 记录】（限定唯一发证 CA 并绑定具体 accounturi），让黑客就算改了解析也签不出合法 HTTPS 证书。

在 Web3 世界里，决定木桶水位的往往不是链上不可篡改的合约，而是链下最脆弱的那个 Web2 登录框。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The timing and outcome of the SEC staff’s review are not within our control.

We also expect to miss the December 31 deadline for furnishing our interim financial information for the first half of 2026, as completion of that report depends on resolution of the same accounting matters.

text:
Today is the last regular working day for the @Balancer  team.

Some of the people on this team have been here since Balancer's earliest days. Others joined along the way. Together, they helped build and evolve the protocol over the years.

From the original weighted pools and liquidity bootstrapping to the v2 Vault, Boosted Pools, and v3, Balancer helped shape how liquidity works in DeFi. Behind all of that were years of research, engineering, integrations, operations, and work with partners that most people never saw.

The last year was especially difficult. The exploit hurt people who trusted Balancer, and the team went through the recovery, restructuring, and eventually the decision to wind down. Even after the end date was set, they continued doing the work needed to support users and partners.

This isn't the ending we worked for. But it doesn't take away what the team built and contributed to DeFi.

The winddown itself continues under BIP-928. For the remaining steps and withdrawal information, please follow the official Balancer updates.

To everyone who helped build Balancer over the years, thank you. 
I'm grateful I got to work with so many of you.

GM☕️ 如何保持自己的 Grok Bot 一直「与时俱进」？

从 @OKxiaohai 海哥那儿学了一招：让自己的 Grok Bot 定期去看 @poteto Lauren Tan 的帖子，学学做这个产品的人，平时到底怎么用它。

Lauren 本人参与 Grok Bot 开发，她分享的实际用法，时效性和实用性都非常高。

比如她最近分享的 tibot，会盯提到自己或指定关键词的帖子，过滤噪音、翻译、定时整理成短摘要，发帖还是她自己写。

她之前还分享过给例程做体检：哪些闲置了，哪些太烧额度；再回看平时纠正 Bot 的地方，找出技能和例程该怎么改。

我想抄的就是这些细节。让 Bot 每天去翻一翻，再对照自己的任务，挑一两条试试：能省哪一步，能减少什么返工，适不适合写进现在的技能或例程。

想试的，可以把下面这段丢给自己的 Bot (可以根据自己需求调整频率）：

「每天查看 @poteto (Lauren Tan) 自上次检查以来的新帖、长文和相关回复，关注 Grok Bot 的技能、例程、额度和验证方法。结合我现有的任务，只报值得借鉴的变化，附原帖链接、适用场景，以及可直接粘贴的技能或例程修改建议。先给建议，改动由我确认。没有值得借鉴的更新就安静，抓取失败要说明。不要代发帖。」

我想抄的就是这些细节。让 Bot 每天去翻一翻，再对照自己的任务，挑一两条试试：能省哪一步，能减少什么返工，适不适合写进现在的技能或例程。

想试的，可以把下面这段丢给自己的 Bot (可以根据自己需求调整频率）：

「每天查看 @poteto (Lauren Tan) 自上次检查以来的新帖、长文和相关回复，关注 Grok Bot 的技能、例程、额度和验证方法。结合我现有的任务，只报值得借鉴的变化，附原帖链接、适用场景，以及可直接粘贴的技能或例程修改建议。先给建议，改动由我确认。没有值得借鉴的更新就安静，抓取失败要说明。不要代发帖。」
